reviewText: t'irla ~The BookSlayer~'s reviewRead from December 29 to 30, 2012Amazing introduction for new author Nulli Para Ora. Dragon Moon is everything a lover of romance could want in a unique PNR novel! A MUST read.Description:A business trip to China. A fight for their lives. Will Angelique and David become pawns in a werewolf war or does fate have something else in store?David Johnson and Angelique Meadows are colleagues on a business trip to China. They've worked together for years, but neither has been able to admit their true feelings for the other. This business trip represents a landmark deal in their careers and an opportunity to reveal the truth of their hearts. Just as love blooms, disaster strikes.The man they're meeting with is Yuen Gao, CEO of a multi-million dollar company. The world sees him as a successful businessman. His pack sees him as their Alpha. Rogues, secret experiments, and the undeniable pull of his mate force him to reveal his secret. Is his love strong enough to overcome the pain of loss?Hearts unite and break as trusted friends become enemies behind the scenes. Love longed for is lost to be replaced by a bond deeper than words. Loyalties are tested as ghosts of the past step into the present.Can true love survive when forbidden hearts are reconnected?My Thoughts:Wow, talk about something different in PNR, I absolutely loved this novel. Nulli Para Ora breathes a breath of fresh air into romantic paranormal suspense. Although interracial couple are not unheard of in PNR it is highly unusual to have Asian/Black/White all in the same book as a love triangle. For me this was my first experience with a Chinese male protagonist and I hope that it is not my last Gao was unbelievably romantic, sensitive and all alpha. David was more aggressive even before the change and still a wonderful alpha. Angelique was everything you could want in a heroine, smart, focused, sensitive and kick-ass. The story NPO weaves was exciting enough to keep me up until 5:30 am this morning reading. I had to find out what happened. The book kept me on the edge of my seat..er.. bed, it was fast paced, and the plot deftly wound around the supporting characters to make them as integral to the story as the main characters. The fact that these characters are  fully dimensional  makes them easy for the reader to identify with and empathize. This complex story  introduced a plot twist right at the end, not a cliff hanger but an "uh oh now what" moment. Overall this is an exciting start to a new series and I for one can't wait for book 2. Ora is a new name in romantic paranormal and I know this novel will springboard her onto everyone's favorite shelf.  She is definitely on mine!4.5 solid gold stars for Dragon Moon and a new fangirl in me. Do yourself a favor read this book now and treat yourself to a taste of Gao/David and Angelique.
summary: Dragon Moon a MUST read for all PNR lovers!!! Don't miss out

reviewText: The first book in the series is really a set up novel. The second book takes you more into the action and the illumination of many of the things that were hinted at in the first.Ann is underground. Her life began to unravel in Washington State. Her situation was compromised. Word about her and her abilities was put into the hands of the wrong people. Her family and friends were put in precarious positions. One thread they all have in common is that they vowed to protect Ann at all costs.Ann's paranormal abilities are growing. She is now able to use them in ways that she did not believe possible. As her abilities increased, the net around her begins to tighten. Those tightening it are her friends willing to protect her and her enemies trying to cut her off.This book has some intense moments. Ann is learning who is friend and who is foe. I highly recommend the second book in the series, but to read it, you must read the first to grasp the intricate plot that Linda has created.Once again, she leaves us on a cliffhanger. Dang! She has however guaranteed that I will be reading the next installment

5 starsI was really excited to find out what happens with Reed and Elle.  The author takes a turn and tells how Elle is trying to get her life back together which I think is good, but it is frustrating because Reed is in town but they still haven't met up in the first ten chapters.  Life seems to be getting better for Elle, but for Reed he is frustrated.  The author starts Reed off, going to college, getting ready for tryouts, and trying to figure out if he can win Elle back.  In the first quarter of the book I really enjoy Reed's POV better than Elle's, because you can tell Elle still doesn't know what she wants, but Reed has a plan.  This is a book of second chances and honestly I loved this book so much more than Breaking Elle.  Reading the last two thirds of this book really picked up.  There is so much drama in this book and still many secrets still there that need to be found out which makes it that more enticing.  Love is a tricky thing and Reed and Elle prove over and over again that it can be so worth it.  With adding Luke, good ole Tyler, Cane, Jace, and a bunch of secondary characters its a cluster of what is going to happen next and who is in trouble this time.  The epilogue,  I would have to say it was perfect, to still see insecurities, even though they have been through so much makes it real, and I truly like real books.  This book of the series did not drag like the first one and it really kept you wanting more, and that is what I liked.On the second book of this series, Reed decides that he needs to go back and make things with Elle.  Elle is trying to regain some composure in her life, but with all honesty she is failing.  She is trying to live, but she misses Reed immensly.  As Reed comes back into the picture.  Tyler has now moved in for the opening and well, it made sense.  With that complication Reed has to figure out how to win his girl back.  With the lingering debt still in his future, his love for Elle, and his mom with her cancer coming back, his plate is full, oh and don't forget his football career that he is trying to pursue.  What is a boy gonna do?  He's gonna fight for everything that he wants.  There is still so much drama that it will keep you intriguged until you finish the book.I absolutely loved this book and not only was the storyline great, it had my favorite sports teams in it.  New England Patriots and the Dallas Cowboys.  How can you go wrong.  You can't.  Read this book, this is one of these books that you will have a hangover for a few days and it will be well worth it.

reviewText: I am a HUGE HUGE HUGE fan of Kristen Ashley. Have lost count of how many novels I have read of hers. Most of them I have really enjoyed. My favorite have been the 'Burg' and Colorado Mountain series. LOVE the Burg series.Storyline in a nutshell:Colin Morgan and Sibyl Godwin are the reincarnated souls of two loves, Royce Morgan and Beatrice Godwin (who were murdered in 1522).Sibyl is a good-hearted, almost angelic-like person who is sometimes careless and impetuous. Colin is a wealthy, alpha-male that is cynical about love and women. Sibyl and Colin embark on a relationship (albeit very rocky at first) and must fight the evils of both the supernatural and 'of this earth' evils.What I liked about this book:- Although Sibyl can be a little goofy and careless, she has a huge selfless heart - who couldn't love someone like this. She loves Colin unselfishly, doesn't lie, isn't super emotional. Solid.- Colin - yes, a bit of the alpha-male, but so sexy and 'take charge'. Can't help but feel safe with that around. When he finally commits to having Sibyl as part of his life-  he does it with the passion and emotion that is breathtaking.- Yum - yes - lots of steamy scenes although not as graphic as some of her other novels. Starts off super hot, then glosses over specifics. Still hot enough to set my Kindle on fire- No cliff hangers- HEA (super HEA)- Other characters are great. Even the animals play a significant role in the book- I enjoyed the beginning a lot. Colin is not falling immediately for Sibyl. He believes that she has malicious motives. I like that they didn't fall madly in love right away.- The mother, Mags is funny. She is goofy, inappropriate and perceptive. I enjoy people like that.What I didn't like about this book:- The story starts well enough. But then it gets into magic and I just can't get my head around it. The magic spells seem like an unfair advantage for the good guys.- The ending. Before their HEA - the evil souls get defeated WAY to easily! The build up was great. Shadows lurking. People that cannot be caught. 500 years of evil waiting for revenge. Etc. But poof - the good guys win almost without a sweat. Was hoping for a better battle. More suspense.- SPOILER------- Colin decides to propose to Sibyl and doesn't even purchase the ring himself. UGH. That threw the romance out the window. Why didn't he get it himself!- I found myself more interested in the secondary characters than the main characters towards the middle and end of the book. Didn't connect as much with Sibyl and Colin after the first part of the book. Not sure what happened. They seemed to react more to their outside environment than to each other.Again, I LOVE this author.Just not this particular book.
summary: Wanted to like it more...but I didn't fall for these characters

When Sam gets transferred to DC, he checks in on Georgie for her brother and the sparks fly...when Sam discovers that Georgie's missing student has dragged her into a huge mess involving a terrorist organization, he does the only thing he can do, he protects her with his life. When Sam whisks her off to a remote location for her protection, those sparks turn into a raging inferno. Georgie is a force to be reckoned with when it comes to getting what she wants and she wants Sam. Will Sam be able to resist her allure and maintain his position as her protector? Will Georgie be able to convince Sam that love is worth the risk? This novella in the HOT series will have you desperate for the next installment of HOT men!!! Way to go Lynn, you hit it out of the park once again!

reviewerName: Mr. C. A. Meade "Christopher Antony Meade"
reviewText: This book contains all the gritty realism, allied with deep humanity, which I found in the other novel I read by this very talented author. The picture that it paints of nineteen eighties/nineties New York is certainly not one of a city I would recognise, but then I'm just a country boy and the lives depicted here are alien territory to me. Only on the surface though. Underneath the skin, the characters in this story of murderous doings in The Big Apple have all the same feelings of love, hate, loyalty and jealousy that have been the lot of all people since the time of the cavemen.All these things are brought out and presented to the reader in this book. If this writer has the skill, (which he undoubtedly does), of making a simple rural soul like me feel a real sense of involvement with the strivings and dilemmas of metropolitan American gang members, how much more relevant is his work going to be to people living in the environments he describes? It is one of the hallmarks of a great writer to be able to get readers, from all backgrounds, to feel a sense of kinship with his characters. Kawand Crawford easily passes that test and possesses the hallmark.
summary: Gritty and absorbing, Not to be missed.

reviewText: When I downloaded this (free) book, my impression was that it was a true story of a family from the UK as they embarked upon their first "naturist" holiday. Prior to reading it, I noticed in the credits and license that it is a work of fiction. He also wrote about real places, and included photos and web sites about said places. Fact or fiction?I must've had expectations because when I finished this very fast read, I was a bit let down. Mr. Harding seemed unable to enjoy any part of his vacation (free time, dining out, being with his family) unless he was not clothed. It IS a freeing experience; however, I have found that people who participate in this type of vacation go in with the understanding that there will be times when clothing will be required. Toward the end, I felt he was "bashing" folks who didn't want to consider this type of vacation, as in his comment: "I genuinely don't know why people have such a hang-up over other people being naked. . . "I'm glad this was a free download - I would be upset if I'd paid for it!

(originally posted on my GR account)After reading 'One Perfect Night' and watching Rafe and Mia making brief appearances, I couldn't wait to read the first book in the Sullivans of Seattle (though book 9 in the whole series).Rafe's being someone whose story I've been curious to read ever since he first showed up on his cousins books (Sullivans of San Francisco) and 'One Perfect Night' only made me more excited to read him.'The Way You Look Tonight' finally gives readers the chance to get to know him, his family and the woman who owns his heart: Brooke Jansen.But before I talk more about Rafe and Brooke, I have to admit I couldn't help feeling nostalgia because I wasn't visiting San Francisco and The Sullivans who own my heart. There are some mentions and one cameo but I really missed them. (And I might start re-reading the first 8 books because of that).Now, onto Rafe and Brooke...I enjoyed their story, I enjoyed getting to know Rafe more, as well as I enjoyed meeting Brooke, BUT their story didn't catch my interest like the previous books in the series.There were things going on between them but sometimes I felt like nothing was going on. I just didn't connect completely with them as a couple.Anyhow, I seem to be one of the few people who've read the book who feels this way, so I encourage you--if you're a contemporary romance fan--to give this book and 'new series' a chance. I certainly will with the next one: Mia Sullivan's book.And if you haven't read any of The Sullivans, I absolutely recommend you to start now.

**3.5 Stars**From the book cover and description, I assumed that Tempted by Trouble was going to be your typical "boy meets girls, they fall in love, and happily ever after." What surprised me was that this story that Michelle Smart has penned was way more than that. It was much deeper, more emotional, and heartbreaking at the same time.Ms. Smart's writing was smooth and the story flowed nicely. As for the characters, Pippa & Marco, they were well developed. Pippa has had a hard past and was quite the rebel in her early days, but one can come to understand why she did the things she did once her childhood story unravelled. She was young, alone and afraid and had needed love, comfort, and reassurance. I just wanted to give her good ol' hugs throughout the story. She had some very heartbreaking moments in the book where my heart just broke out for her. For example, when Pippa was lying in the hospital bed with Marco there reassuring her that there are people who love her and want nothing but the best for her, she replied back, "Name one person who loves me." My heart just broke into pieces.As for Marco...I wanted to slap him on more than one occasion.I had mixed feelings towards him and it was hard for me to like him at first honestly. His derogatory remarks, doubts, and attitude towards Pippa was a bit more than I could stand. I wasn't sure if I was ever going to warm up to him, but thankfully I did...towards the end. I would've liked for him to grovel more as I honestly think that he didn't fully redeemed himself before the story ended, but that's just according to me. Furthermore, I felt that the resolution with her father came a bit too easily and the HEA came a bit too quickly for me.Yet, in the end I thought that Tempted by Trouble was a quick & sexy read with just the right amount of emotions. It was an engaging read overall as I was up long past my bedtime and finished Tempted by Trouble in two sittings.*ARC courtesy of the author in exchange for an honest review.
summary: Tempted by Trouble by Michelle Smart

Set over a period of around seven years from the beginning of the Great War through to the start of the Roaring Twenties, Four Florins tells the stories of a huge cast, with each of their lives interwoven with those of the others, sometimes inextricably, sometimes tenuously, and not always in an apparent manner. Set in Scotland, the stories travel between Edinburgh, Falkirk, Glasgow and the Highlands, pivoting round the tragic tale of a young girl, Isabella, who with her sisters, is unloved by a mother more interested in her causes of womens’ votes and encouraging men to go to war.All too suddenly, young Isa finds herself pregnant to a young man tragically lost to a train wreck on his way to fight in the trenches, and is abandoned to her fate in a poorhouse by her mother. Her father is lost in Aegean, reporting on the war effort, and her siblings and mother are left near destitute.The Four Florins of the title are the saving of Isabella. As a potential parent for Isabella’s new-born daughter takes pity, so Isabella takes flight and escapes the poorhouse. Meanwhile her mother has found work at her father’s old offices. Intertwined are stories of secret agents, the adoptive parents, school teachers, her sisters and a myriad of other characters.Tragedy and sadness abound in this novel, and whilst light is seen towards the end, there is also sadness at the many people lost, not just to war, but also to accident, murder, injury or just forgotten. It is a tale of changing times, when women were beginning to take on, often by necessity, the roles of men, and realise that the old mores of Victorian and Edwardian Britain no longer held sway.The plot is incredibly clever and well-told, but the sheer size of the cast and constant change of scene made the story feel slightly disjointed, not giving you time to feel comfortable with any one of the characters. It became hard to identify with any character as you were thrown over to another aspect to the narrative all too quickly. Then too individuals were introduced only to disappear with barely a second mention whilst others were not given the opportunity to truly flourish.It’s an intriguing novel, but ultimately, the narrative was let down by its complexity, leaving a feeling that you had watched subconscious dreams of fleeting history that never truly coalesced. As the start of a trilogy, I look forward to the next two chapters concentrating more on the principal characters and building strongly on them.
summary: Looking forward to the next two chapters.

reviewText: I read the original series about Rylie, "Seasons of the Moon".  I believe that I rated them all with 4 Stars.  I thought that they were pretty good compared to most of the Werewolf books out there, because they didn't glorify Werewolves.  Rather dark, but interesting.  Although YA, they had a certain general appeal, and the writing wasn't bad.I was afraid that when I found that the author was elaborating on that series with short 'episodes' called  the Cain Chronicles, that I would be disappointed.  And I was, sad to say.This 'book' was under 50 pages.  Again, Rylie and her two romantic interests are the main characters.  NOTE:  This 'book' continued just where the other series left off.  This should be made more clear.  I, having read the other series, knew that.  Other readers may not.  Believe me, if you haven't read that other series, you will have very little idea what is going on in this short story.Nothing really happens in the bulk of this book, other than we are shown that Rylie is still confused with her love life.  She is still pining after Seth.  She is now Alpha of the pack, but is wimpy and doesn't  act like a real Alpha.  Nothing exciting happens until the very last page.  Yes, that's right--the very last page, where it ends with a major cliff hanger.  SO not my idea of a good read.At the end of this book,  the author invites the reader to decide who Rylie will choose for her love.  HUH?  I want a book that decides that for me, and a book that entertains me.  This was neither.  The series should have ended with the last book of Seasons of the Moon, or should have tied up all the loose ends with ONE final full length book.  I will not be strung along with short episodes that are determined by readers.  Nope.  Sorry.

I recommend to any 18+ Reader out there who enjoys some steam with thier paranormal romance.5 out of 5 HeartsLovetiggi' Book Reviews

reviewText: I was pleasantly surprised by the book. When an author takes on a Dickens Classic it had better be good and this book delivered. The book is well written and edited and  stays true to the original book while offering a different perspective on the classic theme. In this sequel Scrooge helps Tiny Tim  open his eyes from his tunnel vision to see all the possibilities in front of him. We all must take a chance on living life. This is a keeper and will be a Christmas reading tradition along with the original.The front cover illustration is very nice and keeps to the Victorian flavor of the book. My only minor complaint is the formatting of the book for the kindle. There are some issues. To get the font to a normal reading size in the paragraphs it changed the font size of the chapter headings to where they were huge and 3 words would take up a whole page. Coming home, he establishes himself in a gorgeous home safe with old magic, and surrounded by forests. One night when he is about to start an agonizing cycle in which he has to keep himself locked away from others, Cora bangs on his front door. Due to poor choices made by her brother before his death, Cora has herself in a tangled mess and is running for her life. Keeping his attraction under control with codes of honor (you don't sleep with a friend's kid sister), Stig finds himself housing Cora in the guestroom while he locks himself in the basement during his dragon cycle.Drawn by curiosity and a very lusty dream, Cora creeps down and eventually finds Stig's secrets and becomes entrapped in his world. Due to a centuries old feud between Knights and Dragons that started with a forbidden love, the Knights are hot on the trails of Stig and using Cora as bait.This story was a very fun romp and I enjoyed that storyline and action that kept the story moving quickly until the end. I enjoyed both Stig's and Cora's characters and their love for each other. Looking forward to the next in the series.Note: Thank you to Netgalley.com and Forever (Grand Central Publishing)for providing me with this book for review.

I couldn't put this book down! I'm aching to know what happens next, and I have nothing else to read to distract me of my suffering. I give it five stars. It's just as good, if not better than Voyage. I don't know if it's just that I have an active imagination, but from the beginning of Voyage I was able to foresee where Flotilla would be headed. I was glad that I was correct, but also still surprised at events that I had not expected.Scott is such a badass leader, which I love. His character is kind, sympathetic, and loving, but at the same time he knows how to stand up for himself and his followers. His confrontations with outsiders, especially government officials, were hilarious and uncomfortable. He always knows exactly what to say and when to say it. So, I guess now I'm wondering what his major character flaw is. His sympathy might get the better of him, but I just can't really see him failing at this point unless he gets killed, which would piss everyone off. Looking into the future of the story, I'll keep my thoughts about what will probably happen to myself, but I'm anxious to know what ends up happening to Clint.This book was a little slower for me than the first, however it was still so gripping. I love the story, all of the characters, the idea, and the author. I have recommended this over and over again to friends, who love zombies as much as I do. It's also gotten to the point where I'm having badass zombie dreams after reading at night, and I love it when a good book isn't ready to let go of my mind even when I have finished reading it. A lot of folks have already read this one, so there are some terrific blog posts covering it. Rather than give you another synopsis, I thought I'd offer a couple specific reasons I like the Rancho Diablo series.First off, it's easily accessible, meaning that if you're a new reader, or someone like me who tends to miss new titles when they're  released, you can stake y'r claim anywhere on the ranch. I didn't get the last book, but that didn't stop me from enjoying this one. Mel Odom wears the Colby Jackson hat this time out, and the narrative voice he and his cohorts (Bill Crider and James Reasoner) have developed is seamless. (I imagine the three of them in front of a roaring fire in some exotic foreign chalet, brainstorming the new year's offerings with abundant stores of rich coffee, heavy ale and roast beast.)I also like the books' ensemble cast. On the screen of my imagination, these stories play like classic TV westerns with familiar characters and surprise guest stars. In THE HOLD UP, I was happy to see Randy Post take the stage, glad to revisit Sam Blaylock and Marshal Tolliver, but happy to meet new faces too. (One of the best being Randy's Bible-thumping cousin, Ruth Ann Deaver.)There's also a lot more action than you'd ever see in those old shows and a lot more depth: two more excuses to add this series to your regular queue.

Genre: Paranormal/Vampire/Shape-ShiftersSeries: Book 1 in the Promise Me SeriesReviewer:BarbHeat Level: 1Review:I am a sucker for vampires (pun intended). I mean what's not to love about finding a handsome unconscious vampire right in your front yard? And it's only a book. So what could go wrong? A lot. Promise Me is packed with exciting surprises, a villain or two to keeps things exciting, and a cast of characters that you will grow to love, starring the hero Danial and Sarelle, the heroine. Both characters are strong-willed and passionate. However, neither overwhelms the other or the story. Hall's casts of secondary characters add that extra punch at just the right moments. And the underlining subplots are edged between facilitating matters between the obsession that is growing stronger between Danial and Sarelle, while other subplots set hurdles.I should mention The Promise Me Series is the type of series, however, where the end of each book leads you into the next, thereby leaving a lot of open-ended voids to be filled. I normally am not too crazy about this type of series. By the time I realized that was the case here, I was too caught up in Promise Me to care. Hall is a talented author and started this series strong with an intriguing lead in PM. So if you normally don't get into these types of series, might I suggest Hall's Promise Me be the one you take a chance on. Here's hoping the next book in this series, Broken Promise will continue what PM started - to keep me riveted and wanting more (*keeping fingers crossed*).Originally Posted at Risque Reviews Website on 8/23/12The Promise Me Series: (In reading order)Promise Me✴ Book I (published May 27 2012) Melange BooksBroken Promise✴ Book II (To be published Fall 2012) Melange BooksTaken in the Night✴ Book III(To be published Winter 2012) Melange BooksTaken for His Own✴ Book IV (To be published early Spring 2013) Melange Books

Just finished reading Book 2 and re-read Book 1 and I must say that I was a little disappointed in Book 2.I found the plot interesting, but I had problems with the main characters.  I had hoped that Jack, Sabre, and George would be a bit more kick-ass.  I mean, they played War as kids, know how to fight with guns, swords, knives and arrows.  I wanted strong female characters who could ride in to save the day as much as the guy.  What I've seen is girls who grew up independent and gutsy turn into simpering ninnies whose only interest is to have sex and whose talents and brains aren't utilized.While Jack at least got to use some of her skills in Book 1, Sabre never gets to use her talents with a sword.  That's disappointing as the first scenes are her dueling Quince and him knowing of her title, the "Whirling Dervish."  Instead, we see her moving into Quince's home and taking over.  She also is much more sexualized than someone in her day and age would have been.  Being interested in kissing is one thing, but it was a bit off-putting that she's trying to initiate sex with Quince, is naked in the tub adjoining his room (she just moves into the Duchess' quarters on her own) and seems to be rather skilled at oral activities before any consummation between the two ever takes place.  She's not a "hero" character, but instead, seems more of a "doxy," which is ironic as that's what the duel was all about.I also have a little trouble with the ages of the Haberdashers.  I've read a LOT of Regency in the past few years, and 18 years old doesn't mean you're "on the shelf."  These girls would barely have had a Season; two tops.  The guys are always surprised at how young they are, ("barely out of the schoolroom" as Quince realizes), so making them the heroine when they're at least 10 years younger than the heroes is a little unbelievable; especially when Gideon and Quince weren't interested in a wife or heirs.I didn't have as much a problem with Quince as others have.  I personally find it refreshing that the H hasn't slept with every milkmaid, servant and prostitute around.  What I had more of an issue with is the reader didn't have a chance to get to know Quince.  He had a horrible father, a mother that was taken from him (why and how old he was when this happened we don't know).  He didn't have siblings or real friends except Gideon and so that all goes into his character as an adult.  There is never a solid back story, so I think that's why Quince came across at times as a bit lethargic and wimpy.The blackmail issue was interesting, but it better be further discussed in Book 3 or else it was totally useless.  We don't get to find out the 4th member of the club, we don't know what happens to Sabre's father and WTF was that about letting the "Dragon" get away?  Quince is horrified to learn what the group has done in the past, but it's fine to let them escape to the Continent so that their evil ways can be plied to unsuspecting innocents?  Gee thanks!  I guess it would be OK if Charles Manson or Jeffrey Dahmer were simply put on a ship and let loose in England.  At least we wouldn't have to deal with them anymore!It's always a bit disappointing to have a storyline build, then fizzle so I'm hoping that Book 3 redeems.  I'm also interested to see what happens to Justin and Sam.  Glad that Robert and Charlie will get their own stories, but hope that we really get to see what makes these characters tick and why they act and think as they do.
summary: Interesting story, but had problems with the main characters

reviewText: The main issue with Weil's writing is the lack of proofreading. Whether it's done by her or a friend of hers it needs some serious work. I can understand not being good with catching your own mistakes, but it shows a disregard to her readers to let so many slide by in a published work. There were too many instances to keep track of where the wrong word was used in a sentence or the tense of the word was incorrect. The amount of seemingly unedited areas in this book makes me think that Weil didn't read through her own story after she wrote it. If she did it was one heck of a speed read on her part. It baffles me that so many errors could go unchecked, especially if there were beta readers. Heck, I'll volunteer my own time to proofread her next book just so I can save other readers the frustration.While I appreciate the pictures she paints, her use of similes was also very noticeable and could've been toned down without losing some of the effect she was going for. When you start noticing how much she compares certain actions or looks to things it becomes distracting. I had the urge to take a red pen to her book more often than not to smooth out the rough edges.Despite the need for better editing or perhaps just some more honest beta readers, Weil still manages a good story. We see how the bond to Chase changes Angel on a physical and emotional level in this book. There's some more action and an introduction to the Hunters as well as some interesting twists.I did find Angel's sarcasm to be a bit much here, however. She had a bit more of a bratty attitude and it was grating at times. I kept reminding myself that she's only 17 and that hopefully Weil grows her character and her maturity in the coming books. That goes for how many times she ended up blubbering and crying about her circumstances. The impression I've gotten so far is that Angel was written to be a strong female, but I just didn't see that as much as I'd hoped. She did manage to pull herself together after her breakdowns, but there were just far too many for my taste.Overall, the issues I've mentioned here won't stop me from reading the next book in Chase and Angel's story. I just hope that Weil takes more care in how she grows her characters and story. I'm also willing to wait a bit longer if it means that she spends more time proofing her work and making sure the end product is worth her readers' time and money.

reviewText: My Review:I really enjoyed this first book of this new series. The story line wasn't completely new and original, but that didn't keep me from enjoying the reading of it at all. It was really well written and I stayed fully engaged with the story from page one.David's a grim reaper. He collects the souls of people minutes after they die. He's been doing this for over sixty years and it's not the easiest job in the world. He's constantly watching people die, many times those are gruesome deaths and then when the souls pass through him, he has to feel the sudden onslaught of their grief. Over the years he's had to numb himself to it just so he can keep going. Right now, he's in the process of training a newly dead cop, Adam. For me, Adam's character was definitely one of the main highlights of this book. I loved him and really hope that the author writes his story soon.David's the head reaper in this area and he manages the schedule for (I think) seven of the other reapers. There are some interesting personalities within the group and it will be interesting to watch their stories develop. They all have their own little coping mechanisms to deal with this very difficult job that they have to do.But at the heart of this story were David and Sarah. Sarah works in biomedical research and is neighbor to David and Adam. The females in Sarah's family have a history of psychic abilities. Sarah has always just thought they were all certifiable until her own abilities start to take hold around David. She's also dealing with a lot of stresses at work, mainly stemming from the fact that her boss is a Class A jerk who's trying to get into her pants. Sarah and David are so fabulous together. She brings some humanity and emotion back into his life, which is why he worked so hard to push her away. That's not something he can handle with his job. I hope that we continue to get to see little glimpses of them in future books in the series.This was an entertaining book. Like I mentioned before, I think my favorite parts were with David and Adam and Adam's training. I loved his character and am super-curious as to why Samuel insisted that he be fast-tracked in his training. I see some intrigue in the future for him. I will definitely be keeping an eye on this series and author. It's off to a great start.I received a complimentary copy of this book in return for an honest review.

I've been doing freezer cooking for a while and I'm always looking for new, tested freezer recipes to try for our family. There were some interesting recipes in this short book, but in my opinion, there weren't many that really lent themselves to freezer cooking. If you want to make some of these for the freezer, you will be on your own for figuring out how to increase the quantities (most recipes serve 4), how to best freeze the results, and how to reheat or cook from frozen. Most recipes have many ingredients and steps. The recipes are not grouped in any kind of time-saving groups where you are saving time and money by cooking all the chicken recipes, chopping all the onions at once, etc.There are 4 recipes for each day of the week, but each recipe serves about 4. The author is suggesting you cook all 4 recipes on one day of the week, but there are no amounts or preparation adjustments included for doubling, etc. Also, the day's recipes aren't related in any way, so they aren't grouped together to save time and ingredients.There is a brief (very brief) introduction to freezer cooking at the beginning of the book, but if you haven't done freezer cooking before, this will not tell you how to do it. I wasn't expecting a "how to" book, but I did expect specific freezer instructions for each recipe. I also totally expected instructions for how to reheat/cook the frozen meal. There are no instructions for that, so you won't know if you should defrost first or microwave or put it directly in the oven...or at what temperature or time. I buy someone else's freezer recipes because I like that someone else has already tested this and will save me the trial and error. I really don't think these have been tested.The cookbook seems to be written by a UK author, so some of the ingredients and measurements are going to be different for a US cook. Since I've cooked from UK cookbooks (not edited for the U.S. cook) in the past, I know that some British measurements may also differ from standard US ones and that could make a difference if you expect to follow the recipe precisely. Some of the ingredients are not ones that most US cooks might not have on hand or even find at the grocery store easily. I was curious, so I had to google to find out what an aubergine or courgette were (eggplant and zucchini.)There are some things that just don't make sense for freezer cooking. There's a roasted chicken recipe that tells you to add various ingredients and then follow the cooking instructions on the package. ??? reviewText: *I received these books from the author in exchange for an honest review. I read all 4 books one after the other, and incorporated all into one review.*4.5 starsMs. Day has woven together a wonderful combination of endearing characters and intriguing plotlines to create The Daughters of the Sea, a five book series that will wrap up with the final book expected to be released in 2014. These are not standalone novels and should be read in order since each continues where the last left off.I love mythology, and was drawn to the plot like a moth to flame. I guess it makes sense that they'd need an entire school to handle the offspring of the Nereids. Those sea nymphs always had a reputation of being a tad promiscuous. I also found it interesting that the offspring of Charon attended the school. For some reason I didn't think he'd find much time to...well, you know.This series is driven by the characters. There are so many intriguing people in these books. Of course I loved main character Stasia. She was amazing in so many ways. I loved tagging along as she discovered and tried to master all of her many powers. Romantic interest Finn is that dark, brooding, secret keeping kind of guy. He'd do anything for Stasia, except reveal secrets that she probably should know. As far as secondary characters go, I really liked Carmen and Olivia. Both had strong personalities that made them stand out from the others. I'd also like to give a nod to Sebastian from book 4. His pursuit of Olivia was quite fun to read.The novels were full of twists and turns, mystery and suspense. Awaken, book 2 in the series was definitely the darkest of the lot. Chosen, book 3, ended in a way that left me reeling. For some reason, I was expecting Hearken to be the final book in the series when I started it. Though, after finishing these four books, I'm not ready to part ways with Stasia and Finn yet, so I'm glad there will be another book.There are some mild sexual situations and a bit of mature language, but nothing that would keep me from recommending this series to mature teen readers. If you like mythology based urban fantasy with a sweeping romance and amazing characters, be sure to add Forsaken, Awaken, Chosen & Hearken to your to-read list.You can find this review and many more at [...]

reviewText: I really enjoyed this story.  The imagery was lovely, the characters well developed and realistic.  It wasn't cluttered or bogged down with unnecessary descriptions or dialog, or supporting characters that had no purpose.  It was short and to the point.Isaak was a sexy, strong character.  He had built a playboy social reputation and a ruthless business one.  As the story progresses we learn why and also that he has a sweet, playful side as well.Kate was  just the right blend of naive and independent.  Her family uses her in really awful ways, and she has closed herself off from just about everyone.  Her mother has shamed her and made her feel less than her entire life and this drives her for most of the story.There is a side plot involving an odd contract, a scandalous family history, and Ivor who sets everything in motion.  It was definitely part of the story but did not overshadow the romance in any way.This was a really great story about perception and how what people say or do can really shape a person and a life. And how you can use those things to hold you back or build a new future entirely.  It was sweet and very, very sexy. I will definitely seek out other books by this author.

Has the honeymoon phase worn off? Do you feel like the man you married has disappeared and has been replaced by someone else? Is marriage not the happily ever after you imagined?Amanda Wright has some solid ideas that will help your marriage to thrive. She explains the reasons men change after they get married and what to do about it. She emphasizes respect, understanding and compassion.Along the way you will learn why men retreat to their caves (an idea promoted by John Gray), what they are doing in their caves and why you should stay the heck out of their cave if at all possible. This book really expands on this idea and also shows why you should lower your expectations.So many books talk about one issue (and it is in this book too) so I'll just say what I think is best. If you have problems, talk to your girlfriends. Don't burden your husband with a list of all the things that went wrong in your day. This is a sure passion killer.After reading this helpful book you will understand your situation more and stress less about your relationship. While dragging your husband off to counseling may be an option for the open-minded man, doing what this book suggests might also be as effective and will cost way less.~The Rebecca Review

reviewText: I would like to thank Heather James for offering me this book in exchange for an honest review.When I agreed to review Fire, I actually thought it had to do with Elementals. But I was wrong. Sort of. This is about a world with four realms and each realm controls a different element. It was almost otherworldly. And it was a great surprise on its different take of controlling the elements that didn't make it sound so witchy like most books with element control. We have the Helians that control fire, Arcans control air, Brizan's control water, and the Sephans control the land. This book focuses mainly on two of these, but does have all four.This book starts off with an introduction to characters, and an invite to the higher ups to a summit in the Helian realm, where they are supposibly all invited to talk of peace treaties. But many alterior motives may be involved.This was told in two female point of views. One was Roxy, who is a Helian princess. She controls fire very well and has trained to be a protector, or a sort of warrior for her people. I liked her almost playful, uncaring of the consequences, wild behaviour in the beginning. But then as I learned more about her people, and didn't really like her very much. She is very spoiled, has an attitude of being better than everyone in other realms, and refers to them as stupid quite often.The other girl is Jasmine, or Jazz. She has been raised in the Arcan realm and isn't really sure what she is or whereshe came from. I liked her and wish there was a little more of her. She seemed genuine and caring, and smart.And both these girls are involved with Brae, the Arcan prince, in different ways. Jazz has been his best friend forever, and Roxy is the girl that is supposed to befriend him for a big takeover plan that the Helians have going on. The Helians are very appropriately named.They came across as a very stuck up group that is out for power.There isn't much romance but I have high hopes for Jazz and Brae. And Roxy may just be getting in the way. I am still scratching my head at a declaration of love that kind of seemed to me to come out of nowhere. I did not see enough happening for this feeling to be coming from Roxy.Overall I think this was an enjoyable story, and I look forward to the rest of the series. It will be interesting to see the different love stories develop, and find out all about what Jazz can do and where she is from, even though I am pretty sure I have the where she is from part down. And this story is clean for all readers. Great first book from Heather James! 3.5 stars

reviewText: There are 3 parts to The Intern serial.  I recommend these novellas be read in order:Part 1: The Intern IPart 2: The Intern IIPart 3: The Intern IIIIn The Intern (part 1) we meet high school student Cecilia West, Ceci seven years after her father was brutally murdered in front of her eyes.  Ever since she has been on a mission to solve his killing.  While attending school she is plotting how to weasel her way into Leighton Enterprises a company with vast access to crime information, data and statistics.  Using her sister's identity she lands an internship.Prodigal son, ex-model and CEO in training Bentley Leighton is her new boss.  From the moment he laid eyes on Ceci he knew she was the best candidate, but also dangerous to his sanity considering his company's strict fraternization policy.The Intern follows Bentley and Ceci as the fight their attraction (and fails miserably) while a focused Ceci continues to plot and learn her way around.  Will she be able to work this closely and still keep her secrets?CECILIA WEST, "Ceci": 18 years/Student/Dark blond.Cecilia West, Ceci is a girl on a mission.  Five words to describe Ceci: Determined, smart, relentless, focused and confident.BENTLEY LEIGHTON: 24 years/Heir/CEO in training/Ex-model/Blond-brown hair/Tattoo.Bentley Leighton is somewhat immature for his age, but there is no denying his attraction to Ceci as the first time he heard her giggle his c*** stirred.  Five words to describe Bentley: Loyal, immature, smart, despondent and conflicted.Plot has a little bit of everything; suspense, mystery, forbidden romance and drama!  Story as well as their relationship moved a long a fast pace as Bentley and Ceci had a bit of insta-attraction followed by insta-lust.  I struggled bit to connect with either most likely due to their ages in comparison to mine.Needless to say The Intern, part 1 ends with a nail-biting cliffy, but fortunately part 2: The Intern II will be released shortly!Forbidden Romance! Reviewed by Evampirefor TheRomanceReviews.comThis futuristic fantasy romance keeps readers on the edge of their seats with action, suspense and romance.A young woman stranded in another dimension is faced with werewolves, vampires and incubi, and she must find a way to not only survive, but adapt to a world with no cities, electricity and no humans.This fast-paced plot keeps readers tingling with anticipation as Susan tries to find her way in the dangerous world she's found herself in. Different groups of people all trying to claim her for their own purposes and her with no idea of the politics or cultures, she's constantly getting herself in more trouble. The author brings the story to life with well written and believable scenes that capture the imagination. The characters are strong, compelling and draw the reader deeper into the story with their own agenda and personalities.The attraction between Susan and Sorin radiates from the pages and the sex scenes are hot, steamy and stimulate the senses with their vibrant intensity. The reader can't help but become emotionally involved in the emotional turmoil of Susan's situation and everything that she ends up going through in her new life. Sorin captures the heart with what he's going through to save his pack after their horrible past and resulting emotional trauma. And then there are the other characters that intrigue the readers with their stories and plights, so no matter what, the reader needs to know more about these captivating characters and their stories.The action and suspense builds throughout with all the drama and betrayals that everyone seems to have valid reasons for, you know the kind that makes the readers feel for the bad guys even though what they did was wrong. I was totally caught up in the story from the beginning and I must say that the more I read the more intriguing and entertaining it got. I can't wait to read the next book about these fascinating characters and their world.
summary: Keeps readers on the edge of their seats with action, suspense and romance

Worth Keeping is a wonderful read, although it has its very dark points that sometimes seem to be glossed over in other books, it is still a true love story about 2 men who are broken in their own way.Nick was abused as a child, which has left him unsure about himself, which has also led him into an abusive relationship that he has since escaped, but is still haunted by the words that are always running through his mind.Owen has lost the love of his life and decided his life would be better if he was no longer living.Fate intervened and brought these two broken men together, but can they heal themselves along with each other? Can Nick fight the demons and nightmares that haunt him and allow himself to open up both physically and emotionally? Can Owen deal with the limits Nick has placed upon himself?I loved this story, yes it is dark and you can't help but feel for Nick and root for him to be able to believe in himself and his abilities to do whatever it is he wants to do. His past makes such a big impact on his life and his future that I couldn't help but cry a few tears in the hope that he could believe in himself half as much as Owen believed in him.And Owen, who loves so easily. Can he continue to show his love and support to the man who doesn't feel worthy? Owen is dealing with his own past, a past that has left him feeling so much more vulnerable that he is left questioning himself.While trying to help Nick, without his knowledge, Owen opened the door to his very abusive past. Can Nick fight one of his greatest fears or will he crumble under his fear and his abusive past? Will Nick and Owen have a future together or will someone or something come in between them?Nick and Owen found a way into my heart and they are continuing to live there. I am looking forward to reading more from this author

What kind of news could be so devastating to you that you would leave everything behind and wander Europe for a year, not telling anyone where you were or even if you were alive? For Katie, her devastating news became global gossip and traveling anonymously was her only escape while she came to terms with a life that had been a huge lie. Her most heartbreaking loss was Jason, her best friend and the man she was in love with, and one-sided love can be a humiliating thing. So far, life on the back roads of Europe hasn't been too bad, until that one terrifying night when she is attacked. A Guardian Angel came to her rescue, the same one who has been following her on her journey, hiding in the shadows. Imagine Katie's shock at discovering it was Jason who saved her, and that he may be the only thing that stands between her and an almost certain death as they begin a nightmarish run for their lives trying to stay one step ahead of the shadowy evil that stalks them. Katie knows Jason is holding something back, not telling her something, but she hasn't quite figured out what that something is. And what is it Jason wants to talk about? Surely, it's just to tell her he doesn't feel "that way" about her, or does he? Who is after Katie and why? Will they reach safety on their own, or will help come from a completely unexpected source?With all of the intrigue and the race to stay alive, Secret Seduction by Jill Sanders is still a tender love story, filled with innocence and passion. Centered around two main characters, Secret Seduction is sigh-worthy. Katie is such a wonderful character, strong and smart in so many ways, yet so nave in others. Jason has a quiet strength, sense of loyalty and a protective nature that makes you want to find out if he has a brother! The dialogue was very realistic, as were the backgrounds and details of each scene. I was glad to be the proverbial fly on the wall during the hiking scenes, which in spite of it being fiction, made my feet hurt!Secret Seduction is a tremendous start to the Secret Series from talented author Jill Sanders! Do you like romance? Action? A refreshing twist of a plot with characters you can truly root for? Give this one a try!
summary: Fabulous Start to a New Series!

Until something “bad” happens—some drunk driver slams into your sedan and leaves you with injuries that stay for life—you cannot possibly appreciate what an incredibly valuable book is Arnold Hernandez’s ‘Settlements Galore’. Indeed, even if you’re living a safe, healthy life right now, you must get a copy of this book at all cost: forewarned is fore-armed, right?‘Settlements Galore’ is exactly what the title says: a comprehensive reference containing every single thing you need to know when it comes to getting a fair settlement after an accident. And when I say comprehensive, I’m not kidding: the book discusses all kinds of possible injuries from all possible accidents—from those arising from traffic, animal bites, slippage, every single thing you can think of. If there’s any situation that may leave you suffering from an injury, trust me, it’s here—and most importantly, the precise ways of getting fair compensation or settlement is discussed in detail, too. Whether you intend to get a lawyer or not, this book will be an immense help—at the very least, it will point you to the right direction regarding what you can do moments after the accident occurs.Overall, I highly, highly recommend this book to everyone—and I mean every single one of you out there. Because at bottom, we’re all vulnerable or at risk to figure in some road accident in the future—knock on wood, but it is what it is—and aside from bewailing misfortune, the best thing you can do right now is to KNOW what you can do so you’ll walk away from an accident not only with a fair settlement, but also with the kind of compensation that will more than fully make up for all the damage you have incurred. Arnold Hernandez’s book is all set to become the “Bible” for those who are seeking just settlement—get a copy of this book today—or much better, send this as a gift to all your loved ones. You’ll never know when you might end up saving a life. A solid five-star rating for this one.

Tower of Obsidian was not what I expected. After a bit of a slow start while the author was building up the setting, theme and characters I feel she really hit her stride about 50 pages into the story where everything came together and the story really started.I love how Tower of Obsidian was set in Ireland and among the Norse people and I'm glad that the author gave the characters in her book authentic sounding names and spellings. What really surprised me about Tower of Obsidian though was the fact that it was penned by a woman. This is a good thing though because these types of historical fiction/mythological novel are penned by men so it was wonderful to see a woman joining the ranks.I loved the mixture of historical fiction and mythology that I found in Tower of Obsidian and I'm glad that I signed up for the blog tour for it or else I wouldn't have been drawn into Kale's story. There was such a sense of adventure and drama it was a hard read for me to put down and even harder to find things I would have liked to have seen happen differently.The characters were well developed, the setting was superb and the author's story telling ability was amazing. She really brought her characters and the story to life for me and I often felt as though I were in the book along side Kale and the other characters while I was reading and as you can probably tell I damn near thought it was perfect. The only problems I had with the book were that sometimes the pace of the novel would be too fast and I would find myself going back a few pages to read what I missed and the fact that there seemed to be a couple plot holes that could have been wrapped up a little better but those are my only complaints.Overall, I thought this book was really, really good and I loved reading it and I can honestly say that it was a pleasure to read and one that I hope to re-read later on. I think the author has a great sense of imagination and she truly has her own unique voice when it comes to her writing style and Tower of Obsidian was a great debut by her and I can't wait to read her next novel.I would recommend Tower of Obsidian to anyone whole loves historical fiction set during the time 1000 A.D. Novels like it are few and far between and you don't want to miss reading this one that has a mythological twist.*I received a free copy of this book in exchange for my free and honest review. All thoughts and opinions expressed herein are 100% my own.

These books are all about the same.  Many were produced in the early years of the 1900's, and paint a picture of lives as slaves. ALMOST MATCHEDThis was my first time reading this author’s work as such I was not sure what to expect. After reading the blurb and a few of the reviews I thought this sounds like an interesting read.Almost matched started out rather interesting. I thought it was rather funny the way that Colin and Natalie met. I give Natalie props because that were to happen to me, I would be totally mortified and probably would not show up for that meeting knowing that the source of my embarrassment would be present.It was easy to relate to Natalie and her problems when it came to finding the right guy. What’s ironic about her situation though is the she is the co-owner of a successful matchmaking company, but she was unable to find her perfect match.What I loved most about this story is the interaction between Natalie and her friends. The bond that existed between these friends appears strong. It’s obvious they care about each other and they had each other’s backs.I also loved the author’s writing style as it made me feel as if I was on the sidelines looking in.My only problem with the story is that the romance between Natalie and Collin felt a bit stilted. There were times it was bit boring and I felt it was not going anywhere. It’s clear that Collin had a secret and his failure to reveal to Natalie was having a negative impact on their relationship.In spite of this I found Almost Matched somewhat enjoyable and I can’t wait to start book two as I would love to know what’s going to happen next.ALMOST BROKEN UPAfter reading Almost Matched I was eager to start Almost Broken Up as I wanted to see exactly which the direction the author was planning to take with this series. Before I go any further, I must admit that I found this to be a more entertaining read than Almost Matched. My judgement may be a bit biased in his instance due to my love of stories that have an element of suspense and drama.Almost Broken Up started out with Collin’s POV, which gives readers an insight as to the guilt that Collin has been living with since that fateful night when his former girlfriend was killed in a motor vehicle accident. It made Collin appear more human and it made it easier for me to connect with him.Almost Broken Up does is not so much about the relationship between Natalie and Collin but more about the lengths that Natalie will go through to protect her man. Two new characters were introduced, one of whom will pose a threat to Natalie’s relationship with Collin and one who will offer her help in dealing with this threat.There were moments when I questioned Natalie’s sanity, especially when she made the decision to face the person who had threatened Collin’s life. I say this because it was clear that this person was absolutely crazy. But I guess when you are in love and you have faith in your partner’s innocence, then you will be willing to face any situation no matter how dangerous to protect him. It also helps when you have the girlfriend of a mob boss helping you out.There were several LOL moments. I found it to be rather hilarious, especially that scene where Natalie, Ali and her new found friend, Svetlana, engaged in a little B&E.; I am not going to say much about this as I don’t want to give the story away. To find out what I am speaking about you will have to get a copy for yourself.The sex scenes between Natalie and Collin was quite erotic. It’s definitely not for the feint of heart.The author’s writing style is quite engaging as it pulls the reader in and makes them feel as if they are a part of the story.Overall this was an enjoyable read. Recommended for readers 18+

The book begins with Princess Yaroslava trying to prepare her small Russian principality for the invasion of the Mongols. The people know the Mongols will show them no mercy and are doing everything they can to prepare to fight them. Unfortunately their efforts are not enough and their home falls to the Mongols. They slaughter most of the people and enslave the attractive woman and craftsman. Yaroslava is among those who becomes a slave and the rest of the book deals with her trying to adjust to being a slave and plotting to free the rest of her people that have survived.This is an interesting book that deals with a topic I have not read about before, the Mongol invasion of Russia. I learned a lot about Russia during this time and I thought Walk did a good job of describing battle scenes and the despair of the people whose homes were being invaded. It was also interesting to read about the nomad life of the Mongols and how they lived, what they wore, what they ate, etc. Walk seems to have done some thorough research in writing her book.The one thing that I would have liked to have seen more of was more descriptions of the country during this time. What I enjoy the most about historical fiction is feeling like I am in another place and time while I am reading and I just didn't feel like enough time was spent on details about Russia to give me a good idea of what it looked like. I also would have liked to have seen some of the characters in the book given some more depth and detail, especially Batu Khan.Besides those issues I had with the book I thought it was an entertaining book that flowed well and had lots of suspense that kept me reading. Yaroslava was a strong character and Walk does and excellent job describing all of the different emotions and fears she felt while being a slave. I would recommend this book to any historical fiction fan or someone who enjoys reading about Russia. I am looking forward to reading other books by this author.

When I first started reading Gloria Piper's Train to Nowhere, my initial reaction wasn't kind. The first chapter immerses readers in the world of Orphans, a hedonistic culture imprisoned in a train on an endless loop for their parents' crimes (think Chinese population control laws). To make it more confusing, the Orphans' language incorporates tons of computer-related words that can be initially baffling (e.g., "deleted" means "killed," "surfing" (the web) means "travelling," etc.) So I will start with the bad: Chapter 1 tosses readers into a society so foreign, culture shock results.Now the good: everything else about Train to Nowhere, from Chapter 2 to the very last word, is absolutely fantastic! Culture shock quickly dissipates, and readers find themselves transported to a full, lively, and understandable world. Chapter 2 introduces the reader to Hedge, and it becomes immediately clear that Hedge, driven by his ambition, is not above stepping on others to get where he feels he deserves to be. But what makes him more dangerous is that he has real talent . . . and cunning as sharp as a tack.Hedge is part of the Landeds' society, a more "civilized" community I imagined to be similar to an Amish community, but with some technology. Although, the Landeds are free to roam about, their actions are subject to another kind of prison - the suffocating prudeness of societal norms. The Landeds are identifiable, perhaps a version of America that has been or is to come.The last of the three societies within Piper's world, kept separate except for prohibited trading, is comprised of the Nomads. They bear a strong resemblance to certain Native American cultures. Admin, who are similar to A.I. but symbolize much more, indirectly oversee Landeds and directly control Orphans. Nomads operate outside their boundaries.The story follows Garland, an Orphan who yearns to experience life beyond the confines of the Orphan train. On the train, Admin provides all. There is no sickness or crime; even emotions are subliminally controlled. The train is like an all-inclusive prison, and it even serves as a vacation spot for Landeds. Although on the Orphan train Garland would never have need of anything, he is still a prisoner, and he senses he does not belong. But the grass isn't always greener on the other side of the fence.Garland's struggles, both internal and external, are equally identifiable. Self-doubt, fear, hope, despair, justice and love prevent him from overcoming some obstacles, while these same concepts propel him past others. He is a strong protagonist, one worth routing for, but he is not impeccable. As devious as Hedge can be, his flaw is almost tragic. The strange and varied characters are fully relatable, a tribute to Piper's ability. One can understand why each character takes the risks they take and makes the sacrifices they make.Train to Nowhere is unique science fiction with elements of fantasy and folklore. If I had to compare it to other works, I'd say a dash of 1984, a pinch of A Brave New World, a hint of The Island, a smidgeon of Fahrenheit 451, a dab of Final Fantasy and a fair dose of LSD (not that I would know). But the combination is something wholly original, a novel that spurns emotion and embraces romanticism in the classical sense. If Orwell and Huxley are required reading for English-language literature courses, Piper's book is surely good enough to find itself alongside them on the syllabi. 5 out of 5 stars.
summary: Beautifully crafted and thought-provoking - Science fiction and fantasy at its best.

4.5 starsKyle Juenger used to be a damn fine pilot and warrior, that was before the shape shifting low-life Glyrinny not only took away the use of his legs, but his self respect as well. Now he is low on money, and not sure if he will ever be able to get back to his home planet of Tamene and possibly get a useable set of cyber-legs. As luck would have it, he gets a message that the Sector Commissar would like to meet with him.  She informs Kyle that she needs a hunter-killer to track down a Glyrinny spy named Kshar who has something she wants.  She tells Kyle that she will make sure he gets his new legs as long as he delivers Kshar, dead or alive makes no difference to her, and if he happens to take down any of his fellow Glyrinny in the process, the happier she will be. His mission is to infiltrate a mercenary ship named the Scorpion. She is pretty confident he will find Kshar on board the ship, either as a passenger or as a stow away.Kyle manages to hook up with the crew at a local eatery, and talks the head merc, a pasty looking large woman named Winter, to get him an introduction to the Pilot and Captain, Grimm. When Kyle meets the captain, he is shocked to discover that not only is he from Kyle's home planet, but wears the tattoos of a warrior cast. Grimm immediately lets Kyle know that he is attracted to him, but Kyle puts his advances off, since his legs weren't the only thing damaged by the Glyrinny. Invited to co-pilot the Scorpion, Kyle now has to not only try to figure out a way to figure out where or even who Kshar may be, but he has to fight his own attraction to the mysterious Grimm. On his part, Grimm knows there is more to Kyle than meets the eye, and is determined to find out just what it is.Having read two other of Mr. Voinov's works, I was prepared for just about anything. He follows no formula other than always giving the reader fascinating characters in a setting that is so real you would swear you were there. With Incursion he takes us to the world of science fiction, and for a little spice, he throws in a little mystery, a little romance and even a life lesson, leaving the reader content, yet wanting more.Kyle has more than just damaged legs, he feels he has lost his entire identity and struggles with living with the pain of that loss. As a warrior who can no longer fight, he drifts through his life just getting by until given this assignment. He knows that he is in for a challenge. How do you find a creature that can literally take on the form of anyone, and how do you know who is friend and who is foe? He fights his attraction to Grimm, I think because in Grimm he sees the man he once was and wants to be again. Grimm is full of self confidence and swagger; he knows exactly who and what he is, and is completely comfortable with himself. He almost takes it as his mission to save Kyle from himself, and show him that legs don't make a person, and he is worthy of Grimm's attention.While this novella is a romance, it has a deep underlying message that pulls the reader in and keeps them engaged. I was completely caught up in Kyle's mission to find the Glyrinny spy and prayed it wasn't who he thought it might be. There are scenes that aren't pretty and were painful to read, and there were scenes that were so moving that they took my breath away. My only problem with this novella, was it just was too short. I felt like there was more that I needed to know and finished feeling like I was missing something. I liken it to diet food, while it will fill you up, when you are finished you aren't completely satisfied. Or since this is an erotic romance, when I was done I was content but had Mr. Voinov given me just a little more time I would have been completely satiated. I'll take whatever I can get though, and can't wait to see what Mr. Voinov gives us next.Member of the Paranormal Romance Guild Dual Review Team

reviewText: I really enjoyed reading Walking Away. I'm a fan of sitting down and reading a short story/novella length romance every now and then. This one hit the spot for me.I'm surprised to know this is Boyd's debut release. It's beautifully written and shows signs that she has a great career as an author ahead of her.I liked Cora's character and to see how she has so much going against her in life, but she keeps plodding along and making the best of it. She's a very likable character. I can see myself enjoying sequel if it meant reading more from Cora's point of view. The other characters are also great. Her twin sister, Abi, isn't a key part to the story, but was still a great addition. The same goes for everyone else the reader encounters. I don't want to name too many to avoid spoiling the fun.Aside from the characters, the plot, the romance, and conflict involved all made me want to keep reading. It's a believable story-line that I feel most readers will be able to relate to in one way or another. I'd also like to applaud the slow and steady build up of relationships. I'm not a fan of things happening immediately, even when the length of the story is short. When things happen at a real world pace, they are more believable.In closing, I want to read more work from Adriane Boyd. I hope more comes out soon because I have a feeling I'll be one to enjoy it.

SUMMER'S BOOK BLOGTrue to the title, this book had ‘Double Coverage’ in every aspect of the phrase! This book was written in third person and focused on more than one couple. The book intertwines two main couples as their stories run parallel in the plot.We have Mason Dashel, the starting receiver for the Denver Stallions and Jake’s friend from the first book in the series Fair Catch, which meets Piper, Lexi’s childhood best friend, on a plane ride to Jake and Lexi’s wedding. Even though they did not have any idea who the other one was, they ended up sitting right next to each other on the flight. After feeling the wrath of Piper’s feisty, foul mouth, Mason deliberately sets forth to make her flight a miserable one. At this point, their contempt for each other begins. Once they get to the wedding, Piper arranges her own revenge and literally causes Mason to be caught with his pants down during the wedding.They begin their back and forth love/hate relationship, but neither can deny the powerful desire that pulls them both towards each other through the entire book. We really fall in love with Mason and Piper as a couple, however, it turns out that Piper has a boyfriend. The southern gentleman Jax that is new in town and has an interesting connection that plays out in the story. Mason has his own problems as his spoiled ex-fiancée, Brooke, makes relentless attempts to win him back and remove Piper from his life.Hannah, Piper’s very sweet, kindhearted co-worker catches the eye of Ryker, Mason’s close friend and fellow Stallion’s receiver. Hannah is in a long-term relationship that is going nowhere very fast. Once Ryker has Hannah in his sites, he is hooked and will stop at nothing to make her his.This book is a complete emotional roller coaster. Just when you think the characters have made it to a high point, the bottom falls out and everything starts heading down for one of the couples. The author did a great job of developing characters that were full of heart and very funny. Many of the scenes had us laughing out loud. This one does end on a cliffhanger. What we do not know is, will Piper stay with her boyfriend Jax, or will she give into Mason attempts at capturing her heart? What will Hannah do? Will she stay with Todd, or allow Ryker to finish sweeping her off her feet?We highly recommend this book because it is very captivating and pulls you in. The character development is done very well and the story line keeps you fascinated.

…. I have just finished reading ‘The Cold Steel Mind’.  It is a worthy and imaginative sequel to ‘Steel Beneath the Skin’.  Aneka Jansen, kidnapped by the alien Xinti in 2011 and reanimated in an android body twelve-hundred years later, has become an accepted member of the crew of the archaeological research ship Garnet Hyde.  They have returned to the wreck of the Agroa Gar, the Xinti ship on which the android body into which her consciousness was downloaded was found in stasis.  There are secrets to be had on the Agroa Gar, some of which someone doesn’t seem to want known.  But, there may be more players in this game than the crew of Garnet Hyde even imagine……. I found this book just as much fun to read as the first.  There is a little less direct action and a little more characterization and world building in this adventure and I found it a nice balance that held my attention from beginning to end.  Once again, I could not put it down.  The sex scenes that some complained about in the first book are here too, but dialed back a bit as a more complicated plot takes over.  Once again, the sex is treated with a generally light (if graphic), and humorous hand with the exception of the actions of one dark character who eventually draws Aneka’s righteous ire.  Again, good job, Niall.  I am looking forward to the next one.  This is shaping up to be a memorable series.
