I love alien romances, especially ones where the h is human and the H is alien and NOT human-looking in appearance, and I got that in this story. From the book cover and the blurb, I wasn't really expecting that about the hero, so that was an added bonus for me. Whereas the heroine Sandrea is a red-haired Aussie, soft and curvy, the hero is definitely less human-looking, described as more reptilian in appearance, with green almond-shaped eyes with brow ridges, bold facial features, and a hairless skull with cranial ridges and scales. Bronzed scales cover most but not all of his big, beautiful body. He and his race are exotic to Sandrea, but she is equally fascinating to this alien general, as humans are unknown in this part of the galaxy.I loved this hero. Sandrea is smart and tough, seems to know a bit about everything, and I do enjoy when a heroine is underestimated but still saves the day; however, it was Eugen who really appealed to me the most, not only for the different appearance, but also for his character. I loved that he was practically smitten from the get-go, totally intrigued by this small, pale human with the long, beautiful hair, wanting to keep her near to him. It was very sweet to see this battle-ready general be protective and possessive of Sandrea. He's curious and bewildered by his attraction to Sandrea, but he can't fight it. He was so sweet in how he hungers for her.I thought the romance was well-played and not overshadowed by all the action and fighting going on in the story. There is a sweet and slow building of their connection, with some cultural misunderstandings along the way, and there was sweet heat to their love scenes. Not overly graphic but still on the page and nicely written with steam and romance. I enjoyed that sexual tension between them and couldn't wait for them to get to the bedroom. And that scene with the head and scalp massage? So cute and even funny and very sensuous. And I guess that's how I'd describe their romance: slow and steady, soft, sweet and sensual.Small quibbles-- I wanted more of Sandrea's reaction to Eugen's homeworld; I would have liked more discussion between h/H about their differences, especially how that may affect reproduction someday; and I wouldn't have minded an epilogue of some sort. I'm sure the author plans to continue the overall storyline (the Alliance fighting the Bluthens, etc.), and there are definitely more characters for her to write about (T'Hargen, Kulluk, Shrenk and more), so I will probably see this couple again and get an update that way.I read this book as a Prime rental, and I enjoyed it a lot, kind of got me out of a reading funk. Just something different in setting and hero and got my attention perked up from page one. I liked the off-world setting, the different aliens and environments encountered, and I liked that there was action and adventure to go along with a slow-burning and sensual romance. Once I started the story, I wanted to keep reading to see what would happen next to Sandrea, this human lost far from home, and this sexy, sweet alien hero who rescues her and captures her heart. Good, entertaining read all around.
summary: A fun, action-y, and sweet alien romance

So ... another book summary which doesn't quite encompass what the book is about. For starters, it fails entirely to mention Sophia, who is one of the main characters of the book and the queen of the Pure Ones. Yes, the story is mostly about Rain and Valerius, but Sophia has a pretty major plotline as well.It took me a while to get into the flow of this novel. Sophia's scenes are a little bit lighthearted and youthful, discovering an attractive male, Ere in her class at Harvard. But then we're taken to the world of Valerius and Rain, and the writing is a little more reflective of these ancient beings than of a teenage girl. The switch between the two styles just threw me. Then it goes into some graphic sexual descriptions that I must admit made me blush just a bit. The Pure Ones as well as their vampire adversaries would definitely fit right in on True Blood with all the steamy scenes that take place. I'd say this is borderline erotica just because of these hot and detailed scenes.I think the author did a good job with character development. The main characters are easy to get to know, as we know their innermost emotions, fears and at times, their pasts. Particularly Valerius. His backstory is important so you understand why he is the way he is. My only complaint about the characters is their emotions seem way out of whack. The Pure Ones are this evolved race - yet they still aren't in tune with their emotions. Rain and Valerius misread each other's facial expressions and body language and it causes them a lot of hurt and misery. Just seems to me like they'd be past the high school antics.But I have to say, my favorite chapters were those with Sophia. Maybe it's because I could relate more to her than to the ancient ones. In fact, she almost seems not to fit in with this group - she's young, she doesn't really seem to have the kinds of powers the others have. Which is strange because she's their Queen. Also, I was eager to find out more about Ere; I had a feeling there was more to him than just a good looking guy, since he was also immediately drawn to her.Last but not least is the cover .. Mee-yowwwww! Hello there sir, are you lost? Looks like you might need a shower. Let me help you ... Anyway, I think that is supposed to be Valerius. Well played, cover artist!This book definitely isn't for everyone. It's racy, it's violent, it's long. But if you want a hot read while you're enjoying these last few days of summer, this will definitely fit the bill.(Review written by Kathy, a Literary R&R; book review blog team member)

reviewText: Under the Burning Sky is a novella that takes place in the Australian outback. I’ve never been to Australia myself but the author pretty much drew a picture for me and had me wishing I was right there with the characters. I finished this book in one sitting and just under 2 hours – it is a great read! I love the characters Ethan (a marine) and Amarin (a beautiful tomboy) and their “realness”. They are very likeable characters and well-developed too. I loved that they were strong-willed, despite their attraction for each other, and I enjoyed their relationship and the romance aspect.I would recommend Under the Burning Sky to anyone who enjoys a good action story mixed with a bit of mystery, suspense and romance. I gave this book (which is the first in the trilogy) 5-stars because I loved the story itself and it was very well written. The ending left me wanting more and I can’t wait to read the next books to see where this story goes. It’s rare that you find the first book in a trilogy so exciting but this one was just that. Could not put this book down!

The fate of the world is on Phoebe Ward's shoulders. Literally. See, Phoebe has never been in love and after several failed relationships, she thinks she's doomed to be alone forever. As Valentine's Day approaches, she's ready to spend it alone, but Cupid has another idea.Cosmo Cupid is THE Cupid's son. He's been sent to Phoebe to make sure she meets her soul mate, Adam. Once their love is bound, the world will be saved. So, Phoebe sets off to make it happen. As she waits out side Adam's condo, she runs into Cal Crawford. It just so happens that Cal is Adam's roommate. While Phoebe believe's she's meant for Adam, she can't help but feel a spark with Cal.As for Cal, he's never been in love either, but he can't help but have strong feelings for Phoebe. His strong attraction to her surprises him, but he decides to help her get closer to Adam. I really loved Cal for his selflessness. He was willing to put his happiness aside, so that Phoebe could be happy with Adam. However, the fates don't always have the final say.A Little Bit Cupid was a fun, short, and sweet read. It's that simple. It's a short story, so it took less than a half hour to read. The characters were likable and the story line was cute. If you're looking for s short, flirty read, check this one out.

The wait for Tank's story was worth it.  I can absolutely say he is my favorite Hellion.  I loved that  we got to learn more about his childhood and why he is Tank.  Sass was absolutely perfect for him.As we follow Sass on her journey of trying a life without the Club.  Sometimes life is not greener on the other side of the fence.  Sass is now going by Savannah.  She no longer has her trade mark red and black hair but a dark auburn color that Nick, the suit, has picked out for her.  Nick is not what he seems.  She is like his puppet to do with what he wants.  He tells her he loves her, buys her clothes to wear, a brand new car and a gorgeous house but all of those things do not mean anything if there is no love to begin with.Tank is trying to fight his way back to Sass.  He is left in a coma from the aftermath of One Ride.  He keeps losing his battle with his mind and sleep consumes him a good part of the book.  Sass continues to visit him daily before work until Nick sets in to end that too.  But Sass being there has helped Tank, she is his angel and light that keeps him going, he finally wakes to realize that he loves her more than anything.  He is determined to get out this hospital bed and make Sass his ole lady.  He finds her but does not push her into anything just buying his time til she realizes that she missed her true life.Finally Sass has had enough, she plans to go back to the true family that she knows with the help of Tank.  But before she can, she realized that she will always part o Nick with her.  He surprises her by coming home early only to not be happy about the situation.  He is furious and leaves his marks on her.  She was just a pawn.  Then Tank shows up to get Sass out of the house and back to where she belongs.Once settles at Tank's house the next day, he notices Nick's marks on her.  No one does that to his woman.  Nick has to learn a lesson.  And boy does he.  Tank will protect what is his.Life goes on for the Hellions.  There is lots to celebrate.  New life and new beginnings.Over all enjoyed this read.  Can not wait to take a the next ride with the Hellions.
summary: MC Read at its best & love Tank!!

Isolated on an frigid island, Albermarle Hall is a sanctum of depravity and the ideal setting for this shockingly cruel and intense story with superb writing. You'll find yourself shackled amidst the horrors of the enslaved man-boy, Finn, your sympathy for him holding you there, frozen in fear. You'll wonder how he was captured, how badly his next job will hurt him, and why his tormentor goes to such lengths to destroy him physically and emotionally.TM is a master at revealing back stories, sometimes with sneaky subtleness, but always sadistic in nature. The tribulations reach the darkest, deepest places. Places you might not know exist.The villains are inventive in their power to induce dread, rage, and paralyzing terror. The excessive rape and violence are graphic, beautifully disturbing, but in no way titillating. In fact, I would not label this erotic or romance, as those terms imply gratification and desire. Reading this stirred the same emotions in me as Jack Ketchum's horror novels. Sick curiosity.The body of this tale is harrowing, allowing little light and warmth to leak in. The sexual cruelty takes horror in an unpredictable direction, using psychological brutality to develop a friendship between an unlikely pair.From the slivers of blood-stained clothing and broken bones resurrects a courageous trust between the drug-addicted Finn and the guest-turned-prisoner painter, Lilith. This friendship is a fierce enough foundation to keep some of the chicken-hearted readers turning pages through the gory, topnotch tension.This vicious, well-crafted psychological thriller might leave you scarred, but it's the soul-deep characterization of Finn and Lilith that makes this book wholly unforgettable.

Sometimes I need a sweet, romantic love story without too much angst or too much pain. Seven Day Fiance fit that to a 'T'. Rachel Harris wrote a fun, deliciously sweet story about Cane Robicheaux and Angelle Prejean. It is set in Cajun country which added some tasty and fun cultural elements.From the very beginning, I found myself laughing along with Angie's internal dialogue; I even felt like smacking myself on the forehead a few times with her when she did something silly. I was rooting for her from the beginning. Angelle needs a fake fiance and finds herself asking her roomie's brother to help her out. Cane, damn, he's a hottie extraordinaire! A tatted up bad boy, restaurant owner, and all around great guy. He's a hard one to pin down and has never wanted a relationship that he could potentially ruin like his father did. Angie caught his eye when she came to town several months ago. Serious fireworks go off between these two!Fun and hilarity ensues after Angie wins Cane in the eligible bachelor auction and he agrees to be her fiance. There are also some sexy moments between Angie and Cane that hint at their time together. Elements of family, relationships, growing a backbone, commitments, and discovering what you really want are also part of the story.Although this is the second book in the series, I did not read the first and I feel this is definitely a standalone. Maybe I would have seen more of Cane and Angie's history if I'd read the first but I loved them just the same. If you want a meet-cute, tasty, fun, light romance that has you sighing and swooning, Seven Day Fiance is the one for you.

Before you pay, understand that Amazon offers this User's Guide for free several times a year.  If you don't want to wait, or are concerned that you will miss it on the day it's offered for free, then go ahead and pay for it.  (You can watch the list at the kindlenationdaily website, which lists free books currently being offered on Amazon.  It stays on there for a couple of days once it's posted.)I have the 2012 version of this User's Guide, and wish I had discovered it earlier.  Since the Kindle is constantly evolving and being upgraded, it's a good idea to download this 2013 version and check it out, even if you have the old one.  You may learn about some new "bells and whistles!" I found this version better and more user-friendly than the User's Guide that comes with the Kindle, and that is downloaded to your device when you first sign in.Keep in mind the User's Guide was published by Amazon, so there is quite a bit of Amazon self-congratulatory hype, and also a lot of product plugs.  You will need to wade through the non-essential marketing information to get to the good stuff, but that doesn't make the good information you will find in the User's Guide any less useful.  And that's the price you pay for getting it for free.You get a lot of tips in the book.  I've been able to use my Kindle to do a lot of things that I didn't even know it could do, and it has enhanced my experience.  And details are provided in one place, allowing you to make side-to-side comparisons of products more easily.One of the ironies of this User's Guide is that you need to understand how to use the Kindle to be able to read the instructions on how to use the Kindle on your Kindle.  Got that?  ;)  Oh, well, you could download the Kindle reading app to your computer and read it from there.  But you'd have to know that's an option before you can do it, and that's not intuitive.The bottom line is that if you download it, you'll find it useful.For more information, you can also download "Kindle Fire Tips, Tricks & How-Tos"Kindle Fire Tips, Tricks and How-Tos: Kindle Nation Daily's Guide To Save You Money, Save You Time, and Help You Get The Most Out Of Your Kindle Fire.  It looks like it's the same book, but it is different.

A fascinating book for a reading assignment for an abnormal psychology class.  I read reviews complaining about how twisted and ugly a romance this is.  I think the problem is the categorization of the book.  It's not a romance but a fictional character study of psychological illness with nail-biting, pulse pounding tension and terror.  Make sure to read the back page about Stockholm Syndrome.  I will never forget this book.  This book is not for everyone. Kelli is busy, very busy every Friday. But she's not having hot dates or girly sleepovers. Kelli is the Friday Night Alibi. Want to date a girl your parents don't approve of? Need a sleepover cover so you can stay at your boyfriend's place? Ask Kelli! She'll be your alibi. For a fee, of course. It sounds exciting, right? Nope, she spends her Friday nights in her pajamas playing Xbox because she can't leave the house. Makes it pretty hard to meet a nice guy.Chase is nothing like the guys Kelli knows, meaning he isn't preppy or privileged and he definitely doesn't want her as an alibi. Her attempts to drive him away; pulling a waxing prank and getting mooned by him... doesn't exactly work. She's being drawn in by the boy with the black t-shirts in excess and wit sharper than Kelli can handle. Almost.I was really drawn into Kelli's story. Her voice is very well written and strong. I found myself laughing at parts and cringing along with the character in parts. Chase. He was adorable. I oddly really liked that he kept his room clean and it wasn't like most male bedrooms."Friday Night Alibi" is a light romance novel with lots of humor and a unique storyline. At times it did feel like Kelli was really young and it read like a young adult novel, but most of the time it fit. I did enjoy the book and I would recommend it to others.My only complaint - there were a few too many oranges. If you read it, you might know what I mean. :)

reviewText: “The Divine Manual” is a New Age self-help book with a little different twist—the author has explored the various theories, practices, and healing techniques into a framework all his own, based on what he has experienced to work.I liked his brief autobiography at the beginning, which gives you a little insight into his youth and character—he says he always felt like he had a profound purpose and set out young to find it, and eventually realized he was getting signs and nudges that he couldn’t run from his Divine Path forever. Thus “The Divine Manual” is meant to help you reach your own Divine Path, too.The book is nicely organized into concrete and distinct chapters dealing with different subjects, from the law of attraction; the ego, subconscious, and superconscious; karma and past and present life challenges, and how they impact your current existence; meditation; and more. I liked the detail of each entry, and the author’s clear explanations of the more difficult subjects and how they can be applied to improve your own life. It’s well-written, conversational, and enjoyable.If you’re interested in New Age philosophies but aren’t sure where to start, “The Divine Manual” is an excellent summary and explanation of much of it, and you could take what you were most interested in and research further; if you’ve already done quite a bit of exploration on your own, “The Divine Manual” still holds a lot of detail to help you on your path.
summary: Thoughtful and Well-Written Exploration of Many New Age Theories

reviewText: This is such a cute short story. Made for some much needed light reading and a few laughs. Lexi, a single mom with 2 children, moves into the house next door to a best selling author suffering from writers block. Lexi works from her home doing a "Martha Stewart" type show. She spends a good part of her day with her children building a beautiful snowman in their front yard for the next taping of her show. Kyle sees this Snowman and as he is trying to find the ending of his latest book he decides that the Snowman may be a way to take care of his ending. As he is removing the head and digging a hole into the belly of the Snowman he meets his angry new neighbor. From that point on the sparks are flying. Lexi and Kyle have such fun conversations and make such a cute couple.So, if you are in the mood for some light, fun reading pick up a copy of this short story.

Indigo Tears by Dennis J. Butler is nothing less than BRILLIANT. I planned on reading this book in a few days and ended up unable to put it down. What Butler does here is somehow give us a positive angle on the disgusting realities of human trafficking. Something that literally goes on right under our noses. Something humanly impossible to focus on but a reality nonetheless. Gavin Hawkins is the hero in this story and sets about to rescue the children who have been stolen thoughtlessly from their families, the loving families and people that care, and forced to have sex with strangers. Usually but children themselves. Where you're considered "lucky" to end up a sex slave as private property, versus a filthy, disease ridden brothel. I literally had to stop and catch my breath in parts of this story. So captivating, terrifyingly real and close to home. I have six children of my own and had to force my mind from even going there.The character descriptions hear so vivid and alive, diverse and magnetic. Each one you will find various levels to relate and that just fuels the desire to want more.Butler manages to take something that literally breaks your heart and spin it so there is a sliver of hope. No silver lining but something for those affected to hang onto in their darkened times.There's no doubt I have been touched by this book. One that deserves reading and recognition for the fabulous story it is. Definitely worth the read!
summary: A Ray of Hope on a Horrific Tragedy~BRILLIANT!

reviewText: If you read the first book I don't think the second book will disappoint. Sakavic has captured the language of youth making it all the more real. A word of caution. You do have to place close attention to the background character explanations to get various relationships. This enables you to follow certain sequences. Admittedly, the author could have a bit more clarity in this area. Eventually, though, you figure it out.The problem I have with a series is when you have to wait for the final installment. It's rather a let down. But, I did read the conclusive segment should occur sometime January, 2014. I can hope. I have one issue with the second book that did follow a conventional mind set that bugs me.  Nicky(Neil's teammate and openly gay character) rants to Neil about the only way Neil will have a happy life is having a significant other.  Otherwise, this dooms Neil to a joyless life. I've commented on this issue previously in other critiques. Are you telling me that even thought I have decent caring friends, a purposeful life, a loving relationship with myself open toward the other  that if I 'don't have someone' I'm doomed to a miserable life.? Listen up. There are people who lead a happy existence with caring attachments and are ok. Don't get me wrong. It is desirable to have a partner but not a need to prevent a fulfilling life. I'll stop now.Ah, don't let me distract from the fact that I still consider the second book highly recommendable.

This book ran out too soon! Tasty characters. The sub, Bret, is a brat but not in an obnoxious, egoistic way. He just knows what he wants and is very honest about his intentions. And what he wants is to submit body and soul to Marcus. He's irrepresible, humorous and not afraid. I read a fair amount of m/m, d/s and I've never come across a sub quite like this one. He was a blast to read.The biggest problem I had was the compressed nature of the storytelling. There was no simmering build up to their first encounter. All we're told is that Bret has been staring silently and yearning for, Marcus' attention for months. Their first scene and all those subsequent are compelling, hot,  touching even and work terrifically on their own. But overall, the story lacks tension. Everything is charming but entirely too easy. I can see Bret falling in love at first sight but what propels the Dom past all his time-tested boundaries? Not enough build-up then release to the story. Kim Dare is a very good writer, but for whatever reason, she left too much unsaid. This is a very tasty snack cake of a novella crying out to be a 7-layer, chocolate extravaganza. Read it anyway.

This book gives a complete overview on how to create a blog and make it successful. Many people are learning the importance of blogging when it comes to just getting a point of view across or using it as a marketing tool. Timepiece by Heather AlbanoAs I've protested before, Steampunk is not my genre. Nor am I a fan of history although I'm not entirely bereft of some grasp of historical events. So, when the book begins at Waterloo in the midst of battle I'm pretty sure I have a grasp of where we are and what the outcome should be. Although I must admit that as I often do before giving a review I paused at some point to recite aloud to Virginia a few items I enjoyed about the book with a brief synopsis of the book itself. So when I started to mention Waterloo and came stuck upon the name of the British duke, Virginia was quick to fill in the blanks with a confident: Wellington. You see it pays to be a reader of romance novels now doesn't it. Virginia's genre is Romance.I thus felt it fell upon me to check what I could. You see the book hinges entirely on being in a world where there are monsters much like Mary Shelly's Frankenstein. These monstrosities were created, by the British, prior to this battle and are now being held in reserve. The biggest puzzle would seem to be the why, to Wellington using them. Was there a change in the original battle that made matters worse for Wellington's troops or are we to believe that Wellington's confidence in his green troops is so low that the change mostly comes from having such a thing in reserve as these monsters as enough to tempt Wellington. It's a difficult puzzle even so because it would seem that Wellington is not happy about his own decision which leads on into history by placing his name upon the whole thing by calling these creatures Wellingtons monsters. Giving them the glory for the victory and taking it away from his troops.If I see things correctly this leads to the Steampunk nature of the story revolving around the events that follow this great battle.But we don't get there directly since the main characters are still within this same time sphere which is what makes this primarily a time travel novel over Steampunk. Elizabeth Barton is anything but a prim an proper young lady. Perhaps she'd be best described as a tomboy despite the efforts of her parents and her aunt. Let me say her aunt is singularly cruel above and beyond the call of duty as regards molding Elizabeth into a fine young marriageable woman. At the age of seventeen Elizabeth is hardly ready to settle down with any suitor. She receives on this day in the mail a strange watch that not only has multiple dials but also a strange movable picture. (Definitely something not of this time.)Next is William Carrington, a former military man who was wounded seriously and has lost the function of one arm. Rather despondent that he is unable to accompany his brother in law back into battle, when Napoleon escapes from prison to begin his 100 day reign. Now unable to join the battle and feeling quite crippled and maimed he has serious doubts of his ability to make a show as a husband in his present condition. It is while getting away from everything that reminds him of his inadequacy that he takes a stroll that leads him to the same place that Elizabeth has gone to escape the mechanization's of her family in trying to match her with anything of flesh and blood and breeding that will tolerate her.She has also gone to examine her watch more closely.William finds her with the watch and confronts her about it. When he opens it to look at it he's mesmerized equally as much as she has been, but because he has some familiarity outside of the cloistered community that oppresses Elizabeth he has a better chance of recognizing that this is something that does not come from anywhere near or far from here. Because of the strange features within the watch there are a number of dials moved and an accidental pushing in of the stem. They both sense that something has happened. When Elizabeth takes possession of the watch and begins to fiddle with the stem William starts to caution her. Too late she presses the stem and they are thrust into immediate darkness.And the adventure begins.They first meet Max-an apparent fellow time traveler who will be able to fill in some gaps and give us the laws of time travel for these stories. Max helps them to find a place to lie low in this world where they are out past curfew and in danger of running afoul of the mechanical monstrosities that were created to put down the Frankenstein like monsters who rebelled against their creators. Those in charge of the mechanical wonders took the advantage after saving everyone and now have control of the empire.The notion is that the creation of the monsters put emphasis on their saving the day in the battle at Waterloo and ensuring that the confidence level of the British foot soldier is lowered enough to change all of their history to a complete reliance upon the monsters to do battle for them. Thus the changes in history that lead to this society of steam and metal are all tightly bound with the first anachronistic event in history.One major law of time travel seems to be that the time traveler is only allowed one attempt to change specific events in specific times and the traveler gets blocked out from those timelines once his presence in that timeline has occurred. (Explained here as not being able to be in the same place at the same time.) We get the sense that Max has already tried several things to zero in on the event that most strikingly determined the outcome, which is, to his unknown timeline, apparently history. Max mentions that his parents were time travelers and he sort of inherited the whole business from them. He possess a watch similar to the one Elizabeth has.This is really a fascinating time travel story. We see mostly that the time travelers are quick to learn that even the most dramatic changes in some of the important or even less important events are not enough to stem the tide of time and history. Now with the three of them working on it perhaps they will have an impact, but will they be able to reconcile the consequences of the outcome of meddling.This is a great book for history fans who aren't too particular about maintaining accuracy or overthinking the fact that there were so many things happening those days at Waterloo that it's difficult to say what would have occurred had any part gone differently. This novel has good solid world building for a Time Travel and Steampunk novel so there is lots here for the Sci-Fi and SFF group to love.This is also a love story that's building slow but believable with the relationship between Elizabeth and William and there's a bit of mystery about Max's over concern at getting those two back to their time line and I think it has something to do with that locket around his neck which Max guards possessively.A fun and fascinating romp through time and altered history.Although I don't need to say it; I will be reading the next novel soon.J.L. Dobias

Save My Soul (Preternaturals Book 2)is my first read from author Zoe Winters but it will not be my last.From the first I was intrigued with Anna's story if a bit confused... There is a lot going on in the story that will keep any reader glued to the pages, the best part is that you never see the twist in the ending coming at you until it happens...For me that makes a great plot, one that keeps you so busy turning pages that while everything is happening it just flows smoothly and you enjoy the action so much there is no stopping until the story finishes...Like everyone else who has read this book I heartily recommend it to anyone who enjoys a hot succubus , humor, paranormal suspense, romance and the consequences of witches curses as well as a little fantasy in their reading diet!I must disclose that this was a review copy received as part of the author's June 7th through July 1st blog tour hosted by The Bookish Snob Promotions with my e-copy provided by the author in exchange for an honest review. reviewText: The MarBlue Vassen Kindle ereader case for the Paperwhite is a good fit. The four straps at the four corners hold the device in place and the case does not get in the way of the standard Amazon USB cable. The case looks good but it's not cutting edge style and design. There are no pockets for a stylus or business cards or anything else. On the outside there is a strap that can hold the case closed, which is a plus if you are putting the device in a bag or backpack with other devices that may come into contact with the screen.When reading, with the cover folded under the device, the left side is slightly raised. This I find gives you a nice hold, with your thumb pressing against the hump. This may be even more useful with the basic Kindle since your thumb can be very close to the page turn buttons on the left side of the device.In addition to the Paperwhite, this Marblue case is also a good fit for the basic Kindle (the one without a touchscreen and without a keyboard). It doesn't get in the way of the charging cable either. However, for the basic Kindle, I find that the official Amazon case (product code B004SD1XB0) is a much more organic fit if you like a slim easy to handhold setup that makes the case disappear.The Marblue also fits the 6-inch Kobo Touch ereader, however, its power button is covered by the top right strap, so if you turn it on/off often, it may get irritating.The Marblue also just barely fits the 6-inch Nook Simple Touch. Its power button however is on the back of the device, so you probably have to remove it from the case if you want to use the power button.Since I was experimenting, I also tried the Marblue with the Kindle with Keyboard and the original Kindle Fire color screen tablet. They don't fit since both devices are bigger than the actual Marblue case.Unboxing: it comes in frustration free packaging and friends of the environment will be thrilled that it does not include a foam padding. As with most cases these days, there is an initial smell, so now I air them all out for 2-3 days whether they need it or not. This one needs it but the smell is not as bad as some other cases. By air it out, I mean, I leave it open near a door or window that gets airflow, but I don't do anything special to it.
summary: Good fit for Kindle Paperwhite and basic Kindle

Wendell Mackey has just escaped from a shadowy building where doctors experiment on people. But now that he’s free Wendell’s nightmare is only just beginning for he is changing into a monster…I was really puzzled by this book. At the end, I still wasn’t clear exactly what was and had happened to Wendell. Had he been changed by experimentation? Was he a killer or just deranged? There is a large element of flashback, Wendell regularly drops into the past from the present, particularly when remembering his difficult childhood and his negligible relationship with his mother. He also believes he’s changing into a monster, a new form of human. Again, I still can’t quite decide whether this was really happening.The writing style is quite interesting, slightly offbeat. However, I struggled to take to the characters. There’s Wendell himself who initially works for the shadowy institute, then starts to partake in the experimentation by swallowing pills left in his locker by the doctors. I couldn’t accept this, would many, if any, people do the same? It wasn’t a reasonable premise in my opinion.The other relatively few characters are also odd – Drake, one of his neighbors is particularly unpleasant and the pair engage in some strange meetings. Sister Agatha, another neighbor and elderly nun takes pity on him for some reason and provides his salvation. I couldn’t see why she would, other than a sense of caring for a fellow human, even one as apparently deranged as Wendell. Perhaps she saw something I couldn’t.At approaching 85,000 words it’s not the longest novel in the world, but the nine chapters (one per day) means long periods between a natural break and sometimes extensive narrative which is more often than not Wendell internalizing and examining his past, present and future – another element I struggled with. Dialogue was in short supply. Therefore, the story didn’t exactly skip along.Not a bad read, but not without its challenges.**originally reviewed for Books and Pals blog. May have received free review copy.**

Just read this in a single day and have to say this is one of the best horror stories I have read in ages! It is absolutely grisly, gruesome and nasty ~ in other words, right up my street!A group of shoppers find themselves trapped in a new supermarket with no hope of escape. On the shelves are disembodied feet (seasoned ready for cooking), pickled eyes and fresh tongue kebabs - all mixed in amongst the usual produce. At first some of them think it is all some kind of sick, practical joke but when some of them try to leave, they quickly learn there is only one way they are getting out of this store...and it's not through the front doors!This is an awesome, awesome, awesome read and one hell of a ride! It is quite simply one of the best short horror novels that I have read in ages! It feels heavily influenced by Richard Laymon in places and is exceptionally nasty right through to the end. The climax alone will leave you gasping, let alone the rest of the novel! It really is a roller coaster ride from start to finish!This is the first piece of fiction I have read by author, Michael Bray but you can be certain, it won't be the last! I was left speechless, reeling and almost sickened at times by the sheer horror and brutality depicted within but you know what? Horror simply doesn't get much better than this!This is how much the book influenced me: mid-reading, I popped into my local Tesco Express to pick up a couple of things. Walking around the shelves, I found myself half-consciously looking around for disembodied limbs and decapitated heads - it wasn't till I got to the till that I realised what I had been doing! This is the sign of a good author, that he can so engross you in his writing that you find yourself actually living what you have been reading in your head! Few writers have this ability and so for M.Bray to achieve this shows just how good a writer he really is!

As usual I picked up this freebie by it's cover.  Never read the description if I had I would have avoided.  While I enjoy mild erotica and vampire stories and adore them when they come together, I don't enjoy the submissive/dominant aspect and while the bondage was very mild and fully consensual it pulled me out of the story.  However, those are my issues and many other readers may enjoy those parts of the the story.  I should add the intimate scenes are lusty, explicit with adult language and are well written.  They include light bondage, oral, and a bit of backdoor action.  All acts are consensual.My main issue here is the universe building.  In this universe all vampires are born male, without souls and have "magical" abilities i.e. conjuring and transportation.  Certain human females are marked with the "tattoo" of their vampire mate, and carries her mate's soul.  However the female doesn't know what the mark is until her mate shows up.  If the couple are not mated by the time the female is 30 then she dies and the vampire is left soulless and basically a Eunuch, good for fighting the "Fallen" or the bad vampires.  Usually the female sends out a call for her mate and once the vampire receives it he goes to her, courts her, they have a public, rough mating, and then they live happily ever after for centuries. In addition, the "Fallen" find unmated female mate's blood very potent and so when they find an unmated vampire mate, they like to drain her.Given the above "rules" of the universe I found it irritating that it was never explained why Brianna doesn't call Ethan until she is nearly on her deathbed.  What makes her not follow the universe's rules?  I realize the concept of "mine" is very popular in vampire serials and has been done well in several i.e. Brotherhood of the Black Dagger.  In this book I found the "mine" and "love" came so quickly and she accepted it even quicker, that it seemed to all be about lust and possession of the body and no real connection between the minds.  As this is a short story/novella, I realize the "erotica" portions are what most people are after, but I would have liked to have more than Hello, You have my soul, drink my blood and bam bam bam thank you maam we are mated for life.If you don't share my issues, then may I recommend this.  As it is a well tightly written story.  The scenes with Ethan's brothers are humorous and for me some of the best in the story.If you have issues with anything I mentioned in the first paragraph, give it a miss.

It took a chapter or two for me to really get into the newest book from Callie Hutton, The Duke's Quandry, but once I did I was hooked! It was impossible not to love Penelope and Drake, even when Drake was at his most priggish and you wanted the smack him upside the head to make him see sense. Penelope's constant running into things and knocking things over, not to mention the ubiquitous dirt on her person, made it impossible not to love her. Though it does make Drake a little crazy..Yeah, he's just a tad bit uptight. Not to mention nervous about living up to the example set by his father--at least, the father that exists in his memory. Fortunately, he has a mother, five sisters, and now Penelope to help him loosen up and set more realistic expectations for himself.Though of course it takes a while.Watching Penelope endear herself to Drake's family is marvelous, as is seeing him fight off his attraction to her. Naturally he's wildly unsuccessful, and at about three-quarters of the way through the event happens that everyone knows will occur from page one. I'm not going to tell you how it happens--you'll of course want to find out for yourself! Rest assured, though, that even as a new duchess, Penelope still has some awkwardly charming moments. :)The botanist aspect was extremely interesting--Penelope's enthusiasm for her passion is contagious. Her scientific mind also makes some interesting connections at unexpected times:"Has my mother spoken to you about what will happen tonight?""Yes, but it wasn't necessary, since in my work with cross-breeding, I have discovered that in order to reproduce you must take two different species. Well, actually not different species per se, but--" She stopped when in one forward motion he pulled her into his arms and lowered his head. His kiss started slow but soon turned burning and needy.Loved it!All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed Penelope and Drake's story. The first book in the series, The Elusive Wife, which tells the story of Drake's best friend Coventry's HEA (his wife was the speaker who caused the newly married Penelope such confusion in the excerpt above) has been in my TBR pile for a while now. It can definitely consider itself officially "moved up". Rating: 4 stars / B+ rating I received a complimentary copy in exchange for an honest review.

It was going to be a full moon and like the shifters say she (the moon) pulls at them and calls to their beast. When he gets Taylor to his house after small chat back and forth and very very uncomfortable awkward feelings he realizes Taylor hasn't fed and she needs to eat.  He offers his neck ( a very strange submission move unheard for an Alpha) but she feeds from his wrist and now the fun begins.  Neither of them can understand the feelings that are occurring and they both try and push them down.Taylor has some serious issues so these feelings frighten her since she has not had any warm and fuzzy feelings for a long time.  While in the custody of her mistress she was severely abused both physically and mentally and doesn't think she will ever be able to have a relationship sexual or not with any male.  There's just no trust not to mention the nightmares.I loved the way this story started unfolding with these two and some very interesting things start happening to Taylor which Victor can't understand.  He is the most loving, gentle and patient person with Taylor trying to earn her trust.  There is a lot of action in this book and some major misunderstandings but this is all I'm giving you. reviewText: Author Helen Hanson describes her writing as “thrillers for geeks.”There’s a certain geek factor in all thrillers. Many thriller authors write loving descriptions of cars, guns, bullets, bombs, or bullets. I have read several descriptions by different authors about how a bullet bounces around inside a skull and precisely what it does to a human brain.But I actually enjoyed the geek factor in Ocean of Fear. Hanson made the geeky-technical aspects integral not only to the plot, but also to one of the main characters.What makes a good thriller?To make a thrill, an author needs to build tension. The readers have to care enough about the characters and believe the situation enough to say “Oh no, don’t do that! You shouldn’t have done that!”When the tension snaps, the author has to surprise you. It’s not a thrill when you know what’s going to happenThere are a lot of those moments in Ocean of Fear.Plot pointsLike any good thriller, Ocean of Fear begins with a murder. Baxter Cruise (character names are not this author’s strong suit), a grad-school dropout turned email spammer, discovers UC Santa Cruz professor, Dr. Allesandra Bisch, dead in her office. Baxter’s employer, Professor Sydney Mantis, had given Baxter a flash drive and asked him to give it personally to Dr. Bisch, as well as to look after his, Mantis’s dog while he suddenly had to leave town for a few days.The mystery is not who killed Dr. Bisch — the author introduces the assassin in Chapter 2. The mystery is why, and the tension rises as the main investigator, FBI Special Agent Claudia Seagal, puts the pieces of the puzzle together, and as Baxter gets pulled deeper and deeper into the trap laid for Dr. Mantis.Hanson knows how to ramp up a story by taking it in unexpected directions. It turns out that the professors, Bisch and Mantis, were developing robotic submarines for drug dealers to use to smuggle their product into the US. Special Agent Seagal. This is the geek factor: Hanson tells us enough about robotics and remote control to make the story work, so that we understand that this story just could not happen without this technical detail. However, she never gives too much, never bores us with technical factoids that we don’t need. Every word is a plot point.Engaging and critical backstoriesDespite their unfortunate names, the characters have interesting backstories. Hanson is also skilled at not drowning the reader in long information dumps, but revealing details about Claudia’s deceased husband, Baxter’s dead parents, Mantis’s habit of seducing students, even the bad guys’ back stories as they’re needed. Readers begin to feel for the characters, to hope that their plans work out. The sibling rivalry between the two main baddies really rang true.Two weaknessesThere are only two weaknesses with this story. First, there are the character names. The author shows us in Chapter 1 that “Dr. Bisch” is an intentional joke, but then there are all the animal names: Dr. Mantis, Agent Seagall. I don’t know if this was an intentional gag, but while there are some humorous moments in the book, it’s not overall a comedy. It’s a thriller that takes engaging, believable characters on an exhilarating ride to an explosive and satisfying conclusion.The other weakness was the cover. It’s professionally done, but maybe a little too clichéd. It gave away too much of the story, instead of making me want to open the book.But those are minor flaws. In the end, Ocean of Fear is a good, satisfying read from a skilled author.4 *.
summary: A geeky thriller that I could not put down

In the middle of the party, Helga, his great grandmother disappears. Everyone starts to search for her with no results. They finally find out where Helga is at, she is at a casino. Natalie leaves Libby's house to meet up with the girls, She tells them everything and they leave to get Helga. Like always trouble finds Natalie and her friends. This is truly a must read it is hilarious. I laughed so much.Reviewed by Maribel

Only The Strongest Survive by IanThis book starts out with a kidnapping of the CEO of a huge company that is worth billions in the stock market.Although I don't normally read thriller books this one held my interest because of the many aspects of it.The book concentrates on those who now run the company and the decisions they make with Emeily gone-they are still not sure if it was a kidnapping or she just needed a week away from things.Love the story line and learning about the stock market.Her life is spared, brought back to life and must now live where she has no outside contact with others but has transferred 2 million dollars to John. She had taken over his familys company several years ago and now John wants what the company was really worth-10 million.One brother, Ronald has no idea she is alive again, last he left her was in the ground in a coffin, buried.I am caught up in the moment of reading this and I can't seem to read fast enough to find the answers I want.John leaves many nights and from her basement room she can hear the alarm that sounds when one comes and goes into the complex.The story goes back in time as to how she got the position she held at the company and then to the present: She does get to spend some time with John as she advises him what to buy and sell and they get to talk about the past. She gets to know him.Love the explanations of how to buy and sell and why.Journalism during war or earthquakes was a new one for me.I am totally petrified for her and then he announces he will set her free.There is some sex and at times it appears to be rather brutal and at other times it's just a passion for sex.

truely excellent. this book exceeds many that we are paying through the nose for. have no problems donating to my animal shelter cos thats agiven anyway. great book, characters are interesting and I'll def. be reading all of them.

The book was pretty good overall but the author left you wanting more in the wrong way. There were numerous instances left unexplained or felt rushed in an inappropriate way. Stella Griffin, the fire chief of the Sweet Pepper Fire Brigade, is mystified when Hero, theDalmatian puppy training to be their rescue dog, turns up missing.  Even more mystifying are the reports that a puppy matching Hero's description has rescued some children.I like this series, the characters, and the small-town atmosphere.
WHAT A GREAT ENDING TO THE BOOK  SORRY IT IS OVER  BUT I LOVED THEM BOTH  SO GLAD THEY FINALLY DID WHAT SHE HAD TO DO  GONNA MISS THEM A LOT

This is a short, sweet wrap up of the three couples that we have met in the Billionaire Bachelors Club Series. We get them in the the different stages of their perspective relationships: Gage and Marina are getting married, Archer and Ivy are having their 1st baby, and Matt and Bryn have settled nicely into their exclusive relationship and they work well together at Matt's winery, which is the scene of the nuptials.It is always nice to see how couples that you have read about end up down the road, and this was a nice way to end the series. It was much shorter than I anticipated, and just touched the surface of each couple, but all in all it was a lighthearted, fun wrap up to a sweet series.
summary: 3.5 A nice little novella for our 3 Billionaire Bachelors, who are Bachelors no more!

I highly recommend this book to anyone looking for great appetizer recipes, even if they don't have to follow a gluten-free diet.Marg RuttanInternational Best-Selling Cookbook Author

I've never been a fan of the romance genre, but this tale has a compelling aspect that makes the romantic element interesting, and feel natural. Set first in modern day Scotland, then in an eighteenth century version of the same country, the descriptions were so vivid, it felt as if I was there. I know from the author's blog that she spent last summer in the UK. Her familiarity with the countryside shines through in this story.Even though there aren't any "new" story elements here, the author weaves plot threads together in a way that feels fresh. This is far more than another time-traveling romance. Sure there's a "happy-ever-after" ending, but there's ever so much more than that along with it. I don't want to say any more because I don't want to spoil the story, but it's well worth your time to take a look at this one.
summary: I Could Almost Feel the Mists of Scotland

reviewText: This book starts off with a great list of herbs, all their great healing properties and how they can be used in medicinal ways. From there, it goes on to explain other natural remedies such as meditation, acupuncture, and art as therapy. This book goes into such detail about how you can benefit from these natural remedies and why they should be tried as an alternative to conventional medicine. I would definitely recommend this book.

The story is pure fantasy of how the author imagines a boy-meeting-boy scenario. Viewing it as such, the story is okay. Otherwise it would be a bit difficult to believe (at least towards the end - no spoilers from me).Two men in different places in life – thanks to their age-difference, of course – meet through their occupation and feel instant connection. There are several things that they have in common – not only the profession, but also the level of inexperience and almost narcissistic behaviour prior their meeting. Some of the characters around them made me smile, because they are just that – characters. The plot is quite clever although a little thin.

This is one of those books that I liked but I didn't love.  It had a good story and I love to see how everything seemed to come together and work out.In saying that, Sierra did not have an easy road with Evan.  He had suffered a tragic loss and kept to himself, afraid of ever trying to love again.  Sierra knew from the moment she saw him that he was alone and needed someone.  She seemed to be able to see into his heart and know what he needed to move forward.The more he pushed her away, the more I wanted to slap him.  Then, the more she hung on and waited for him, I wanted to tell her to just give up.  She was very persistent and what a patient woman she was.All in all, I loved seeing her break down those walls that no one had been able to do before.  With a little twist into the mix, Evan soon finds out how much she means to him.At times, this book seemed to be a little slow and I'm not a big sports fan, so I'm not saying it turned me off, but I did seem to just skim through some of that, but overall it was a good read.
summary: Liked it, but didn't love it.

reviewText: Finished book 2 in less than 12 hours. You will not want to sleep while reading story of Angel and Slade. Can't wait to see how this one ends and this author is in my top10

“The Art of Wedding a Greek Billionaire” by the amazing Marien Tee is one intense read.  I have been waiting for this since I read the first part.  I love Mairi and Damen chemistry and the emotional roller coaster that is their love.  This is one series, this gives a HEA, that always requires that I have tissues at hand and makes the hubby think that I am weird since I do talk to the characters.  I truly enjoyed how the secondary characters are included into the story without taking away from the main story.  I am thinking that there might be several books coming in the future about some of the characters.If you are like me and love to feel the emotional charge of books then this one is the one for you. Jocelyn Hewitt, an anthropologist, joined a team in Cambodia to try and find the remains of her father and the cause of his death. A broken man, with no hope, he hears Jocelyn's pain and lets her know she is not alone. He gives her the courage she needs to risk escape and their adventure and romance begins.The chemistry between Oliver and Josie is divine.This novel was fast-paced, violent, exciting, full of adventure, suspense and romance.A Must Read !

reviewText: No that is not the start to a bad joke, it's the start to your next smexy fantasy featuring Talan, the dirty hottie, make you want to lick him, tattoo artist that is the center of this delicious little series starter. So Talan is a man-whore, yes this is pretty clear from the beginning but he is one of those man-whores you can't help but dream about getting in your bedroom despite his reputation, he is delectable and in Marking Her he meets not only the woman of his dreams but his mental match.Maya aka Bitty which is Talan's term of endearment for her, is a spunky 20yr old college student. She is full of vibrance, intelligence and man can she put you in your place.Damsel in distress in this book? No no, Maya is just about as feisty, balls to the walls and tough as her counterpart. She gives Talan a challenge to his skills department as well as his boundaries on relationships and what does Talan give her in return? Sexual Frustration, yes that is exactly what he does.  Talan and Bitty decide to take things slow in the book and that is exactly what happens and guess what I loved it. It was a breath of fresh air that these two were not humping each other and proclaiming their undying love 20 pages in especially since the book itself is not too long. Elena gives us a relationship that we can actually relate too. Its up and down, confusing, new, fun, nerve-racking, intense and REAL. Talan and Maya have their moments of flaming attraction and their moments of genuine tenderness where you can see how their relationship is developing into something more.I think this is a great start to the series. The male POV is done well and I like the pace and flow of the story. I would have liked a little more background into the characters, maybe some more info on not just Talan's past but Maya's as well. I am also very curious of the supporting characters like Esther, Simon, Lance and Veronica and I am excited to see how their stories may develop through out this series.
summary: So this 6'4 Tatted guy walks into a bar...

I am not usually drawn to time travel type books... but this was really different. This story was extremely exciting, being first of a two book series, the second one being "Kingdom Come". The story flowed beautifully between the two. Character development was rich and detailed. As with Kathryn's books, family names are recognized because her characters have relationship through relatives or associations, I love that. In this story the Knight is a "Crusader" in the Holy land and has a mighty mission.... I will not say anymore about the plot.... there are lot of twist and turns... and a beautiful love that crosses through the centuries. I highly recommend the book.... buy it, read it, and enjoy!

I found this book helpful on many levels. As a mom of two elementary school students, as a business owner and entrepreneur, the tools in this concise, highly-enjoyable book gave me valuable insights for better utilizing my resources to nurture a culture of prosperity in running my days. A novice at understanding the principles of Feng Shui, I found this book to be well-written in terms of giving educating me on the five elements of Feng Shui and I was initially intrigued by this title because marrying what I knew of Feng Shui with wealth seemed a strange marriage to strike. But this book didn’t disappoint in any way.The author’s style is informative without being too technical, as well as engaging and attention-grabbing. Clear learning objectives are identified, so you know exactly what you’ll learn by reading this book! For the value this book brings in giving much food for thought to all those inclined to succeed and for teaching me several excellent techniques I can immediately implement at home as a mom and in my business, I highly recommend this book.

Wicked Thing is an awkward read. The story lacked any tension or chemistry. The dialogue was weak, and the characters were shallow/underdeveloped. I gave up at the 42% point (and it was a struggle getting that far). The writing quality is below what I enjoy reading. The following quote is from Camryn (it is her internal dialogue in describing Dallas' sculpture). It confirmed for me that I needed to cut bait and abandon ship :"This belongs in a museum or a fountain of a high end casino. It looks high end and very expensive."I returned this book for a refund.

Dragon Dreams is an interesting story. I was hooked from the first and should not have started reading it before bed. The characters grab you and you will find yourself longing to know what is happening in dream world. You will keep coming back drawn to the land of Terradin, back to Nachal and Auri.The scenery is richly described as you travel with the characters through the different lands of, elves, dwarves, and dragons! If you are a fan of The Hobbit, or Eragon series you will love this book. It has many similar characters.Dusty Lynn Holloway has a haunting quality to her writing. The story is described in such intense detail that you feel immediately pulled into the story. If you want to escape your world, I would recommend Dragon Dreams.

She rode around in Sincere's car,  and played dress up.......  Not anything I could see that would hail her the first female King.My name is K Sherrie,And I DO NOT approve this read

I received this book for review from HeartFelt Promos and the author.  I was not compensated nor was I required to write a positive review.Renny Morgan is having a very sexy discussion with Luna Kalen and that’s just the Prologue.  This is Luna’s story to tell so it’s told in the first person.  And be warned, the language is graphic.Luna has a very sexy encounter with a man she’s just met – a man without a name.  How many of you would like to have one of those same encounters?  This may be one of those cases where you’re either going to have to open a window or turn on a fan.  For me, thank goodness it’s wintertime.Trevor Gary is Luna’s mystery man.  Their stories are perplexing but also seem to be so similar.  This vampire tale is different from any ones that I have read before – our author has put a slight twist to it.  And that is what makes it so interesting.  Maya’s book is like an addiction – once you start you just don’t want to put it down.The Epilogue will come as a surprise and will have you questioning all that you have read.  I felt it was a great ending and it will leave you wanting more.  The second book hasn’t come out yet but she does have other vampire books out that you can read until the next Naughty Vampire makes its appearance.
summary: A Story That Will Suck You In.

reviewText: I was completely charmed by Tom and Bev and their romance. Bev is fifty-nine years old, Tom sixty-two, and they are total opposites. Forced to spend time together as Thanksgiving approaches, they somehow bring out the best in each other. She needs to loosen up, he needs to soften up, and it was fun to watch.Bev is locked up tight, about ready to snap, but Tom is growly, lives loud, and takes no prisoners in life. Bev's a sweet and soft woman, really liked her, but Tom was it for me. Like one of my gruff, alpha heroes aged to perfection. He's so rough around the edges, but does he come through with gentleness and caring when it counts! Very romantic ending to this story. Just proves that a fine man, a real man, only gets better with age.A sweet, sexy and tender little novella about finding love, passion, and happiness no matter how old we are. A sure feel-good read.
summary: An alpha hero aged to perfection

reviewText: An excellent, well-written plot with well-defined, believable characters.  I couldn't put it down and highly recommend it.  I can't wait for the sequel, which is due shortly.
I took a chance at this book after reading the reviews and I'm glad I did. Don't know what some were reading but this book was good!!! Loved the characters, especially Kyle.

This is the second book in the series (not counting the prequel, Destined) and it just gets better! Follow Mia, Gabe, Lexi and Doug as their relationships deepen and grow, and see how they handle what life throws their way. The dialogue is real and the situations are real. As a reader, I felt that I could relate to one or more of these characters, which for me, is always a plus. You will not be disappointed and it will make you want to pick up the next book to find out what happens next! Fallowfield has done a wonderful job!

Everything is going pretty well.  Erin does legal work for Non-Profits and Seth's firm has made them even wealthier, but they still live a simple family life, even with the money.  Mac is almost 17 and is finally going out on her first date with Justin, who tormented her in First grade.  She is still like Seth and has those model looks that Erin longed for in high school.  Mac is nervous about how her Dad will react to her dating so she asks Erin to pave the way, which she does with extra effort sex.  Seth freaks out and of course remembers the name of the kid who bothered his precious daughter and wants to kill him.  Erin settles everything down, but finds out she has a new problem.  Anna knew that they were not married when Mac was born, but she does not know that guilt makes Seth so worried about Mac.  When he finds that helping one daughter is hurting another, he shuts down until Erin brings him back to focus on not guilt tripping but fixing things.Poor Justin is grilled by a sharp defense attorney and comes out of the ordeal reasonably well.  Seth has a plan to help Anna.  The fact that Seth is only 50 and Erin still in her 40's made me feel old when Anna told them they had entirely too much sex for old people.  Seth's creative ideas for improving Anna's self esteem issues and lowering his shields to explain to his youngest daughter why it may have looked like he was paying more attention to Mac was a beautiful piece of writing.  What we lose in youth we can frequently make up in the richness of our life when we age.  Parenting is about hard work, luck and reaping what you sow.  These two damaged people made a great life together and I would love to keep checking in on them.
summary: I would like to keep checking in on Seth and Erin

reviewText: *** ARC/BETA Received by authors, in exchange for an honest review***Firstly let me say, these two lady's are amazing authors to BETA read for. It always helps when the quality of the writing, grammar, phrasing etc makes you forget that you are in fact, reading a BETA copy and not a finalised novel straight from amazon!!I adored my ARC of Chase, and as such threatened to throw a big girl tantrum if I wasn't able to get my hands on the next in this series!!I have to give reference to the line in the movie 'Jerry McGuire'" You had me at hello. "This ^ is how I felt reading the first paragraph of Kade, and this line came up:'He looks a little like Jax Teller from Sons Of Anarchy.'Instant swoon, as this is my celebrity hard core crush!!Now into the book.HOW IS IT EVEN POSSIBLE THAT I LOVED THIS MORE THEN 'CHASE'?!?!The Steele men are hott!!Funny, sweet, protective, I love them!Nikki and Kade I heart you!! I also hate you!! It's a fine line that is crossed many, many times throughout this novel.Nikki is a strong, self assured female character, with whom I fell in love with in 'Chase'I knew they had slept together, but the way that man goes after her....dominant Alfa male hotness right there!!I feel for Nikki, after her past with Ben, I can understand why she is so hesitant. To have such STRONG feelings for someone, instantly, is intense, not to mention scary as hell!' I just don't know if I can survive Kade.'Me either Nikki, me either :('Don't need to be on somebody's arm to look good(I like who I am)I'm not saying I don't wanna fall in love cos I wouldI'm not gonna get hooked up just cos you say I should(can't romance on demand)I'm gonna wait so I'm sorry if you misunderstood'Again the karaoke scene gets me! The angst these two go through is frustrating, beautiful, emotional, oh yer, did I mention frustrating!!!!I love a good game of cat and mouse. That's exactly what I got!We get so much before anything serious even happens between these two.Kade is just as strong of a character. He is difficult to describe, as he is a constant contradiction. He is sweet, but rude. Caring one minute, ignoring the next. You love him, then you love to hate him. He is never downright nasty , but he has his moments that you want to strangle him.Am I confusing you yet?!?'He stomps off and James comes over to me and pulls me into his side. "I think Kade is more pussy whipped than Chase," he says with a twinkle in his eyes.With that we both burst out laughing.'Out of the two I couldn't help but feel worse for Kade at first.' I want Nikki, by my side. To go to sleep with, wake up with, and everything in between. I know Nikki is the woman for me, now I just need to convince her. To get her to let me in, let me prove myself. Prove my worth. It will never be over between Nikki and I.'He is head over heals for this wild red head, and it is affecting him so deeply, you want to cry, then he turns around and does something so sweet, you feel the need to swoon, or something so Alfa and cocky, it makes you blush and giggle.I think I need my own Steele man!!I LOVED Lucy ( the boys mother) in the first bookAnd she got me again this time, I was seriously hoping the YOLO scene would be replayed and I wasn't disappointed!! How could you NOT love this woman?!?'When I find out Lucy put alcohol into James' coffee I burst out laughing, and when she says YOLO, I almost choke with laughter. Who knew this prim and proper looking woman had a sense of humor?'This novel moves smoothly and with easy from one POV to the next. It was never choppy, Which is something I really enjoyed.Ashley, oh boy, can you say drama?!?"You should probably run for an extra hour, you need it," She grates.I'm usually yelling at the female in the lovers 'tiffs', but this time it was all directed at Kade!!That boy had no clue.I can't stand when people use and abuse kind hearted people. It really is my pet peeve.The fact that Ashley was able to manipulate him so easily annoyed the hell out of me, but only adds to show Kades loving protective nature.This is something that is not resolved quickly, but I think it's a HUGH compliment to Dawn and Chantal, that I wanted to jump into my tablet and slap Ashley into submission, while yelling at her that Kade will NEVER be hers!!! Angry much! She just doesn't let up, Reminding me of one of those little chiwawa dogs, yap, yap, yap, < curse word removed> yap, don't bother asking because yes I would kick her!!!I really enjoyed Ryder this time round. In ' Chase ' he just turned me off for some reason. However I am looking forward to reading more about his story.' I want him, and I want him bad, I just don't know if I can.'I like the fact that Kade and Nikki start again by being friends. It's not rushed. It just flows from there and they let it take its course.I LOVED THIS:"She sure is, and I've seen her half naked," Kade says casually, shoveling ice cream into his mouth."I'm sorry, what?" Chase says in a deadly tone. I bite my lip. Kade is such a shit stirrer. I kick him under the table."Ouch! What was that for?" James growls. Oops. I try again."Nikki, what the f <curse word removed> " Chase complains.Oh come on. Third time's a charm right? I kick harder, knowing it hits my target when Kade grunts.I had tears, I was laughing so hard!!I love pregnant Layla!!!"I need candy NOW!"Oh boy she made me giggle.I'm desperate to know what's going on with James!!I'm hoping his is the next in the series after Ryder.This relationship is up and down and so so good. It is just so real!! I love the writing style. I was NEVER board, I laughed, I cried, I yelled, I was frustrated to the point of wanted to throw my reader across the room!!I HIGHLY recommended this book, you won't be disappointed!!I am so very much looking forward to the next instalment with Ryder.
