Mari'es Tempting Reads Review:This has got to be one of the BEST books by Indigo Sin yet! I absolutely was taken in with Damaged and didn't want it to end. We have Monica a woman who was forced to pickpocket to survive after running away from home with her two siblings in tow because of her step-dad, and losing her job. It was very rough for her and her sister and brother. They were living in poverty, and weren't really making it with their bills when she was caught red-handed by the most SEXIEST and wonderful cop imaginable.Seth stole my heart from the moment I read he caught up to little Miss pickpocket Monica and wouldn't stop chasing her until she let him help her and her siblings. He was utterly the most fascinating male cop I have read about in a LONG time. I couldn't help but to be fascinated by the story of a damaged young woman who needed protection and a gentle caring man, a cop, that was sexy as all get out and just about the most protective man I read about in a long while.The sex was sweet, gentle, and surprisingly alluring. I thought, with the kind of past Monica had, this gentle love-making was perfect for this type of romance story and to me, it was steamy and ever so sexy.Indigo Sin created, in my opinion, the most intriguing and captivating story as of yet. She not only created this masterpiece but she attempted a whole new genre in romance and just made it work in the best way possible. I can't tell you how much I enjoyed this story. Or maybe I can. I give Damaged by Indigo Sin a FIVE OUT OF FIVE STARS! I am ever so curious to see what else Indigo Sin has in store in the future in her writing career and I can't wait to find out!If you haven't picked up Damaged, don't walk, but RUN to Amazon and pick your copy up. I am sure you won't be disappointed.

You know things you would expect from a college relationships. I wont ruin it but believe me when I say that you will not be dissapointed with the level of sexual romance in this book.  Renee knows how to hold her audience!As I am reading along and loving the way the story is progressing Renee throws in a twist that literally kills me!  Yes, she brought me to tears like a little girl! It made such an impression that I had to take a BREATHER!  After I was done bawling like a little girl that lost her teddy, I finished reading the story.  What can I say?  I fell in love with a story that not only gave me a lustful read but showed me that romance is not only for romantic reasons but a romance of kinship can soothe the soul and make this a beautifully complete full circle kind of story.So now for the rating....  I give this book 9 stars!  Any book that can bring me joy, smoking hot guys, tears and soulful love is totally worth 9 stars!

They are adult oriented and the love scenes are steamy as well which would be better understood by an adult reader.  This series tackles some heavy issues of rape, the sex trade, molestation, physical and sexual abuse so please be advised before reading.Summary:The third in the Highlands Trilogy, HIGHLAND MAGIC begins where HIGHLAND GRACE ended, giving you Branwenn and Callum's story.Set in the turn of the 13th century Scottish Highlands. After fleeing her wedding to her Norman betrothed and being swept into the Irish Sea during a storm, Branwenn Maclean finds herself once more in the land of the Highland Scots. Little does she know, however, that the maimed man who drops through the ceiling of her hiding place is none other than Callum MacGregor, the man who both vexes and beguiles her.Callum awakens in a darkened sea cave believing he's being nursed by a sea nymph. Little does he know, however, that the fey creature is in actuality none other than his massive warrior Maclean cousins' foster sister, Branwenn, the lass that has taunted and haunted him since his first encounter with her one year past.

I am a huge lover of anything PNR and have been a Tiffany Allee fan since I read her book Vampire Games. So of course I jumped at the chance to read this book even though I have not read the first book in this series, Don't Bite the Bridesmaid (yet). I did know enough about the first book that there were no issues with understanding the premise and characters in this book but I would suggest that someone who hasn't read the blurb (and any excerpts that were available) read and enjoy her first book before jumping into and enjoying this one. I think it would benefit the reader to have that knowledge of the characters in the first book that are referenced here and of course, the one who is being threatened.Everyone should be lucky enough to have family (or friends) like Charles and Rachel. These two are willing to set aside their own lives for a while to help out their family. Charles has had to befriend Brent and spend time with him - the man he suspects of threatening his brother's fiancee! And Rachel has agreed to try and be nice to Brent - the man who cheated with her sister (on his previous fiancee) and on her since then! This guy (Brent) is in serious trouble if he thinks he can get away with anything untoward since these two have teamed up to make sure he leaves their loved ones alone.I enjoyed the interaction and by-play between Charles and Rachel throughout the book. They are both strong-willed, opinionated people who don't like asking for help or admitting they may have been wrong about something. It is hilarious to watch as they work together to mess with Brent on this ill-fated skiing trip! Rachel discovers Charles is a vampire quite soon after she realizes he is the business contact Brent is meeting. Charles and Rachel actually meet before this while she is waiting for her sister and Brent to show up. reviewText: 3-3.5 starsThis was an enjoyable story. I liked both Samantha and Chase and the story was good but there were a couple points that left me a bit frustrated. This is the first story I've read by this author. Based off this story I may try more of her work in the future.Samantha (aka Sam) is in her last year of medical studies at Duke. She's a wolf shifter and the eldest born of her sisters. Her family is of the "Noble" shifter bloodlines and holds a council seat. Since she has no brothers, her future mate will take over the council seat. Her family holds to a tradition of not waiting for their fated mate but instead mating for power and money. Since Sam just turned 25 (the "time" when the mating should occur according to their traditions) Sam has been doing her best to avoid getting pushed in to the mating hunt but she has to go home for the holidays and worries about her situation.Chase is a wolf shifter and in the Army. He's 75 years old and has been waiting for his mate to show up and in the mean time has been away in the army most of his life. Chase is just getting off a flight coming home for the holidays when he meets another shifter in the airport and she connects with him in a way he's been waiting for feel for years.Chase and Sam exchange names but don't get more at the airport. Chase's family isn't of "noble" shifter blood and her mother makes her opinion of Chase known but Sam doesn't care about any of that and wants to see more of Chase. When Sam gets home she finds that her parents decided to spring the mating hunt on her in surprise and there are 3 strange men there waiting to hunt her to be their mate. Sam is completely freaked and her and her sisters go out. While out they happen (with a little help from a friend) to meet up with Chase and his brother. Sam and Chase talk and Sam doesn't want to tell him about the mate hunt because she's worried he could get killed in the hunt. She does tell him in the end however and he demands to join the hunt. Fortunately tradition makes it so anyone that request entry has to be allowed so Chase is in whether her parents like it or not. There's some drama as the race comes up and Sam's parents had me wondering WTF!!! a couple times because there were some weird vibes going on with the actions of both her mother and father. The hunt takes place and ends with Chase and Sam together with their mate bond complete so they'll have their HEA.While I liked the story and liked both Chase and Sam, I wish we'd gotten a little more time with them together. The story leading up to the hunt was pretty good but I have to admit that I was slightly frustrated with the ending. Chase and Sam are mated so they can't be separated now but there was no discussion of how they would proceed into the future and there was no explanation of her parents behavior or confrontation with them once all was said and done. Regardless of the plot points that were left unresolved, the story was good and I did enjoy it. :)

Rating: 4.75 starsHank Calder is a good man, he's worked hard  to get a home and be responsible, remarkable considering his background.  So when his sister dropped off her 4 year old daughter and left without a word, Hank accepted Josie into his home and heart because he wanted for her more than what he had growing up.  But Josie is so young and missing her mother while all Hank wants is  to make everything as perfect for her as possible, with as little drama as possible.  Drama is something both Josie and Hank have had too much of in their lives. Stressed out, Hank turns to his gym workouts for relief and takes Josie along to the gym's daycare.Enter Justin, daycare worker extraordinaire, young and flamboyant as they come.  Justin consistently helps Hank with Josie even though Hank is determined to leave drama and Justin out of their lives.  But fate and Josie intervene until Hank realizes that Justin with all his goodness and all his support just might be the man he needs and has been looking for all his life, that Justin might be his "turkey in the snow".I am not going to even attempt to explain that "turkey in the snow" reference.  It has to be read in context but let's just say it had me in stitches and is such a perfect Amy Laneism that I was absolutely delighted.  It had me giggling and going back to reread it again and again.  It made me laugh, it made Justin laugh and it will make you laugh too.  But as this is a Amy Lane story, there will also be angst that will arrive on the heels of  such laughter and love.  Another perfect moment, this of sadness and regret between Hank and his sister, Amanda.  Everything here rings of authentic human emotion, pangs of despair, anger over past actions, and so much remembered love to help conquer life's worst moments as well.  That scene will stick with me for some time to come.I don't need to go into the author's gift for characters, it is there in every book she writes.  With her characters and her story lines, you can count on depth and layering that feels effortless that it goes by almost unnoticed.  Just sit back and enjoy the wonder of two men, both so different on the outside, but match up as equals in the inside where it counts.  I just loved Turkey in the Snow.  It brightened my holiday reading and left me full of smiles and joy.  That to me is the perfect holiday story.  Grab up Turkey in the Snow and make your holiday brighter too!This cover by Catt Ford just amazed me. .  Here the gentle edges are softened by snow, the darkness of the turkey illuminated by the light around it.  But instead of a harsh mood, the contrast is soft, you can almost hear the whispering of the snow as it falls.  Really, one of the best covers of 2012.  Just outstanding.
summary: A Heartwarming Christmas Tale You Won't Want To Miss

reviewText: "I was completely obsessed with her. Addicted wasn't a strong enough word. She had surpassed my addictive tendencies, and I was full-blown obsessed. There was nothing I wouldn't do for her. All she had to do was ask. I would give anything up just to get to hold her like this again." Krit CorbinSeriously? If that didn't stir something up in you, I don't know what will.If you've figured anything out yet about me. You have to know I am a HUGE Abbi Glines fan. I think the woman is a genius. I have read every book she's written (including the Existence series) and loved every one. Abbi's books are books I have gone back and read more than one time. Another useful factoid about me is I have the attention span of a gnat. So basically for something to hold my attention from the front cover (dayum did you see it?) to the last page it has to be amazeballs....Bad for You was exactly that book. I am completely and utterly in love with Krit Corbin (Yes I know he's not real.) But damn, that boy did something to me.....EVERYWHEREI have read very few books that I immediately wanted to reread the second I put them down. Bad for You is one of those books for me.Blythe Blakely is the girl who nobody wanted. Orphaned as an infant, she is raised by her church Pastor and his abomination of a wife. For some reason unknown to anyone (well for now.) Margaret Williams hates the child that she and her husband offered to raise. Margaret Williams tells Blythe how disgusting and gross she is. Throw in some random beatings and a small town that treats her like she's garbage and you get a socially awkward, self loathing young woman.So thank goodness after Mrs. Williams dies, Pastor Williams does the only decent thing he could do. He sends Blythe off to Sea Breeze, Alabama (lucky girl.) There she has her own apartment, an opportunity at community college and a new job. Add to this mix some totally hot new neighbors and that makes for good reading.Enter Krit Corbin. You remember him right? The womanizing, man whore lead singer of the band Jackdown? Well anyway, Krit runs into Blythe the first day she's at her apartment. Krit and his best friend, room mate and band mate Green are her upstairs neighbors. In case I didn't mention, Blythe is painfully shy and afraid of social situations. Krit sees Blythe and is immediately drawn to her. Of course Krit has his own demons and decides he can't touch Blythe because he would break her.The two of them feel like they're not good enough. Blythe has lived her whole life believing there was evil inside her and Krit just believes he's only good for one thing. He feels he could never be good enough for Blythe.I forgot to mention, Blythe is clearly, absolutely stunning. There's not a boy in Sea Breeze who doesn't want to get to know her. Including the son of the new Pastor at the church Blythe works as a secretary. Eh, a few dates, but clearly not Krit (oh until the bombshell drops and I was like "Whoa, didn't see that coming.)But I digress....Blythe and Krit begin this sort of tenuous friendship. They can both be themselves around each other. Blythe sees all the good in Krit that he doesn't realize is there. Krit feels like he needs to protect Blythe. Their friendship is genuine and sweet. I adore Blythe's innocence and I love the person Krit is when he's with her. But don't think for a minute that there's no sexual tension, because, oh yea, it's getting hot in hurr.I think these are two of Abbi's strongest characters. They're so different, but they're so good together and I was cheering for them the whole way through. Now I'm not giving anything away, but Krit has a little freak out and then this happens:"No one in my life had ever done that. Not even my sister. I was positive at that moment, when my sweet quiet Blythe was loudly telling a room full of people who knew better that I was a nice guy who was treated unfairly, that I would follow her off the edge of a cliff if she asked me to." KritAt this point I was swooning. You can already guess that they get together at some point and holy hell....Krit got me all sorts of hot and bothered.Before you think the story is done....it's not. There have to be "bumps" as my book partner Emily calls them. One is fairly devastating. So I'm now going to tell you to get the book and read it. It is probably the best Abbi Glines novel to date. Oh and even though it's a stand alone, you know you're going to want to read the whole Sea Breeze series.Well I've talked too much as usual.  A resounding five lip smack review from me.  Read it! Let me know what you think!

My Review:Whoa, what an incredible erotic read. This very short novella is about an engaged couple, Nathan & Cait. Cait reads erotica featuring menage and Nathan really wants to fulfill this fantasy for her. The perfect opportunity arises when their mutual friend, Liam, comes to visit for the weekend before his assignment heading out to Afghanistan.Cait may be aroused by the idea, but she does NOT want them to have a menage. She worries about what it will do to their relationship. She feels shame at her arousal by Liam. She is worried that if they do this then Nate will view her differently and it will change their wonderful relationship. This book is so honest in what Cait is feeling. It just rang really true. The book is incredibly hot, but through it all you feel Cait's doubts and her incredible love for Nate.Nate & Liam are best friends and have shared women before, so he knows that if he can trust anyone with this woman that he loves, he can trust Liam. He also knows that Liam is attracted to her and honestly respects her. He is very conscious of the fact that Cait is uncomfortable with the idea, but he also knows her well enough to be able to tell that she is really turned on by the idea.Like I said the entire book has a really honest feel about it. Menage is one of those fantasy things and most books treat it like that without the reality of the doubts that can come from it. This book touches on all those doubts, but still manages to keep the entire feel incredibly sexy and arousing. Callie Croix knows how to write some seriously sexy scenes...whoa!! I really liked the way that she handled it at the end for Nate. Like I said, it has a true feeling to the story that you can't help but love! Gorgeous writing. I plan to check out more by this author!

reviewText: Still a bit shell shocked from this crazy, roller-coaster of a book.  There is an intensity in Eve Davids writing that keeps your heart rate up as you dig into the characters and story she created. I must admit that my first reaction was train wreck and it may still end up that way. Rene is the self-possessed man that gets whatever he wants and everyone knows not to mess with him. He suddenly sees Eve and she is what he wants but Eve isn't that easy. Factor in Bash, Eve's boyfriend, who throws Eve at Rene but at the same time doesn't want her connected to Rene. It all evolves into one crazy puzzle that you are dying to know the solution to. Some readers may be frustrated by all the character development but this is a series and Eve Davids does a great job giving you the back story in part 1 which I believe will lead to all the pieces evolving in the subsequent parts. This for me, was one of those books you are drawn to open out of curiousity, not intending to actually settle into, only soon you find you have done just exactly that.  The cover is beautiful and mysterious, it was calling out to me.  I just meant to take a quick peek...You open up to the first page - a super short half page PREFACE, which is ingeniously used as "bait and catch".  I read alot of books and I have never seen this done before - if I have, I've never seen it done this effectively.  Read the PREFACE, turn to page one, and then try to tell me you are not gonna stick around! Even if I were not interested in the story, I have NEVER experienced a better beginning that I can recall - so just that deserves a little more of my complete attention.In the beginning pages you witness a bunch of ladies in the break room at work talkin' entertainment gossip; dropping familiar actor and movie names all over the place.  Who doesn't love celebrity gossip?  The book is off to a PERFECT start...now, does it keep you reeled in?  Absolutely, YES!I connected to the main character immediately, and I think in different ways, all of us can.  She's in a rut, just livin' life the only way she knows how - when she gets hit with a crazy new neighbor, David.  David is off-putting and odd, yet somehow...you LIKE him.  Maddie doesn't see him quite that way just yet.  She gets forced into spending some time with David and little by little, the intrigue begins.  With the presence of David next door, Maddie's life begins to very slowly open up around her.  A man who seems so plain and simple and flawed has this incredible magnetism and Maddie is drawn to him.Ya gotta read the rest to find out the best stuff for yourself.  It's a fantastic book!I am an American reader, so having this set in the UK gave it a little bit of wonder for me.  It may be a humdrum life, but being set someplace unfamiliar turns the humdrum into something new and special. Everything from language to how they watch the Oscars in Britain with the time difference.I was lucky to run into this as a kindle freebie, but had I paid for this book, I would NOT have felt at ALL jipped!  Very entertaining, characters u will love, a sampling of London life - and if grammar and spelling errors matter to you - this is pretty darn well edited, too.  Not perfect, possibly less perfect than I know what with the British spelling and use of language; but I didn't feel there was anything significant enough to distract from the flow of the read.

reviewText: I quite enjoyed this lighthearted romance.Three Days With Molly is a romantic story about Molly, a cynical secretary working for a divorce lawyer, who takes an enforced break from the sad duties of settling other people's failed relationships. A childhood friend finds her a temporary job working as Finn Riley's personal assistant. Finn is a well-known country music star who is just starting a new tour. He needs a personal cook who is also willing to wash his clothes and bedding, and to follow his orders.After meeting Finn, the H.B., "heartless bastard", Molly has her doubts that this job, temporary as it may be, will work out. And unfortunately, Finn feels the same way about his clumsy new employee... so why can't they keep their hands off each other?Well known for her witty, humorous stories, Jan Romes once again wields her sharp wit in this entertaining romance.

reviewText: I'm just beginning to take the Kindle opportunity seriously, so I checked this book out.Although JA Konrath's name is listed first, this is Scott Nicholson's book (Konrath and the others all contributed an article).I respect Nicholson enormously as a writer, and applaud him for achieving the time freedom he desires. However, as a former hippie myself, I think you should take his view on money with a big grain of salt. He's the type satisfied with making just enough of it to get by, and mentions the figure of $3,000 per month. He also refers to Eisler turning down a $500,000 offer from a traditional publisher by saying that's enough money to last a sensible family forever.My family is not sensible, and demands a lot more, so I suggest reading Konrath and Eisler's Be the Monkey as Well, to get a broader horizon. Neither you nor I may ever catch up to those guys, but I think we should try.With that caveat, this book is recommended for the info you can use to help your Kindle career.

FAITH HOPE AND LOVE starts out well. Rachel Carstairs, a relief worker, has traveled from her third-world post to California to fight for custody of her dead cousin's son. Her opponent, Luke Summers, is the child's paternal uncle. The initial court room scene has a lot of tension and sizzle as both Rachel and Luke size one another up. Neither is quite the monster that the other expected. Luke, being wealthy and settled, wins the case hands down. But his curiosity about Rachel and her motives leads him to seek her out at her motel. He finds her ill with exhaustion and takes her to stay at his luxurious ranch.Here's where the story should have really taken off. Luke is a standard alpha male. He's attracted to Rachel and does everything he can to engineer her extended stay and convince her to take an interest in him.But Rachel just won't engage. She's secretive and evasive and off-putting. Kakade explains this as her character's way of protecting herself from the pain of leaving the baby and Luke to return to her relief work. Rachel's father, an unloving man, saddled her with serious self-esteem issues. Despite Luke virtually throwing his heart and his fortune at her feet, she can't believe anyone could really want her. Problem is that instead of arousing our sympathy, this emotional complication seems thin and artificial. I guess what it comes down to is that there IS NO complication. No real reason for this couple not to come together. Which means that when they do, it's rushed and then completely deflated by an epilogue that covers several decades of Rachel and Luke's family life.Kakade had the makings of a nice romance here, but she just didn't carry it off.

reviewText: Christine Nolfi made me an instant fan of her writing with her 2011 debut, Treasure Me, and I continue to look forward to her books with anticipation. Her fourth release, The Dream You Make, is the story of Annie McDaniel, a determined woman trying to stay positive in the face of troubling situations. Annie's family life has been no walk in the park: her mother gone too soon, her father recently deceased, and her sister Toria a victim of a tragic crime. In the midst of her loss, Annie has been made the beneficiary of two most unexpected treasures: Green Interiors, the greenhouse that was her father's life work - and Dillon, Toria's five year-old son. Annie falls head-over-heels for Dillon as she gets to know him for the first time, but she'll have to fight a draining custody battle against a well-off couple from Dillon's past before she can truly call him her own. In her efforts to keep Dillon, Annie takes on a second job at Rowe Marketing where she finds an entirely new complication in the attractive and stubborn Michael Rowe. If she pursues her attraction to her new boss it could hinder her chances of adopting Dillon, but Michael could also prove to be a sound and stable port in the storm of her life.The Dream You Make is a honeyed combination of love, humor and real-world poignancy that fills the reader with the butterfly-inducing beauty of life. Those of us who've been reading Nolfi's books from the beginning feel an unspoken guarantee that we'll find a world of charm, humor and joy between the pages and this novel follows through on that promise solidly. Books don't often grab me from the literal beginning, the very first scene, but The Dream You Make felt familiar and comfortable as soon as I fell into its world. The story deals with adoption, a topic Nolfi exposed deep passion for and talent with in her second book, The Tree of Everlasting Knowledge, and she handles it here with the same very real finesse, but with less heaviness. It keeps the novel feeling light and makes it a great counterpart to Tree, showing the same expanse of Nolfi's talent for writing about the heart of family in an entirely different way.Another of the novel's great accomplishments is the lively cast of characters; Nolfi is a definite master at crafting a host of memorable characters to color the reader's world, and she exercises that ability very well in The Dream You Make. Some, like the adorable Dillon, are studies in sensitivity and hope. An altogether shattered boy, seeing him come to life under Annie's guardianship - and in his interactions with best friend Chip and kindly neighbor Mariam - is perfectly heartwarming. Other characters, such as Rowe Marketing's flamboyant and temperamental artist Terence, are a canvas for hilarity and theatrics. Annie and Michael, the grown-up portion of the novel's primary focus, have an instant chemistry that captured my interest from the beginning. Their faults - one's inability to open up, another's hot impatience - set them on a long journey toward ironing out their budding romance, but their utterly human imperfections kept me rooting for them.This novel felt more simplistic in story than Nolfi's previous works, which have included books that interweave dark tragedy, cozy mystery, and treasure hunts woven through American history. All the same, there was nothing lacking in this story. Nolfi's books have a way of evading definition; she writes so broadly across the genres that her books have created a niche all their own, and The Dream You Make fits in perfectly. It's a life-affirming story that bursts with hope and dares the reader to relentlessly pursue their own dreams.(Review  Casee Marie, originally published on June 26, 2013 at LiteraryInklings.com. I received a copy of the book for the purpose of review.)
summary: A life-affirming story that bursts with hope

reviewText: With the blurb doing such a great job of laying out the basics of HUNTER'S MOON let me skip resummarizing it and jump into why I loved it.Kessler has quickly become an "auto-buy" author for me. Not only does she have an exceptional talent for taking paranormal romance staples and giving them great new elements that rock, she has an amazing gift for voice. I don't care for first-person alternating perspectives much, and especially not in romances, but she managed to really make it work. I'd dare go so far as to say that I felt much more invested in Aren and Sasha's relationship getting their story right from them. If you tend to read both Urban Fantasy and Paranormal Romance Kessler is an author you should be paying attention to.Action-packed and intense, HUNTER'S MOON delivers everything I love in a good read. As a fated-mates hater I love that while the werewolves find their one mate, jaguars don't in this series. It adds an excellent drama that makes Aren and Sasha's feelings for one another so much more enjoyable. I love that they even talk about whether his feelings would be the same if he wasn't forced to love her by his animal instincts. Meanwhile, the villainous figure after Sasha and her sister keeps them from getting too comfortable.If you enjoyed MOONLIGHT you're going to dig the new information on Nero and even some new stuff about the Sloan family. By the time the central action ends the world has opened and twisted and will leave you anxious for the next book. The romance itself ties up in a fashion I found pretty amusing (and those of you who have some knowledge of Kessler's interests will love it) and sweet in a theatrical kind of way.Sasha and Aren are one of my favorite romance couplings to date, the only problem I found with the story was the hang up she had that prolonged the inevitable HEA. I just wanted to give Sasha a nudge in the side with my elbow and say, "come on... seriously?". Once she gets her head on straight though it makes for an excellent ending.If you love shifter romances and heroines who don't really need rescuing, just a partner to have their back you simply must read HUNTER'S MOON.Notes: ARC received via publisher.

Justice Healed (Cowboy Justice Association Book 2) by Olivia JaymesOlivia Jaymes was a new author for me, the subject matter looked like it would have the elements of a good read, and thee-book was free. What more could I ask for at this point?Justice Healed, turned out to be a fun, playful, true to life themed story, with a bit of suspense, and a fair bit of action. The plot was simple but well written, with additional side threads to add complexity and dimension to the story, as well as expanding on the lives and roles of the 5 other cowboys /officers.The romance was tender and sweet, growing from smoldering to hot. It was nice to read a book where both the H/h were well out of their twenties, educated, employed, and not perfect. The sex scenes were tasteful, and complementary to the story line, never becoming the focus of the books plot. I enjoyed the playfulness, locations and sexual attitudes of Tanner and Madison, I felt like they actually enjoyed being with each other, and finding ways to bring further enjoyment to each other.The dialogue and reactions of the characters was realistic, the action scenes filled with tension, and the chemistry between Tanner and Madison strong. I have to complement the author on leaving no portions of the plot dangling or left unresolved, there is no cliffhanger - in fact this book can be read as a standalone, even though the 6 main cowboys/officers will each have their own books, and I suspect cameos by characters we have already meet.I enjoyed the ease of reading, characters, the town, and the overall premise of the series and suspect that I will be back for a visit as the other books in the series are published.

reviewText: My rating for the story is in the context of it's genre, namely 'paranormal romance'-- it's a story that is expected to be a romance at heart, with a happily-ever-after in a world with paranormal elements.I have read the previous stories in the series and I have enjoyed the basic premise--a coyote shapeshifting community as the setting, with plenty of hot steam and devoted, monogamous pairs (at least once they find out they are mates!).  The background for the world-view is touched upon in enough detail to understand it without trying to give a hard-science type explanation.  Part of the story is just accepting it as is and getting on with the reading.The other entries in the series are:Coyote HomeCoyote WildandCoyote Run<<---this one is a prequel to Coyote Home, setting some of the history for the first book.I liked the first two reads, and the third one which was not quite a stand alone as it was more like a slice-of-life (under 500 Kindle locations) and benefited from the knowledge of subsequent events.I had hoped Coyote Whispers would be more like the first two in terms of it's ability to function as a stand alone, but it unfortunately this was just not the case.  It has been long enough since Coyote Wild that several details were a little more difficult to recall and the story was written as though the memory was completely fresh.  I'm sure this could have been rectified by re-reading the others, but end result left me feeling like there were big holes in the story line.I also felt as though the villain was reduced to being no more than a paper cut-out bad guy.  Again, referencing events of the prior stories more perhaps would have helped, but at no point did you ever get in the bad guy's head or have more than a passing idea as to why he chose to do the things he did and to whom.Perhaps reading these sequentially/immediately together would have helped but time has passed between the publications and it was just a bit much to pull back the details of the rest of the series, if in fact the details to help this story were really there.  I did read the first two together, and like I said I enjoyed them and don't remember thinking there were plotting issues.In terms of who the intended audience is, well this is DEFINITELY a book geared towards an audience looking for explicit nookie between a man/woman without kink.  It is a lot of nookie--to the point where at times I was feeling like 'please just get on with the story' only the story didn't quite get on.  I think adding about 25% more story to complete the details would have made this a 4.5 star read.I do plan to read whatever title comes next...and I recommend the series in total if you are looking for the 'paranormal porn' type read.  I would read them in close time proximity however, and the next book I will go back and re-read everything first (the first three will add up to a regular length novel in terms of Kindle locations and this one is the longest at 3272 locations).JTG

reviewText: Yes, it could benefit from some editing - that's why the 5th star is missing.It's not realistic, but then it's not supposed to be.  It's called fiction for a reason, and I don't understand why so many reviewers seem hung up on the facts that he's 30 and dreams of being a pro football player, and he can't "get over" his mother's murder of 20 years before.  There are some things that stay with us for life.  He spent years expecting and being expected to play pro football.  An injury took that dream away, but 30 isn't 60, and why shouldn't he go for it? Also, if you've ever lost a parent, you know it's a pain that you never "get over".  It's something that haunts you for the rest of your life. Some pretty harsh reviewers on this page!Jim's a bit cocky, but it's in the way of someone who's insecure and posturing so people don't realize how insecure he really is.  I found his character believable in most ways.  The disregard for danger and nonchalance regarding the hit man after him was taking the arrogance a bit far, I have to admit. I also thought he was needlessly violent at times.  For instance, the wife beater could have been sent to jail rather than having his butt kicked.The language didn't bother me in the least. This is a book for adults, not children or YA, so why the outrage over language? I don't blame the author for having fairly realistic dialogue. In fact, I found the dialogue refreshing after reading so many robotic/stilted conversations in kindle books lately.God in McDonald's was hilarious!  I'm an atheist, and even I loved those mysterious, often prophetic chats.  What a great, creative touch! Without those talks, it would be virtually indistinguishable from many other PI action novels.  Kudos to Mr. Rain for originality!Not many characters were realistic.  Mostly, they seemed like parodies of stereotypes.  The nosy yet dignified lady gardening and offering iced tea, pretending to be put off about the murder but secretly enjoying the attention.  The black kid from an all-white school who tries to speak like a tough guy to hide his fear.  The uppity lawyer, Charlie Brown, was fantastic. The hit man was very outlandish, a great parody of white trash criminals. The cold, calculating villain. I could go on but there's no point.  Maybe some of the readers just didn't get it.  I didn't find it shallow at all.  It had all the classic types of characters we love and love to hate.With some editing, I would recommend this book to any adult who wants something light-hearted and whimsical to distract them from reality for an afternoon.

reviewText: And so the crazy love affair of Bo and November continues.In just a short time...ten days...the world of these two characters is transformed into the best love anyone can imagine, but trust and fear are two things that take their world and turn it upside down...and love may not be enough.Never in my wildest dreams would I have thought this story would take the path it did. There were quite a few times I found myself...mouth open...gasping  in shock, and wondering what the hell was November thinking as she made certain decisions. It was a long, troubled road but through it all I was pleased with the results.When this book begins we pick up with November pushing away from her happiness and running away from her fears. November grew as an individual and found her way in life. She made choices thinking they were what were best, but after living through a tough five months she realized she needed to go back and be true to herself.Bo has a lot to fight for and is willing to be strong and wait it out until the time is right. He has a business he wills to succeed and a lost love he dreams to restore.Loved this story and anxious to read more!!

reviewText: "Seal of the King" is a thrilling fantasy that brims with action, romance, and a deeper moral message. Ralph Smith uses the realm of fantasy to evoke the values of a simpler time in an exciting and imaginative tale.This book contains all of the freedom of expression, symbolism, and world building that we have come to expect from a good fantasy novel. reviewText: A BEAUTIFUL MESSWOW...is about the only word I can muster after reading "A Beautiful Mess." The title is very fitting because I'm a complete and utter MESS and still reeling from this book hangover!From the beginning, these complex characters completely drew me in. I was on edge, jittery and wanted to bite my fingernails off in complete anticipation of where the story was headed. It definitely kept me on my toes and was not the typical romance novel that I'm used to - the suspense was going to be the death of me. I connected and felt every emotion the characters were feeling - the happiness, anger, hurt and sadness! AND...that's when you know you've picked up a damn good book, when you've completely lost yourself in all the story.I truly appreciated the character build-up and how T.K. allowed Alexander and Olivia to date, experience the butterflies and get to know each other, rather than the typical "insta-love" that we're all used to, where the characters are declaring their love for one another and jumping in the sack immediately after meeting each other. (That totally irritates me and I constantly roll my eyes at that complete B.S. because it's just not realistic). However, when they did decide to finally become intimate, HOLY CRAP it was HOT!! From talking dirty, the dirty texts, when Alexander went to Libby's office and of course their first time having sex after they made up from their major fight!! Uhmm...Mr. Burnham can blindfold me and tie me up any day!I LOVED A Beautiful Mess!! Great plot, character development, edgy, and the suspense is to die for! Great job by T.K. Leigh for extracting and evoking every emotion in me!!! I couldn't wait for A Tragic Wreck!!A TRAGIC WRECKThis book definitely deserves way more than 5 stars!! "A Tragic Wreck" was utterly riveting, mind blowing and beyond remarkable.First and foremost, I would like to forewarn you to have a box of Kleenex handy, as you will definitely need it (maybe another box, depending on your emotional stability...I wasn't stable at all and it seemed like I was ugly crying the entire book! LOL)I loved Alex and Olivia with all my heart and soul, but throughout the book, there were parts where they both made me so angry I wanted to smack the hell out of both of them - oh my goodness, they were so frustrating!! You can't even fathom the amount of drama and suspense that builds up throughout the book, it'll keep your heart racing, so make sure you take blood pressure meds (if needed)."Promise me you'll always remember me, walking out on you, then coming back here and losing you all over again has been painful enough. But as long as it wasn't for nothing, as long as it meant something, then maybe I can move on like you have." - Olivia"I want you every second of every day. I want the good. I want the bad. I want the sweet. I want the ill-tempered. I want the hot. I want the cold. I want the crazy, irrational, exasperating pain-in-the-ass girl that I love with my entire f'n heart."- AlexT.K. introduced Cam in this book and although I'm Team Alex all the way, you can't help but have love for Cam, as he was so sweet, understanding and nurtured crazy ass Olivia and practically saved her life. Kiera and Mo are as supportive to Olivia as ever and they actually have a little romance of their own blossoming. Adele is back and I wanna bitch slap her more than ever, but there are also other characters in the book you will definitely love to hate and will make you wanna "cut a bitch."I hope you're ready for a wild ride because it's going to be a bumpy, emotional roller coaster ride on the Alexander and Olivia express. The emotional intensity of these two characters were so powerful, you can't help but feel their struggle, sadness, disappointment, passion, anger and happiness - it was like a vortex that completely sucked you in, you felt it all! I was so wrapped up in their relationship and I completely immersed myself in it, needless to say, I was emotionally spent after reading the book.GORGEOUS CHAOSIt took me quite some time to finally put my feelings about this book into words, as I just didn’t know how and where to begin and frankly, I didn’t want to acknowledge that this was the end of an outstanding series. To say that T.K. Leigh did a phenomenal job at concluding Alexander and Olivia’s story would be an understatement. Her exquisite writing truly pulls you in; you feel such an emotional connection to the characters and you just can’t fathom the thought of saying good-bye to characters you’ve grown to LOVE.With every book in the series, you grow a stronger connection to both Alexander and Olivia and although these two will frustrate the hell out of you, you begin to understand why they do the crazy sh-tuff that they do, and although you may not agree with some of their actions/decisions, I believe that it was paramount for T.K. to have them take the path they’ve taken, in order to develop and solidify their characters.The Alexander and Olivia saga will definitely make you feel like you’re caught in an inescapable rip-tide that you won’t want to be rescued from. They take you on a powerful, emotional journey filled with heartache, courage, hope and love that will leave your heart pounding and gasping for air.“With everything going on, he was her constant…the one person she could depend on. The one person who had loved her throughout her entire life.”“I can’t survive without you, Olivia. You’re my heart, and I’ll die without you.”“Tears fell from his eyes as he buried his head against Olivi’s still body, not wanting to come to terms with the idea of losing her all over again.” “Please…Don’t leave me…”Gorgeous Chaos is without a doubt, the most intense book in the series. ALL the mysteries and unanswered questions established in “A Beautiful Mess” and “A Tragic Wreck” will definitely be revealed. Have several boxes of Kleenex handy because it’s definitely not going to be a walk in the park. The plot is certainly raw and gritty, and the suspense is incredibly palpable. Let’s just say, Gorgeous Chaos will smack you with the most jaw dropping, shocking revelation that will completely blow your mind!THANK YOU to T.K. Leigh for sharing her wonderful masterpiece and allowing us to fall in-love with Alexander and Olivia. I’m utterly torn and heartbroken that we have to say good-bye, but I’m certainly looking forward to more of T.K.’s work and especially that sexy surfer Cam! Alexander and Olivia will always have a special place in my heart.

The Collide series was the first series that I started to read by Ms. Crane (before I found Significance) and I was sad to find out that this was the last book in the series.Ms. Crane has a way of bringing her characters to life, they jump off the page and the reader actually feels as though that they know them personally, you can not help but become engrossed in their lives (at least a real avid reader).  Someone who reads all the time, know the difference between just liking a character and actually feeling like they know them and Ms. Crane has a way with writing that makes the characters feel like your friends.  You get mad at the enemy for messing with your friends!!!!Again I laughed and I cried while reading this book.  I hurt when I had to say good bye to my "friends".Although there was heart ache and pain, I was glad that there was still a happy ending.  I could have  reached into the book and hugged Sherry I was so happy for her.I have one more series to read by Ms. Crane, and I hope she starts on another one while I am reading her other series, I can't seem to get enough of her....

I implore you don't make my mistake - Read this book & savor the experience . Happy Reading!!F.Y.I -I don't know this author nor have I ever been approached to write this review or any other. I'm just someone addicted to reading and who have no issues in expressing heartfelt thanks and encouragement to others, who seek to un-wind after a long day with a beautifully crafted storyline that keeps one so engaged in the lives of fictional characters it's an escape from the general hustle and bustle of our everyday reality!

reviewText: The story takes place in Cardiff, England (although I have never been to Cardiff I love it when books are based in my home country!) Despite the annoying format problem I had with this, it was an easy read. The story flowed and it had a good pace.Tales of a vampire falling in love with the mortal have been told countless time, but I haven't tired of them... yet. Besides, there are a few twists in Judgement of Souls, making it different from the regular stories. Firstly, the vampire in this book is female, and the mortal is male, plus the vampire was once in love with the villain!Arun and Daniel's arguments made me smile, mainly because Arun wanted to kill Daniel in order to simplify things, and Daniel refused to leave Rachel. I can tell this is going to be a series because there is no way the book could end on that note. Plus, we need to find out why Daniel's grandfather hid the book and what other secrets does his family hide?Overall, an enjoyable read. A little gruesome at times but definitely worth it.Favourite Quotes:She would fly over to some European city and spot one without having to look too hard. You could see them on any street corner or alleyway, drug pushers, pimps, muggers. Who would miss this type of mortal? But part of her pitied her prey; the poor unfortunate whose only weakness was their frailty; perhaps that was what she craved the most."...When you've been alive as long as I have, you begin to get immune to the horror. Then one day you wake to find that you don't care anymore, you let them fight and you stay out of the way.""He's a nut job!" said Arun. "He freaked at high speed driving, but he loved flying through the air."Rachel interrupted. "I've had it with you two! You," she said, pointing at Arun. "He stays." Then, pointing at Daniel "And you, just follow and keep yourself tucked behind one of us. Right now I'm thinking I don't need either of you, so unless this bitching stops I'll do this myself!" She spun and hurried out of the Temple.
summary: A twist on the classic vampire loves mortal tale

reviewText: Why Melissa, Why? Why do I let you do this to my heart!!!!Wolf Pact Part 3 is the most captivating piece of the Wolf Pact novella to date! We return to Bliss and the wolves right after the attack. Bliss finally tells the wolves about her mother and how she was sent to find them and Arthur admits he knew the whole time. While Arthur vows to stall the hellhounds Bliss and the boys head of to find Tala. When they arrive at the hospital it is not Tala but another girl from the wolves past. With this new girl in tow they set off to find the rest of the wolves who have escaped the underworld. Will they find the wolves, or is this all an elaborate trap set by Romulus? Read Wolf Pact Part 4 to find out.Melissa did it again. She played with my heart and left me hanging without a goodnight kiss. This book was AMAZING. So yes, maybe I harbor a very deep obsession with this series but seriously, amazing. We start to see the characters all open up a little bit and we begin to see them work as a team. We are finally starting to see hope for the cause. With the addition of the new character we also see a new tension and possibly an evil plan in the works. I cannot wait for the final installment of this novella to come out. It will be epic, I know it. (Sorry this review is so short but if I keep writing I will totally give away some killer spoilers and that is just not cool, so read the book and we can gush about it later.)

I downloaded this book when it was free, I mean seriously with a front cover like that how could I not and I liked the blurb but there's just so many free books out there I didn't know if I'd ever actually get round to reading it. Anyway my kindle was getting too full so while removing some books I noticed this again and decided to give it a go, it's a slightly different read for me but after a few pages I was hooked, I started it last night and finished it this morning and I really enjoyed it.Sandy Guilianno is your normal hard working student, she works hard in class and out of it as well, she's law-abiding and well, good. Her brother Lou however has fallen in with the wrong crowd and she can see him slipping deeper and deeper. Lou's also dating her best friend Lisa and through these she meets Lou's partner in crime Romeo, now despite the fact that she suspects and disapproves of what Lou's doing, which by association is what Romeo's doing she can't stay away.Romeo is FBI and he has a job to do and nothing is going to stand in his way, he's worked too hard for anything to interfere but then he hadn't counted on Sandy.Like I said I really enjoyed this book, it had enough story to keep me interested, some good characters and of course a little romance because what would a book be without it.If I'm being totally honest I felt that more time should have been spent on Romeo and Sandy's relationship, I know the attraction was there from the first moment but I personally, being a romantic at heart, would have liked more.This is not the last we'll see of these characters since a sequel is being planned as well as several short spin-offs but all things considered this is really good first book by this author.

Traders have debated the merits of Technical and Fundamental analysis for years but most traders probably utilize a little of both methods in their trading strategies.  The key trading tools of technical analysis are basic chart patterns.  You don’t even need a computer as long as you have current price data but it makes analysis much easier and faster.  Continuation Chart patterns rely heavily on the rule of physics that a “Trend in motion tends to stay in motion.”  The Trend Line is the most powerful continuation pattern but other price movements also indicate that current trends will continue.  Continuation charts are especially helpful in determining what the current trend is likely to do.  I really appreciate how Wilson broke his book into two parts; Bullish Continuation and Bearish Continuation patterns so that readers could understand the characteristics of patterns that occur under different circumstances without getting confused.  He then gives a detailed explanation of the major patterns for each type of market.  Very well done!

This is easily one of the better if not the best treatments I have ever read involving psychics and crime investigation - and believe me I have read a lot of screenplays and books with this theme. It works here because author Linda Prather smartly downplays everything and makes proceedings as realistic as possible. Her detectives are highly attuned, highly intuitive individuals, rather than people just experiencing 'visions.' The plot is told through character interactions that are compelling - we care what happens because we like Catherine and want her to succeed. These feel like real people with emotional depth. This is the kind of book that gives you that lump in the throat feeling as you read. It's convincing, exciting and not at all predictable, which is exactly what I look for in a book like this. I'm off to read more by this interesting thriller author who I was not aware of before. Good stuff.
summary: Top Notch Writing. Very Suspenseful. Authentic Crime Novel.

reviewText: The novel is a follow up to Mr. Boyden's award winning novel "Three Days Road", recounting the histories and lives of two fictional James Bay Cree families (The Birds and the Whiskeyjacks).This latest novel centers on Will Bird, son of Xavier Bird, the heroic soldier we were introduced to previously. The story comes to live through two intertwined monologues. We follow Will's thoughts while he recovers from a serious plane crash, a near death encounter that has left him comatose in a hospital bed. Will is an engaging storyteller, a bush pilot by trade and a charming alcoholic by fate with many tales of adventure to tell, some a hoot and some distressful to hear. Alternate chapters are narrated by his niece Annie Bird while she sits in vigil by his bedside trying to stimulate him back to the living. She uses the time to recount her adventures in Toronto, Montreal and New York while in search of her lost sister Suzanne.These flashbacks create short stories in their lives, each one a glimpse into the desolate forests that surround James Bay and the all too similar affect the underground fashion world can have on someone not accustom to the rat race of the big cities. Each layer reveals secrets of violence, incompetence, kindness, love and compassion.The novel is hard to get into at first, the story launches quickly into two narratives, each one hard to decipher which character is talking and how the bits of information fit together. I gradually immersed myself into the tale and once settle, let the story run its course. I was drawn in by the vivid description of Canada's vast wilderness and its inhabitants who call it home, the Cree. It was an eye opener realizing the challenges and hardship native people face in big cities where there is a multitude of cultures all trying to survive. The characterization is powerful and the players come across as genuine and loveable. Although the pacing is very slow and the reading is tedious at times, in retrospect I enjoyed the refreshing and informative look into another way of life..

This book is very New Adult, not YA (Young Adult). Beware of that before reading.Alive is a story about Eve, a girl brought up in a strict almost cult like religious home, and what happens to her and the boy she loved, (and who broke her heart) Gage, after the zombie apocalypse hits.The story starts off four years after the zombies infect the world. We meet Eve right as she is ready to give up and stop fighting. She is saved by Gage. The boy she knew from her past that broke her heart. Her only love and she is still very bitter.Eve is determined to find her sister, Olive. Eve was the unwanted nuisance and Olive the golden child of the family. A lot of how Eve and Olive feel about themselves and how they react to others is based on this.The book switches points of view from Eve to Gage and eventually Olive. It’s confusing at first because it doesn’t go by chapter. They can switch from paragraph to paragraph. You have to read closely at times to know who’s POV it is. And there are grammatical errors, he instead of she, that can make it even trickier.I had just given into the fact that this is a book about two horny people in the apocalypse when the plot really started taking shape and drew me in. Once Olive’s character started chiming in I was hooked and had to know more.The story slips back and forth to the present and past so to explain why each person acts the way they do. I really enjoyed this part of the book. Each person evolved in an interesting manner.I think the lust in the book sort of overshadowed the great story line. It could have been toned down a bit and made more of an impact. But the plot was great and I am really interested to read the next one! What a cliff hanger!!!Only part that really bothered me was Gage’s obsession with Eve being “mine”. It made it sound like he was more interested in controlling her than being in love with her. Like he saw her as a possession and not a person. Plus, I kept thinking of the Disney bird, “mine, mine, mine”. LOL!Worth the read.

I was asked by the author to read this book in exchange for an honest review.Bright Star by Nickie Anderson is about Sadira, who watches her genius father, take off in a spaceship that then loses control and crashes. He is presumed dead. Sadira meets another young soldier whose brother was lost in the crash, and together, they realize there is more going on than meets the eye. These two journey across desert sand and harrowing dangers to try to find their loved ones as well as piece together a mystery that just seems to get more confusing as they learn more and more.I don't want to give away more than that, because finding out the book's secrets is part of the fun. I loved the world building-- I could taste the sand from the setting. Everything is so gritty and dry, and Anderson does a great job giving the prose that feel. Sadira is a great protagonist-- smart, resourceful, but yet scared-- a perfect combination of strong traits yet growth that needs to happen. My other favorite character has to be her nutty professor friend who helps her piece together the puzzle. The plot had plenty of twists and I was entertained from start to finish.I do wish there were a bit more world building in the sense of I'm not sure why the society is the way it is-- perhaps more will be revealed in the next installment as Sadira learns more. Also, I felt that one particular character became rather two dimensional-- but again, maybe we will learn more in the second book.Overall, a fast paced, imaginative dystopian with a winning protagonist. I'm eager to see what Anderson has up her sleeve!
summary: Entertaining and fast paced dystopian with a winning protagonist

reviewText: "Shattered Ink" is the second book in her new series, the "Wicked Ink Chronicles".  I was given this book by the author, Laura Wright, for an honest review and so I shall deliver.The Review:The book starts with Addison and Lisa(her best friend, who we met in "First Ink"(Read my Review Here) standing outside a party.  Lisa is dressed for a night of seduction, while Addison is dressed for a night in jail, wearing her orange sweatpants and t-shirt.  She's desperately missing Rush like a smoker misses cigarettes.Umm....who the hell wouldn't!!! It's RUSH!!!  Don't you remember the kitchen scene in "First Ink"??!!  If not...buy "First Ink", read it, then re-read "Shattered Ink". Okay, moving on...[BOOK QUOTE]"I'm just going to say one thing to you: Vegas."My insides go instantly hot and soft. It's a depressing feeling , but addicting and predictable. Kind of like my life has been over the past five weeks . When Rush and I chucked the past and decided to try this again, I was so happy. So excited. A second chance at a first love. But as Lisa put it, I'm losing it. In the past five weeks, I've only seen him three times, and for no more than a day or two. I have school and finals and graduation, and he has work and travel. It's like the most beautiful torture in the world, seeing him. I'm on a high when I'm around him. When he's gone, I crash. And I can't seem to bounce back. I'm utterly and completely addicted to him. I'm jealous of anything and anyone who gets to be near him, and there are actually times when I don't give a shit about graduating, about getting my marketing degree--about a job or a future. I just want to be in his atmosphere. I just want those eyes locked on mine, and those inked arms around me.Of course, I haven't told him any of this. I don't want him to think I'm a loser. I don't want him to know the truth. I don't want him to walk away from me-- or shit, run-- because this time, it's not just love that would be lost. It'd be my heart, my breath... my sanity.[/BOOK QUOTE]Well hey, if you're too scared, get the hell out of my way! I'll tell him!I love you Rush!!!!!Uuummm.....Ok, moving on yet again....Addison isn't the only one having those feelings.  Rush went years without her and now that he has her back in his life, he doesn't want to be without her for a second. So when he picks her up at the airport, he has full intention of asking her to move in with him. But they get a little sidetracked on the motorcycle ride back home.[BOOK QUOTE]"Addison." I hear the warning-laced call on the wind, but I'm barely registering it. I want him so badly I can't see straight.He groans as my fingers brush lightly over the top of his burgeoning erection. I want it. I want to slip my hand inside his jeans and make him as hard as the red rocks around us."Baby, I'm going to crash," he hollers back, his voice strained.I know . I hear him, and I know what he's saying is true . Shit, I know what I'm doing is totally freaking dangerous. But I don't care. I swear to god, I want him so bad I don't care if we crash.What the hell is wrong with me? And how can I make it stop?With a hard jerk to the right and a squeal of tires, Rush pulls off the road. I curl into him, holding on tight as he speeds into the desert, hauling ass until he spots a large palo verde tree about quarter mile out. He guns for it , and once there, jerks the bike to the right, then brings it to an abrupt, dust-clouded stop before killing the engine. He's off the thing in two seconds. Has me on my feet in one. And rips off my helmet with a curse and look so fierce, I shiver and erupt into flames."That wasn't very smart, Ads," he says, unbuttoning the top of his jeans.[/BOOK QUOTE]Huh? What?  Oh yeah...I'm supposed to tell you what I thought of this book...right. Gotcha.This book is flippin' amazing and lives up to the yummy goodness of the first one.  There might not have been the kitchen scene...but the scene when they finally get home? Holy sheep! Have your lover or fire extinguisher handy!!!But there was more then just sex in this book...there was love making, exposing fears we all have, relationship issues we all have had and the struggle of learning what path should be taken to get past it all. It was sexy and sweet. The absolute PERFECT recipe.So, if Addison and Rush have been the stars of the first two books, will they be the stars of the third??  NO! And Laura Wright makes darn sure we're craving Vincent and Lisa's story at the end!!  Can't wait for "Rebel Ink" to come out!!!  2014, people...be watching for it!!!~Robin(bookreadsandreviews.com)
summary: This book is AMAZING and lives up to the yummy goodness of the first one.

Essentialism is the third book in the Life.Destiny.Love series by LK Collins, and could be read as a stand alone, however I read books 1 - 3 back to back to get the whole story (Book 1 Fatalism; Book 2 Determinism).Bridgette and Troy first meet when he helps her move house. There is that instant spark between the two of them, that can't help but ignite into something more.Troy is FINE!! Sexy firefighter, who seems to have bit of a hero complex - not that that is a bad thing, but can get him into trouble!Bridgette is just starting out in her life and career. When she meets Troy, things definitely start to change for the better. Things start out truly platonic ~~ texting, innocent (or is it) flirting. But both realise things are never going to stay in the "friend zone" and things progress to the next levelBut secrets and lies (or lies by omission) tear them apart. They both have things in their past that are still causing troubles to this day.Add to the mix a psycho ex hell bent on keeping their partner, and we are taken on one hell of a ride.Can their feelings and attraction to each other be enough to get them their HEA?Uh uh, for that you are going to have to read for yourself.I really did love Bridge and Troy, both together and apart. They are both smart mouthed, funny, sexy. Love their text messaging, and when they do get together.. HOT HOT HOT!!! I mean tie me up, tie me down, burn up the sheets smokin hot!!I love that we get more of the characters from the first two book, Vincent and Alexa, Abel and Cara. This is such a tight knit group of family and friends and their lives interweave so much that it would not have felt right if we didn't get more of them.Probably the only thing that annoyed me about this book. Too much sex. I know, you are shocked, right? I love a steamy, sexy book as much as the next person, but I felt that in the case of Essentialism, it was a little bit too much. I felt like I was coming down with a case of "proximity honeymoon cystitis" and poor Bridgette would have been constantly walking bow legged!! But this could just be me!I have thoroughly enjoyed the Life. Destiny. Love series so far, and can't wait to get into the next couple of books!

PRINCE OF SHADOWS has lots of potential, but for me, the execution fell flat.With Kendra's hand came the crown, and she has to choose wisely among the unmated princes the one who would be worthy of her. In truth, she is stalling for time until her cousins can come rescue her...The opening drew me right into the story, and I felt empathy for the little boy that Cale was, and I couldn't help but want to know more about what would happen next. The grown-up Cale was an attractive, all-hard body Alpha male, with controlled restraint and seething frustration beneath the surface. All he has endured, all he has sacrificed is culminating soon in the reward that he hoped would soon be his. But about a third of the way in, everything unravelled for me.First of all, I have to say Cale's characterization was great. Despite the in-fighting within their ranks, Cale taught his younger brothers how to fight, to give them a chance for survival. In their competition for Kendra's hand, he even gave one of them a tip. I thought that was big of him and spoke of his innate humanity. And the things he endured... Maybe because he was the runt of the litter, he had to do more, to train more, to be more, in order to even have a chance to win over his brothers. It spoke of an admirable tenacity not to let his "defects" be an excuse for failure. I was absolutely rooting for Cale all the way.Now, Kendra somehow became the "prize" for the unmated princes. Whoever won her would also win the crown. Fine, I accepted it at face value initially, but as I read on, I begin to wonder: What made her so special? Why give her the choice at all? It could be argued that her father was well-loved by the clan, but her father was gone and she herself didn't have any allies among their people. What can she bring to the marriage? Nothing, as far as I could see (this is not counting her connections to the MacCreedy and their alliances, which I'm sure wasn't taken into account by the king at that point anyway). So, why didn't the king just decree for her to marry one of his sons? Since he's such a tyrant, that would be more in keeping with his character.Hence, Kendra didn't make sense to me. Moreover, I don't see what Cale could've seen in her to love her that much. All he had was a childhood "love" that magically became a grown-up "love" now that they were older. People change as they grow, and considering they didn't spend time with each other for eighteen years, and they didn't really talk much now, I had a hard time believing in their "love".I'm not sure if I missed things--significant things--because I picked up this book in the middle of the series. Certainly, there were references to past events (specifically, Cale's past altercation with Kendra's cousin Silas, and Kendra's family's situation) that would've been clearer if I'd read about them.That said, the world building was great, with a shifter world fully realized and integrated into the human community. The pace of the story was just right, but the dialogue between Cale and Kendra could've been better. As this is book 8 in the series, new readers should probably not start here.Reviewed by Ashiafor TheRomanceReviews.com

"Xenophobia" has an intriguing premise that I was drawn to. I found it a bit of a difficult and slow read in the beginning and middle. Too much time was dedicated to political socioeconomic conditions in Africa and too much detail put into the "pre-story".  One could assume the author was working toward deep character development as well as a supporting basis for the "anti-war" / "conservation" message. Ultimately I didn't really need the detail. I would have been happier if this book was 50-60 pages shorter. I was shocked to read in the authors notes that a friend had convinced him to reduce the size of the book by 25,000 words. I can only imagine the amount of unnecessary detail that was removed, from the length and color of the Rangers shoelaces, to the species of flies surrounding the field hospital patients heads.All of that being said, the author CAN write, and the story was promising enough that I kept reading. The last third of the book was excellent, perfectly paced, and entirely original in approach. I thoroughly enjoyed it and had problems putting it down. If the first two-thirds of the book was shorter and better paced this would be a five star review...but hey, I'm just one guy...read and decide for yourself.  You'll enjoy the premise and the story...promise...
summary: An enjoyable, if not an overly long read

Daniel Raynes - we should hear more about this writer as he has shared writing tips to create a successful book as well as anyone who has addressed this subject. Hopefully one of his own novels will appear soon. Raynes is a young, handsome lad born in Baltimore, Maryland.  His own writing to date has resulted in multiple awards and helped earn a scholarship to Washington College in Chestertown, Maryland where he studied poetry, short stories, plays, screenplays, and novels. Apparently screenplays are his forte but writing novels is his passion. This excellent book feels very much like a deep breath on his part to open the door to writing serious novels again.Not only is this book bound to become a bible for writers of all stages of their careers, it is a very accessible seminar on writing. As he states in his opening remarks, `By using many examples from great authors and looking at what their prose is supposed to achieve within their story, I aim to show you how and why they did it, and hopefully their success can help you as well. I have chosen select passages from classic novels to illustrate their techniques, and I will compliment the published examples with some of my own, which I created just to highlight and expand upon the lessons.'What follows is a step by step approach to offering advice on how to avoid pitfalls, overcome tendencies that may indicate failure, and in general how to go about writing  - from the beginning idea to the finished product. It seems his flow is best defined by simply outlining the names of his chapters with a few excerpts dotting the landscape:Chapter 1 Getting Started, Chapter 2 The Importance of Writing Quickly, Chapter 3 Writing in Layers, Chapter 4 How to Develop a Style (The way an author expresses their story, with word choice, grammar, sentence structure, and how they use many types of literary devices.), Chapter 5 How to Find Your Voice (The culmination of style, tone, themes, and morals that the author presents in a work of fiction.), Chapter 6 Writing a Setting, Chapter 7 Writing Action (In many ways the mood of the action is more important than the action itself.), Chapter 8 Writing Description, Chapter 9 Writing Dialogue (All the poetic prose in the world isn't going to cover up a lousy story.), Chapter 10 Dialogue or Description? (In the end, people are all people, and the differences are subtle at best.), Chapter 11 Writing Emotional Prose (You can break the rules whenever you feel you need to. Whenever you feel your story needs it. Break the rules while keeping your prose readable and don't apologize for it.), Chapter 12 Writing to an Audience (Something has to happen early in the story to get the reader to commit to finishing the novel.), Chapter 13 Doing Research, Chapter 14 To Prewrite or Not to Prewrite?, Chapter 15 The Importance of Murphy's Law (They don't want crisis averted. They want crisis overcome.), Chapter 16 Choosing Your Narrator, Chapter 17 Pacing a Story, Chapter 18 Writing an Ending, Chapter 19 Read with Your Ears!, Chapter 20 Genre Novels vs. Literary Novels, Chapter 21 Where Ideas Come From, Chapter 22 Should You Write What You Know?, Chapter 23 Writing Other Formats As Well, Chapter 24 Writing and Videogames, Chapter 25 Writing Classes and Groups, Chapter 26 Why We Write, Chapter 27 Breaking Through Writer's Block, Chapter 28 General Writing Tips, and Chapter 29 Final Thoughts.This is considerable information well related and the aspect that helps the `student' buy into Raynes' flow of ideas is his personalization and his very wise reference examples from the great authors of our time and the past. This is an excellent book that may just help writing dreams be realized!Grady Harp, June 14
summary: `I hope this book carries the torch.'

This was a heartbreaking yet triumphant story, all rolled up into one. Dealing with some heavy issues that unfortunately happen in today’s society with teens, you get a glimpse into the life of one particular girl, and the struggles she goes through on a daily basis.Zar is a senior in high school, who’s been keeping some major secrets from her family, because she’s felt somewhat like the black sheep for years now. She feels if she talks to them about what’s been going on with her, they’d somehow look at her differently, and that’s something she doesn’t want.She’s been a loner for so long, she doesn’t quite know how to react when she goes into a pizzeria one day, and spots a guy she has an instant attraction to. It’s such a change of behavior for her, she feels overwhelmed. After that first “meeting”, she can’t get him out of her mind, and it so happens the feeling is mutual. The guy turns out to be her brother’s fiancé’s younger brother, Loudon.Zar and Loudon become instantly attached, and Loudon finds out there’s a lot more to her than she shares with anyone. He wants to know her secrets and help her anyway he can, but she’s scared to let him in. I love the fact that he cares about her so much, and has the “won’t give up on you” attitude; it’s super sweet!She finally realizes that there are people that truly care for her, and she slowly opens up to them.
