Her descriptions can be so realistic at time, that you will find yourself feeling the characters pain or getting goose bumps(seriously). The downfall of the story is I didn't like the way it ended. I wanted more. Don't just leave me wanting more. The author endings are NEVER predictable.

This book is perfect for any new investors looking for a simple yet effective investment strategy. All of the info provided in this book is laid out in a way that is simple to understand even if you are a complete newbie to finance and investments. It describes what all of the terms mean so that it is impossible to get lost. Do not be fooled by its relatively small size, this book is jam packed with various helpful info.I highly recommend checking out this book to anyone who is just getting into investing and is looking for a comprehensible strategy.

About a year ago, I read this author's "Glimmer" Trilogy and really enjoyed it. Hundreds of e books later, those characters and story have stuck with me.  When this book popped up available for a free Amazon download, I jumped at the chance to give it a try. Boy am I happy I did!  This book was so well written and addressed a subject I've not yet to see dealt with in a YA novel.  When I bounced to the author's facebook page I noticed her banner said that she is a misfit writing about misfits for misfits. Well, Amen to that!  I am a proud misfit and always have been.  In my younger days I had self esteem issues such as the ones that inhabit the soul of the protagonist, Dani. She was very relatable for me.  Liam is the perfect young man for her and that becomes more evident as the plot unfolds.  Dani is an exuberant, intelligent, open minded, young woman and she is able to embrace diversity. Her best friend in high school was gay and she enjoys a romp in the local, college town, bar that features drag performers. Liam, straight, works there, so we know going in that he is open minded as well. He is very lucky to find his soul mate in Dani.  I just love reading YA novels that are inclusive of all.  A lifelong Californian, I have been an Oregon resident for the past two years so it was also fun to see that the book was set in Oregon. I also have been a fan of red lipstick since my mid-twenties and still proudly wear it still today now that I am fast approaching fifty nine. Long live red lipstick in all its incarnations!I don't believe in writing reviews with spoilers so you will have to trust me that this is a good read about a sensitive subject most of us have no experience with.  The author's note at the end of the book was a brave one for the author to share and I applaud her candour. This appears to be the first in a series with the next book due in May 2014. I can't wait!

I have read several books by The Black and this one is my new favorite. The journey that The Black takes us on with Lucas Cain is AMAZING.Lucas' story begins when he is a teenager who after losing his mother to cancer is taken in by his aunt. She raises him as though he was hers with alot of love. But, cancer comes along again and takes away another important person from his life. He is only 18 years and alone. However, this is where life begins for him.Lucas' journey is an amazing one. It prepared him for where he ultimately ended up. This is a journey I strongly reccommend you taking. Characters from other works by The Black are also in this story for example: ELLE.I am sure that for all those who read this book, one of the burning questions is, what is Javaris' story? I am anxiously but patiently waiting for her story.THE PROFESSIONAL, WELL DONE!!!
What happens when a everyday joe confronts the undead in a nowhere trailer park in New Mexico? A great story happens, that's what. Give this one a try, it is very good!
summary: A fun take on the zombie Genre

reviewText: I was pleasantly surprised with this book. I was worried at first since it starts with the main character right in the mix, but it grabbed my attention and held it all the way to the end.
I enjoyed this set of books.  There are times that it's good to have  a "nasty" book or two.  thank you.

If this book isn't a sanity saver, I don't know what is!  Sheesh - between the weather and the holidays and the flu going around, this book has proven priceless in keeping my little ones occupied while allowing me to keep a little bit of the sanity I have left!  Since I used to be an assistant in an elementary school, I have helped children with multiple crafts, but most of the crafts detailed in this books are ones I have never done with children - my own or anyone else's.  That makes it fun for  my own creative side as well.  Dividing the book into seasonal categories is a lot of help as is having some crafts that are for either gender and then ones geared to specific genders.  We just loved the castle crafts during our last bout of illness...when my son and daughter both felt well enough to craft, we worked on the castle together and then when just one or the other felt better, we worked on the details that were specifically appealing to whichever kid.  My daughter loved the princess and the pea craft while my son enjoyed making the royal court people.  I loved how cheap it was - just needed regular craft supplies and empty toilet paper and paper towel tubes that I have been saving knowing they would be of use sooner or later.  This book is one I will enjoy sharing with my siblings as well - in the interest of sanity saving, of course!
summary: Fun sanity savers with inexpensive craft supplies!!

reviewText: This was such a nice , well written little story that I would have loved to see how it would have been as a full length.  So far I have read two of this author's works and one thing that she does that I do not see a lot of in the IR sub genre is that she infuses a little bit of humor in her work.  The dialogue and situations are great.  Fun, sexy, flirty.  Even the sex scenes have a bit of playfulness in them "We are going to go out on a date and do date-like things" <--- the hero says this, teeth clenched, in the throes of sex, acknowledging that they went about things a little backwards.  It was such a fun little moment in the midst of hot-sexy times that showed me this writer knows how to inject a little bit of whimsy into the heat and drama.  I liked that, it appeals to my own sense humor.  I would love to read a full length by this author!

Everything you would want and expect from a Christmas romance. Nice change to have the female half of the romantic couple to be the one with the money, as I am getting so tired of the millionaire businessman cliche.

With the main characters being 15 (or there abouts), I wonder if this is for early teenagers. It was a good book. I'm not a big fantasy fan. I bought the book for something different to read.The lads have been picked to be squires. They've gone off to squire school. After a few trials, they're divided into "colors", which designates what type of learning they will receive. Once they're finished with school and have proven themselves, they get to be knights.This is a continuation type series. The first book is being given a color and getting themselves into an adventure that almost gets them expelled. But the kingdom is in trouble and one of the boys is supposed to be able to read a language no one else can. That indicates he can split his mind in two and focus on two things at once. Hopefully, this skill will save the kingdom.I don't feel qualified to recommend this book, but I will say it was entertaining.

I'm continually impressed with Deaver's skills as a short story writer - and there's not as much demand for short fiction in any other genre as their is in mystery/thriller.  I enjoy Lincoln Rhyme as a character generally, although this story is probably a bit more enjoyable if you know a little about Rhyme and Amelia Sachs beforehand.
summary: Another strong short submission from Deaver

reviewText: It just really seems that there could be so much more depth to these characters.  There has to be MORE to the story.
summary: Hot, hot, hot but over too soon

reviewText: This is a promising start to a series.  The mythology has a very old world feel to it that I greatly enjoyed.  Hope it does not devolve into too much of a romance series.
This was just a nice read.  I loved the romance and would recommend it to others.  It isn't a huge convoluted story it is a simple love story about falling in love with big bad wolf.

This book was very emotional. I enjoy most all books, but this one was touching, I sympathized with the main character and felt connected. The story was sad, however it gave the characters an option to make up for the choices they chose.

The premise of this story was a good one, but it wasn't well-executed. I liked India and Andre, both individually and as a couple; however, I could never get a feel for why they were in love. Andre's tormenting of India in high school grew out of his attraction to her, but they weren't friends and never really interacted, so how was he in love with her after all these years? Infatuated with, maybe, but love? It would have been nice if we had seen the relationship grow and develop between these two.  In addition, we meet Mariah (the baby mama) when she calls to tell Andre that she can't keep Haile because she is going out of town; this is a dilemma for him, because he has a conference that he must attend in order to get his Master's or some such and needs someone to keep Haile. I thought that India would end up keeping Haile for him, thereby developing a relationship between the two, but sadly, we never learn how this is resolved and the matter is never brought up again. In fact, we never see much interaction between India and Haile.  There are several scenes where we see Andre and India, but no mention is made of where Haile is (for example, when they have dinner with Andre's mom). Oversights like this just frustrated me.I would be remiss if I didn't mention my biggest pet-peeve of all: poor editing. It's getting hard these days to review a book without pointing out the over-abundance of grammatical errors.  Do better, authors!This is not a bad book, and I will most likely be reading the other books in the trilogy. This author has a lot of potential; I just want her to take her time with the next book and not sell us short on the story.

I have loved reading all of Jayne Rylon's books and this one did not dissapoint.The character of Kate is very understandable from a reader's perspective and let's just say that the "Crew" did not dissapoint.  The book is hot and so is the action in this book!

What a wonderful urban diversion of a tale. I absolutely loved the storyline and the author's ability to connect the past to the present without so much of a giveaway. Being a native New Yorker and Brooklyn born, the landmarks and street names indicated in the book took me back down memory lane, while allowing me to be front and center relative to the character's whereabouts. The story touched on a few different issues of the harsh reality of life and the consequences that usually ensue, as well as depict a true NYC account of it all. I simply love...loved...loved it, and from one author to another...Thank you Aaron Verbalkent Bebo for gifting us with this adverse example of urban literature!!

Well the characters are well described even for a short story. Jane is a BBW that is intrigued with a new direction in her life. She also dreams and then they come. With a new job in Montana, she meets the distant Mr Ellis and his daughter. She finds that she has a lot in common with Morgan, the daughter. They both can see ghosts.

I really like this story.  I loved both the leads in this one, and the secondary characters are great as well.Hero is damaged but is still a loving person and doesn't let tragedy and his wealth define him.  And he has aequal in Jennifer, she is damaged but she is determined to make a success out of not only her career butalso her life.Can't wait to read book 2...which I have already bought!4.5 STARS

I received a free kindle copy of this book for this review. I will try to be as honest as I can be in this review.The author interviewed a collection of women that others had recommended to her as strong Christians.  Each chapter tells the story of one of the women.While some of the women had very touching stories, others had dry and uninteresting stories. The last chapter had statements from the women with their names.  I found myself unable to remember who the women were while reading the last chapter. I think the book would have been much better if the author had selected the most touching stories and dropped the more superficial stories. Some people are not comfortable with sharing their stories in depth. I think some of the women may have felt uncomfortable sharing at a deeper level.
summary: touching stories mixed with dry stories

reviewText: If you've read anything else by H.T. Night and enjoyed it, I urge you to buy this boxed set! If you're new to this author and enjoy vampires, werewolves, or any kind if creatures of the night, books, I urge you to buy this boxed set. H.T. Night has very quickly become a favorite of mine. His tales are so creative and unique and always leave you wanting more. While his books tend to be very easy and quick reads, do not mistake that for lack if quality or quantity. The main characters are so real to me and come alive page after page! Do yourself a pleasant favor and treat yourself to Night's books. I don't think you'll regret that decision in anyway. I sure haven't!!

In this part the brothers are geting it in. Dexter gets the job at the hospital and starts a relationship with his boss, whose ex-husband is a cop.He and Portia have spoken as well as his baby,Yanacia. David and Monica, who has just gotten out of jail have have hooked up and the brother's have a new friend Jermaine, who Cody brought in. They have hooked up with the OG Big Lou whose son is in the Fed pen about to get 30-life on drug charges.David is leary about the deal but couldn't resist the good money. Robert falls in love with Nicole, who is Stacia's sister and Maurice get's caugt making a drug deal by the Feds and Gotti turns out to be snitching.
This is a fantastic continuation of the Blood and Snow series.  I read thru the volumes in just two days.  I can't wait to see what happens next and how the author ends the series.
summary: Blood and Snow Volumes 5-8:Prey and Magic

reviewText: I liked that it started right in the suspense sequence but would have liked a little more info about the couple first. Great story!

**Originally written for Book Bliss book blog.**Review: 4.5 starsGeneral: Jade Lee wrote an amazing slice of regency life in this novella. I loved that the simplicity of the plot compared to the complexity of the heroine. It's not often to find something well written about the "husband hunting" season in London, normally something dastardly happens but Jade Lee's novella was entertaining and kept my attention without grand dramatics. The world was easy to into with the wonderful descriptions. All of the characters were different and had a unique way of interacting with one another. Greg and Caroline were a wonderful match, their chemistry easy to get behind and their interactions were entertaining.Overall the pace was smooth however at the end it felt a little too rushed to me. There was and wasn't enough justification for the happily ever after. By that I mean I could certainly see it coming but I can't say I felt the characters arrive their own their own where it arrived in the book.Characters: Caroline- Caroline was a very endearing female. She came from a background and yet could do nothing more than dream about living in the royal/nobel world. Her reactions to much were so genuine and I truly wanted her to get her day in court, what girl wouldn't want pretty dresses and flirting with well to do men? She was feisty from her past (which was well described but I'm hoping is present in other novels in the series) but knew her place in the world. Only once did I find her a little too pathetic when she begged Greg to give her a child so she could have something of him. It is in time with the period but it didn't work for me based on what I know of her from the two books I've read in this wonderful series.Greg- Greg was a hot piece of Scottish lord. I loved that he typically spoke with a refined British accent but would slip into his Burr at times…made it all the more sexy. He didn't have much time to act like an alpha male in this book and I liked it. He was possessive and demanding but not overly aggressive. I loved that he was a man of science and had explosion scars, fantastic touch!
Amazing book, and it was free! I would reccomend this book to anyone who loves a steamy romance with just the right amount of action.

I am a huge Kristen Ashley fan/junkie/addict, sadly I am scared of ghosts! The love of the author made me read the entire series. I read through this slowly as parts were very intricate. Makes me wonder how she has that much imagination. A lot of love and sex involved with Belle and Jack and they  had some HUGE heartbreaks, sad but recovering was explained well. Loved the characters and the quirkiness of Belle's Dad Jensen was a hoot too. For the POV's it was by chapter so it was easy to follow. The "wee ones' ghosts Lewis and Myrtle have been held in sort of ghost purgatory for 200 years. Now it is up to a reporter and the cast of ghost whisperers and clairvoyant to help them to find peace.Loved it even though there were parts that made me scared. Oh well not scared enough to get out the holy water!
summary: Guess I like a ghost story too

reviewText: Dark Soul Vol. 3 was a bit of a shocker. There was one scene in the story which was particularly hard to digest. I was both disgusted by what Silvio did and felt sorry for him. I couldn't believe that he actually went there. He truly has no boundaries and no shame. I guess that is what makes him such a fascinating character.I wanted to know more about Silvio's brother. The conversations that they had left me with a lot of questions. I'm hoping to hear more about him in the next installment.This wasn't a night read for sure. A little darker than the Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 and more disturbing, but just as interesting and hard to put it down.
A well written adventure and sweet romance. I enjoyed it immensely. The story was inspirational and fun. Virginia Carmichael is an author I will search for and read in the future.

This was a nice little read. Went fast but was written fast but in a good way. A little misplaced words but nothing serious. Some of the end parts to me would only happen in a book but hay it's a book. Wonder what the next one is going to be about. Nice job.

This book was cute!!!  I enjoyed seeing the other characters of the series and could actually remember points of this book that happened in the previous book.Hunter and Blake were too cute!!  When reading this book, I kept thinking of the movie "I Now Pronounce You Chuck and Larry" and the fact that firemen, like policemen and other jobs, face possible persecution from their fellow mates for being gay.  Seeing two sides of two men who fell in love with each other and have similar stories was cute!

A sweet second chance story that will tug at your heart. Glory and Johnny were meant to be together, but life got in the way. Glory is a famous actress who left home to follow her dreams at the urging of Johnny. She comes back home to help her sister who is going through her own personal hell.  This is more of a story about family than love,but there you can still feel the love all through the book.

This being the final book in this trilogy had a lot to live up to, and I can honestly say that I was not disappointed.This was written form the perspectives of Nick and Sam. Sam has been told by her father for years that she is to marry Nick (who is in love and engaged to Lizzie). She is sent back to Boston from Texas by her father to split the happy couple up where she is to then take her rightful place as his wife to be.She gets in between the couple and when the timing is right her father makes sure Lizzie loses her job then Sam swoops in to tell her that she is not the right person for Nick and doesn't belong in his world. Lizzie packs up and leaves with her son whilst Nick is at work and he returns to an empty house.He tries everyone he knows to find where she has gone but no one knows.When he does find her she is with Teagan (her irish ex and father to Niall). Nick lets her have the time she needs to sort herself out, but when she returns to their apartment with Teagan in tow he wonders whether its all over. Teagan apparently only wants money from them!! Nice I know!! Once he leaves they start to work on Sam and her father after the truth comes out.Sam hits the hard times, alcohol, drugs and sex.Her father gets his jus desserts too.

Alethea and Marc are the perfect addition to the Legacy Collection.Alethea is strong, independent and wounded by the pulling away of the only family she's ever had.  Marc is fighting his own battle with constantly being called a hero that he feels is undeserved.  They are both fiercely loyal to the people around them and balance each other out perfectly.The Legacy Collection is one of my absolute favorite series!  Romance, intrigue, suspense, and humor you'll find it all in this series!

By offering information in bite-size pieces, this book on Martin Luther King, Jr. makes it an easy book to read and an easy book to discuss with your child. And, along with incredibly important information, there are some interesting tid-bits to keep kids engaged (e.g., the MLK Star Trek connection). "55 Fun Facts About Martin Luther King Jr." should be part of your home library.
summary: should be part of your home library

reviewText: Every book was just enough to make me hot under the collar. I was excited to read the next and the next. I didn't want them to end.

It was an okay read but moved a little slow with too many minute details.  The plot was drawn out and I was worn out before I got to the end.  I love to read so this was a little disappointing.  It is a good story line and I love the characters but...
Up until today my son didn’t want to go sleep at bedtime or to be covered. Nowadays, my son insists to be covered by his own dream night blanket

I started following Stephanie Jackson when she wrote her bestselling book - When Angels Fall.  After that, I fell in love with her other book - The Reaper Within - so I knew that I had to continue on.  I have yet to be disappointed.The Reaper Within (Dark Rain) is a great addition to the series.  The story of the seven Dark Souls is a great one.  I love Jackson's incorporation of angels into all of her books - this one is no different.  The plot moves fast as the danger is real.  The story picks up pace and time is running out as the book gets intense.  Are they going to be able to save planet Earth?This book is fast-paced, imaginative, and completely thrilling.  Stephanie Jackson never disappoints me.  I highly recommend this book and anything else that she decides to leave her mark on.  Good work!
summary: One of the many solid books by Stephanie Jackson.  She never ceases to amaze me!

reviewText: I have always been a bit of a fitness freak and have been taking CLO and krill oil for many years and one of the things I have noticed when I stop taking it is my mood levels begin to drop... so when I saw this book and it confirmed my suspicion that fish oil does indeed have real link to your psychological state! Well worth a read at this price.

I never knew there was so many uses for Apple Cider Vinegar. But the one amazing use I never knew was the dramatic benefits it can have on your health. There isn't a health issue Apple Cider Vinegar can't help you with practically. I learned for example dandruff, cholesterol and weight loss all can be remedied with the use of Apple Cider Vinegar. And the great plus of this is that its cheap and affordable and can do so much for you. This book is a mandatory read and you will probably never use it in all its applications because they are so varied and many.

Too much of the story was illogical and the characters, though intended to be complex, were superficially drawn by trying too hard to pack too much into too little. Because it was short, I did read to the end, but have deleted and won't buy more from this author.

I'm not sure why Trina wanted her sister dead or why Terrance wanted his brother dead. I guess that will be revealed in the next installment. I feel more should have been revealed to get the reader coming back for more.

Having really enjoyed "Karma I, II & III", I was happy to see this new book by Kenni York. It did not disappoint. It was also extremely well-written, and the story was captivating. It captures the positive emotions of a father-daughter relationship, and of a friendship, and the negative emotions of an individual seeking revenge. Highly recommended.

In this economy we are all looking for ways to cut our expenses and live happier, more simple, lives. This book explains how creating a minimalist budget can allow you to save more and stop living from paycheck to paycheck. It takes you step by step through decluttering your life and your finances and teaches you how to cut back on unnecessary expenses. In just 14 days you can be on your way to being freer, happier, and out of debt. I highly recommend this book to anyone who wants to make the most of the money they earn and improve their lives and the lives of those they love.
summary: Simplify your Life and Save Money!

reviewText: I like post apocalyptic books and the beginning of this one is pretty good.The first few chapters were new and different from the rest of the books I read.But then the plot becomes very straight forward and simple.The good guys are good, the bad guys are really bad and the hero turns from an interesting characters to typecast of a kids books hero.
summary: Not too bad but not too good

reviewText: I really enjoyed this book.  It's the first for this author that I've read, and I have to say that I was impressed.  Not only did I enjoy the story, but I also liked Ms. De Medeiros' writing style.  The story is romantic, and sweet, with hot sex, and LOL humor.  As much as I loved Gabriel and Melody, I have to say that for me, Gabe's grandfather,Fergus, stole the show!  Gabriel is the head of the family and has carried the weight of responsibility on his shoulders, ever since his parents' death.  In the seven years since, the now 30 year old Gabe, has worked hard and built up a successful ranch.  He also has the task of TRYING to keep his grandfather from continually getting into trouble, and raising his two younger brothers, ages 15 and 13.  There is nothing Fergus wants more than to see Gabriel happily settled.  To that end, unknown to Gabe, Fergus (along with his cohorts on the town council) advertises for a mail-order bride on Gabe's behalf.  When Melody responds to the ad, Pops then embarks on a "courtship" with Melody--who believes that she's corresponding with Gabe.  Fergus says nothing about the scheme until AFTER he sends for Melody.  He then blithely informs Gabe that he has sent for a bride for him.  Gabriel, of course, is absolutely furious!  The last thing he wants is to get married, and he certainly doesn't want a bride that his grandfather chose for him.  Initially, Gabriel is adamantly opposed to the idea, but with pressure from Fergus and both his brothers endorsing the idea, not to mention the fact that his "bride" is already en route, he decides to give her a chance.  Melody is a really sweet character.  She too has endured her share of life's hardships.  Since the recent death of her parents, 23 year old Melody is left destitute and responsible for her 9 year old sister, Lily  In the intervening five months since their parents died, Melody and Lily lost their farm to foreclosure and have been existing hand to mouth.  In desperation, Melody answered Fergus' ad for a mail-order bride and the sisters make the journey to Liberty.  Gabe and Melody first meet, when he picks her up at the stagecoach.  Needless to say, their relationship doesn't get off to a smooth start.  The story that unfolds is sweet, with lots of LOL moment, mostly involving Fergus and his town council cronies.  The plot is also chock full of excitement with murder, kidnapping, and race-related violence.  I thoroughly enjoyed this book and would recommend it to anyone who enjoys historical westerns.  FYI, this is NOT a clean romance.  Happy reading!
Great reading. Love the romance and the detail. Curl up with a hot cup of cocoa and a blanket and loose yourself.!

Firstly id like to thank Beckie Stevenson for giving me this book in exchange for an honest reviewThank you Beckie for taking pity on me after i begged you for a copy because if you hadn't i would have left this on my to-read shelf for god knows how long and would have kicked myself for it, so you saved me days of self loathing LOL.This was a wonderful book about a young girl named Serena who's world gets turned upside down by a boy named Kaiden and thrust into a life whe was meant to live but was stolen from her. She must find the strength to sort between the thruths and lies told to her throughout her life while trying to fit into a place she has only read about in books.I liked Serena and thought even from a young age she was starting to recognize things weren't quite right with her life and although she has lived apart from civilisation all her life she adjusts well and realises that just because her surroundings are different doesn't mean she is. An example of this is when she says:"I glance at myself in the mirror and notice that my green eyes sparkle, just like they did when we were in the wookds. I'm still me. I'm still serena. I'm just cleaner, have nicer smelling hair and now know that i've bee lied to most of my life"I can only imagine what Angela and Auden went through and can't believe Lydia (the crazy B***H) did everything out of a warped sense of jealousy and entitlement. Oh and id also like to state for the record i still wanna round house kick Anastasia in the face. I was so glad we got that juicy little bit in the epilogue because i had being dieing for it since Kaiden and Serena met. Highly Recommend
I could barely finish reading this book because of all of the editing errors.  It seemed like a lot of the lines were repeated over and over.

It's all about the purple boots or is it? This is a short story hopefully a bridge from the last Deadwood book to the next. I'm not a fan of short stories as a rule, this being the exception. This time it was a great story to keep you in the loop it started, had a middle and then gave you a ending to fan your imagination. Good writing, great story with some of my favorite characters cannot wait for a full book to cuddle up with. Ann you always put a smile in my heart with your books.

This is a tale for adventerous young souls who want to explore. The illustrations are gorgeous and only add to the text. The theme of the story is to follow your dreams. The book is really written for the younger ages- those just learning to read. However, it's a lovely book and worthy of being read by older children as well. Completely enjoyable.

This had a couple reunited from when they were at uni to 20 years later, purely by accident. There is a secret she is hiding from him, which made her a little annoying in some ways. Throw in a huge slice of suspense and thriller snippets, add juicy sex scenes,, and this wasn't bad at all. Storyline overall, pretty good, and kept me enthralled!
I loved the story and the characters. It was exciting and kept my attention. I loved how the multi incidents all came together at the end.

Normally, I really love murder mysteries. The Glass Room Murder has a great story-line, but the book just seems to go from interview one person to the next. The Glass Room Murder has not yet been professionally edited, as a result, the book has an assortment of punctual and grammatical errors.The Glass Room Murder is the story of detective Ryan Cook, investigating a very interesting murder. When millionaire businessman Henrik is murdered inside his impenetrable glass room it quickly becomes a high profile case. The glass room company uses high tech to create the ultimate room, that no one can access except the owner. However, a man named Elvin acquires the ability to bi-locate (otherwise known as out of body experiences) when he is in a horrific car crash. He uses his ability to penetrate the glass room, while staging a trance in public so that he is seen in both places at the same time. Elvin ends up murdered, and the confessions just start pouring out.It turns out that more than one person wanted Henrik dead, for many different reasons, not just his money. Very fast-paced book.
summary: Not the best, but a good story.

reviewText: Amanda Chayse is such a great author she got my attention at the beginning of the story book 1 all the way to the last. Great story and series highly recommend for everyone to read.

loved, loved, loved this sequel! could not stop reading the book because it was so entertaining. love all the characters Kaitlyn Cross created in this story. loved the ending and of course I'm hoping that it was left open enough for there to maybe even be a third book in this series. I really enjoyed this one! It's a Crime by C.E. Hansen reminded me why I've always liked the Romantic Suspense genre.. and although this one was not real suspenseful, it had just enough to add a bit of nail biting.First we've got Grace Preston.. she's gorgeous, has money, owns her own boutique, and has a great bff. She lost her fiancé 5 years ago and even though she's pretty much got past the loss.. she still feels like no one else could take his place. She's not looking for a relationship...Then we've got Cole Grayson.. extremely sexy commercial real estate mogul. He also happens to be a billionaire. He's suffered loss also... losing his family as a young teen he closed himself to the outside world. The only thing he wanted to do was make a name for himself..but even more so, he wanted to find the person responsible for killing his mother, father, and little brother. He'll never be able to let his demons go until he gets revenge.Grace and Cole meet each other for the first time at a local bar called Luke's. It's lust at first sight.... Cole is just in town for business.. he owns one of the hotels and has a permanent penthouse suite..so they go back to his place that night and holy hotness!! OK.. listen up.. we've got some serious sexy times going on here.. Ms. Hansen did not skip on the details at all. I'm a details kinda girl and whoa.. these were just the type of scenes that I LOVE.So as Grace and Cole are getting to know each other and both are falling quickly.. Cole is still keeping himself at a distance. He wants Grace, but he can't let himself have her. He's not ready and wont be until he gets his revenge on the guy that killed his family. While all this is going on..there is a crazy psycho serial killer out there..killing girls that look just like Grace and it appears Grace may be his ultimate target.. but why?I will say that the coincidence and the connection between Cole, Grace, and the crazy dude was a bit far fetched... I still really enjoyed it. I figured out who the baddy was early and you probably will too but that didn't take away from the story.I read this one in one day, didn't want to put it down.. I was really enjoying the story of Grace and Cole. We've got some super hot sex, a little suspense, a crazy dude, and an hea.I'd recommend it if you love some good sexy times with some suspense thrown in and have a thing for tongue talented billionaires.. ;)

We are often our own worst enemy. We all have negative thoughts at times, and over time these negative thoughts can take their toll and taint how we see ourselves. In this little book, author Mike Adams offers 25 action steps for "refocusing" - changing the way we see things in order to turn things around for the better. The first step in boosting self esteem is to let go of the past and look to the future. Some of the action steps are obvious, like "Low self esteem thrives on negative thoughts." Taken as a whole, however, the book includes some sound advice for raising one's self esteem. A sampling of the action steps:* Forget about perfection. Boost your self esteem by being okay with who you are at this moment.* Don't compare yourself with others.* Stay away from negative people.* Learn to laugh at yourself. Laughter is the best medicine, even for building self esteem.The book has no earthshaking new ideas about developing self esteem, but it does give some helpful insight into the issue of self esteem and how to raise it.

I didn't really know what to expect from The Zombie Story. I knew it was the first novella in a series, that it was about zombies (obviously), but other than those two things I was taking a shot in the dark. As I began reading the novel I was wondering one thing: What sets The Zombie Story apart from other zombie stories. Since as most of you should know, there are a lot of them.  Well there is a long list of reasons why this novella sets the bar far from other zombie based stories: The world is still normal and not dystopian. Not everybody knows about the existence of zombies. And did I forget to mention the part where everybody is tested to see just how powerful their magick is?Yes, I just said that: Magick. With a capital (well actually lower case) K.  In the wonderful world of The Chronicles of Orlando everybody on planet Earth has magical powers but to some extent and our MC Orlando is yet to be tested.When I began reading the novel I found it well written and interesting. Poor Orlando being forced to move to L.A. and then seeing a zombie get killed on his first day in town. Sure it doesn't sound like a great way to start the day, but it was a great way to start a novel (la).  As the story progressed I did notice the way the building of characters and the way that the Zombie Hunter's worked, but like any story you need a bad guy! And in The Zombie Story our bad guy is Maxwell who came off as unpredictable and like a mad-scientist. Not to mention that the other main bad guys in the story were the zombies themselves, who (contrary to popular belief) are still semi-intelligent?While I did hope that maybe we would get to see some romance (because come on who doesn't like a little bit of romance?) I did think that when Orlando was around our main female character Elodie that their friendship could definitely change into something more and what the note that The Zombie Story ends on, I wouldn't ignore the idea.As for the ending, it totally left you waiting for the sequel with their being so many lose ends and so many more people left to die...
summary: Chapter by Chapter's Review of The Zombie Story

I don't usually review childrens books, but this AM the covers were sticking straight into my face from Kindle recommendations area on my reader. I finally remembered that I just ordered a set of childrens books for my little niece, so, it was Amazon tracking.  LOL...  I am a very open minded person so if it's interesting, I will read anything.  So, the title of the book is what grabbed me.  So, I purchased it to my e-ink reader to prescreen it, and see if it was appropriate for my niece.Well, I am glad I did!  This was a delightful tale that actually had me laughing this morning. The author starts the book of with a very appropriate, warning to children to not try this at home. We all know how curious children can be at this age, that was very responsible. It's a very short story that follows 7 yr old Falisha Whiskers, trying to get her 5 yr old annoying brother Jesse out of her, because he never gets her name right.  Purposely, calling her Faseesha all the time. So once he can't be found by their Mom, and she questions her daughter for his whereabouts. This stumbles out of sister's mouth, " I flushed Jesse down the toilet" with the matching detailed illustration to it on the next page, as an adult I was hooked and hysterical.This author a wrote an excellent, funny, very imaginative adventure into the yucky toilet world now having to get her little brother back, under house orders. This book teaches children to love each other no matter what, and we need a little more of this in our world now. I would definitely recommend this book for children, but I am going to order the paperbacks, because in school storytelling time, the teachers are still using book.I was amazed though, how clear and detailed the illustrations stood out on my e-ink reader.This author's writing was excellent, a new, very creative tale and gaged perfectly towards children.  I loved it!  I am going to read the second part.I think my niece is going to have me reading this story over and over, especially because of the funny, rhyming words.  I do anything to put a smile on her face.

reviewText: Before reading this series, I scheduled a past life regression session. I had no idea this series would discuss anything about past lives. It was recommended to me by a friend. Now this is what I have been waiting for!  Does everything I want to see in a romance to perfection. Smart, funny, great female friendships, taut tension, well-formed characters, friendships...the story and characters just leapt from the pages. We get to hear both dating guru magazine columnist Julie's perspective as well as uptight (and hot) Wall Street broker Mitchell's. Each is trying to get over on the other, she-"dared" by her boss to write a "what happens after the first date-taking it to the next step" column, he "dared" by a co-worker to have a fling- and each of the dares the complete opposite of their mutual histories.  She has a million flings, he just out of a near 10-year relationship. Love that the women (Julie's friends/boss) are strong but very real, natural human beings. Very relatable. Loved Mitchell, his humor, sexual prowess, yet a nice blend of tenderness too. Steamy, but not overly so. Well-balanced. OH and the "dark moment" had me teary-eyed. Kept me gobbling up the words so I could find out what happened!

This kindle book is missing huge chunks of the story and then whole pages will be repeated.  I am requesting a refund on this.....did no one proofread this book?!

Demon's Dream is the sixth and last book of the High Demon series and to me, it is the jewel of the series.  Each page of the book is filled with drama or humour. So many questions from prior books are answered in Demon's Dream and you may not like them.  Reah finally finds someone who truly loves her without reservations.  Edward is the only prospective mate who asked her to marry him.  This is so important to Reah because she is uncertain if she will keep all her mates or send some away.  Her love for them died during the years she was effectively in exile. She can not easily set aside the pain and heartbreak of the 25 years she was ignored by her mates and family. Nor can she forgive Kifirin for giving her daughters away to the King and Queen of the High Demon planet. Reah is determined to keep her unborn son (Teeg is the father) with her and in her care.  Be prepared for some shocking surprises to be revealed and an ending that will leave you wanting more.  Knowing Demon's Dream is the last of the High Demon series leaves me sad.  I want to know how Reah's marriage with Edward plays out, who the new Dark Lord will be, who the shining woman is, does Griffin find Amara, will they reconcile and on and on go the new unanswered questions.  Maybe the author will expand the series with a seventh book to address these questions.  For new readers some advice - read the prior books or you will be lost as you read Demon's Dream.
Definitely a must read for anyone who loves a little bit of everything, from romance, mystery, super natural and action it has it all!!

This was a fun peek into Harper's Cove. If you love erotica this is a series you don't want to miss. This book is more than sexy or hot it's amazing! I enjoyed the glimpse into these peoples lives and how they sincerely care for each other. They are more than friends, lovers, or partners. They are a part of each other. I can't wait to read of this series and find out what other secrets are hiding on Harper's Cove.
Way too short!!!! Loved it! I truly enjoy Maya banks.I  would have read this book in one sitting even if it were 4 times longer.
Excellent book. I could not put this book. Up all night reason the 2 books. Can't wait for the 3rd book to be released.

Who would not want to kiss an adorable firefighter who also repairs toys to give them to needy children?  and if there's mistletoe, who can resist?  Julia and Jake have a rocky road as she is already engaged and he won't kiss a girl until he is sure she's the "one" for him.  This book just made me feel good. It is a sweet romance and definitely make me recall my own moments of falling in love.  Starlight sounds like a delightful town to live in and the town just has a "family feel" to it.  Read this sweet book to find out if Jake  and Julia find love and get a kiss underneath the mistletoe.5 StarsI won a copy of this book from the author in a holiday giveaway. "How to Write a Book" is a comprehensive A-Z guide for beginners in the field of writing. Many of us have thought of writing a book, but author Joan Bartlett informs us about everything that goes into it.Bartlett does a great job of explaining the specifics of the book writing and revision process, such as setting up a comfortable work environment, deciding on a topic, researching, developing characters, outlining, and editing. She also shares tips on finding a reputable cover designer, book marketing, and more.If you're contemplating writing a book, "How to Write a Book" will serve as an excellent reference. Highly recommended!

This book touched my heart. One of my favorite authors and now one of my favorite books! This book is about friendship, loss, and love. Never give more to one than the other in everything they do. Until one night Jase and Whisk make a decision for Heaven that changes all their life's. This book had me on the first page! It had me so emotional I had to stop reading to get myself together! Bec you know how to drawl in hearts and put it on paper. You had me feel as tho I was going through all this at the same time had me hoping for the best. I do love your books great detail! Just wish it was longer lol To everybody tho check this book out. LOved Kelly Hunter's What a bride Wants. I am not one of those people that will write a review and spoil the book. I will say Ella is a sassy young female and her father is so frustrated that she is not seeing anyone of even planning on getting married. Then we meet Sawyer!! Ladies you will dream about him. I wanted to love this book but for me it was just missing something.  I loved the premise of the book but I feel the author in so many places left out details that would have made the relationships and storyline flow.  I don't truly consider this a "romance" book although it does end that way.  In fact I believe the romance storyline was the weakest part.  The two characters  didn't spend much time together and when they did the author didn't really describe much of their conversations so falling in love seemed odd.Some parts of this book did intrigue me.  I liked the premise of a true modern day miracle occurring and it bringing the main character to a faith in Christ.  I felt the reactions of her family and friends were realistically portrayed with skepticism and disbelief as what occurred seems too amazing to be believed.  I liked the points the author was trying to make just felt the delivery was a bit off.Overall I think this book has some promise as it is an an interesting  storyline but the author really needs to make all of the parts flow together.  I found it at times hard to follow.  I also don't think enough details are provided to make you feel like the two characters are in love.  The portion with the young girl also doesn't seem to flow.I don't regret reading this as it was the kind of book that makes you think.

The sex was really great.What I had problems with....well, its short, I finished it in a few hours of straight reading. I think the next one in the series is $2.99, wont do it, not for a short story.I must say, the story is great, and I really wish that instead of breaking the story up into different books, she kept it all in one, which I would have paid for a complete story. That was another concern of mine.As far as my ice cube rating...3 ice cubes to cool down, would have gotten a lot more, but my sizzle fizzled when the book ended as quickly as it did.I wish I could give it a better rating, its really a well written book....

The author has a near obsession with random commas and incomplete sentences.  The writing was so fragmented it was too painful to continue.  I can't give a decent review to a book I can't even read.  The editorial review gives no insight as to content or quality, and lacks descriptive language to entice readers.  Reader beware; a writer's "traditionally published" background does not guarantee success in independent projects.  The claim that the author accidentally "downloaded an unedited copy" is slightly suspect;  If this is the edited copy, I urge the author to get a new, professional editor.  A dirth of incomplete sentences and misplaced punctuation severely disrupt the flow of ideas and prohibit intellectual progress.*updateA gracious response to my critical review warranted an amendment to my opinion of the author.  I will take the time to read the book and post an update with my professional opinion of its potential.  I would suggest a beta exchange group for invaluable editing, grammar, and character and story development coaching. A thick skin and an open mind will get you everywhere.

Kellen Jamison, rhythm guitarist for Sole Regret, can Tie Me up any day!Although his heart is tied to his past and the fiance that he lost to cancer, Kellen is trying to untie the strings and remove the cuffs that keep reminding him of what he no longer has. She and Kellen have a spark that ignites instantly and they discover how strong ties can bind and how good the release can be!This night with Sole Regret was one of my favorites. I love the thought of severing the ties to your past while tying them to your future in a completely erotic and sexy way. Olivia Cunning has a way with words and has mastered the hot rock stars. I snagged a copy of this book when it was offered as a freebie last week (I think, my days run together fairly often) because the cover was cute and who wouldn't want to read a chick-lit Assassin novel? Flirting With Death has a fairly unique plot (at least I've never seen one like it) and the writing was concise, fun and even a tad snarky. I just love me a good dose of Snark!Compelling supporting characters gave bad-girl-turned-good-girl Kayla a lot to keep her busy while she tries to figure out how to live a "normal" life, who exactly tried to kill her, and why that earned her a one-way ticket out of the CIA. In the middle of all that, Kayla finds some time to right a few local wrongs, even if it means turning her kitchen into a temporary kennel. Who says assassins can't have a heart of gold, even if it's a little tarnished?Flirting with Death is no longer free, but at $3.99 it's still a Fab bargain. And right now it's also ranked in the Top 20 of multiple categories on Amazon- so clearly I'm not the only one who loved it!
summary: Such a fun book! Witty, with a bit of sass!

reviewText: I received an ebook copy of both book from Netgalley.I felt that this books had the potential to be a great book to kick off the series. The author has created an interesting world that as a reader I would love to explore through their books.  However, the book was a let down.This world of dragons is intriguing. I haven't come across a dragon shifter outside of a novel in the Sherrilyn Kenyon Dark-Hunter series.  The author has this great world to play with and she just hits at it's existence. I would have loved to have some more background into the life of the dragons.The pace moved too quickly.  Things that felt as if the characters should have more resistance or adjustment period too, where easily accepted. I think if the pace had been slowed the story could have been flushed out a little bit more.Another thing that I would have liked to seen, is a lead into the next novel. At least introduce the next hero or heroine, and more than just a brief appearance.  Give me a reason to want to pick up the next novel.Review originally published at Little Thoughts About Books.

When an author can take the preconceived notions of "ugly & terrifying" gargoyles and turns them into "hot & sexy, yet terrifying" gargoyles, you know you've got a winner! I was excited about this series way back when Jen told me she was even attempting to write a book about gargoyles, where we appropriately joked about the actual cartoon show, Gargoyles. I knew if anyone could do these creatures justice, it would be Jen. And boy, did she! Barely getting a glimpse of these creatures, known as Wardens, I'm already intrigued and eager to learn more. Not only that, Jen introduces a slew of new (to me) creatures (i.e. Herbert) and adds her twists to some known ones. In between learning about all these fascinating creatures, you get the typical unrivaled JLA romance that I love so much.Dez is yet another guy I'll be adding to my list of book boyfriends, in the special top "JLA section" that all her boys tend to be categorized in. Seriously, her boys need to be placed in a category all of their own, because damn, can they make me swoon! Dez is sexy, strong, sweet, and considerate. Sure the way he left Jasmine three years ago was abrupt and hurtful, but when the truth comes out, you can't help but feel for the guy. I loved their relationship, how they grew up together, friends-turned-lovers. Their dialogue was fun and their personalities clicked together very well. Jasmine also gets props for not giving into Dez right away and learning to trust him again, despite moments of lust-driven slips. I also liked that she wasn't afraid to break free from the norms in her race of creatures, yearning for more and not content with what the women in their world were supposed to do.Oh, and I loved seeing Zayne, Layla, and even Roth a bit in this, too. They are the main characters in the first book in this series, White Hot Kiss, which I can't wait to read!Bitter Sweet Love was a great prequel to what I'm sure will be an amazing series. I'm already intrigued by the cast of characters, the supernatural world, and the mesmerizing romances Jen has created and I know it will only get better and more intense as the series progresses. Trust me, this is one series you don't want to miss!
summary: JLA has gone and made gargoyles sexy! Who can top that?!

Willamena Dunn and Knox Loveless have a history of feuding and wagers dating back to childhood. Willa's family runs Dunn-Right Preservation, and the Loveless family's construction company is responsible for those horrible McMansions. Willa can't understand or condone her baby sister's upcoming marriage to Knox's older brother, but things get worse for her when Knox outbids her for the historic cottage she has always dreamed of owning. When Knox offers a wager, with the cottage as prize, Willa can't say no, even if it means hurting her older sister.Willa and Knox have a history, and it is fun watching them finally understand what everyone has always seen: all their bickering is hiding that they were meant to be together.The characters and location are well written, and pull the reader in. I love Magnolia Bay, and watching Knox and Willa find each other was extremely entertaining.Bet the House by Erika Marks was a fun read. It was a novella that did not feel like one, but on the other hand, I didn't want to see it end.

reviewText: This story kicks off with Emma partaking in a crazy dare to help cheer up her best friend after a breakup. This is the first time Emma meets Tobias, naked as the day she was born, with a cop car doing patrols of the neighbourhood. He saves her from possibly being lifted, even though he doesn't know she's his future business partner.Tobias is utterly gorgeous, and the poor guy is getting over the murder of his fiancé. He's quiet, reserved, and the ex-cop in him can't help try to figure Emma out. He moved to town with his younger brother Josh--by the way, he totally needs his own story when he grows up--who Tobias has also been keeping secrets from. His first instinct is to protect those in his life. Though a bit stuffy in the beginning (the dare/stunt was frowned upon) Tobias quickly won me over with the way he cared for Emma and Josh.Emma is the quiet one in her trio of friends. She's wary, a little bit of a pushover, and a queen desert maker. But she is in no way shallow. Emma has a horrid past, losing her parents at a young age and trying to make her way in the world. She hurts, she feels, she cares and when she does I was right there with her. Tobias managed to coax her out of her shell to the point where she even stood up to the strongest personality in her group, and I think I fell for him a little more around then.All in all, Double Dare was a fantastic story and I can't wait for the second in the series, Twice Smitten. The humour one expects from a Melissa Blue story is inherent from the first page, right to the end. Both characters are a little broken, even though they may at times not think it, but they heal each other up nicely and I'm not ashamed to say I cried at the end. The scenes with Emma and her two best friends Sasha and Abigail are brilliant and I could picture being there, rolling my eyes at something Abigail said, or giggling at one of Sasha's one liners.I highly recommend this story, and can't wait for the second! Get to work Ms Blue.
summary: Funny, heartwarming and sexy as sin

reviewText: Kathyrn Shay did a wonderful job of bringing romance, humor and time travel together in the first of her trilogies Portals of Time.  Three women travel back from the future to change the course of history to save mankind.  I found it an enjoyable, well written story.  The characters were well balanced and realistic.  I like when each book in a trilogy can be read alone or as part of the series.  I can not stand when there is a cliff hanger at the end and you must purchase the sequels.  This is definitely one of those books that can be read alone or if you love it, like I did, and want to purchase the rest you can.  Time travel, romance and humor...what more can one ask from a book?

CoverThe horse on the cover, as I found out while reading, is a racing horse named Credo's Hope.  The lady with the gun on the front is Detective Alex Wolfe.  So, the cover is an apt depiction of a couple of main character(s) that is in the story.Plot/CharactersAlex is an arse-kicking, quick-tempered detective who has a knack for getting into trouble without even trying.  Her mother is constantly trying to get her invited to get-togethers where Alex could possibly meet "Mr. Right."Casey is Alex's work partner.  She thinks before speaking and tries her best to get Alex to do the same thing.Kate is Alex and Casey's boss and finds Alex's antics somewhat humorous, but extremely tiresome.  She is a hard boss, but fair.Megan has been Alex's best friend since pre-K and teaches dog training classes.  She helps Alex and Casey on a side investigation that Alex is working on in her spare time.OverallThe story is very engaging and will keep you reading wanting to know more.  There seem to be two main plots with a few sub-plots, but it is all kept well organized and does not get confusing at all.  As a matter of fact, it is part of what keeps you engaged and continuing to read.I would recommend this book to those who enjoy a good mystery with a strong female lead who can kick arse with the best of them.  =)
summary: Very Engaging With A Strong Female Lead

reviewText: I have been a fan of Lauren Dane for quite awhile now. I adore her Chase Brothers series, and have read those books numerous times. I am so glad that she decided to continue to give fans trips to Petal GA.Count On Me, book three in the Petal GA. series, is the story of Royal Watson, who is the on-again off-again boyfriend of Murphy sibling Anne. I was really worried that I would not enjoy reading Royal finally finding his HEA with anyone but Anne. Once I met Caroline, I knew she was his ONE.Caroline Mendoza was raised in Petal until she was 16. She moved away to live with her father’s family after her father was convicted of killing her mother. Caroline believed with all her heart and soul that there was no way her father was capable of murdering her mother. Caroline spent most of her adult life trying to prove her father was not the one who killed her mother. She has now come back to Petal to help build a stronger relationship with her sister, brother and grandparents.I have to say that I LOVED Caroline’s spunk and whit. She is written perfectly as the strong heroine. She is fighter and she will let nothing stand in her way. Not even her own grandparents. Who I honestly wanted to reach through my kindle and slap. Her grandmother is a piece of work to say the least.Royal Watson has been on-again and off-again SO many times with Anne Murphy. After they decide that they are over once and all, Royal is more than ready to find what his friends have found with their wives. Royal is a smart, SEXY farmer. Who would not want to be in love with a sexy farmer like Royal. I always thought Anne was crazy for not settling down with Royal, but once you see Royal and Caroline together all those thoughts go out the window.I really enjoyed Royal and Caroline together. Like I said before I was worried that I would continue to want Royal with Anne, but Mrs. Dane does a wonderful of job of showing that Caroline is the one made for Royal. These two are just great together.There is a mystery in this story and I was hooked from the beginning trying to figure it out. I have to say I never did figure it out. Mrs. Dane does a fabulous job of keeping the mystery in the forefront of the story line, but not making it overkill. This is truly the love story of Royal and Caroline. All the good, bad and the ugly.Oh, and how can you not love getting to spend time with Edward and Polly Chase. These two characters are two that I don’t think I could ever get enough of. I am crossing my fingers that one day we get a full length story. We also get updates on all our favorite Chase brothers and Murphy siblings. I hope they all keep having kids, so we will hopefully continue to get trips to Petal for many years to come.Count On Me is another fabulous addition to the Petal GA series. It is a perfectly written story about fighting for what you believe in and never giving up on family and love.Happy Reading!Review copy provided for a honest review.
summary: A  perfectly written story about fighting for what you believe in and never giving up on family and love.

Wow... I don't even know where to start. This book was great. It kept me on the edge of my seat with where it was going the entire time. I absolutely love Mace and Cora. Knox.... I don't know how I feel about him.I'm going to start at the one thing that I didn't like, however this did not drop the rating of my review because I know there will be another book. The cliff hanger. :)Darn was it hot! Hot, yes it was hot, hmmmm. How to put that in better terms? Yep there are no better terms then HOT!Ok, enough of the babble lets get down to business.Cora is an amazing leading lady. Her past is intense and very sad, but she is such a strong character and you can't help but feel sorry for her and love her at the same time. She came from nothing and became something.Mace oh sexy Mace. I wasn't sure what to think of him when I started this book, however over the pages of reading I started to fall more and more in love with him. He knows where his feelings stand, but he has to be careful, especially with Cora, the poor ol' Cora, she needs a lot of tending to and Mace has to be very gentle or she may break. Some of the things that he said throughout the book, I couldn't help but laugh out loud, I even blushed (which that isn't something hard to do).Then you have Knox.... I have such mixed feelings towards him. From the time he comes in until the very end, I feel as if he is really up to no good. He is cocky and has a constant attitude and I just can't put my finger on what I really don't like about him yet. Maybe in the next book my feelings for him will become clear and I will be able to give you an honest portrayal of Knox.You then have a few small characters and they were all amazing.All in all I give this book 5 stars:1. The characters - Ms. Fay created some amazing and very well thought characters.2. The story line - is beautiful, again as the characters, very well thought out.

Vic Hayes owns her own salon and is a successful businesswoman. Hauk Michaelson runs the local bar and is a widower raising a young daughter, Sophie, whilst trying to maintain his business. He is determined to be a success for his daughter and also to never fall in love again after loving and losing two women both in tragic circumstances. Vic and Hauk are best friends, she has stood by him during the good and bad periods of his life, she is terrified that admitting to her feelings for this man might ruin the perfect friendship that they have. Until they work together on the Fall festival together which effectively, with a little outside help, throws them together.There has very rarely been a novel that could make me cry. In one chapter it is steamy and straight into heart and gut wrenching in the next. Nikki captures your heart by sharing with us an essay written for a competition by Sophie, it hits the soft part in your heart, thus putting you in the position of willing the characters to explore a love that you know would be good for both of the main characters. From the moment I read the essay, with tears in my heart you find yourself wishing for them to get together and have a happy ending. After all, with all the heartache that Hauk has gone through, you turn each page hoping that things work out for him. An enjoyable read from start to finish. Looking forward to reading more from Whispering Cove.-Michelle, [...]

I was privileged to attend South Carolina State University in the early 90's.  I was a music major with dreams towards becoming a high school music teacher. But alas, life stepped in and I only completed two years before leaving. The job I took afterwards I kept for the next nine years but I will always remember SCSU. College happens during our most formative years and, for most of us, it is the best time of our life. One of the most enjoyable traits that we (as humans) share is the need to reminisce about "the good old days".For me, reminiscing about "the good old days" at SCSU consists of living at South Campus, eating at South Campus (breakfast was always bomb), meeting a charming lady who went by the name of 'Sister' who you did not want to cross but who was sweet as pie, and who always saved me pear juice. Looking out the window of the library as the Marching 101 made their way to the stadium. Having a crush in a girl named Michelle Miller (who I still can't find) and then meeting her gorgeous cousin.  The Champagne Girls (lawd have mercy!!), kicking hacky sack in front of Miller Hall, meeting Alfreda, making friends with a very promiscuous and very *ahem* endowed roommate that went to Claflin. Trips to Charleston, homecoming, our night march to the President's house, my sanctuary reading spot inside Henderson-Davis theater, the Pitt, the ATM where I could still get a $5 bill, and the beautiful, beautiful sisters.Yeah... college life was a dream and it helped mold the person many of us are today. In 'The Education of Nia Simone Bijou'  by Eric Jerome Dickey we get a small glimpse of how Nia became the sexual tsunami she is now. And like most sculptures, the beginning is always rough. In 'Pleasure' we see Nia in her full blown sexual-ness, in this short story we see how this universe of eroticism came to be.Nia Simone, how do I love thee?  Let me count the ways.  This story starts out a little like this review, with Nia reminiscing. Past conversations, past decisions, past loves, and past lovers.  Few people are born being great lovers, Nia damn sure wasn't. But like a scholar she studied. She studied because she wanted to learn, she studied because she wanted to teach.  Unfortunately, the beginning for Nia was not pretty. Funny as hell but not pretty. Matter of fact there is a scene near the beginning where Nia is learning how to give oral pleasure and... oh my god!!  This sexual experiences could easily be formatted into one of them "Do This, Not That" books because, I swear this woman...Now... although this short story is a very erotic look into the college life of Nia Simone Bijou, Eric doesn't allow that to eclipse the story.  I've said before that Eric has an intellect that is very rarely matched in modern literature. And that is not laying it on thick. I was able to read this eBook early because the publisher made it available, but I had to read it using an extremely crappy reading app (first world problem I know, so shut up). Because of this I was unable to take notes. You will not have that problem and I envy you. There are so many intellectual one-liners and snippets of conversation that you wonder if you are reading a short story about modern philosophy or a co-ed sex manual. Lucky for us it's both.Who else can talk about macro sociology, Jesus, Sylvia Plath, and the Book of the Dead all while naked after sex and just before another round?  I can think of two, maybe three authors who could pull it off.  Eric is one of them. Make no mistake, Eric's books are as sexual and carnal as they come, but reading Eric's books only for the sex is like driving a Jeep only because you can sit high. You're missing the point.As the sensual awakening of Nia continues we're given hints to something else. Nia is taking us on a lustful trip down memory lane, but what is causing this to begin with?  One woman, Siobhan.  One small hiccup.  And strawberries.  Want to know how good this story is?  I wanted to eat strawberries and I don't even LIKE strawberries!!  Eric paints a story so vivid that he made me crave something I don't even like. Damn.While Nia is on this journey she is surrounded by her friends (lovers) that are, at times, interchangeable and they add yet another angle to this literary orgy. I think the lesson learned here is that no matter how strong our convictions, it all means nothing if you're horny. Yes, Nia and her friends are extremely intellectual, but the same blood that fuels their brain also fuels their lust. That same need to understand Henry Miller is also that same need to understand why your body is still shaking ten minutes after your orgasm. You can't be Type-A in the classroom and Type-C in the bedroom. No?  Don't think so?  OK, ask any politician. Or sports star. Or your preacher.'The Education of Nia Simone Bijou' is a lusty, exciting voyeur into the beginnings of a woman for whom sex is a beginning, a sport, a past time, a need, a want, an exercise, an itch, an experiment, a release, a desire, a crutch, a strength, a pro, and a con. 'Decadence', the sequel to 'Pleasure' featuring Nia Simone will be out in April. This short story is the perfect appetizer to feed your Nia habit until then.
summary: Nia Simone Bijou is my girl... (I wish)

Yes, Sade's lyrics could be Julian Savant's soundtrack.  I will be revising my review as I'm sure most here will.  However, my first scandalous read was Tattooed Moon by Tiana Laveen.  If you know of her work, you know that it was a lesson within a lesson wrapped in all consuming love.  I can never say enough about how she transports you to the scene and sits you at the table to watch, feel, smell and taste the story as it unfolds.  Like you are an invisible being eavesdropping into people's lives unknowingly.  Magnificent.  Her books are not easy reads. They are cerebral, thought provoking and often mind bending.  It may take a page or two to develop the backstory, the backdrop, complete the scene but you are not thumping your fingers and skipping pages, twisting your mouth or sucking your teeth to get there, you just get there and it is always worth it.  It's about the ride, the journey into self awareness.  I always come away thinking, man where is he?  You get a vision of what it feels to be wooed, captivated, ensnared and drowned in love and to a man that deserves to be called head of the house and ruler of your heart.  Do I trust him to know what is best for me?  Do I trust him to tell me what I need to hear to make me a better me?  Do I trust him to let me be his side kick but build me up enough as a woman to stand on my own, alone.  Tiana writes about the kind of men your father walks you up the aisle to and prays with all he has within him that this person facing him will take care of his daughter as only he thought he could.  Julian was unconventional but rare.  He was sweet and tart all at once.  His tattoos had a life and his life he decided had meaning and he knew the target at first glance.  This book deals a lot in grief and grief management, how to purge and reconcile fate.  If you ever find yourself or someone you care about struggling with the process, hand them this book, it is a manual of soul healing.  I promise you.  Don't forget to keep the tissue until much later, the tears need to wash, you need to cleanse.  Tiana Laveen is a beast when it comes to the heart.

“There’s no one to take care of me, no matter how many people surround me. I’m all I’ve got. Those words became my mantra.”I identified with Kate from the very beginning of this book. Here she is, a young woman simply going through the motions of life. She has a job as a reporter and she is in a relationship but it all seems flat and still has her feeling empty. She has lost her spark and something needs to change immediately.Kate has a few people in her corner that truly believe in her and one is her boss. He sends her on an assignment and basically says do not come back until you snap out of your funk. Kate has no idea of the adventure that awaits her.I do not know if there are enough words to truly convey how much I adore Renee’s writing style. Yes, there is a hint of insta-love, but it is quite believable in this instance. As I stated earlier, Kate is a character that I think people, including myself, can identify with. Without telling too much of the book, she has begun to settle and we get a front row seat to see her realize that she deserves more out of life and her relationships.And, Jamie!!! Oh my, what a leading man!!! I don’t do the whole book boyfriend thing, but if I did, he would be in the running. He symbolizes the very basic thing we all want, whether we are a man or a woman: someone to see beyond the exterior and what’s on paper and to see us for us and who we are at our core.Kate and Jamie’s story has a little bit of everything. There is a little drama, there is some sweetness, there is some sex, and there is plenty of humor! Nowhere But Here is one of the best books I’ve read so far in 2014!!!

3.5 STARS"I'm too old to believe in fairy tales, Gareth," she said quietly. "And my kids are too young to have to stop believing in them."Setting aside the dialogue that tips the cheesy scale a few times too often, the severely dated character details on the hero (because, seriously, what man can pull off a ponytail at 42 in 2013 and not get any grief?) and the pathologically stereotypical plot progression…This was a pretty decent read.This was, for all intents and purposes, a fairytale story between 42-year old Welsh actor Gareth Connor who suddenly finds himself in a small town in Ottawa falling in love with 35-year old single mother of 3 Gwynneth Jacobs and her baggage. Except Gareth has his own kind of baggage not including the silly double Gs between their names.The plot is so familiar I may or may not have watched a Dennis Quaid movie about it and yet, I couldn't help but be utterly charmed by the unassuming delivery of the story. There are a lot of soapbox-worthy issues here that were foregone in favor of the uncomplicated storyline which I really REALLY liked. Not every story about a single mother finding a second chance at love need to be an opportunity to celebrate feminism and I'm happy that the heroine in this one was likable enough on her own to not need any of that added flavor. Sometimes I just want some fluffeh adult-style and this one pretty much brought it.I may hate her name a little but as a heroine, Gwyn was pretty awesome. I'm not a parent, but I find her dealing with the difficulties of being a single mother of three realistic and utterly refreshing. The attraction between the protagonists may be instant but the progression of their relationship was believably paced. And while the conflict between and within the characters were hardly original, I liked how it was handled logically and maturely.The ending was a bit contrived and felt a bit too cinematic. Airport chasing followed by the chaser finding the chasee waiting at home with the ex, the long lost daughter, the best friend and the kids could easily be the end to any Sandra Bullock movie. Hmmm, now I'm beginning to wonder if this was a 90s Sandra Bullock movie with Dennis Quaid, but I digress. Gareth's dialogue could've also reined in the cheese but then he's an actor so I'm giving him a pass. Though I can imagine Katie (Gwyn's eldest) snarking against it a few years down the line.I do wish the author would update some of the character details, and twists on this one. I think it was published first in 2010 under a different title but something about the story screamed 90s to me. Because some readers may be turned off by the dated feel of the story and miss out on the enjoyable moments this book did bring.ARC provided by Michem Publising thru Netgalley in exchange for an unbiased review.
