Moscow Dreams by Julia GoussevaIt's 1991 in the city of Moscow and simply put...fourteen year old Marina has a dream.  That dream is to pass the college entrance exams in two years and to be accepted into the Moscow State Linguistics University.  There is an equally important dream in her plans. Marina would like to "travel and see the world just like her father, Vasily Fedorovich", a cameraman. He has just spent two weeks on the job in Tibet. Upon his return, he shares a vial of sand which is a gift from a beautiful sand painting created by Tibetan Monks. It seems to signify the impermanence of life similar to sand sifting through ones fingers as Marina's grandmother explains. On the other hand, Marina's mother Vera Nikolaevna, has never had the opportunity with her job as an engineer to leave the Soviet Union.In order for Marina to fulfil her dreams, she has every desire to master the English language. Being fluent in the English language will definitely open up a whole host of opportunities for Marina. Her parents are encouraging her in this endeavour so that she may broaden her horizons and experience life outside of the Soviet Union.At this point in Marina's life, she appears to be no different than her teenage friends. She has every desire to move out of her comfort zone and make her college years memorable and exciting. However, a drastic change in the political climate is unfolding before her very eyes. On the way to meet her friend Nadia, Marina notices a huge tank driving down the street. This is unheard of at this time of the year as tanks are usually only visible when there is a parade in May...that is nine months away.  She pays little heed and continues to make her way to her rendez-vous with Nadia.  After they've enjoyed a meal at the new McDonald's, they soon encounter several more tanks. Both Marina and Nadia are curious about this odd activity and by asking a few questions, they quickly learn that there has been a shift in the political and military power of the country. An unlawful coup has been created called the State Emergency Committee that believes in the previous hard line philosophy of Communism akin to Stalin's era.  They are in the process of trying to usurp the power of Mikhail Gorbachev, legitimate President of the USSR with his democratic ideas. When Marina and Nadia make their way to the Parliament Building to listen to Boris Yeltsin address the crowds with his beliefs of democracy and freedom and the unlawful confinement of Gorbachev, he appeals to the Muscovites to stand their ground and support their leader.  Marina is angered as she sees the possibility of her dreams going by the wayside...Within a few weeks and soon after Marina and Nadia attend a new school in the fall, life seems to settle down.  However, Marina is focused on other important quests while Nadia is spending a great deal of time with her new boyfriend, Stanislav. Marina is also intrigue by Nikolai, with his brilliant mind and his desire to dream and make a difference especially when it comes to Communism and its lack of freedom and democracy.In reading and reviewing this incredible novel, I could go on and on about its merits. It is a fictional novel, a wonderful history lesson, and a story about blossoming young romance all in one.  Talented Author Julia Gousseva has done a brilliant job of embracing both fact and fiction in order to entice her young reading audience. This delightful novel will be of interest, not only as an educational tool, but also as a brush up history lesson for those of us that lived in this era.  Even much more than that, she describes the lives of two typical teenage girls and boys in Moscow and how different their long term goals are, yet very similar in other respects, as they dream of their individual futures. "Moscow Dreams" will touch the heart of its reading audience as it reaches out and informs others of life in other parts of the world.  There is always a price to pay in order to achieve freedom...to dare to dream...and to accomplish those dreams. As Author Julia Gousseva so adeptly states, when people begin to have choices, these choices can result in "more responsibilities, successes, and failures". Our world would never evolve or grow without taking risks and this can certainly create feelings of uncertainty. However, Marina and Nikolai in their innocence and exuberance soon realize that it is a risk well worth taking!Inspirational Author & Book Reviewer ~ Dolores AyotteI'm Not Perfect and It's Okay

Review for Ramblings From This Chick. ramblingsfromthischick.blogspot.comBurning Down the House was the first book that I have ever read by Allie Gail, and I absolutely couldn't put this one down! It kept me awake until the very early hours of the morning because I absolutely had to keep reading. I enjoyed this story so much, and I can't wait to read more from Allie Gail. This book was the perfect combination of sweet moments, steamy scenes and enough suspense to keep you turning the pages. I am definitely a new fan of Allie Gail's, and I really enjoyed her writing style.When Sara moves back with her father, she never expects to end up sharing her house with the creepy goth kid that was her father's best friend's son. After his parents died in a questionable house fire, her dad took Rob in because he had nowhere else to go. But when Sara shows up, Rob is no longer the same goth kid dressed in black but now is a super hot football stud. Only problem is, Rob still has a major attitude problem and Sara has no idea why he hates her so much. Even though they barely talk and when they do its only to argue or insult each other, the attraction between them is undeniable. However living under the same roof, they begin to get to know each other and the more they are around each other the more their attraction and feelings grow. Unable to fight the passion that is growing between them, Sara and Rob finally give in and are soon together. But when another house fire happens killing a girl they go to school with, Sara begins to wonder if maybe she is dating an arsonist.I really liked Rob. I didn't understand why he was so rude when we first met him, but I did get that he had been through a lot. As his past is revealed though, you really get to see just how much he had to deal with and why he was the way he was. I really liked how he was with Sara though, and I thought that he was really funny and sweet. He was also protective and possessive of her, but it was in a way that was really attractive rather than being overbearing. I liked that he wanted to take care of her and look out for her. Sara was smart and funny also, and she was also really nice and kind. I loved how she kept trying to be friendly even when Rob wasn't very receptive at first. I also really loved how sweet she was with Peyton, the little girl that she babysat. She was always thinking of others, and it was really nice to see a girl that I would actually be friends with and that didn't annoy me. I thought that Rob and Sara had a really great relationship together, and I loved watching as it evolved and happened naturally rather than instantly. I liked that they took their time and that it wasn't rushed at all. It made what they shared real and believable. They were also really hot together, but it was so much more than just steam. They really belonged together, and you could really see the love they shared. I just really adored Rob and Sara as a couple!Overall, I thought that this book was fantastic. It was so much different than anything I have read before, and I liked that it was something completely new. I loved all the twists and turns, and I will admit that I honestly didn't have a clue what would happen next. I had no idea who had done what, and this book was impossible to put down. I had to keep reading to see what would happen next, and I loved every second of it. This book was one of the most well written and entertaining books that I have read in a really long time. I highly recommend this book to not only New Adult fans, but also Romantic Suspense fans as well. This book is one that you definitely won't want to miss out on. I look forward to reading more from Allie Gail in the future and can't wait to see what she writes next!**Complimentary Copy provided by Author**

After reading The Trunk Key, a taut, suspenseful Kindle Single, and Love is Strong as Death, a spooky supernatural serial novel, I was sold on Carolyn Nash's writing, so when she invited me to review her latest work, Phoenix Heart, I gladly accepted. It's a marvelous romantic thriller about graduate biology student Melanie Brenner and her heartthrob professor, Dr. Andrew Richards, a rising star in the field of developmental biology. Accused of blowing up his own laboratory in order to cover up his failings, Dr. Richards and Melanie are soon running for their lives from professional killers, trying to stay alive and to find the evidence to prove who really planted the bomb in the biology lab. Building up to the dramatic climax, Melanie's loyalty to Richards is tested as the killers who are after them close in, and her feelings for Richards intensify. Is it love or just a student's crush on her professor, and will the two survive to find out?I liked the author's breezy writing style, with likeable characters who could be funny in serious - often deadly - situations. It was also fun to watch their feelings for each other blossom into a full-blown romance during the story. Phoenix Heart was an enjoyable, heart-pounding suspense thriller with a very satisfying ending.

reviewText: Like with all reviews I do that follow a series, please do not read if you have not read the previous books. But the final thoughts of what Kane sacrificed for them weighs heavily in the small confinement. Now is not the time to lose herself to his memories...now is the time to fight. And fight they will.**I could cry later. I could mourn Kane later.First I had to get the people I loved, the people that were still alive, to anywhere but here.**This episode was the most action packed yet. Probably of both seasons. My heart is still hammering in my chest. There were times just knew that they were not going to be okay. That too many close calls were going to be final calls.I hate coming to an end of a series that has encroached on my heart, my time, and my emotions over the past few months. The only bright side of the series ending is that it will be back by the end of the year.Season Two was the group facing a new threat. Humans. Alive Humans, Humans whose souls were so perverse that the zombies were never really the threat. With this season over, I look forward to the new dangers the group will possibly face. Same characters, new troubles.Well done Higginson. I look forward to where your imagination will take us in season three. I look forward to new people and *fingers crossed* to renewed love. I just look forward to it all...most of the zombies. 5 Why Do Things Have to End Stars!
summary: Sad to see the season end...but looking forward to more next season!

"Love is an earthquake. It comes when you least expect it. It shakes your foundation to the core.It rips the ground clear away. Right out from under you. "Just reading this line in the beginning of the story was enough to tell me that this book would be different.  It is not your typical love story.  Sisters who both want the same guy.  A guy suddenly torn between them and completely undecided.  Betrayal.  Unrequited love.  Pain and Heartbreak. The joy of a love meant to be.I immediately fell in love with this story!  How many of us have pined over an unrequited love?  Lia fell in love with Grayson when she was fourteen.  Unfortunately, several years older than her- he saw her as a friend and fell for her older sister.  For years, Lia watched Alex (her sister) and Grayson's stormy relationship all the while hiding her own feelings.Just when she feels that she is finally over it and has recovered somewhat from the pain of this love- who shows up but her sister & Grayson- ENGAGED..  Seriously people, this was a complete WTF moment.  Poor Lia, how much more can she take?  Imagine everyone's surprise when Grayson finally notices that Lia is no longer the 14yr old tomboy but now a pretty sexy grown woman.The torment of their attraction, is breathtaking.  Lia is pulled between the love she's always felt for him yet not hurting her sister, while Grayson is pulled between his passion for Lia and being the man who doesn't leave but stands firm in a relationship..  Sophie created an amazing story that will stand the test of time.  A story of love, desire and the bittersweet joy of finally getting the man of your dreams.  Just writing about it, pulls me back in and makes me want to laugh and cry at the same time.  I am anxious to see what Sophie comes up with for the next in the series!  Be warned- this book is going to cause you to go thru a lot of emotions.  Anxiety, betrayal, heartache..  Sometimes there is a second chance, make the most of it when you can!5+++ Stars!  I can't say enough good things about this one!

Cory’s sister worked at a strip club and was murdered. The police have not found the killer so she goesundercover at the club as a waitress to see if she can figure it out. She finds some people that she bondswith really quick. Others that are really shady. Some that are high on her suspect list and one she just can’tget out of her head no matter how hard she tries. If she wasn’t trying to find her sisters killer she would reallywant to explore Jason. But she needs to be focused right now.Jason is in law enforcement but he is currently on a break from work. He is helping his cousin out. She wantshim to try and find out who is killing the strippers in her club. He can’t seem to keep his eyes off of the prettynew waitress. She calls to every protective instinct that he has. He knows that she is hiding something. Everytime that they are alone he can’t keep his hands off of her. What will happen when the killer decides to target Cory?My Opinion:  This was a very short story but I thought that it was really great. It was well plotted, well writtenand drew me in from the start. I liked the characters. I liked the love/hate dynamic with Jason’s cousin and herex. I can definitely see myself reading more from this author and I highly recommend reading.‘Read and Reviewed by LSK Sweetheart Reviews’

Can't get enough of this series or writer. Enjoyed the basic story and it moved along well.Hoping for another in the series to finish off the romances. Do they ever find the other Mors? Does the traitor turn again or even admit to her past life, and crimes. Does the possible war of the future, come to fruition. (from the regent's [queen] helper that the queen gave instructions to.) Does this happen in a few thousand years or not? Is there another prophecy? Do the White & Black Dragons come down to fight for themselves at some time?We need another set of books in this series to carry on. It's too good to stop now.

Imagine traveling around the world and tasting coffee in a variety of locations. That is exactly what Serge Remy does and he tells his stories very well. I love that this book is not just researched on the Internet, it is the story of one man's personal experience. This book is filled with original thoughts and explanations of how coffee is served in many different countries.You will find out what is in Sicilian coffee, read about wild tigers roaming around coffee plantations and discover what it is like to go to a crocodile farm. I also didn't know there was a coffee-themed Disneyland. Who also knew there were coffee pots made of gold?Along with lots of pictures there is some history and some humor. You will also learn the origin of the croissant. Since the best coffee I've ever tasted so far comes from Hawaii I was eager to learn about coffee in various countries. I enjoyed this book and hope to read more by this author.~The Rebecca Review
summary: Stories of Coffee Around The World

reviewText: Dom Wars was a breath of fresh air in the BDSM genre. It seemed every author dabbled in BDSM erotica after the FSOG craze and unfortunately with little experience or knowledge of the lifestyle.In Dom Wars Lucian Bane shows a side to BDSM that isn't all about control, power and punishment. He focuses on the trust and emotional aspects of the lifestyle. This book gives you a true recollection of a D/s type relationship in such an entertaining way that I think you would enjoy it even if BDSM is not your normal genre.I love the reality tv theme in the book, it adds so  many plot twists it is as if you are right there with Lucian & Tara on their journey to win. Another thing I absolutely adore about this book is the strength and determination that Tara has. While she may be a bit naive in some things she is no way weak or lacking a mind of her own.Lucian Bane took his experience in the lifestyle and created a masterpiece of words that can enlighten people that a D/s relationship is about protecting, cherishing, trusting and not all about Dominating, punishing, controlling.Give it a chance, what do you have to lose?

I currently have more than 20 eBooks on my hard drive, and most of the time I keep starting a book here, a book there, and then taking weeks or months to finish because the stories just can't sustain my interest. This was the first book in I can't even say how long that I read in a single sitting, even though I stayed up until nearly 2:00 am to finish it. I kept wanting to find out what happened next until I was at the last page.I do agree with some of the other reviews here that it's not perfect--Flynn's sexuality is a bit ambiguous and the sudden twist caused by the (alien? magic?) piece of technology felt a bit odd a choice given the larger plot arc of the hunt for a killer. That said, I really loved the way the author handled it. It wasn't that the powers or even Flynn's reaction to them were particularly unusual, but rather the way that the author portrayed the real-world ramifications of having these exceptional abilities. I didn't envy Flynn one bit and I doubt you will either. I also thought the way the two agents' dealt with each other and Flynn's new powers was brilliant and indeed ended up being my favourite aspect of the story.I was also impressed with how well the author showed that being gay, even in San Francisco in the new century, is far from all sweetness and light. Parker's loneliness and gritted teeth-endurance of the constant low-level homophobia felt painfully real. The leitmotif of everyone thinking that Flynn and Parker were already in a relationship was both funny and uncomfortable for much the same reason. That added unexpected and admirable depth to the story.It seems obvious that there will be a sequel, and I'm looking forward to it. I want to find out about that superpower zap device, and the agents still have two murders to solve. :)

The storyline has been sufficiently outlined by other reviewers. Suffice it to say that the author does an excellent job of engaging the reader and creating a did-he or didn't-he kind of drama regarding a star-struck young girl who longs for a wisp of glamor to remove her from a somewhat drab existence.There are multi levels of a play-within-a-play as Jessica seeks to find meaning in her life and enacts a fantasy that has captivated her. Not understanding the educational levels in the British system, i was surprised to learn from another reviewer that she was (only) seventeen years old. An extra star for a typo-free text!

Loved it, loved it, loved it. I'm a sucker for these sorts of sweet -with a touch of spice- stories, and a lover of power-play between characters so this story was addictive me. I read it in one sitting. For lovers of shifters and beam
This was just ok for me.I liked the first book better but this was good to.I would recommend this book.
Such great characters and too short an airing for them.  This is one shorter story that should put on long pants and become a longer story

reviewText: Wow!  I received an ARC copy for an honest review and can honestly say - Wow!  This is the first book I have read by Michelle Fox and it most certainly won't be my last!  I loved that the heroine Audrey was a full sized woman and a little self-conscious about her weight.  She was a thoroughly likable character that you felt was voluptuously beautiful.  Tao, our werewolf hero, was exciting, sexy and hero worthy!  I thoroughly enjoyed Audrey and Tao's story!  Not only was it a steamy romance, it was an intimate look at werewolves and full of werewolf conflicts within a pack!  This story had unique action moments that were totally unexpected and I thoroughly enjoyed!  If you love steamy paranormal romance, action & adventure, you will love this book!  Michelle Fox has been added to my MUST-READ list of authors!
Lexy, Nana and Sprinkles are always a delight. and Jack is delightful mental eye candy. Good mystery, fun plot.  good easy fun read

Nothing too heavy or too involved in the occult, Treasure of the Jaguar was a fun read! I thoroughly enjoyed it! The author did a great job of keeping me, the reader, involved without being overly wordy.  Sometimes I just enjoy an easy, fun and enjoyable book rather than the more involved, stressful type of plotting book.  Again, if you are ready for some fun, here it is!

This is now my favorite book in The Last Rider's series.  I waited anxiously for this book to be released, and I am not disappointed.  Shade's and Lily's story was so full of frustration, doubt, dedication, possessiveness and love; I enjoyed every minute of it.  This is a book I'll be able to read over and over again.
So good! Malcolm and Red are my new favorite couple. I couldn't have asked for a better story. Read this book in one day.

This brief but compelling set of stories about those who are HFA and maintain their jobs and lifestyle nonetheless was eye opening. I suspect that a few of my friends are HFA. The author's narrative comments helped me understand the dynamics of the alcoholic's approach to everyday life that much better. The author makes the point that half of all alcoholics are actually high functioning and tells a variety of stories about them (e.g., the nurse who drinks rum and coke during slow periods on the job) as well as those who live with them. I appreciated being able to examine the issues from a range of perspectives. I also thought the practical advice about how to beat the problem was more than worthwhile. Good information and clear.

A sweet story about finding real love.  Emmy has wonderful friends. An amazing little boy.  Success in her work.  She puts everyone’s needs ahead of her own. She is resolute that she doesn’t have time for love.  And that she is not anyone that would have love.Grady is new to town.  Out of an ugly relationship, and recent injury, he is not looking for love.  Once he sees Emmy all bets are off.I love alternate POV books.  Being able to know what each character is thinking- perfect!  It also makes me want to shake them when they misunderstand or jump to conclusions which all of the characters do in this book.The steamy factor- wow!And there is some intrigue- nice addition and well written.The ending was a little rushed but they get a tender HEA- and isn’t that what we all want in a romance??  Looking forward to reading more from Amber.

When it comes to being a positive thinker, Stephen Williams is able to show why you should think positive and how positive thinking can benefit you.  This book teaches the importance of being positive.  It shows how people can accomplishes their goals and dreams as a result of thinking positive.  Stephen Williams is able to make sense of the impact of positive thinking.  He found a way of making his book so easy to understand that it is a great benefit no matter who the reader is.If someone wants to accomplish great things, they should not think negatively about the accomplishment, or what it takes to get there.  A person should think about what it will take to get there and hold on to each of the smaller accomplishments along the way.  Simply put whether someone thinks they can do something or they think that they cannot do something, they are right.  If a person thinks that they are going to fail a test, they will self-sabotage themselves by methods like not even bothering to study.  If a person thinks that they will pass the test, they will study and do whatever is necessary to be able to pass the test.Stephen Williams did a good job on making this easy to understand, but the information seemed to be too drawn out.  The information could have been condensed, but overall was very informative and to the point.  Stephen Williams was able to give people a good reference in positive thinking.
summary: A good reference for positive thinking

reviewText: I enjoyed this story, it was gripping enough to keep me reading until I finished (mainly to see what happened next); more for kids though I think. It was much like another story I read where something caused people to go underground for years, then "accidentally" find out it's safe to be above ground. This is not the type of book I usually like, but it was well written and engaging.  Very few grammatical errors, which interrupt the flow of the story.  It was obvious who had attacked Ruby with the crowbar, but the ending was still a surprise.

Brian Springer has written a well crafted novel if you like fast paced thrillers you will love this book and the main characters Kelton and Jessica both have a lot of spunk and the ending is a real surprise great read.

Lydia is almost forty years old. It's been a year since she and Douglas had divorced, Tiffany Douglas's new wife, was years younger than him. That's what had hurt the most, Douglas telling her he no longer found her sexually exciting, so he had replaced her with a younger woman.Lydia's BF Saffron has insisted that she come on a night out instead of moping at home. It's at the bar that Lydia meets Tristan, he wants to buy Lydia a drink. But she refuses, he can't be more than twenty five. But once back at home she begins to regret her decision. He might be a lot younger than her. But he had looked at her as though he wanted her.Lydia works part time in a book store, this is where she meets Tristan again. But this time when he invites her out, she readily accepts.First read for me by this author. I really enjoyed it. I loved Lydia and Tristan they were easy to relate to. There are quite a few hot and heavy sex scenes in this, but this is a very romantic story. Tristan has a secret, but it's very obvious what it is. But I did like the ending it was not what I expected.

The previous book I read by Mari Carr - "Covert Lessons", published by Ellora's Cave - was terrible, so I didn't go into this one with very high expectations. However, this book was put out by a different publisher and therefore had a different editor. I found this book to be a great improvement over "Covert Lessons".Gwen Preston has written a popular book of sex-themed short stories called Evening Songs. One of the stories, The Darkest Night, contained scenes of BDSM and Gwen, ashamed of her real-life interest in BDSM because (in part) of a previous relationship that went bad, used a pen name for that story.Ty Ransome is a Hollywood action star who wants to turn over a new leaf and do "serious" films. He has read Evening Songs and thinks the book would make a good basis for a movie. He has also discovered that Gwen was the true author of *all* of the stories in the book. This intrigues him because he is secretly a sexual dominant. He offers to purchase the movie rights to the stories with the requirement that Gwen help him write the screenplay.Gwen comes to Hollywood, and Ty puts her up in his guest house. He begins to visit her late every night, after she is in bed, and they talk for hours. Ty makes it clear that he is interested in her in more than a platonic way. Gwen initially keeps him at bay, but he eventually convinces her that he is sincere and also that they should reenact the scenes in her short stories as a way to help them develop the screenplay. Gwen agrees. During the course of this reenactment, Gwen and Ty discover each others secrets - that she is a submissive who craves (some) pain with sex and that he is a dominant who enjoys dishing out what she needs.I liked the chemistry between the main characters and the fact that the relationship didn't start out with sex right away. I do wish that we had gotten to experience a little more of that initial phase of the relationship rather than simply being told that it happened. I also liked that Gwen has a spine. She doesn't immediately cave to Ty's desires, and she's got a few good zippy comebacks for him. Ty is good hero; he is patient when Gwen seems to need it and later forceful in way that doesn't make him seem like an ass.However, this book still suffers from some of the same basic writing problems as "Covert Lessons" - avoiding "said" as a dialogue tag (my biggest pet peeve); characters inferring the thoughts of other characters and telling the readers that, rather than the author *showing* the reader, occasional bits of stilted dialogue. The flaws are not as prevalent, though, so I don't know if it's result of the different editor, or if the author is improving her craft on her own.I might try another of Ms. Carr's books if the plot sounded interesting and as long as it wasn't from EC.
summary: Better than thought it would be

reviewText: This book has a pretty bad fanfiction and seems to like to add porn wherever the author felt like adding it. I would not read this again.

Also, not sure who sets prices, but at $2.99, you get alot of bang for your buck!I thought, kind of a cliffhanger at the end,so perhaps another story? We can only hope!

Mitch on his side is still dazzled by exotic Lewis and his manipulative personality, or was it manipulative Lewis with exotic personality? reviewText: As the story begins, Pike Logan's newly formed Taskforce, is on a training exercise in Charleston. The training involves committing an actual burglary and avoiding arrest. All without any sanction from the 'authorities'-because they are an off the record group.The new Taskforce is called upon for an urgent mission in Yemen, ready to go, or not to perform. Not all members were 'ready' and the mission goes south.I know this was a short story to give a little background on the Taskforce, but it was too short to do justice to the author's talent. A bonus at the end is an excerpt from the next full size novel, Enemy of Mine!This copy was provided by NetGalley and the Penguin Group in exchange for an honest review!

Talker is a lyrical story filled with pain, anguish and love. Talker is a short story by Amy Lane about two unlikely friends: Tate "Talker" Walker and Brian Cooper. The two young college men meet during a track team bus ride and become fast friends and why not? They are both hiding secrets from each other and themselves. Tate is a talker with a quip for every situation, thus his nickname. Behind his bad boy rocker facade, he is hiding a lot of personal pain and fear of rejection. Brian is hiding too, but he's hiding behind a facade of "normality". He has a stream of faceless girlfriends who come in and out of his life, but don't mean anything to him. It takes one of those girlfriends to wake him up to some realities about himself.Amy Lane's Talker touched me with its fluid language, which is almost poetical at times. While reading the book, I had the feeling that I was listening to a poet. Reading Talker was my first experience with Amy Lane's writing. I plan to enjoy listening to this voice in the future. I read constantly and it's been a while since a book warmed me as this one did. This one is definitely 5 stars. I can't wait to read the sequel.

Zombie RunAmucks are just not high on my to do list when looking for my next "must read".  I try to read some classics, some best-sellers, local writers, historians, and everything by a handful of favorite writers I have met or gotten to know in other ways.  SciFi is rarely me.  I get Orson Scott Card's stuff because he's local, you can ask him questions in the carpool line at school and he doesn't treat you like a dink...and he is descriptive.This story hit on my high points...avoid excessive blood and guts.  My imaginationation fills in the empty places well enough, thank you.  Assume communications will be less than perfect.  I hate these weather people who must be beachfront for a category 5 hurricaine making shore.  Uh...It will be wet, windy, above normal high tides, stuff will be flooded and utilities are expected to fail.  Get to higher grounds with more evacuation routes, access to medical centers and backup plans for these events.  Don't fly a kite on the outerbanks where you need a MILESLong bridge or Coast Guard run Ferries to get you on/off that strip of sandbar...when you know bad stuff is headed in.Props for a love story/family caring...instead of brutality being the main course.  This brought back memories of tracking family on 9/11.  My church lost a flight attendant in PA.  My sister had been at meetings in the Pentagon that week.  My best friend lived in a commuterberg for many in NYC.  I attended her close knit church on visits North.  It was days before we knew travelling coworkers were safe, and weeks before we knew how we could help the faith community of this small town.  Our characters are too fresh to their pain for these questions to even hit them yet...Much less where does that sports career playout now.I really was drawn in and look forward to more.
summary: I had my doubts...but was won over.

reviewText: Pearl is raised by a woman who is teaching her how to live in the "units", which every child goes to when they turn 13. Once Pearl gets there she realizes life is not all sunshine. This is an interesting story line that pulls you in and you are sad to see it end, which it does and quite abruptly. This book reminds me of the Hunger Game series. Great read, I just wish the ending didn't leave you wanting more, but the author did her job "hooking" you.

The first book "Jingling Our Change" was a bit better. In spite of having some slow spots I did manage to finish "Nanny State". This in itself is a recommendation and is more than I can say of several samples/e-books I've read lately. The scenario is certainly possible, perhaps not next year, but eventually. The characters act as I expect most people would act (and do act now). Some dither and say "It can't happen here". Others are more proactive. Decisions, decisions! I do wonder where the author will go with the plot in the next book, so I'll buy the next one too.
summary: A little slow in places, but...

reviewText: The story is definitely a unique twist on a fairy-tale king line, and the plot and characters are easy to follow and relatable. Very reminiscent of The Prince and the Pauper.While overall an enjoyable read, I felt as though the beginning of Paul's journey from urchin to royalty could have been paced a bit better. It was as though it had come too easily, and at some of the turns, there was a bit too much exposition.Nevertheless, a very good story, and the author makes it work.
Why pay even a dollar and clutter your kindle when ell of this is available elsewhere - and for free? Just go to the author's blog!

Gah! Clowns. Why'd there have to be clowns? I think I need to cultivate Gin's scowl to make them run away if they get too close. Or just wear a handful of knives on me at all times.So. Gin and Bria are looking for a missing girl. Bad things happen. Gin gets to kill folks. I love that part. I also love that Gin unabashedly chows down on corn dogs and cotton candy. I approve of BOTH those things. *thumbs up* all around. Well, except for the clowns. They get a thumbs DOWN.-Kelly @ Reading the Paranormal
My only complaint is that it was too short!  However, this is the first in Cash's adventures, so there's more to come!
Totally took me by surprise to find it had vampires in the story.  I hope there is another book with more surprises. I dearly loved this book great writer.

A truly steamy story about giving up control and trusting that your partner will protect it instead of abuse it, knowing that pleasure comes with a little submission and dominance but you are safe and free to enjoy it without fear that it will get out of hand.I really liked this story because it did not involve pain just mistrust and fear but with tenderness Paul shows Xander that he can let go because Paul will catch him, I will be reading this one again.
This second book and last, was fantastic!!  I highly recommend it to anyone!  I haven't read one as good as this in a while.  Great job Kaitlyn you are the BOMB!!!!!

HOT, HOT, HOT!  Black Cherry Rules. Very sexy story. The things we think we do in the dark will come to light. You might want to check out your next Lover.  What a very small, small, small world. Make sure you have a fan near by you will need it. LOL

When I first started this series a while back, I was hesitant. Not really sure what I would discover from this author. I have been absolutely captivated and drawn into all of her books especially about these three best friends. She showed us a dark side of the world by telling callies story. I had no idea how far she had planned her past to go. She was able to really develop Lily and show her healing process in this book. I had been so eager to know how these two characters could possibly find each other. I was extremely happy with how she wrote their story. I can't wait to read more from this author.If you haven't read the others in both the last riders series and the VIP room, do so before hand. You will miss the drive you get when wanting to see Lilys story.Definitely will be recommending this series.
An interesting book to take to the beach. I think you will be in love with it from page one.

There are so many diets and diet books out there that it is hard to tell what is good for you, what is bad, how much you should eat this, etc. I find it hard to understand most of them. Not this one. This was a very good book. It was very informative and easy to follow. I liked the way that it was written so it made it seem like Ms. Tomlinson was talking to me personal. It was easy to understand exactly what she was talking about. The breakdown of what different things cause belly fat and why it is dangerous; what different diseases it can cause. Then she proceeds to explain what can be done about it. The changes needed in diet, exercise and stress management are discussed. It also gives several helpful sites to visit for more information. This is a book I would recommend to everyone who wanted to lose their belly fat forever, not just for bikini season. As I read this book, I could really relate to what she was saying. I could understand what she was talking about. My New Year's resolution was to lose 50 lbs. I really didn't have a plan yet. I do now! After reading this book, I am more motivated. I have a plan coming together. I know what I need to change and how to change it. Thank you Ms Tomlinson.
summary: Excellent Overview about Body Fat, its effects on our bodies, and what we can do about it.

reviewText: This is the definitive book on every person in management in every company of note.  Being able to recite or recognize quotes from the book is more a requirement than going above and beyond.Many of the quotes in the book are horoscope like.  They are so broad, that of course they are applicable in darn near every situation.  That being said, if you are in corporate America, being able to quote Sun Tzu is much more important that anything written by Chaucer or Melville.
summary: I assume you have read this

reviewText: If you want to plan your financial goals and want to learn how to manage your money, then this is the right book for you. It is short, simple and easy to follow guide that makes you think. I enjoyed this read! I would recommend it!

Interesting short story. Two things I wished were different was grammar and the ending. The story itself was interesting enough to overlook the grammar issues for the most part. The ending should have been drawn out, and made a little more excruciating. This is supposed to be the climactic finish and it just felt rushed the way it happened, but it was a good short read over all.

This book was not what I expected.  I expected a gritty story on a boat with a haphazard love story thrown in.  What I got instead was the story of 5 sisters who journey through life.  No one sister is given undue attention by the author.  All main characters are well developed.  We only gain insight of certain characters when necessary.  It is quite long, but needed to construct the story.  The ending and the author's honesty was priceless.

I wish all books would be written with such adorable men as Stanley and Johnny. I loved being in Stanley's mind and seeing the world opening up for him after he decided to get serious with life. Who knew that knitting would do the trick? Ha! It is really true though, that when you knit for someone, its a gift of love. I felt Johnny was not given much page-space here, that Stanley just upstaged everyone else, but that was alright, he was such a star, I just wish I could have learnt more about Johnny in the course of this book. The ending was sweet and very Hollywood but I took it all at face-value and loved it all. One of my favorite Amy Lane books.Upped to 5 stars because I have re-read this a few times.
That Maggie has the patience and forgiveness of a saint.  This is an enjoyable story without a ton of angst.  It does end in a HEA.
Excellent read, from beginning to end. You find yourself cheering outloud for Captain Hook!  Wonderful twist on one of the worlds' best loved classics.

Well-written, and excellent character development (especially for a short story).  The characters were very likable, and some were quite colorful.  The story was long enough, but be aware that it ended at 34% of the book.  Wish I had been aware of this so that I was ready for the quick ending. The story was touching and realistic.  The remainder was a sampling of another book, *The Best of Us* which I did not read.
summary: A touching and realistic story -- great character development for a short story

reviewText: Persephone(Percy) Cole is the first female detective that she knows of. Her father and uncle own a small agency and even though she has her private investigator license, she is still the secretary and research person. Then a phone call about a murder in a Broadway theater changes everything. Her uncle had died and her father is undercover on another case. This is her chance and nothing is stopping her not death threats, thrown daggers or falling scenery. This is a fun look at the theatre world and a very determined middle age woman turned detective. She is no fainting sister and nothing stops her for long. Can't wait to see what she gets into next.
I always read customer reviews before I purchase a book and I must agree this series is exciting. Love the roller coaster ride.  "Big ups" to the author this one had more pages to enjoy.

I just love the idea as presented in this book. The characters are well-rounded and interesting. There are surprises at every turn. I would highly recommend this book for anyone who enjoys a fun and we'll-developed storyline.

First off, I wouldn't really even get into the book the way I would have liked from the beginning. The writing was kinda all over the place and the imagery was lacking to say the least. Also, the story is more about HOW they fall in love rather than THE ACTIONS of being in love. Didn't even sizzle. The heroine was a little too fickle for me and he was kinda too man-whorish. Also for 27yrs old, he seems just a bit childish in character. Not because she's a rapper but because he was kind of all over the place. It was also WAAAAAY too long for me. It was kinda drawn out. I mean 90% of the book took place the first five days after they met. Now I see way she couldn't keep track of how long she had known him...I felt like it was longer too lol. Also, who really has unprotected sex with a guy from his background who you know JUST sleep with 2 people within the span of 7 days before knowing you (and no I'm not counting zebra-head). You would think that her character would be smarter than that. I mean the characters actions weren't quite as believable as I hoped for. I was just glad when it was over.
This is another wonderful book in the Cat Kimbridge series.  This a thrilling fantastical story of space battles and the brave men and women who fight in them.  ENJOY.

I loved the story.  The give and take between Sloane and Kat is amazing.  The insight into Kat's character wows me throughout the book.  That whole pool scene with the kid asking about her scars... reviewerName: The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club
reviewText: We are The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club, to know more about this book, go to the post in our website:[...]If you are interested, you can visit our website:[...]The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club's Review:"Beauty is sometimes hidden under a veil of tragedy."Review:Crossing is definitely a different book. You look at the cover and you think, wow, such a cute cover, it must be a sweet contemporary romance, for sure. Then you read the description, and confirm your suspicions. However, I was truly surprised when I knew Liam's secret, because it changes everything!This secret makes the story different and intriguing, because you don't know what is going to happen; If this secret would make Dani leave Liam or not.I never read a similar story and it was refreshing. A different story from our usual stack of books where the main characters have a perfect relationship. Because not everything is perfect in live, and relationships are no exceptions.Dani, the main characters, might cause different impressions. I really liked her. She's real and says whatever she wants whenever she wants. Like I said, real. She can talk with the guys she is falling in love with about her virtues and also talking about her flaws, fears and shady memories.She's also brave to me. Her best friend was gay and killed himself. I felt really bad for her and for her friend and also wanted to encourage her to live the way she was living this situation.She's also funny and it's not scared about Liam's personality at all. She tries to open her mind and not only being talking-but-not-accepting.Why I say talking-but-not-accepting? Because there are two types of people in this group: people who say they accept other people ideals, sex preferences, etc., but when the person who is different is a familiar or someone close, doesn't accept it. Aka talking-but-not-accepting people. Not really accepting other people, just an illusive idea in their minds to feel better. Or the other type. The ones that truly accept people for who they are.As for Liam's character, he's plain sweet. He's a nice and adorable guy that is such a great person that you must be heartless If you don't fall for him. However, he has a secret. And it's a huge one. One that you don't see it coming.In every story there's a moment when everything goes perfectly fine, that you even see the happily ever after coming and all that, and then it comes the part that I like to call: when-everything-goes-wrong. Well, in this book when-everything-goes-wrong, it's not that Liam's secret tear the lovely couple apart, but the secret not being a secret anymore. When Liam's secret is revealed to the "world", it brings consequences that makes the couple suffer. At this point, I was heartbroken. Not only for Dani, but mostly for Liam. I felt really bad and hated the people that hurt them.However, I was really happy with the ending. With a few quotes from the beginning, that reminds us when Dani and Liam met, to end this wonderful story, and make it more sweet and cute. If that was even possible.But what really got me was the fact that it's based in a true story. I loved that. Knowing that Dani and Liam's story is based in a real Dani and a real Liam, makes it all way too cute to not give a chance to this book.I strongly recommend this book to everyone who likes to read romance stories and New Adult. the romance in this book is unique and different from every other romance we are used to and it's worth it to give it a try. I think that this book also makes you think a little bit of... well, everything. Everything related to Liam's secret and having the always expected perfect relationship.That's why I'm giving this wonderful and real story a four gorjuss dolls and thank the author, Stacey Wallace Benefiel, for writing such a lovely story and Shane, from Itching for Books, for organizing this wonderful tour and giving us the great opportunity of reading and reviewing Crossing.
summary: The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club Review: A sweet and different story

reviewText: This was a great edition to another wonderful series by Caridad.  The best part about it? The decisions Michaela is forced to make result in how the flow of their relationship, and the relationship with their friends will continue.  Its not easy for Michaela because she has been alone for so long, she has no idea how to rely on someone and take others considerations before her own.  She believes that friendship and love will make you weak.  But she is a well of compassion.....and secretly hates killing.  Such a charming contradiction our Michaela, and even though it is amazing obvious that she is totally in love with Jesus, she is struggling so hard to come to terms with it.Jesus or J as she refers to him, is a power all on his own.  Totally human, but a solid support system, and all the man Michaela(and might I say any of us?) can handle.  He is loyal, loving, caring, all wrapped up in a deadly exterior package.So there are a few surprises that pop up if you have read the series...quite a few actually. The poor guy wouldn't leave if he could though, because one whiff of the pungent plant's fragrance and he was hooked. As the days progress, he finds himself in quite a "stew". The woman next door seems to have some eccentricities. Or perhaps she doesn't really live alone . . . This is another of author Jerry McKinney's well-wrought tales. But one thing is certain: You will be enthralled and entertained from start to finish!

reviewText: This is an exceptionally written book. This book, just like the two before it, suck you in and make you feel every emotion they do.  This series has caused me tears, laughter, pain, joy, and a deep frustration. I have never read a book before that has caused me to become so emotionally invested, let alone three books. You know an author knows what they are doing when you become so involved you are yelling, crying, and laughing out loud.Hadley Beckett has wanted only one thing since she met Finn Wilder. To have her own family with him. The average woman does expect a relationship to progress into a marriage and usually with children. Hadley is definitely not and exception to this. She is madly in love with her Sparks and only wants the honor of being his wife and giving him children.Finn Wilder has been emotionally scarred from the divorces all around him since his early childhood. After watching marriage after marriage fall apart and ruin the lives of so many, he has drawn the conclusion that it has to be that damn piece of paper that signifies permanence yet rips them apart instead. He loves Hadley with every breath he takes but he can't make himself marry her. He knows it will end them. So how is he supposed to keep her happy if he can't give her the two main things she wants out of life?As Hadley and Finn continue to fight their way towards each other, outside intrusions are working just as hard to keep them from one another. Will either of them be able to concede and their points and find away to make them both happy? Will Hadley get her wedding and baby? Or will Finn get his woman without his preconceived curse of marriage? Only one way to find out where Hadley and Finn will stand by the end of Igniting the Wild Sparks, grab a copy and join our friends for their journey. I am personally looking out for more from this author.
summary: Wild Sparks is better than anything you could find on screen!!

This brilliant serio-comedy has all the elements for a great mystery.  The Mary Celeste was a Brigantine set sail from New York in 1872, bound for Genoa, found near Gibraltar, deserted, with no signs of foul play.  Fast forward to 1975 and we have artistic Francine, "disinclined to share her nature with others," except sweet Vincent, a model boarder and the foil for brash Dave.  When Vincent is murdered, Francine finds herself holding the key to 100 years of mystery, and everyone from the mafia to Mother Teresa are suspects.  Francine is a dear, guileless character, completely charming whether she's singing Sweet Home Alabama while being interrogated by Scotland Yard or illustrating her masterful comics.  She's totally earnest and her "heart-on-sleeve" mannerisms wins over even the most hardened detectives, including the unforgettable Hastings, "a consummate career performer" hoping to play his cards properly and parlay a murder case into national celebrity.  This is a story with no ending, a flying machine, and ghost ship government experiments that will keep you guessing- and laughing, and loving it- until the very end.

It's been a while since Penelope Fairweather became The Dutchess of Blackthorne. Now, when she is pregnant, she needs help for the household. And who can do the job better than her own sister, Celine?Celine didn't like the life in Finnshire, it was quite boring for a young woman. So the call from her older sister came like a salvation. London was much more interesting than that village. With the younger sister Dorothy, they arrived in Blacktorne Mansion. But Celine had a goal, to find the love of her life, Philbert Woodbead, the poet, who wrote  her beautiful poems. Even when he left the village, her admirer sent her poems. But the poems suddenly stopped arriving, so Celine assumed that something happened to Philbert.Lord Elmer also stays at Blacktorne Mansion.  Well sort of. He is hiding, running away from something. He needs Celine to help him hiding, in return he will help her to find her poet. Fair trade. And the adventure begins.In the meantime, cooks are disappearing and appearing all over England, and no one knows why.I really adore Anya Wylde's stories. They are always so funny and entertaining. I always enjoy reading them, especially after a hard day at work. I enjoyed reading the first book of The Fairweather Sisters Series, I enjoyed reading  the second one too. Romance, humor, mystery, this story has it all. Fairweather sisters are so interesting characters. Adventurous, little bit naive, brave, these are the characteristics of the siblings. On the other side, there is  Lord Elmer and his host The Duke of Blacktorne,with the heart of gold and always serious face.Looking for a humorous and romantic read, with a light touch of mystery?Then this is a story for you.

This book wasn't written as a great piece of literature, it wasn't even supposed to be a great and believable romance. It is what it is -- a JOKE!I want to thank a pal of mine who pointed this book out to me and thought I would enjoy it after I had surgery. I'm sure she never figured I would actually read it, but darn it contained stuff that I just couldn't resist and I'm glad she found this for me.Dear God I hate to think of the research that Luke Young had to put up with. Every trite stereotype of the romance genre was in here and every mistake a certain type of author could make was in here, all drenched in glorious white chocolate!I have never seen so many cliches of the genre all rolled into one novella like this. I was simultaneously cringing as I was laughing my butt off while reading this.In one package we have a billionaire chocolate mogul who is also a part time navy SEAL out for revenge,he has a HUGE man part and ten-pack abs. He is also handsome and a stuttering sort of simple man who is sort of a virgin and all these traits are rolled up into our 'hero'. We also have a *itch of a fiance,a father forcing his son into marriage, a chocolate company that is going down the tubes, the best friend of the hero's deceased girlfriend who has been known to get it on with almost an entire football team...at one time, and some fabulous but unbelievable sex scenes.This made me laugh until I almost popped out the new lens I had put during cataract surgery!

reviewText: In a world where we are rapidly losing our freedom and civil rights, I found Electronic Gags to be a great concept with fresh situations that fit perfectly with current times.  It's a look at the condition of our nation and projecting where it could go in the future.  In addition to being very timely, it's a concept that will stay will you and won't leave you alone long after you set the book aside, something not every dystopian book can claim.In this story the government "collars" every individual to control their speech and force them to sing the national anthem.  You have to purchase time to be able to speak and if you run out of time the collar shocks you.  There are also certain words you are not allowed to say - words of negativity about the gov't and its leaders - and if you say them you will be shocked.  Removing the collar causes it to explode.The story is engaging and fast paced and will pull you in right from the start.  It's an easy read and most likely the combination of drawing you in and being an enjoyable read will have you dashing through the story in no time as the protagonist makes his escape and finds a way to disarm the collar.  And while one commenter noted it's apparent that English is not the author's first language, I didn't find this to be a flaw at all.  It was in fact, engaging, and I actually felt it added more realism to the story.Though the subject matter is a little dark, there is humor in the book as well and it keeps the story lively and real.  Something we all appreciate in a good story and this is a good story.  For .99 you can't go wrong.  Give this new author a try and see what you think.  Pick up a copy and take a look at the future possibility of being collared and controlled by your government.  Like I said, it's a story that won't leave you alone long after you're done.

Crossing Worlds by Zoe Saadia is the second installment of The Rise of the Aztecs series. This is an excellent historical novel dealing with the post classic period of Mesoamerican history in central Mexico.Crossing Worlds, along with Book - The Highlander, held my attention and kept me gasping for more. The author did an excellent job of continuing the story she had started with Book 1. The action and adventure is none stop and the storyline is well defined. I found it easy to put myself into the story and follow along. Each twist and turn into the story added more excitement as the plot thickens.By continuing the adventures of the main characters from the first book it is easy to follow them as they grow and mature into young men and warriors. With the author's writing style it is easy to identify with the characters , sharing their thoughts and emotions.If you loved The Highlander, you will not be disappointed with Crossing Worlds by Zoe Saadia. I thoroughly enjoyed this book and cannot wait to read more of the continuing adventures of the heroes.I highly recommend this book to all readers.[Please note: I was given a free copy of this book in exchange for my honest review.]

This is a pretty good sci-fi/futuristic romance. The author created an imaginative setting, with there being only a few things I would have liked a bit more description or explanation of. I actually think the author could take this story and expand it, making it longer and more detailed, and she would have a good series to develop.The story starts with the heroine Mali in a small village in the Barrenlands. And that's exactly what it is-  a rough, dry, hard and barren place. Here the women seem to be in charge, as they outnumber the men about three to one. Also, the population is dwindling, with few men, and most of those are infertile and/or old. Mali is a receiver, a fertile woman, one who will be bred with someone in the village in hopes of producing a strong, healthy child. I'm not sure how many receivers there are, but in the book we meet two more besides Mali.Once a woman has had a child, the village takes it from her and raises it as a community; the child is really community property, an asset to ensure the survival of the village. Mali, who does want a child, also wants a man to love. She remembers stories from long ago, from a time when the village was different, when a woman had one man, who was hers alone and who helped raise their child together, as parents. This is what Mali wishes for.Now of age, it is Mali's turn to be bred, to see if she can reproduce, and as receivers are considered holy and significant to the life of the village, Mali is a virgin, having been kept away from the men in order not to be 'fouled' by the infertile. For five years, the elders had been searching for a breeder, a fertile man. One night, a small hunting party of the men bring back a prisoner to the village. Mali is fascinated with this man right away. He is taller than the local men; he's also young and muscular and virile looking. And she realizes they have taken this man in hopes of forcing him to breed with her.The hero Jaeger is furious with these backward, ignorant savages, and it takes almost all the men to subdue him. He is forcibly taken to the council meeting where he first gets a good look at Mali. Mali thinks it is wrong what they are forcing him to do and so she is burned by his furious glare at her, all that anger and hatred stinging her. Mali reacts by refusing Jaeger, spurning him publicly. And ironically, this makes him reconsider her.Mali is punished very harshly for standing up to the council, who also threaten to expel her from the village if she does not do her duty and copulate with the prisoner. After her punishment, which was being caged for four days and nights, fully exposed to the cruel elements, with only bread and water to eat, Mali, somewhat broken, resigns herself to doing what she must to survive.There's more to the story, about why the village is the way it is, backwards and barren, about Jaeger's identity, and about how Mali and Jaeger end up and where. There were a couple times I was a bit worried about what was going to happen. All in all, I enjoyed this story, Jaeger and Mali, and the captive theme as well.

Echo Falls was a quick and enjoyable read. The book centers on two main characters, Phoebe and Aidan. This book is a book that focuses on werewolves, there are no other supernatural elements within this book. That being sad this a face paced, mystery, love story, and over all small town adventure.The book starts out with Phoebe arriving in Echo Falls, and it's quite clear from the beginning that Phoebe is on the run from something. Not only is she afraid and on the run to begin with but when she makes it to Echo Falls she is attacked, and not by any random person, but by a werewolf. Clearly this has not been the best couple of days of Phoebe. A man named Aidan rescues her, and as the story progresses we find out that Echo Falls has been falling victim to the work of a serial killer, and Aidan (werewolf cop extraordinaire) is trying to find the culprit.I think this book falls under the paranormal romance category because the really the chemistry between Phoebe and Aidan is palpable from the very beginning of the book. I do appreciate that the romantic elements did not just exploded at the beginning of the book, but rather McDougall allowed the chemistry to build and the two people to really get to know each other. The romance was more organic than just completely lust based.One of the characters I would like to mention right of the bat is Mia, she is the mean girl all of us new in high school. I don't think there is a girl who hasn't experienced a mean girls wrath at some point or another, and a werewolf mean girl brings being a mean girl to a whole new level. Mia I think is one of the more well developed characters in the book, she was the easiest character for me to paint a picture off in my head.I appreciate that the book was very fast paced, and it did a great job of keeping my attention throughout the book. Although there were several occasions where the book moved so quickly it almost felt a little disjointed. Also in some scenes where both Aidan and Phoebe were in it, it felt as if McDougall switched point of view every couple of paragraphs, which sometimes made it hard for me to follow.Another point to bring up is that the action moves very quickly within the book and because of the characters don't really have a chance to evolve or for the reader to get to know them fully. If the author decides to do a sequel there is certainly enough character knowledge in this book to build on down the line. But if this is a stand alone only book then I wish I had gotten to know the characters a little bit better.I think this is a good book for anyone looking for an urban fantasy book that is both action packed with a romantic element. I know a lot of us book readers out there love books that focus on werewolves only, and if you are one of those people then this is certainly a book you will enjoy. If you are looking for a book that contains a lot of world/character building this may not be the book for you, this is more of an enjoyable weekend escape kind of book. Overall, this is a good solid book.

reviewText: I absolutely adored the first novel in this series, Becoming Alpha, so I had to see what happened next.This novel focused on the fact that Tessa’s best friend, Meredith, has become sick because her wolf is fighting the curse that the witches placed on her. And if Tessa can’t find a way to quiet her wolf, her best friend will die. This novel takes place over merely a day, but it seemed so much longer than that. Tessa does a lot of dangerous things in this novel to find help, and with all of it going on, I found myself frequently forgetting that it all happened in one day. Erin was able to draw this day out extremely long—and she did it very well. By the end of the novel, she had me crossing my fingers in suspense of what would happen.Tessa was the leading lady in this novel, as she was in the previous one. In this novel, she comes to learn more about her witchy heritage. She travels to the coven and learns more about magic in this novel than the last. But she is also having trouble controlling her wolf—she is hesitant to shift and it’s something that she struggles with for the duration of the novel. In this novel, we really see Tessa’s selfless side—she is willing to risk anything and everything to save her best friend. It made me love her character even more.Dastien would be considered the main male protagonist in this novel. Dastien was the rock in this novel, always there for Tessa for support, even though he was dealing with the impending Tribunal. We didn’t see quite as much of him in this novel, seeing as the main focus was Meredith and Tessa. But he was there and as calming as ever.There wasn’t too much romance in this novel, again because the main focus was helping Meredith. But Tessa and Dastien did have their moments, which was nice. They got along with each other just as well as they did in the previous novel, with both of them being pretty Alpha but getting along well because they love each other. I wish there would have been more romance simply because I love this couple so much, but that being said, I didn’t really even realize the lack of it until I was finished reading: the plot was that captivating.This novel revolves around Meredith and calming her wolf. We finally get Meredith’s story about her curse in this novel, which was something that I had been wondering about after reading the previous novel. We also get a glimpse into Meredith’s love life, which was interesting to say the least. We learned a lot more about Meredith’s back-story in this novel.Avoiding Alpha was another fantastically written and engaging novel from Aileen Erin. It hinted towards the Tribunal, which is hopefully what the next installment will be about. This novel was as great read and I couldn’t recommend this series more highly.

reviewText: Marquita is another of my favorite authors and it has been a while since I had the pleasure of reading one of her books so I was definitely looking forward to Live For You. She has the unique ability to capture my interest right from the start with her characters and story lines. And Live For You was no exception.I was immediately interested in Cole and Violet. Wow...Marquita really puts this couple through the emotional ringer~especially Cole. UGH...his mother was  truly an evil bitch~that scene when she comes to the house just about killed me. I just wanted to wrap him up in my arms.  Oh...his tattoos...I loved that they were sayings and not just pictures or designs.  I just wanted to lick him all over~he was such a sexy tattooed badass!! lol ;) Marquita really got me with his character and I just loved everything about him and I was so happy with the ending and his HEA.  He need such a special heroine to take care of him and give him the love and support and strength that he had been denied and so desperately deserved. I loved that he found that in Violet.  Such a great couple. Cole is definitely on of my favorite heroes from Marquita. I only wish there was more of them because they were still so young and there was still so much story left to tell for him and Violet.  There were some great secondary characters that I fell in love with~Parker, Kelly, Wyatt, Lacie and Beau. So good!!This book is a perfect example of why I enjoy Marquita's writing so much. A great story with fun, lovable, real characters and hot, emotional sex scenes and laughter, tears, love and especially a HEA. I am so looking forward to more in this series and hopefully more of Violet and Cole.***ARC provided by Marquita Valentine~Thanks!! :)

Waking Sarah is Krystal Shannan's third book in her Vegas Mates Series. Each book can be read as a stand alone book but I do recommend reading each book in order because there are lots of continuing plots that can be confusing if you haven't read the other books.In Waking Sarah, Sarah is depressed over the death of her fiancee and she medicates herself to stop the voices in her head. Turns out she is a latent shifter and with Chris Michael's help she discovers her true self.This is hard for me to review because I don't want to spoil the story. There is a lot going on in the story line that it would be easy to spoil. I liked Sarah and Chris and all the on-going characters. The author Krystal Shannan has created a unique shifter world with fascinating characters and true villains.  All the trials and tribulations they have to go through are quite interesting but all the drama made me frustrated several times. I like drama but not tons of drama and this book has lots of drama. On the other hand, I can look past the drama because for someone like me who has read tons of shifter books, it is great to read a story that is original and different from other shifter series.I received an ARC copy in exchange for an honest review.
summary: Another great read by Krystal Shannan

BOOK REVIEW by Michelle:I really enjoy reading anything that Kirsty writes. She doesn’t disappoint.Tortured Soul was no exception. A darker read, with a villain and his minions who are pure evil.Braiden has his own sins to deal with having been raised by his stepfather, the Russian, Alexander Toropov who is on the FBI’s most wanted list. Braiden was molded to be a killer, an assassin.I had been groomed to be his right hand man. At thirteen I had made my first kill and by fourteen, I was f*&ng.; At fifteen I spoke fluent Russian and Spanish and could drive a car better than most twice my age. At seventeen I had mastered most weapons and could plan and strategize the perfect assassination. At twenty-one my world seemed to collapse in on itself and I began questioning my life.He has left that life behind him and is in partnership with his cousin Dillon at Montgomery Securities in Claymont.I really liked how Braiden was written. Braiden is a most delicious book boyfriend who is patient , caring and just growl worthy.“Settle down, Malen’kaya, I’ve got you now.”Emily left home with a dream at a young age and fell into a nightmare. Braiden and his team have come to the rescue.Emily needs to be brought back from the life she had brutally been conditioned to. Listening to Emily’s inner monologue you quickly realize how conditioned her mind was to slavery and servitude. How dehumanized she had been forced to become.There was no Emily left in Emily. Tough love had to be dealt.“I understand sin, Em, I understand what it feels like to be beyond redemption.”Jax, Charlie, Rebecca, Ella, Mercy, Eli... all have roles to play in this book. I do love having them pop into the storyline. Jax and Charlie are just cool lads. They love their women and they have big hearts.We are introduced to new characters and I think Bomber is quite a lad. The sexual banter between him and Gabriella reminded me of PJ and Cole in Maya Banks KGI series. I’m hoping we get a book on Gabbie and Bomber.Larz is such a gentleman, but I wouldn’t want to fight him. He sounds like a really cool guy that has sacrificed a lot because of his dedication to the job.I am rather intrigued about Samuel and his rather busty, lusty wench of a woman he has in tow. I’m not sure if I like her. I’m not sure I am supposed to?Kirsty has left us with ample characters that she can write a book about in this series and I for one will read them.I saw a certain movie a while back and there was a line in it that I just have wanted to hear repeated. It just sounded cool. Not sure of the copyright laws, but it was perfect for a scene in this book.“I think we need to pull a Panama.”“A Panama. A Panama?”I could so hear Bomber or Braiden yelling that out. Ha!The town of Claymont is never dull, there is always something exciting and dangerous going down, not to mention the smexi lads that reside there.I highly recommend Mercy’s Angels series.Michelle

I'd been wanting to read this book for ages because I really enjoyed the first book in the series, Rock'n'Roll Suicide. Although this is book 2 in a series, it is a totally different story, rather than a continuation, and can be read as an individual novel.Jack Lockwood is probably the luckiest or unluckiest man on the planet (depending on how you look at it). He always manages to get himself into life-threatening situations, yet he always gets out alive! This is actually one of the most enjoyable things about the two books in this series, there is endless action and tension, and page-turning suspense.In this book, Jack Lockwood finds himself falling in love with a woman, who it later turns out could have a very dark past. Or does she just look like the woman who could be a murderer? This is one of the mysteries Jack has to solve. Meanwhile, there is a contract on his life because of a book he is writing. We follow Jack as he tries to survive and also tries to find out who his new love interest actually is.As a further twist, he meets another woman who falls head over heels in love with him. Which woman will he choose?Another part of the storyline is the investigation into a spate of recent murders in Canterbury. The serial killer has been dubbed The Bible Killer. Could this serial killer be a bit closer to home than Jack first thinks?Geoffrey West's writing is addictive and I'm very happy to have discovered such a talented author. I'm looking forward to book 3.If you like traditional crime fiction you'll love this book.

Cute Polymer Clay Popsicles & Ice Cream is an adorable instructional book that anyone can follow. It teaches you simple ways to use polymer clay to make little decorative popsicles and ice cream cones that you can attach to a clothing item, turn into a magnet or find many other uses for.This instructional book teaches people of all ages to use basic supplies they either have around the house or can easily obtain at a store. It is a great rainy day activity that kids and parents can always do together in order to spark their creativity and make beautiful items that can be given as homemade gifts.Using simple language and photo illustrated steps anyone can easily become an artist using this book. reviewText: Entertaining and perversely romantic (the battle for love to overcome obstacles is lengthy and full of spirited retorts and cave man tactics) as always this book charms the reader from the first page to the last much the same way the previous books have done.  It is beautifully written with a very clever world-building more obvious in this book as it takes us back to the start before drawing us into the present to prepare for the future.  Does this sound a little obscure, confusing?  It isn't at all as everything falls into place as all our characters and not just Alia and Tristan gather to finally deal with the forces of the Dark.  It is a masterpiece of jig saw pieces falling into place as purposes begin to reveal themselves. I love the humour, the clever plot, the romantic leads and the continued foray into the world of vampires and witches who live in this incredible realm on the fringe of unaware humans.If I was to offer a criticism it would be perhaps the discussion of time.  I found Alia and her disappearance for a millennium a little jarring.  To exist for so long without any kind of relationship, and where exactly and how exactly does she survive to then reach the modern day and become famous? To not question her decision about her mate and herself and just exist?  It was too long a time away from the action and too long a time for Alaric for instance not to have caused more damage if his purpose was to rule the world so to speak, and given his evil partner it makes no sense.  How could so much go unnoticed?  The other thing is how exactly do the vampires feed, that is on whom and when?  Their mates? This would make sense but then what do the others that are unmated do?  This is never discussed and could be left alone but the book is too good to have ambiguities, or unexplained bits and pieces despite the fact that it is often a trend in the paranormal genre.  I feel strongly that the warmth and fluidity of words and plot the author brings to her books raises them above this but understand other readers may not really consider this important.I may question some things but it doesn't alter the fact that I enjoyed the book anyway, more than that I loved reading it and will wait with pleasure for the next one.  Heather brings delight and joy to the reading experience and makes us wish for more hours in the day to do more.
