reviewText: I enjoyed this book from a new author and found it to be a nice change of pace in the zombie genre.  The "Zombie Rules" are the life lessons propagated by Zach, a not so unlikely 16 year old zombie outbreak survivor.  They seem like a take off from the movie "Zombieland" but are none the less, pretty insightful.  Our first person view of Zach shows a kid who is smarter and mentally tougher than his classmates even though they do not see his brains as a real survival tool.Zach is an orphan being raised by his grandmother and he has already lived a life with plenty of hard knocks, so adjusting to the zombie apocalypse did not leave him overwhelmed.  Okay,  not too overwhelmed.  This is a kid who hardens up pretty quick once the zombies and "real" people start trying to kill him, and he is always planning ahead.  The book has plenty of surprises and some complicated characters often not seen in this genre.  I cannot write much more without risking spoilers, but this author has a nice touch at hitting the homely, everyday elements of survival that are often overlooked.  I appreciated the detail as it explains later why some characters are starving while Zach and his people are making their way just fine, but I saw some reviewers complaining about the slow parts.  Be warned, this book is not all explosions and car chases, thoguh there is plenty of action, but the author chose to actually explain how some things get done.In all, I truly found this book entertaining and thoughtful in a way not often seen in a zombie story.  This is not "great literature" but the story is well told and the editing is sufficient for an indie book.  As a final note, I saw one reviewer commenting on the unlikelihood of a 16 year old kid knowing how to raise cattle and I wondered if that person bothered to read the first few chapters describing his after school job working on a farm, raising cattle.  If you like zombie books with complex characters and intersting dynamics, do not pass up this book.

Mainly filled with one night stands, but exciting none the less.When Kathryn and Rachel meet under contrived circumstances, the attraction between them is immediate, mutual and deep. If only their meeting had been coincidental things between them may have not taken the turn for the worse it did.As time passes and attraction turns to love, will their chance of a happy ever after be lost when the truth finally comes out?A lovely well written story of a deception with a slow and tender romance burning brightly throughout. There are a number of exciting twists and turns along the way, making this book more than just a simple romance.The two main characters, Kathryn and Rachel, are fully developed and backed up by a wonderful cast of characters all essential in progressing the story forward.From the outset I felt an affinity with all the characters and their lives. Although Kathryn is closeted, married and successful, she's also a novice where love is concerned. Rachel is a bit of a player, but is also a novice at love. When these two women meet and begin to get to know one another, I felt their yearning and vulnerability shine through the pages. This review can be found at The Blogger Girls review site.I’m going to be completely honest here. Last year, I tried to read this one and just couldn’t get into it so I set it aside for when I was in the right mood. Then a few days ago, I found it on my kindle and thought, “Oh, a Derr book? Perfect!” and dived right into the story, so engrossed in it that I barely stopped to sleep.Ms. Derr tells a tale where there are many types of creatures that inhabit the world: Paladins, Necromancers, Demons, Priests, Warlocks and Alchemists. In this world, paladins and priests fight often against demons and necromancers and a different part of the country enslaves alchemists because they’re so ‘dangerous’ they can’t be trusted without a master. The story is complicated and, honestly, goes into several different directions, with twists and turns, harsh moments and sweet moments, and even has a few anxious and funny parts. I don’t want to go into detail because it’s hard to cover everything. What I will say is that this world starts off with every creature being divided and hated or feared. As the story progresses, lies are uncovered, feelings are developed and by the end, powerful forces bond together to make something that revitalized not only the people but the world. This probably sounds like a bunch of mumbo jumbo but it was an AMAZING book and had so much depth and uniqueness that I couldn’t help but love it!The novel really features only one main couple – Sorin and Koray – and how the two are opposites but have a connection they can’t break. As Sorin is the High Paladin, he’s been engrained to hate and kill necromancers, which is what Koray is. Where Sorin is light and warmth with a sunny smile, Koray is dark and cold, quick to give a sneer. Between them, there’s something deeper than just attraction but there are misunderstandings they can’t seem to work past and confusion that causes them some strain.There are other characters that make a big impact on the story, though, such as Cerant & Neikirk and Brekk & Emel. While their stories aren’t as deep as Sorin and Koray, readers should be aware that there are multiple couples and POV switches throughout the book to accommodate their parts in the story. The novel takes the reader on a journey where the Goddess is guiding all these characters into saving her people. It was interesting to see how old history was uncovered and how it ended up linking all these people together.I absolutely loved this story. It was fascinating, captivating and I honestly did not want it to end. Megan Derr has been a favorite author of mine for years now and that hasn’t changed at all. This story was just as great as her other stories I’ve read. If you’re a fantasy lover who likes some action and suspense with a dash of romance, give this one a try because I highly doubt you’ll be disappointed.

In Rescuing Dawn by Nicole Flockton, Dawn Granger has been living a monotonous life for the past two years since her husband and baby's death. She has kept away from all her family and friends saying that she is okay, but all she does is work, eat andsleep. She has no personal life beyond that, her life as a nurse defines her.Andrew Holmes used to love to sail, to the point that he left his one true love in order to sail around the world competing. But after an accident where his best friend and another member of the crew died and while he was rescued has made him change his priorities now he is a paramedic and he lives to help save the lives of others.When Dawn receives a call about a call about a car accident she expects it to be like any other night in the ER, but when she sees the paramedic trying to keep the patient alive she knows her life is about to change again if she doesn't keep tight control. Andrew left her 10 years ago and now he seems to be back, but his search for adrenaline and his call to sail may just take him away from land again and she won't risk her heart again.When Andrew recognizes Dawn he wants to catch-up with her and see if they have a chance again. In all the time he was away he never forgot her and saw her in every woman that crossed his path, but none ever compared to her. He knows that she married after he left and that her husband and baby died in an accident. But what he doesn't know is what she has been through since then and that is what is keeping her from accepting his offer to catch-up.Dawn cannot put her heart and herself up to loss or disappointment again. She knows that if she accepts Andrews offer she will risk everything she has accomplished so far, and when he leaves her again it will destroy her completely this time.Andrew will have a lot of explaining to do and also a lot of hard work ahead of him. He may want to re-kindle what he had with Dawn, but her pain has made her wary of risking herself again, and convincing her to give him another chance will not be easy.The things that both Andrew and Dawn went through in the 10 years they were apart have not been easy. But if they are to have a happy future together they must first release the demons that haunt them and let the past go.An extremely emotional and sweet romance that will break your heart, make you cry and make you smile, don't miss Rescuing Dawn by Nicole Flockton.

reviewText: I always wince a bit when I'm hit with a "buy my other books" before I even see a single recipe.There's a good bit of text before the recipes start at location 261.  There is a section about organics in general, the Naked Organic cookbooks, the invitation-only community the author is hoping to start (and I'm a bit bemused about that; one would think that one would wish the "organic is good" message to spread freely), and about scones in general.The introduction says "Discoveries have been made that show obesity, cancer and almost any illness you can imagine, all stem from not giving our bodies the nutrition they need. The cancer and obesity epidemic are pretty new to America, and in parts of the world where people live off the land, eating natural foods- those diseases are virtually non-existent."This, to me, seems written as a more definitive and absolute statement than the facts really warrant.  Granted, obesity is certainly affected by what we eat, and there has been some research into whether cancer rates are indeed rising and how linked it is to what we eat.  (There are other factors such as an increased population, environment, exposures, more sensitive screening tests, and more people receiving such tests.)I would imagine there are indeed parts of the world where obesity is not an issue.  It's the "almost any illness" and that they "all stem from" diet that gets me a bit hot under the collar.  Diet is a factor in health, a huge one, but it's not necessarily the cause of "almost any illness" and it's rarely a cure for diseases not related to the digestive process.If the author is going to make such a blanket statement, I think citing some actual facts about "parts of the world" (which parts?) where "these diseases are virtually non-existent" (which diseases, specifically?) would be appropriate."while organic foods can cost more, it's very possible to eat organic on the cheap."  I would have really liked to hear more about this rather than just a toss-off sentence.  This possibly could have made the book more than 2 stars, at least to me.I am not sure why one would need separate "organic" recipe cookbooks rather than using organic ingredients for recipes one already has on hand.  The author says one can use whatever flour one has on hand instead of spelt flour without mentioning any kind of adjustment, so it's not like that makes the recipes any different.The recipes themselves are, as far as I can tell, essentially regular recipes with some ingredients specified as organic.  This type of cookbook, to me, makes using organic ingredients seem very complicated or "different," when in reality, there's no reason one can't just use such ingredients in whatever one would normally cook.  I make "organic chocolate chip cookies" by using my old recipe and organic ingredients, for example, and I didn't need an "organic cookie cookbook" to tell me how.In fact, I noticed that the very first line of this book's description is praise from a reviewer who says she made these recipes with "regular" ingredients!Then, after reading through the recipes, I started to wonder if inserting "organic" into recipes was exactly what the author had done.  The recipe for "Prickly Pear Scones" is essentially identical to the recipe listed on Allrecipes.com for Pear Scones (note that the recipe in this book does NOT call for 'prickly pear,' but rather just a chopped pear).  The difference is that the author has inserted the word "organic" and changed the pinch of salt to a "pinch of celtic sea salt."I did spot some errors along the way."be my Scott-Irish heritage.""an after diner treat.""I'd just like to say thank you for supporting my family and I"Punctuation is also rather hit-and-miss throughout the book.There is a hyperlinked table of contents but it doesn't work with the Go To Table of Contents command on the Kindle for PC.The Traditional Scones recipe says "Feel free to add your own unique ideas to this great recipe."  Some suggestions and guidelines would be helpful to get people thinking about it.  Do some kinds of nuts work better than others?  How about adding fresh grapes and cherries, would that work?Some of the recipes have some text issues, as well."Lightly grease a baking sheet or line with baking parchment. Flour and baking powder into a medium bowl. Rub butter and sugar into flour to form a fine crumble." Sift?  Mix?  Pour?One recipe calls for 3/4 cup buttermilk and 2 tablespoons buttermilk.  The recipe says at one point to "mix in buttermilk with fork" and then "brush tops with remaining 1 tablespoon buttermilk."  Where does the other tablespoon fit in?The current scones recipe says "1/2 cup nonfat dry milk powder (You can find an organic substitute for this in your local co-op)." This seems out of character with the rest of the recipes, which simply say "organic this" and "organic that."  (I was somewhat surprised to see a reference to "apple pie spice" without the word 'organic' in front of it.  Okay, yes, I'm joking a little bit, but the word is very highly utilized.)  I also wonder what those of us without "local co-ops" should do?The Maple Oatmeal Scones call for real maple syrup (not specified as organic) and "maple flavored extract."  Perhaps it's just me, but this seems out of place in all the emphasis on natural, healthy, and organic.  This makes me suspect another recipe where the word "organic" has just been inserted before a freely available recipe.Ultimately, I don't see the point of keeping this book.  I identified at least one recipe that basically just inserted the word "organic" which (to me) doesn't make me think any of the other recipes are all that special or unique or creative.  I won't be keeping it, so my rating is 2 stars.It may be useful to someone who wants scone recipes but doesn't have them already and doesn't want to look online for free recipes.  The text expounding the organic philosophy is not worth buying the book for, in my opinion, for the reasons I noted above.

OHHH FUN!! A new suspense author for me to read!  Cynthia Hickey writes a delightful story in this first River Valley Mystery.  Marsha Steele lives at home with her mother, and her daughter.  A widow for the past ten years, she is not sure how she feels about the fact that her first love has returned to town.  The fact that he is/was her brother-in-law feeds into the fact that her feeling are muddled.His return however is not the big news in town, the big news in town is someone needs money. Actually it seems lots of someones are needing money. However how will she clear her daughter's name after she is accused in two of the thefts that have occurred in the small town of River Valley Arkansas.  A list of the suspects seems the way to begin, there is Kyle, whose sister stole money from him before she disappeared from town, then there is Melvin, Kyle's good buddy who is trying to save money to start a landscape business.  Add in Billy, her daughter new squeeze, who is really wanting to attend summer football camp, the curvy Marilyn who is a local dog walker, intent on raising money to head to Hollywood for her big break in the movies.  Another person needing money is Stephanie, the ladies ministry leader at church who is saving money to adopt a baby.  Yes lots of people need money, but would any of them steal it?  When people start dying  in town, the whole mystery takes a big shift.  Robbery is one thing, but murder, someone is desperate and the small town local Barney Fife only seems to want Marsha to keep her nose out of it all.A great story, lots of action and lots of suspense.  Of course as a suspense fiction fan, I have my idea who "dunnit" and was happy to see that I was right.  You will enjoy this book, as you follow the clues to who is causing all the trouble in town.  204 pages $1.99 e-book format 4 stars.This book was provided in e-book format for review purposes only, no payment was received for this review

reviewText: I liked this book that contained 6 short stories. They were mostly events that people would associate with the holidays, but with a twist. I wouldn't necessarily say they put me in the Christmas spirit, but they didn't make me go bah humbug either.A Time For Giving-The Binderbergs are excited to let the town cut down their big tree so it can be decorated at the Rockfeller Center. Before the town knows it, tree related incidents keep popping up, causing one cop to joke that the tree is haunted. I thought it was cute who's really acting mischievous.The List-My favorite line: "Somebody had to laugh at the geeky kid-it was a rule of the kid cosmos." Due to the Translation Effect, Toby finds Santa's liar and  looks to see if he's on the nice or naughty list. His dad had created the invention (time machine). This story was great with the setting details; I could picture the liar and his dad's work space vividly.Love Story at Gate 6B-Flight 373 is delayed because no clear landing. I couldn't really connect with any characters because no names were given. An older gentleman waits on a woman (I'm assuming his wife), then they go home.Behavior Modifications-This story was pretty cool. Casey thinks his new mean teacher Ms. Chantre is turning people into caged animals. I don't really know what it had to do with Christmas, but it was my favorite one. I loved the suspense of Casey's friends nor principal nor parents believing a word he says. It's only a matter of time before Ms. Chantre gets angry and comes after him. I liked the build-up and the twists at the end.Vanishing Skills-For the holidays, a student has a school project-interview someone. Amy attempts to interview Malachi in the park; he made magic lamps before he retired. I'm talking the Aladdin or I Dream of Genie types.No Marbles This Year-This was another one of my favorites. I loved the drama involved. Jedidiah is 10 years old and enjoys spending time with his family for Christmas, especially his granddad. The granddad gave out the same snow globes to everyone; a year later he passes away. Jedidiah doesn't understand the true meaning of the gift until adulthood.I RECOMMEND this book to read.

reviewText: Mia Asher, I bow down to your genius. I finished Arsen 2 hours ago and I am still emotional. I am emotional for all of my friends that have had miscarriages. I am emotional for all of my friends and family that have endured the pain of adultery. I am emotional from my own demons. I am emotional for Ben and Cathy's heartbreak and love. And I am emotional for Asher's loss and the world of regret and pain sitting on his shoulders. I wouldn't be surprised if Hollywood comes knocking on your door because this would be one hell of a movie.This book is raw, emotional, realistic, beautiful, sexy, hopeful, powerful, heartbreaking, soul-crushing, hot, and earth shatteringly painful. This story brings up every emotion in the human species.When Ben and Cathy meet there was an instant attraction and he swept her off of her feet. He is To. Die. For. Perfect. He is the husband we all dreamed about and the husband we all want. He would do anything for her and they are the couple that everyone wants to be."Falling in love with the wrong person is easy. Falling in love with right person is easier. But falling in love with your soul mate is easiest."However, Cathy is falling apart inside because she can't give Ben the one thing that they both want more than anything. A baby. Their baby. Cathy is broken from her four miscarriages and there is nothing Ben can do to make that pain, loss, hopelessness, and her feelings of inadequacy go away."Love can destroy you. Love can erase you. Love can heal you. Love can reinvent you. And, if you are lucky enough, love can make you whole again."Arsen is the son of the owner of the company that Cathy works for and she is teaching him the business. He is younger and a man whore....very smooth with the ladies. He is drop dead gorgeous and sexy as hell. He has a swoon worthy way of flirting with every women he comes across, basically he is sex-on-legs."It's funny that his name reminded me of fire because he certainly looked like someone who could burn you to the ground. With one look, he made me feel as if my body was burning scarlet."Arsen comes into Cathy's life after she finds out that she is pregnant for the fourth time. He comes on to her and flirts with her every chance that he gets. She makes it clear that she is happily married and expecting. They form a friendship and an emotional affair (although I do not think Cathy realized that confiding in Arsen and not her husband was opening the door to more).After she lost the baby, she went to a very dark and scary place that no one could pull her out of. That is when she turned to Arsen and their affair began....An affair that will break and destroy all three of them."Love is infinite. There is no beginning and no end. There's no starting point and no finishing line. Love just is. Love is born, grows, matures, and sometimes it dies. But the memory will remain with you for the rest of your breathing hours."So, clear your To-Read list.Put down what you are reading now.Order take-out.Put the kids to bed or take them to a play date.Open a bottle of wine or take a Xanax.Grab some tissues.And READ ARSEN!!!!!READ ARSEN!!!!!READ ARSEN!!!!!READ ARSEN!!!!!
summary: Mia Asher, I bow down to your genius.

Heather Robbins or Heath as her best friend Creed calls her is about to take a very important step in her life since graduating from high school. She's going to college at Washington University starting in four days. Creed isn't happy about Heather leaving yet accepts her reasons why she's doing it this soon. Heather isn't like most young people going off to college she is trying to move forward with her life yet shuts people out of getting to know her better. Since Heather's mom passed away she's afraid of love and friendship Creed knows about Heather. Heather has rules like don't get too close and keep to yourself. All this is about to change when she meets Nick or Hat as she likes to call him. Heather is drawn to him like no else in her whole life except for her mom, Creed, and Grandma V. Nick remains aloof to her while they share two classes together. Heather wants to get to know him yet struggles to do so because of her rules. Heather slowly lets's Nick in yet doesn't tell him the truth about her family for fear he won't love or accept her. Nick likes that Heather fixes things on her own. He doesn't understand the meaning behind the ring Creed gave her. She tells him it's a promise but doesn't explain further. Heather asks Nick to talk about himself yet he counters no promises. Heather has been in an accident and coma yet remembers dreaming about Nick. Where is Nick? Why is Creed here? How long was the coma? Why did Heather dream and think while in a coma? Your answers await you in Reflection.

THIS IS ONE OF MY FAVORITE PARTS OF THE BOOK.......... As the phone rings,“It could be Cecily,” I pled as I tried to slide off his lap echoing his groan of disapproval. I remained on his lap and strained to grab my phone. I looked at the number not recognizing it so I sent it to voicemail. “I don’t know the number. If it’s important they’ll leave a message.”I tossed the phone down on the couch beside us as he tightened his arms around me. I needed to be closer to him so I repositioned myself. What Not to Bare was a classic lesson for me in "don't judge a book by its cover". Literally. I loved the book, but I hated the cover. More on that later.Lady Charlotte is known in society as The Abomination due to her taste in clothes, or lack thereof. She's not oblivious to the fact that everyone hates her clothing, but she persists in dressing the way she wants. She's funny and self-deprecating, but sadly thinks of herself as an Eternal Burden.Lord David, nicknamed, Mister Gorgeous (Which sounds like a professional wrestler to me. Maybe that explains the cover?) has just returned from India and is eager to return. When his superior informs him that courting Charlotte is the way to get there, he is less than pleased.Both characters are used to being judged solely by appearance, but they learn quickly to see beyond that with each other. David and Charlotte are both likable. We spend time in both their heads and I found myself laughing with both of them, especially Charlotte. I adore the way that girl thinks and truly felt like her friend by the end of the book. And poor, normally silver-tongued David. He is so completely thrown by Charlotte and set adrift in her presence. His thoughts and the decidedly un-charming things that end up leaving his mouth while bypassing his brain ("You're not ugly" comes to mind) made his character so much more than just the "handsome rake who falls in love with the unexpected girl" that so often appears in romance novels.I loved this book. The cover, however, left me decidedly cold. What is going on? Is he a werewolf? A vampire? Does he just have an aversion to wearing shirts? Wait! He's got a belt! He's content to show off his shiny chest (Where is that light coming from?), but modest enough to not want to flash his lower bits.Maybe I'm so irked by the cover, just because the book itself is so charming. It was humorous and sweet, without being sappy (there were a few steamy parts).And this cover just seems...wrong.* I received this book for free from Netgalley in exchange for an honest review.This does not affect my opinion of the book or the content of my review.

I received this book for free in exchange for an honest review. This does not affect my opinion of the book or the content of my review.After reading Bound to be Taken (Emergence #1) by Becca Jameson, I needed time to mull over my review. Usually it’s pretty black and white as to whether I like a book. This time I’m finding it more in shades of gray and I wanted to properly explain my thoughts.So I’ll start with all the things I loved about Bound to be Taken. (By the way, this list is definitely longer than what I didn’t like.) First of all, it’s about a ménage a trios. I’m a sucker for ménage and this trio is hot, hot, hot.Aiden and Dane are an established couple and it’s obvious in their connection and ability to communicate. But both consider themselves bisexual so they are looking for the perfect woman to add to their life. Both men have developed a passion for domination and submission, so the woman they choose has to be willing to be part of that scene.Stephanie needs a date for a work party to prove to her bosses that she’s the right person for a promotion. She’s been lusting after her neighbors for quite some time but thinks they are gay. She finally gets to know them better after a chance encounter in the elevator and learns that they are interested in her. The three work out a trade. One of them will be Stephanie’s date while she will be their sub for a date at a party at a BDSM club.Starting four days before the party at the club, the three embark on preparing Stefanie for her role as a sub. What follows is some of the hottest sex that I have read in a while. Ms. Jameson knows just how to describe the tension the partners are feeling as they withhold orgasms or the relief when finally allowed to come.The relationship between the men was so beautifully authentic and their inclusion of Stephanie flowed seamlessly. I loved how the men were able to push her sexually while still cherishing her and treating Stephanie like a princess. The writing flowed effortlessly and I found myself unwilling to put the book down. The dialogue was natural and I could easily picture each conversation as it was happening.So you’re probably wondering why I am so torn about Bound to be Taken. It comes down to the actual BDSM part of the storyline. Dane and Aiden have only been exploring this lifestyle for six months but feel confident that they can teach Stephanie. Then instead of easing her into everything, she’s given a crash course and expected to understand and like it all. At one point, Stephanie is punished for some infractions. Aiden tells her directly “We’re exaggerating a bit on what offenses you might have committed today. But for the sake of the experience, we’re going to be harsh.” Huh? How is this safe, same and consensual?Some of the things they do to Stephanie she found degrading. I don’t understand why she doesn’t speak up or share her concerns. She is way too new to all of this to be pushed so harshly and quickly.Now I know this is fiction. That’s why I accept that she agrees to be their sub and develops the sense of trust needed for this type of relationship in only four days. It’s why I accept that they could also fall completely in love in only four days. I just wish Ms. Jameson had been more careful in her treatment of domination and submission.This is only my opinion and I still recommend that you read Bound to be Taken and form your own. It’s still a good story with interesting characters and Ms. Jameson is a good writer. I am certainly intrigued enough to read other books of hers including the next book in the Emergence series.

Being the descendant of Cain, one of the first sons and having a demon inside him that wants nothing more than to kill his brother has pushed Jax away from everyone he loves. But when Jax finds out Sam's life is in danger he stops at nothing to save her. With Sam as stubborn as before Jax finds himself spending more and more time with her, and new light shown that not everything Jax ever thought was true and that Sam's strength and love for him is stronger than he thought.As Sam and Jax start putting the pieces together of Sam's attacker Jax starts to realize that the demon living inside him isn't what he seemed to be, and that Jax is more connected to the problems following Sam that he thought. Jus Accardo did a really good job switching between Jax and Sam's characters and each time the character views switched it felt very easy and true to the characters.  This isn't my normal read but I found myself wrapped into the book and hoping what I was guessing was the story line actually was the story line. The book actually started out pretty well. But then it was like the author decided that doing things the right way was going to take to long and basically turned Melena into a simpering arm-piece for an angel.  The romance began feeling more like Stockholm syndrome, as our "heroine" had no real power in the relationship and despite hating the angel, she apparently secretly loved him.  For no real reason as of yet.  And then he forced his mark on her and the rationale was that she secretly wanted to be claimed even if she didn't consciously know it.  This is pretty much the same logic that is used to justify sexual assault.  I was so put out by the sudden shift in the author's writing, and wonder why she (or anyone) would consider this kind of relationship either healthy, romantic, or anything but disturbing.

reviewText: Today's review is on Diary of a Vampire Stripper by Cinsearae SantiagoDiary of a Vampire Stripper is a fun and snarky take on today's hottest paranormals, Vampires and Werewolves. And though it still has elements we all know and love; love triangles, battles between the two clans, I can assure you that it is nothing like anything that you have read before.Audra Perez is a no-holds-barred kind of girl who knows B.S. when she hears it, and doesn't tolerate it. So finding a job to pay for her college education was on the top of her to do list. But even she didn't know she would get a job working as a stripper at the Hoochie Coochie Club. Hell, she didn't know how "miss hairy crotch" got a job there either, but it was what it was.Audra's always had an affinity for older men, so when the handsome and distinguished Darren Von Eldon sweep's her off of her feet she doesn't hesitate to date him. (even if it is against the rules) But unknown to her, Darren is actually a vampire. And after a night of wining and dining, he turns her and then he vanishes.Left alone to fend for herself isn't an easy task, what with getting enough bird's to drink from, getting caught up with a ring of radical cops hell-bent on killing Vampires and Werewolves, and stopping a huge war from happening between the two groups of supernaturals. But when Darren comes back into her life, things just go from bad to worse.I loved Audra's spit and fire and gave her credit for not falling apart during different times in the book. And because I too have an affinity for older men, I must say that I also fell in love with Darren. I think the only character I didn't fall in love with is Paul. (You'll just have to read the book to find out why)Snarky and funny with strong female characters......who wouldn't love that?! I can't wait for the next installment to come out this winter!3.5 of 5 starsAvailable at Amazon

I always laughingly say that Stephani Hecht's Lost Shifter series is one of my guilty secrets.  I just love all the characters.  I actually read Andrew and Vapor's book first then back tracked from there.  Riley's Regret was great but also not as good as the last two.  Here's my line of reasoning....It was great because for fans who didn't like Assassin's Touch and Shane's Fury, you'll love this.  Hecht has gone back to her original recipe and this book was all about Riley and Collin. There is build up, there are secrets, and we get to see a bit of the old gang (Trevor, Gage, Noah and Ranger).  I love what's going on in Riley's head and how he's actually got quite depth and darkness in him.What I didn't like was that I absolutely loved Assassin's Touch and Shane's Fury... I adored that the story and plot line were hard core, I loved that there was so much violence and how the books weren't just centered around Shane claiming Trevor, but so much more.  I honestly was a little sad that Riley's story didn't have bigger problems/violence/resolutions.  It almost felt a bit like a filler book.  The kindle count was 159 (ridiculous!) and of course it was a novella and a breezy read.... which also ticked me off that the price tag was still sitting at $4.99.  I don't think any novella printed, and especially digital, should cost more than $1.99. But anyway, I was sad this wasn't as deep as Shane's story.Now having said that I still adore all of Hecht's works.  This one was no exception, I love her characters, her plots and especially the world she has created.  I'm also looking forward to the next book because the ending of this one introduces us to some interesting characters, whom we've never met before.  This is worth the read if you were wishing for her old formula for books back, or if you are a die hard Lost Shifter fan like me.  If you were hoping for more like Shane's books, then perhaps pass this one up or lend from a friend.  All in all I had to give it 3.5 stars because I really do love Hecht's work.  I just hope in the future the price is lowered or the books lengthened so the readers really feel they got their money's worth. Enjoy!

For just as long, Reka has lived in fear of drawing the eye of a Haloran, keeping her head down, hoping not to be caught in their sights.The only time she has ever been bold, tried to get what she wanted, a god, one more powerful, more dangerous than all others is watchingEdition Info:Kindle Edition - Published (first published December 24th 2011)ASINB006PZFWQ6In a nut shell:  I got this book from Goodreads.com as a Read to Review book. I really did enjoy the story and the characters.My Rating: 3.5/5 StarsDetails:Ok I know what you are thinking...  Why only 3.5 if you cried?  **because we all know I don't usually cry reading books** buuuuuuuut I didn't love the book... I liked it yes, but didn't love it. It isn't that it was confusing or anything like that; there just wasn't any time frame on when things happened... had Reka been there a day, a week, a month, what? I like the fight that Reka has in her and the inner issues she has throughout the book.The last thing I want to say is about the ending of this book - which absolutely gutted me... not going to even try to lie about it - I hated the ending, but it is good because it brought out the emotion I felt for the characters. I'm not the author - I don't have a say - it is hated in the best possible way.So you need to pick up a copy of this book, and once you read it come back and let me know what you think!  It is a steal for only $2.99!Until Next Time,@jendsmit

reviewText: I started Just Once late at night after finishing another book, thinking just one chapter! Six chapters later with drooping eyelids and the school run looming in just a few hours I had to force myself to switch my Kindle off.Julianna Keyes writes with ease and fluidity, imagining lives for her characters which are believable and a world which the reader would comfortable inhabit.Kate is definitely the wildcard but despite her initial aloofness and secretiveness she is a character we can easily engage with.Just Once is not without its drama as Julianna Keyes attempts to introduce several serious threads to the plot; Kate's 'story'; the money argument and video-gate, but in essence the focus is on Shane and Kate.The romance between the rancher and kitchen/cabin manager begins as hot and steamy 'just once' deal, with neither able to resist returning for more! The passion between them is fervent and Julianna Keyes' love scenes are, well . . . .WOW!Just Once is a book I could have returned to and read again immediately and I hope Julianna Keyes considers writing a sequel. A must for snuggling up with over winter!I received this as a review copy, but this has had no influence on my opinion.

The Game by Shawnte BorrisReview by Mary Beth4.75 Stars"This is a man's world."Well no one told that to Kristen Backhard. She is a sexy beautiful woman with a take no prisoner attitude which suit her just fine, especially since she is a Senior Negotiating Executive. She isn't afraid to be herself and is thankfully a strong yet vulnerable woman who is comfortable in her own skin. This book follows Kristen and her group of family and friends through what seems like a lifetime but in reality is a short blip of time.During this time we have Betrayal and heart break, Family issues (her mom is nuts), love and romance, life and death, forgiveness, some more love and romance, hot steamy sex, and endless possibilities. I found myself laughing so hard my sides hurt, envious of the love and friendship these characters have, wanting to knock some sense into her mother, wanting a twin so I could have that bond, covering my mouth in shock while saying "Oh my god!" and crying because something beautiful and terrible happened at the same time (thanks for that *sniffle sniffle*). I was emotionally exhausted by the end of this story.The only thing that I was disappointed I didn't see in this story was a conflict resolution between Kristen with the misunderstanding,  I also would have liked to have known what happened to the plane. There were also some typos and grammatical errors but it wasn't enough to take away from the story.I am very excited to find a new author that I will be following especially since there is going to be another story that follows the same group of friends. Hopefully it will be in the same style of the multiple POV's throughout the book.

Scott McElhaney has quickly become one of my favorite authors. My favorite TV show ever was the X-Files and my favorite movie is Gattaca. His brand of Science-Fiction, Time travel and speculative themes appeal to me greatly. Quite possibly, he just might be the perfect writer for my particular tastes. And as a Christian, I love his subtle and sometimes not so subtle use of Christian themes.This book falls in the latter category. I won't repeat the synopsis here, but I will say his execution was flawless. So many things examined here: Our idealized expectations compared to reality, our selfishness when faced with real adversity, our lack of faith in times of trial. Yes, this book is decidedly Christian but it has it's feet planted firmly on the earth. Spencer didn't get the Francesca he envisioned, but he did come to see her as the Lord saw her. Very Highly recommended!!!

However, after reading this prequel novella, I have a feeling The Asylum Tales series will be every bit as good as the Dark Days books, if not even better. Gage is such an interesting character, and I really enjoyed the hints into his past that looks like it will play a large role in trouble in his future. I'm chomping at the bit to discover his secrets. As far as Bronx, well he's the cool calm and collected friend that everyone should have, at least anyone who seems as prone to get into trouble as Gage is. I have a feeling Bronx will be doing a whole lot of bailing out in the future.I really enjoyed this novella, to the point where my anticipation for the first full installment in The Asylum Tales has increased tenfold. Considering how excited I already was, that is no small feat. I highly recommend The Asylum Interviews: Bronx as it is an entertaining sneak peak into a fascinating new world that will only leave you desperate for more.

Michael Bunker's final installment in his Silo trilogy, Renew, is packed full of action, drama, literary references, and philosophical ideas about freedom that you will find yourself pondering long after you have finished this short story.  Although the setting for the story is in Hugh Howey's Wool universe, Bunker has used the Silo as a microcosm of a larger human problem of freedom versus societal control. Specifically, the freedom of the Samizdat to publish what they want, versus the Silo authorities who want to control all that is written or read.  Leah, the main character of the series, is now caught up in events that are beyond her control, yet that she managed to inspire with some of her simple acts of conscience. Her decision to write the truth as she saw it, despite the consequences, turns out to have a surprising power to open minds to the possibility of freedom.  I believe Mr. Bunker's stories may have a similiar effect.

reviewText: I read 'Jake' over the course of a week and, during that time, the character really got under my skin.  Throughout a lot of the book, nothing spectacular actually happens.  It's a fairly mundane account of a teenager growing up in family and school life.  This is not a negative, though.  The writing is beautiful and perfectly captures the thoughts of a teenage boy, his awkwardness around family, friends and his new girlfriend.  It feels very true to real life and, at times, it is painfully real.The ordinary day-to-day descriptions of Jake's life could be seen as being slightly repetitive, but for me it was a master-stroke and Jake's whole existence had an undercurrent of impending tragedy.  But, there are lots of small smiles to be raised in the book, especially in Jake's relationship with his brother, Ben, which is genuinely tender and achingly touching.  Jake's relationships with his family and friends are all too real and believable.  This is perhaps what makes the last quarter of the book all the more shocking and tragic.Be warned, this isn't an uplifting read, but it is written with real skill and feeling.  I was incredibly moved by Jake's story and it is well worth a look.
summary: Painfully real and achingly moving account of a teenage boy

reviewText: I have to say that "Mermaid Inc." turned out to be a charming, entertaining and romantic novel that had me grinning and laughing the whole way through. The author has a talent for storytelling that uses strong dialogue and vivid imagery to propel the plot along, creating new ways to entertain the reader as Miranda's new experience as a human brings along with it a bit of humor and emotion as she falls down the rabbit hole and into love with Justin. The story is fast-paced with a smooth plot, making for an entertaining read from start to finish.

reviewText: Can two people overcome their painful pasts and learn to live perfectly broken together?After a traumatic event and years of therapy sessions, Peyton Mayfield still feels broken. She lives a quiet life working in her grandmother's New Orleans bakery. She detracts attention from herself and hides her natural beauty by dressing unprovocatively in baggy clothing. She has little desire to date as she doesn't trust easily, choosing only to socialize with her best friends Quinn and Bret.Reed Langston is a wealthy successful architect, who is known to be a major player, a commitment-phobe who doesn't do relationships ... just casual sex. That is until he meets Peyton ...Peyton meets Reed when her best friend Quinn's boyfriend Brett brings him to the bakery. There is an instant attraction, but when she finds out about Reed's reputation Peyton resists his charms and shies away, only making him more determined to win her heart. Can Peyton let go of her traumatic past and open herself up to Reed?Perfectly Broken is a captivating romantic love story about two broken people who come together and help each other heal and learn to love.Written in the third person narrative and set in the vibrant city of New Orleans, author Prescott Lane weaves a beautifully written tale full of pain, angst, drama, humor, and tender romantic moments that easily draws the reader into Peyton and Reed's story. The slow building development of their relationship makes this compelling story worth the read, as their instant attraction and sexual chemistry is put to the test by the remnants of their dark pasts. You can't help but feel for Peyton as she struggles with deep traumatic scars, as well as for Reed who struggles with being wrongly judged by his family his entire life. The author does a wonderful job of balancing the serious issues of Peyton and Reed's pasts with their flirty and playful budding relationship.Perfectly Broken has an intriguing cast of characters who are realistic,flawed, and easy to relate to; witty dialogue and engaging interactions; a flirty fun New Orleans setting; and a breathtaking storyline that will tug at your heartstrings and stir your soul.If you are looking for a hopeful love story that follows the journey of two broken people who learn to let go of their dark pasts and open themselves up to a healing and loving relationship, then Perfectly Broken is the story for you!Disclaimer: I received a copy of the book from the author in exchange for my honest review.

When I read The Illegal Gardener, I rather liked it.  By now I have read all five books of the series till now, and I think every book is a little worse than the previous one.  I don't think I will be reading the next one.Perhaps Sara Alexi should turn to another subject, because it starts to get boring and repetitive.  The descriptions of the island are very similar to those used in Black Butterflies, the story of Costas Voulgaris, the waiter who turns out to be a manque astrophysicist and a rich hotel owner, has been told in another book.As for the story itself, I found it to be highly unlikely.  A young goodlooking 24-year old guy who falls head over heels in love with a 50-year old woman, to the point of wanting to marry her a few days after meeting her...  Wishful thinking, perhaps?  Both in The Illegal Gardener and in Black Butterflies there is fleeting mention of older women having feelings for men half their age, in this book it is, if not the exactly central theme, an important one...Although it probably is not the writer's intention, she paints a rather condescending picture of Greece as a quaint, backward country where everybody loves each other and money is not important.  A lot of the things she describes might be true thirty-forty years ago, but not anymore.  And believe me, in crisis--ridden Greece money is VERY important!  But I suppose this "sunny" approach appeals to non-Greeks...What annoys me most, not only in this book but in the previous ones too, is that there is way too much internal dialogue.  I don't need to know the hero's or heroine's every thought and rumination.  I am quite capable of filling in the blanks myself.  A good writer tells more by writing less, leaving space for the reader's imagination.All in all, not a good book.  Perhaps the writer should stop cranking out stories as fast as she can.  A good book takes time, you may need to distance yourself from it for a while and revisit it with a fresh outlook.  Sorry Sara, I know this is not a nice review, but I didn't write it to be mean.  Sometimes a bad well-meant review can help a writer to become better!

Finding a trove of treasure in the backyard, this turns the notion of “Goonies” and drives it through the same kind of adventure that was at the heart of works like “Goosebumps” without the macabre twists.This sometimes humorous story, may find a good home with middle schoolers, but adults may get a kick out of the camp at times, the relatable characters and fast pace. This is a cool book that is a perfect give for children, and early teens. It definitely has heart, and that’s what makes great reads. I recommend this one, it’s good clean fun. No pretense, just fun.

I absolutely loved this book. I was given this book by Netgalley for a honest review and I am just in awe!Becca is a girl who has had to take care of herself and her younger brother Chad for most of their lives. She heads off to college to start a new life and hopefully a new Becca. She needs to free herself from her painful past, but how do you escape it? She had a plan and a dream for herself...Ballet. Distractions were not what she needed until she literally ran into Levi Klein.Levi Klein hot, rich and extremely sweet. He instantly fell for Becca. He wanted to date her, but first he needed to get her attention. Levi was going to turn her world upside down and show her what she had to offer the world....love. Would she let him in and love him in return?This story is amazing and it's about love, forgiveness, growing up and healing. Becca's life broke my heart and I could feel the pain she was going through. Her sisters death, growing up too early, not feeling loved by her parents, feeling like the world rested on her shoulders. When Levi started to break down her barriers, I instantly fell in love with him. He was like a breath of fresh air in her life and just what she needed.The secondary characters are easy to love. Sadie, Julian, Levis parents and Chad. Each one brought more to the story and they were very well written. I'm excited too see more of them.Favorite quotes:Sadie: "Your past won't define you if you don't let it. College is a place to reinvent yourself and to move forward."Becca: "How can you love me when I'm so broken inside? My heart is shattered into so many pieces. I can't even begin to scrape them all together."Ruth: "I'm a firm believer that sometimes we are placed in people's lives for a reason. You and Levi found each other and because of that, we found you and Chad."Levi: "I love you however you. Broken, fixed, empty, whole. I love you, all of you"Levi: "Becca I will always catch you when you fall."I devoured this book in a matter of hours, couldn't put it down. This book will make you laugh, cry, swoon and feel heartbroken. This book is a great read and loved all the characters I loved how Jessica Gibson let each character tell their own story in a way. Loved loved it!  Can't wait too read more by her :)

I think this is the first book I have read by this author. I love her writing style. The story is well written, the characters are believable, the romance is filled with love and suspence at the same time.Sydney is a very successful lawyer. She has been led and controlled by her lawyer father for her whole life. Sydney was the son her father (Sid) never had. Her mother, rather than argue with her husband, let him have control of Sydney.John Appleton is a widower with 2 kids. His wife's death hurt him so bad that he has decided to play it safe. He gave up his lawyer job so he could stay home with the kids, give them stability and love, making up for the death of their mother. He and his sister have a small business that they work at out of his home. He's playing it safe. He doesn't want to get hurt again.Then, a short time after they meet, they both notice a chemistry between them. Each of them are surprised. Sydney has little experience with love, and John was living in the days when his wife was still alive.As the story goes on, we will see who will win out for Sydney's love and attention. Will it be her father, or John and his kids?I think this story, although a work of fiction, is something males and females should read. Life is hard and sometimes we need to take chances. As you read the story, you will see how good for each other Sydney and John are. With their growing love, they help each other overcome fears and insecurities. they grow into better and more loving people.I recommend this book highly.

reviewText: As a teenager Lily Saunders faces problems like all teens. But when her mom and dad decide to divorce her world starts falling apart around her.Lily's mom starts drinking away her problems; her dad doesn't seem to give a damn about her or her mother and Lily is left to deal with everything. She has a best friend Andy Green who have stand by her through life. But when Lily approaches Andy to find comfort her best friend is pushing her away and forces her to bend to his crew of friends or be left out.All alone Lily finds comfort, support and understanding from someone she least expected it from, her childhood bully Gabe Green. Gabe is Andy's brother and the two of them doesn't get along. When Andy sees Lily hanging around with Gabe his real reasons starts to show. But Lily's life takes a huge fall and she fights heartbreak around every corner. Can she win this battle? But even more can she survive Gabe Green?What an amazing story. Lily's the odd girl out that doesn't take crap from anybody. Her best tactic is hitting home with sarcasm. But when Gabe comes into the picture she is finding it hard to keep her defense up around him. Gabe was the perfect dark hero. With troubles of his own, the mix between the two was electrifying.This was such an incredible read. If more than five stars could be awarded it would be to this novel. I found myself crying in a lot of places, and screaming in frustration with others. Stephanie Witter has packed in so many emotions it turns into a wild roller coaster ride. Perfect execution and the ending was perfect. From the news I have heard about this fabulous new author we are just starting to see her wonderful talents with great novels. She has captured my heart and attention! I recommend this book to everyone, what a fabulous read this was.Quote from the book: "Well, you're not wrong. I was afraid to die from boredom around you,"

Twombly’s writing makes it very easy to visualise the scenery and the events throughout the novel.  This would have easily been a 5 star novel if the author had gone for another round of editing.  There were a few times where I was tripping over the grammar and spelling which detracted from the story a bit.The main characters in this novel were even more vivid than in the first novel in the series.  They were also even more memorable (if that’s possible).  They may just be my favourite lead couple in a series.  The supporting cast is also perfectly developed.  They are so much more than secondary characters.  They are family and friends, and amongst the worst of enemies.  It makes for a brilliant tale.This is a brilliantly crafted story that kept me captivated throughout.  I cannot wait to see what the future will hold for this series.Please note that I received a complimentary copy of this work in exchange for an honest review.

I have been waiting eagerly for release day for this book, the first of a terrific new series of smart, funny, intense erotic romance novels from Samhain Publishing. The author, Katie Porter, is the pen name for the partnership of two edgy romance authors whose separate historical romances I have enjoyed, and  I very much liked their joint foray into contemporary erotic romance. In other words, WIN.Double Down Is the first book in the Vegas Top Guns series. The core group of characters are United States Air Force pilots, assigned to the 64th Aggressor Squadron. Thanks to Wikipedia, I know that the 64th is a real squadron, actually stationed at Nellis AFB in Las Vegas. Aggressor squadrons are teaching units; they "use enemy tactics, techniques, and procedures to give a realistic simulation of air combat (as opposed to training against one's own forces)." (from Wikipedia) The men, and woman, of the Top Guns know enemy tactics from having flown and fought against them, and although they are no longer deployed overseas, they are still taking risks in their high-powered aircraft. It's a great setting for hot romance, because there's a tension involved in the fighting, and in the need to train pilots well for their own protection, that goes beyond most domestic military deployments, but the characters are not under actual combat conditions. They have free time, and that time is spent in Las Vegas, a terrific place for anything-goes romance.Erotic romance is tricky territory for me, but this book really hit my sweet spot (heh). Ryan has a thing for role-playing, but he is ashamed of his kink and does his best to deny it. Cass is looking to break out of her "nice girl" life, and pretending to be someone else helps her free up her naughty side. These two characters are hot together, and a sweet couple even when they're having steamy hot sex; I wanted them to get together, but Ryan had a lot to overcome for that to happen. At one point I thought I was fed up with Ryan and his inability to accept his own sexual needs, and then a plot twist made his hesitation very real and believable to me.The book really sucked me in; I kept finding myself torn between rushing ahead and savoring the moment. I liked the involvement and development of the secondary characters in the squadron, too; there was a real feeling of camaraderie and trust between Ryan and his friends, which felt solid in this book and made me look forward to the next. I liked these characters, and I enjoyed spending time with them. Plus the erotic scenes were not only written well, they were integrated fully into the development of Ryan and Cass's relationship -- not that I mind gratuitous sex, if it's actually sexy, but this was even better.Kudos to "Ms Katie Porter" for an excellent debut, and thanks for a great reading experience. (This review originally appeared on my blog, Another Day in Paradise.)

reviewText: 2.75 starsSam lives for his job. When a fire on his territory threatens the life of the FBI agent intent of capturing a fugitive, he will not stop until he has every one secured.Oooops! Sam sure was not expecting to run into the woman who left him behind ten years ago. Funny how the passion that burns through him at seeing her again, burns as brighter as the fire that threatens their lives.Okay, so maybe not funny, but it sure was fun to see him all bent out shape because of her. Not to say that she wasn't affected by him at all. Who could resist a sexy, alpha male type with a body made for worshipping and a heart of gold? Well, not me. That's for sure!I liked this story. Anne Marsh definitely brought the heat to this pairing and kept the fast-paced action throughout the story. And therein lies the reason why my rating is what it is. I found the pace to be too fast for my liking. Just as I was settling to enjoy a good, dangerous hunt of the bad guy, it all came to a close. Like I said, I enjoyed the story, but I thought the concept deserved a bit more exploration. The burning park setting with a fugitive on the run and the danger that it provided plus the sparks that were flying between these two would have made for some awesome reading if it would have been spread out a little more.Having said that, it did have great elements to it that kept me engaged in the story. I wouldn't have minded a bit more character development and more dialogue and emotion, but the plot was interesting and the chemistry between the Sam and Olivia jumped off the page.All in all, a fast-paced, little sexy read about rekindling a past romance. Reburn was a fun story to read.I received this title from the publisher through NetGalley in exchange of my honest opinion.

reviewText: It is extremely rare for me to give anything in life a rating of five stars; films, plays or especially books.  But 'Chattanooga' is a book that so effortlessly took me back to 1944 and to the city of Chattanooga that I had no choice but to review it so highly.Being the ultimate character driven novel, the book changes point of view with every chapter, rotating among a handful of characters who seamlessly tell the story.  And what a wonderful story it is.  Nothing grandiose, majestic or even particularly exciting; simply day-to-day life amid a family with more than its share of 'characters'.I reference that great play, 'You Can't Take it With You' in my title for this review because almost from the opening page I was reminded of Kaufman and Hart's masterpiece.  That is not to say that 'Chattanooga' has the same degree of ridiculous humor; no the comparison is based more on the richness of characters who will all remind readers of idiosyncratic members of their own families.When I was finished reading, I couldn't help but wish that I had been there, living in the house with the Buffon family, during that summer of 1944; and that's the highest praise I can give to any entertainment.

Review written March 9, 2013 and transferred from another site.Ok, so a few things. I enjoyed this book the most in the series so far. I was on the edge of my seat the whole time and was up until 5am reading this! Even with the flaws, I was drawn in by the twists and turns and even the characters I dislike had redeeming moments.Everyone knows I'm not a Selange fan but, even so, I felt she was done a disservice in this book. The whole Nico/Selange cheating angle isn't plausible to me. There was always an attraction there, but the 'missing my husband' business should have been worked a bit better. It would have made more sense in Book 1 when Selange was really struggling. In this book, Alfonzo is a doting husband and father. Selange is the one who encourages Alfonzo to come out of retirement and claims she's down to ride or die. They're all lovey dovey and 'I love you more than air' and all of a sudden she can't talk to him and say, 'the anniversary of my parents' death is coming up and I need you?' Since when?? Their relationship was going too well for that. I might have given her a pass (MIGHT) if the infidelity was a one-off but the fact that they continued the affair in the light of day? Not buying it. It doesn't match either of their personalities and, like I said, I don't like Selange so me sticking up for her is saying something. Nico is way too honorable to repeatedly cheat with another man's wife, especially Alfonzo's. I don't care how much it was attempted to prove that he was so in love with her; it goes against the very grain of who he is. And Selange was way too in love with her husband to repeatedly disregard his feelings. Sorry, again yo no lo compro! They were both entirely too unapologetic about their cheating to remain likeable characters, and I will really need my hand held and lots of tequila shots to survive Alfonzo forgiving her in Book 5. Not only did she cheat but was dumb enough to so without protection and now everyone has to live with the consequences and Alfonzo is supposed to be ok with that? He is a MOB BOSS. That is a no, no.  Then again, I have never really been convinced that Alfonzo is this multi million dollar business man and feared mob boss. Sorry Alfie. I know you try, but I still see you as a small time street hustler. You've never done anything to prove otherwise. Sure, he's cut a body in half here and there, but it's not ingrained. I kind of indulge him like you would a kid walking around in his father's shoes. If Alfonzo met Giovanni Battaglia or Dmitry Medlov in a dark alley, he would crap himself. This book is completely enjoyable, but more so because of the soap opera, entertainment value. It's light on the true mafia business.As much as Nico disappointed me in this book, if you want to see a true Mafia boss then Nico stands head and shoulders over everyone else in this series and, if Alfonzo went head to head against Nico in a no holds barred match up, Alfonzo would die. Plain and simple. Anything else is pure folly. And it's not because Nico is built like a brick s*** house or trained to be an enforcer, it's because Alfonzo is NOT READY. He is not ruthless enough. Even his reaction to the infidelity is NOT mob boss like. A huge, drunken, public spectacle. 'I trusted youuuuu'. Uh huh. Righttt.Other niggles - What is with the $3 words? I know sometimes authors want to change things up a bit to avoid sounding repetitive, but it shouldn't sound like they're trying too hard. A bullet is a bullet; we don't need to refer to it as a 'projectile'. "Emilio tried to 'tamponade' his relationship with Jessica." What?? That doesn't even LOOK right.Some of the prose got a little too preachy and public service announcement-ish. Yes, there is prejudice in America and it sucks, but the references were a bit heavy handed at times.It sounds like I didn't enjoy this book, but I did. I just need Alfonzo to grow a pair and stop being so p-whipped and to truly step up as a Mob boss. Hopefully, Selange and Nico's betrayal will unleash some fortitude within him, and he will rely more on his instincts and LEAD. I really don't know if I can survive Book 5 if he's all reactionary and allowing Selange to guilt him into forgiveness. Selange actually had the gall to tell Alfonzo he never loved her. I never wanted to kick her in the throat more than I did at that moment. Ray Charles can see how much Alfonzo loves her, but true to form, Alfonzo totally allowed Selange and Nico to punk him.A friend will have to read Book 5 first and tell me yay or nay. I really don't know if I can hack it on my own.

Her brother's gotten more and more out of control until he puts her life, and the man she loves, in danger through his constant need to control her.  She's immediately drawn to Teague for his strength without being a bully, like her brother.  Their relationship progresses at a rapid pace which leads to a lot of sexual interludes which almost overwhelms the storyline.  In the heat of the battle against the out of the blue villains she's quite able to take care of herself which makes her Teague's equal.Teague wanted a quiet life after the war but soon becomes entangled with Vivica and her criminal brother and his gang.  He's more than physically up to the challenge and I must say this made him a very delectable hero.  The action sequences start immediately and never let up and it's this adrenaline rush that brings him and Vivica together.  Along with Teague protecting Vivica came numerous relatives whose large numbers made it difficult to keep track of them all.  Teague's war buddies also made an appearance which bogged down the story even more as they all tried to leave a lasting impression.  With all these introductions it felt as though things were being set up for a series which further became a distraction as the story progressed and more characters stepped forward.On a whole this is an entertaining story that keeps your heart racing.  From its battles to its breathless bedroom sequences The Ninja Tattoo offers something for everyone and shows great promise for the talented Dellani Oakes and a wish to read more from her.

reviewText: This is a relatively short novel, part I in a larger tale. The prologue started off fairly slowly for me, but the middle and end moved along very quickly. Primus Seneca wants to live up to the (general) father he's not seen for 6 years. Some parts are difficult to read, as I'm not a huge fan of axes, swords, and other sharply-bladed things. Without going into too much gory detail, there's a scene with a big-behinded tree, a guy's scrawny legs, and an axe ... yeah, ouch. Other than that and a random section filled with dialogue that featured soldiers' ability to crudely curse, I'd say this was a smooth, swift, action-packed read.Conclusion: If you enjoy historical fiction and can ignore possible small detail inaccuracies, please try this. It's well-written, quick, and intriguing. The end is a bit abrupt, but there's enough closure to make you feel like that story arc has come to its inevitable conclusion.

No one is safe as one woman's journey to revenge continues in this second installment in the Disgraced Lords series.  When two people marry out of guilt and desperation you'd expect things to end badly, but for these two strong-willed people love unexpectedly flourishes just as danger comes knocking.  With their lives hanging in the balance they realize that love is the most important thing in a marriage and that they'll do anything to keep the other safe as they join together to find out who wants them living in shame and misery.After being framed for murdering a young noble in a duel over a mistress, Sebastian feels indebted to the young man's family and will do anything to make amends....including marrying the woman all of the ton thinks of as endlessly nagging.  As he doesn't want anything to do with love she seems to be perfect for a wife.  He'll take care of her family in exchange for wedding and bedding her for an heir and in exchange he'll carry on as a bachelor in any bed he desires.  The moment he sees her walking down the aisle though everything changes and he realizes there's more to her than meets the eye and against his will he becomes drawn to her.  He soon wants to bed only her and becomes a more responsible man because of the belief she has in his kindness and honor.  When she's put in danger by manipulative members of the ton who have their own plans for revenge, he realizes her importance in his life and puts his life on the line to get her back in a pulse pounding and desperate race to the story's conclusion.  Sebastian was a sexy and charming hero who had trust issues because of his parent's miserable marriage full of vengeful infidelities.  Love means heartache and he wants nothing of it.  He's a loving brother though and cherishes his two sisters.  Seeing this proves he has a heart and made him even more endearing and had me rooting for Beatrice to win him over.Beatrice is her family's only hope to stay out of the poor house as she bravely goes to the devil himself to force him into marrying her out of guilt.  She doesn't expect him to be so sexy though and is surprised by how warm he makes her feel.  After what Sebastian did to her brother she's angry with herself but can't help being drawn to him.  Though his offer of marriage without love saddens her as she hoped for more when she finally married, she knows an old and plain spinster like her should be grateful.  As they spend more time together she discovers more about her husband, the truth of what happened that day at the duel and the danger he's in from an unknown enemy, and stays by his side helping him get one step closer to his enemy and falling in love with him.  I adored Beatrice from the very start as she did whatever necessary to save her family.  She knew what the ton thought of her and didn't care as her actions were in care of her family.  She was open with Sebastian, loyal, and understanding.  She never jumped to conclusions but made them talk through their issues.  She's strong-willed and a perfect match for Sebastian as he needed someone to make him see the truth about the taint his parent's marriage left on his soul which allowed for an immensely satisfying HEA.The romance between Sebastian and Beatrice was steamy from the very start as their verbal banter was as sexy as foreplay.  Their sexual interludes were equally hot and nicely paced throughout the story.  I enjoyed seeing Sebastian learn that his feelings were in fact love and was awed by the emotional depths he went to to express himself to Beatrice.  Along with the immensely likable main couple we get reintroduced to the other Libertine Scholars as they come together once again to help one of their own.  Each of the men are unique in their personalities and compelling in the glimpses we've gotten of each thus far and I look forward to their stories being told.  The mystery continues to be suspenseful with little headway made this time around as to the vengeful woman's identity.  The mystery was perfectly interwoven into the scorching and burgeoning relationship between Beatrice and Sebastian to keep the reader engaged on every level and I'm on edge to learn more about the woman's identity and what nastiness she has planned next as no one seems safe.  Ms. Evans continues to entertain and delight in this compelling series and I can hardly wait for the next installment as the brief glimpse we get of it at the end of this book sounds amazing!
