I give it three stars, barely. My problem with Flynn remains the same, she NEEDS to GET AN EDITOR or to do a better job or editing her work, herself. Her spelling and grammar:subject and verb agreement, use of pronouns and proper nouns, punctuation, where and where not to put paragraph break, poor sentence structure (usage of incomplete sentences or phrases, instead of complete sentences) leaves much, Much, MUCH to be desired. Seriously, if I had wrote anything as badly as this was written, despite the plot content, character and setting development, during my time in 9th - 12 grade grammar and lit, English, and creative writing, college English 101, 102, and 300 level creative writing classes, most of my teachers would have given me a D or lower, a C- possibly a C+ (if they were being generous). I know, because I have failed my grammar score more than once in school, for writing as poorly as Flynn. But whatever, she is published and her work does sell. Some readers are more sensitive to such things than others. Obviously, I fit in the former group. Just because the story premise is good or very good, and you are able to get it published and sell it (sell many copies or even make the best seller list), in my opinion, is no excuse for bad spelling and grammar. I find it sloppy, when an author's is either UN-edited or poorly edited. If you are wondering what qualifies me, probably nothing - other than I really do know what good writing looks like. I read and I write a lot. I have retained a lot of what I have been taught about writing. You do not have to be a writer to know good writing when you read.I have so wanted to say to many an author, including and sometimes especially Flynn: When you were conjugating those verbs, learning when and when not to use a pronoun, the difference between and direct or indirect objects and when to use one versus the other, proper sentence punctuation and is proper usage, the difference between a sentence fragment or incomplete, complete, compound, and run-on sentences, which to use and which not to, the difference between an interrogative, a declarative or command sentence, when to put a paragraph break and then in literature: about tone, plot, setting, character development, how to stay on plot and not stray, how to determine if a detail supports the plot of not, and not to add details to your writing that do not support the plot, conflict and resolution, and you wondered, "When am I ever going to use this in life?". To that I would say you will use it when, you wake up one day and decide to be a writer and sell your books for others to read, and you want to be good at it, but if not, than never mind, you will probably never have a need for it.Now on to what I did like:I liked the basic plot, the paranomals being tricked into taking a potion, that spelled them so that they had 24 to find a mate for life (and in this universe they have the potential it seems to live forever), or unpleasant things would happened to them, and if they tried to break or tamper with the spell in anyway, for that also, unpleasant things would happen to them. At first, from the summary, it sounded a rather funny, but cruel joke to play with the lives of others about something so important. But after reading this one and learning the reason behind it, I understand the reason, but still think that giving them only 24 to do, was a bit drastic and as it turned out extremely dangerously for many in attendance of conference, and not well thought out on the elders.  I thought elders were supposed to be wise especially ones that have lived so long. I figure they were either insensitive or thought they were that desperate, for some it seemed a little of both. I think it would have better to give them at least a week or two or three. That would have been more reasonable, albeit not by much. Of course, I realize that the point of the plot is to be unreasonable and unrealistic, incredibly so, so that you could get all of these wild situations for the various volumes. But, I got the impression, which I thought was made obvious, that the writers of this series were not taking in too seriously, as in trying to create a more credible, more realistic, more doable and well-thought solution to the problem. And thus that is why I liked the plot.I really like Ant. When he realizes how serious Gavin was about not being physically or otherwise affectionate, even though he was portrayed and physically small as a human and an animal, with a rather shy and introverted personality, he did not whine, complain or cry to Gavin. Of course, he pouted, and reasonably so in my opinion, but he did not bother Gavin with it and he didn't try to retaliate by trying to get out of his presence or refusing to talk to Gavin when asked for an explanation of the ice. I found it amusing that Gavin realized he was being iced out, when he was the one, that didn't want to be affection or talk to or be anyone, even his own mate, any more than was necessary. As usual, it's fine as long as you are on the giving end, but not so much when you're on the receiving end. I liked that detail. Also that Ant, despite his size contrast with Gavin, introverted personality and soft-spokenness, he was not a push over. Thank-you! I don't enjoy the common archetype of the submissive, twink looking guy (despite age and species), that is also a complete and utter doormat. Ant was not particularly submissive or really aggressive even, but he was assertive, which in my opinion is a great way to be, unless or until, of the other is actually needed and then only for the time being. When Gavin overreacted, Ant told him so and that he was done apologizing. And when Gavin was flat out abusive toward Ant, Ant not only realized it as such, and decided that he didn't like it, that is was wrong, AND that he most certainly did NOT deserve, he knew right away that he would not tolerate it, and he didn't waste time in doing something about it. I also like that small as he was, a mouse even, he did not wait around for and act as if he always needed Gavin to fight his battles for him. He, himself was a fighter. He just wanted Gavin to be on his side, as a mate should, whether he fights your battles for or with you or not. I really liked, how it first seemed like Ant would be this totally submissive, fearful, because after all, he did look the type and fit the profile, but he turned out to be assertive and courageous.  Awesome! For me, that is a good character type.I do not like Gavin as much, but I didn't dislike him. I thought he and Ant made a good pair. I liked that for all his talk in the beginning, it turned out that Gavin was or at lease decided to be more reasonable in the situation of having to take a mate that he knew nothing about or at all, than it first appeared. I liked the display of vulnerability, when Gavin freaked out, after he and Ant had made up. I like that Gavin realized that he had over done with the way the had treated Ant in that abusive manner, and that it did not take him as long as some, to realize that he needed to fix it, and then when the first opportunity came he fix it.Again, Ant was such a trooper and tolerant and forgiving. Gavin had to learn not be so rigid and intolerant, he did learn though. When Gavin went to him in the hospital, Ant could have behave much worse toward him and reasonably so, giving the situation, but despite how upset he was and justified in that anger, he was calm and willing to hear Gavin out and accept his apology, which at that point was more than Gavin had been, not once but twice already. By the end, it's flipped on it's head as to who appeared to be the strong and more dominant one in the relationship. Gavin was all over the place emotionally, which is understandable and well placed considering his issues that had yet to be worked out. But Ant however, he was the rock. He was always the one who kept it together, who was more tolerant, understanding, willing to give the benefit of the doubt, trusting of his mate and forgiving. Gavin had the physical, size and strength and has the position of Alpha, where as Ant did not technically share leadership, because Gi-Gi had the actual position that was held by the alpha-mate, even though she was not the alpha-mate, Ant was. Despite that, Ant did have the wisdom in that relationship, but it seemed only fitting given he was twice Gavin's age. At the time, I thought it was rather fitting that Gi-Gi held the position of the Alpha-mate even though she was not. But now after reconsidering, I think, Ant was shafted. He was included in the swearing in ceremony for the Alpha, the Alpha-Mate, position and the Alpha's second, but he really had no actually rank and status. Not that he was treated that way, and he totally helped Gavin lead, but still, the position should have been his, despite the lack of ovaries and uterus, but whatever.Despite the poor writing, it was a fairly decent story. I probably wouldn't highly recommend this to others who like this sub-genre, but I would say, do not read it. I was not bad. And if she had gotten an editor, I probably would have said it was fairly good and not just decent.
summary: Poor Writing Technique, But Good Story

Romance. Just the word brings to mind the idea of rose petals, champagne, knights in shining armor, and happily ever after. But here in the real world, rose petals turn to dust, champagne gets spilt, knight's armor is scuffed and dull from battle and wear, and 'ever after' is only happy if you make it so.In ALL FOR LOVE, Liz and Quinn have a storybook romance ... until life comes knocking. Burdened by what is right, weighted by society's standards, and tortured most of all by themselves, this couple fights to remain in love no matter trial is being faced, and there are many... most of which are being faced today by thousands of people the world over.Read this story and you'll laugh ... you'll cry ... you may even cuss Quinn now and then only to accept him back with open arms ... your heart will wrench ... you'll want to reach into the pages and shake some sense into some of the characters ... Then, when you're done with this eloquent anti-romance, you'll sit there in your chair, reflecting, and wondering how Ms. Ann Swann was able to not only strike you through the heart with her story, but also how she was able to see into your soul and shine a light onto your own fears, secrets, regrets, and mistakes.As for me? I'm hoping for a sequel.

Wes Lawson is the golden boy next door, a ‘bad boy’ stuntman who works for Jax Chamberlin at Renegades. Rubi Russo is an ex-supermodel-turned-tech-guru, who has abandonment issues or, better known as, daddy issues. She is convinced she’s not loveable and refuses to let anyone into her heart. Rubi and Wes have become very good friends over a couple of months; always together and playfully flirting with one another. The chemistry between them has always been strong and lately it’s become harder for them to resist each other. Wes usually goes for the ‘good girls’ and Rubi is far from his type. She’s a sassy and sexy brainiac that gives Wes a run for his money. He wants her BAD. But Wes is a commitment kind of guy, whereas Rubi doesn’t do relationships.“Let’s make an arrangement so you can get on with your day. If you need or want sex, you come to me...…and I’ll give it to you any way you want it, any way you need it.” - WesDespite Rubi’s trepidation when it comes to commitments, she sexually craves Wes yet won’t let herself give into her want. Then Wes offers Rubi a friends-with-benefits relationship. Rubi adamantly says no to him, unable to get past her fears. But the sexy temptation that is Wes Lawson is too hard to resist, so she decides to take a chance with him and a whirlwind sizzling affair begins. And the more time they spend entangled within one another, the stronger their feelings grow. Will Rubi finally give in to her feelings for Wes or will she let her fears and doubts hold her back from the man that she not only wants but most definitely needs in her life?I really do like Rubi, even though I had some issues with her character. Her abandonment issues are understandable and touched me on a personal level. Though I have to say with the way she let her issues dictate her life was flat-out frustrating. One of the main things I didn’t care for is the way she dragged Wes around in circles. He proved himself to be dependable and trustworthy more than enough. And I found a lot of her inner turmoil to be repetitive and back to that word again - frustrating. Rubi was much easier to love the second half of the story. Wes showed her what it’s like to be with a trustworthy, strong, and reliable man. He also showed her what having a loving family is like. I loved Wes’ family. And I was happy to see all of the character growth Rubi had by the end. She still has issues, but she’s working on them.Wes is our amazing hero and saving grace in this story. I adore him. He’s fun-loving, attentive, understanding, playful, gorgeous, and fiercely sexy in the bedroom. He made no bones about it - he was determined to have Rubi. Wes, with all his charm and persistence, slowly broke down Rubi’s defenses. She had no idea how to cope with what she was feeling for him but Wes never gave up on her while she tried to figure her shit out. No doubt about it, Wes has the patience of a saint and a beautiful heart.Wes and Rubi had smoking hot chemistry from the moment they met. And I knew once that raging sexual tension was finally acted upon these two would be smoking hot x 100. I love it when I’m right. This book is titillating. SEX-AY. I will NEVER look at melted chocolate ice cream the same again. Can I get a Wes-chocolate-sundae please?Skye Jordan’s writing is smart and fun with a lot of great moments and fabulous banter. Her characters are always well-fleshed out and written vividly. But sometimes too much description can bog down a book. I say this because some of the tech descriptions and conversations between Rubi and Wes really needed to be cut out. I get it; they’re both super smart, but it just made my eyes glaze over.Skye Jordan has created a fun and sexy series that I’m having a good time reading. I have so much love for her bad boy stuntmen. And Wes is the kind of hero that will make your book boyfriend list. With its sweet romance, scorching sexy times, and tons of emotion in the words, Rebel is a recommended read. I’m excited for the next book in the series, Ricochet, comes out Winter 2014.Rating: BHeat: Hot--Romantic Book Affairs

reviewText: Second Time Lucky by Ethan Day is hilariously funny and sweet tale of reflection and getting a second chance with your first love. I loved this story! While it is the second book of the Middletown Romance series, you really don't need to have read the first book so go out and get this one today because it is that good!Mr. Day brings his unique charm and sarcastically lovable wit to this story told from Luke's point of view. Luke has just turned thirty-five and finds himself taking stock of his life when his college flame, Owen, re-enters the picture. There are various reasons the relationship didn't work out fifteen years ago, but the one thing that was never a problem was chemistry. There are quite a few steamy scenes between these two, but they don't overpower the story.We learn a lot about Luke and his life over the past years and we also learn about Owen. One of my favorite scenes in the book is when Luke goes home with Owen to visit his parents. Being surrounded by the influential people in Owen's life, both Luke and the reader can see why Owen is such a stand-up guy. The secondary characters in this book are quite charming and vary dramatically from Luke's cold and slightly bitchy mother to Marco, Luke's boss and surrogate father.If you like fun romantic comedies that capture the complexities of life, then this book is for you! Mr. Day does a fantastic job of painting a picture that is both charming and deep. Second Time Lucky is about opening yourself to new possibilities while owning your past, accepting who you are today, and striving to become whole.

The supporting characters play important roles in the story and while some people may not like that they are not more developed, that didn’t bother me.  Nothing comes easy for this group of young adults and the author draws you into the struggle and leaves you hopeful for the future.

It's amazing what He does behind the scenes".I recommend you give yourself a nice block of time so you can sit back and enjoy this suspenseful romantic story that you won't want to put down until you have finished it. reviewText: Lyv and Ten have grown up together, offering one another support, friendship and the love that each of them crave but have never received from their families. When Lyv meets Alexander, Ten is happy that Lyv has found someone that loves her and makes her happy. Lyv knows that Alexander’s music is going to take him from her, but they cherish the time they have together before he has to leave on tour. When Lyv learns she is pregnant and both Alexander and Ten, who is studying abroad for a semester, are not available to help, she must forge ahead with all that is thrown at her…and let me tell you there is a lot thrown at her!I really enjoyed this book and was drawn into the relationship that Lyv and Ten shared. It’s not often in life that you meet someone who you know will be there for you no matter what, and the depth of Lyv and Ten’s relationship was portrayed in such a way that you could feel the bond that existed between them. I was so thrilled for Lyv when she met Alexander – she was finally able to see her true beauty through his eyes, which helped her begin to heal some of the scars that had been created by the abuse she suffered at home from her mother. Lyv was a very strong character and it was wonderful watching her find her strength and see her self-worth.I don’t want to say too much more about the book since anything more will be a spoiler, but I loved the emotions that I felt while reading Lyv’s story and the depth of the characters. I especially loved Ten and just how much he truly loved Lyv and wanted nothing more than for her to be happy – he was definitely swoon-worthy! The other thing about this book that I enjoyed was that it took place in the past – the book starts in 1978. This definitely impacted the plot and storyline, and it was refreshing to read a story where cell phones and computers were not a factor!Although this book isn’t a cliffhanger, there are several things that are left open that will hopefully be brought to closure in the next book in this series. This was a great read that had me hooked from the first chapter and kept me turning pages all night!
summary: Loved the emotions that I felt while reading this book!

Hot men, wine, good food, love, and some angst. What more could I possibly ask for? 'A Good Vintage' by Ashlyn Kane is the third book of this author's works that I've read and due to how much I enjoyed the other two, I fully anticipated getting the most that I could from this story.Luke is the saddest, most miserable person I've ever met at the beginning of this book. He's twenty-seven, has a good job, but he is horrible at relationships, with men and women, and judging character. His most recent boyfriend, Luke caught him selling Luke's belongings and himself to pay off his gambling debts. Just one more loser in a long line of poor choices. Luke's heart has been broken more times than he can count. He's still trying, unsuccessfully, to deal with his anger at his dad and the way his childhood turned out. His very well meaning, loving, but worry wart brother and his wife, Val and Julie, send him on vacation to a vineyard in Napa Valley. Luke spent a summer working at a vineyard when he was nineteen and it was the best and worst time of his life. Turns out this is the same vineyard, a little bigger, with a new name, but still owned by Mal, his boss he fell for the summer he was nineteen."Why didn't I know you'd be this persistent?"Because Mal suspected, Luke didn't think he was worth the effort. But what he said was "I just know what I want."Luke flushed a little. "I guess you came to hear the rest of the story.""I came because I wanted to spend time with you."Oh. My. Goodness. Mal and Luke were so amazing together, and not just sexually, although they could've set fire to the vineyard with their lust, but in all the ways that make a strong and lasting relationship. Scary for Luke because he doesn't know how those kinds of relationships work. A little scary for Mal, too, because he hasn't been with anyone in nine years since his wife died, and maybe he won't be good at the day-to-day. It doesn't help that Luke's time at the guesthouse is very limited and then he'll return to Los Angeles and his life, what there is of it. Two men, both new to relationships, who stink at communicating, begin a long distance relationship. Yeah, I know. Where's the punch line, huh?I adored how the author fashioned the story with intertwining short vignettes from the past. Normally I'm not a big fan of back and forth, past and present, in a book, but these were done supremely well and were short enough that they didn't distract me from the entire tale, while simultaneously giving me the insight I needed at the time. This was definitely one of the better love stories I've read. It was gentle and sweet, with some drama, but overall it just rang true for me. I thoroughly enjoyed both Luke and Malachi and was happy to see them each get what they needed. Thank you, Ashlyn, for another winner!NOTE: This book was provided by Dreamspinner Press for the purpose of a review on Rainbow Book Reviews

reviewText: I purchased this e-book while it was free.Danny doesn't like to take baths, and by the book seems as if he hardly ever did if he did at all. Because of this, he got the name Stinky Dinky. As  a parent, I did have the issue with the boy being called names....that is a no no in my house. These boxed collections are such a great deal!  I can finish the Damaged Heroes Series for less than what it cost for one book!!  I purchased and read the first two books in the author's Damaged Heroes Collection and loved them both. Unlike some of these boxed sets, these are all stand alone stories.  I started reading Ms James work a couple years ago with the first book in this series - "Murphy's Law.".  She is a terrific romance writer. Her stories and characters are about real people with real lives - and you like them.

I've read most of Bryan Hall's work so far, and I have yet to be disappointed. This short story collection is a great starting point for the author's work, and it has the same general feel as the rest of his writing, which I love. If you're a fan of Scott Nicholson and any of his Appalachia settings, you'll be a fan of this author as well.With about half of the stories, by the end, you wanted to read more. The author could easily take the rich settings he's created here and spin them into full-blown novellas or novels, because he creates memorable characters and settings. That's a compliment, because (especially with short story collections) after awhile reading the same author's work it starts to blend together and bores me. Not these stories, and he has such a unique style that you might think the tales were written by a dozen different authors, all equally skilled.I will be reading anything and everything this guy puts out!Armand Rosamilia

reviewText: In this second installment of the Fire on Ice series Ryker and Kate dig just a little bit deeper into your heart.  They were brought together in book one under unfortunate circumstances, made the best of it and are now ready for a full future together.It seems as if Kate and Ryker can't catch a friggin break, reeling from tragedy, they are both plunged right back into it yet again. Luckily for them, they are pros at dealing with pain and tragedy and need to put all of their tools to work now.  Kate and Ryker feel like they are a strong couple and are brought to the test time and time again in this book.Ryker is on the road with his team leaving Kate alone quite a bit to deal with her feelings.  She is a grief counselor, however sometimes telling somebody what to to and doing it yourself is a different story.  Kate and Ryker start to drift apart, holding in feelings only to make it worse in the end.  Things haven't changed on the road for Ryker either, he is still a hot hockey player at the top of his game.  There is temptation all around and  with trouble at home, sometimes a bad decision is easier to make.There are tons of emotions at play again for this sweet couple (quickly becoming one of my favorites) as they work through tragedy and hope for triumph.  We see Kate break out of her shell more this time around, doing things she wouldn't usually so and showing she is stronger than she was.  Ryker is  looking to show his wife how much he loves her, even when she is at her worst.  While there are some low points for Ryker, he proves how much he loves Kate over and over, and treads into book boyfriend territory this time around.  We get to see him as a loving husband, almost forgetting his puck bunny days of the past-almost.Captive is well written and despite the emotional roller coaster we are on with Kate and Ryker, they still steam up the pages.  Great addition to a great series and I am looking forward to the next one!

Gift of Gamman is a thought-provoking science fiction thriller but it doesn’t end there. This story encompasses many genres as an original and gripping read.It is important in this story to read the prologue. If this is something you normally skip you would be remiss to do that with this story. Adam Blake awakes after nearly 50 years of deep slumber to find he has arrived at his destination. On a one way mission to collect data for the United Planets Federation of a peculiar black hole the ship would collect the necessary data while Adam would add to it human observation and insight. Only once Adam arrives he finds that what he expected to happen - what should be happening - is not happening. What happens next is a fascinating exploration into a reality where energy is manipulated but our consciousness remains. Adam is able to transverse time and space in an epic journey that could only be brought to us by Stan I.S. Law.Author Stan I.S. Law has outdone himself with Gift of Gamman. This story not only engages science fiction but spirituality, love, adventure, history and hope. As Adam chooses to return to earth and inhabit the body of John Galt he experiences even further awakenings. He is exposed to an alien race that is enigmatic and intriguing. John-Adam finds enlightenment in the esoteric.The story has incredible characters, scenery and dialogue. The humor and seriousness flow together beautifully. The underlying possibilities fill us with wonder and intrigue. The ending is beautiful and hopeful. I highly recommend it!

Do today's extreme weather events corroborate global warming? This is the question that Rough Winds attempts to answer. Skeptics will find facts to consider without which their opinion is incomplete. Those who demand a "preponderance of the evidence" before committing to action may find it here. Regardless of your opinion about global warming, if you want to be informed on this subject Rough Winds is worth reading.Author James Lawrence Powell methodically examines the occurrence of record temperatures, drought, fires, rain and snow, floods, tornadoes and hurricanes to understand the connection between these events and climate change. He quotes government and scientific authorities worldwide each of whom expresses his or her opinion about their nation's extreme weather disasters and global warming.Global warming is the megatrend of our lifetimes. This book serves a specific purpose: it documents the geophysical evidence as of late 2011 that global warming is responsible for an increase in the frequency and severity of weather-related disasters. And it does so in a very interesting and entertaining fashion for the lay reader.In particular I appreciate the succinct summary and conclusion chapter entitled "Playing Dice with the Planet." This is the section what I wanted to see in Powell's earlier novella "2084" as mentioned in my review of that book.When you put all of the evidence together in one short book, the phenomenon of global warming is at once fascinating, frightening and undeniable.  I rate this book four stars. See my profile for an explanation of my Amazon rating system.
summary: Climate Change Facts, Evidence and Analysis Well Told

The Last Good KnightBy Tiffany ReiszRating 4 StarsThe Last Good Knight: An Original Sinners novella told in five parts.Part I: Scars and StripesIt's lust at first sight when Mistress Nora encounters a sexy newcomer to The 8th Circle. She's happy for the distraction, since she left her lover, Sren, but her session with Lance is cut short when her boss, Kingsley Edge, reveals they're all in danger….Part II: Sore SpotsWith a potential stalker on the loose, Kingsley hires Lance as Nora's bodyguard, but stipulates no sex while he's on duty. Frustrated by the ex-SEAL's noble chivalry, Nora is driven to seek release with the one man she's trying to forget….Part III: The Games Destiny PlaysShocked to see Nora's bruises, Lance is furious that she put herself in danger and demands to know where she got them. As Nora confesses her true nature, she's equally shocked to learn that Lance has some secrets of his own, drawing them together despite Kingsley's orders…With her feelings for Lance warring with her recent encounter with Sren, Nora returns to Lance's bed and finds herself toying with the idea of…toying with him on a permanent basis. But after she gets a glimpse into his personal angst, Nora realizes she has the power to rescue this white knight….Part V: The Last Good NightNow that the perpetrator has been apprehended, Nora sadly acknowledges she doesn't need a bodyguard anymore. She adores Lance and wants to keep him but is faced with a dilemma—if she uses her connections to help Lance, she'll have to give him up forever…My Thoughts:I am a huge Tiffany Reisz fan, so I jumped at the chance to take part in this tour. The Last Good Knight is a five-part serial. I have decided to write my review as an overview of all five parts.Tiffany is a freaking genius who continually brings such captivating, lust filled, freaking awesome stories. The Last Good Knight serial is another notch to add to her belt. Yes, they were quick reads, but Ms. Reisz never lacks in her story telling abilities. She has created such wonderful characters that we have all fallen in love with. Each book I read adds layers to each of those characters. This story is another layer added onto the onion of Nora's life.Nora has always come across very independent and strong. She is sarcastic and rough around the edges, but everyone around her loves and respects her. This story gives us a sneak peek of Nora's softer side.These stories take place after Sren and Nora ended their Dom/Sub relationship. She is working for Kingsley as a dominatrix and is feeling lonely after her sub is taken from under her nose by non other than Sren himself.She has a chance encounter with a handsome man by the name of Lance. He is a newcomer to the 8th Circle and she is drawn to him immediately. It's too bad things get interrupted by some very distributing news.Nora decides that she needs to keep her schedule even though her safety may be at risk. Kinglsey agrees to let her continue as long as she has protection with her every where she goes. That protection comes in the form of a SEXY Navy Seal.Over the course of the stories you learn about Lance and how he ended up working for Kingsley. Nora and Lance struggle to keep their attraction for one another hidden and remain strictly professional.Will Nora be able to have her cake and eat it too? You need to read to find out. :)~Andrea

reviewText: This book was mentioned several times in the blogging community, and I finally decided to check it out and see what all the fuss was about. I’d never read anything by Brittainy Cherry before, and the book sounded promising. Then I went on Goodreads and saw the slew of 5 star reviews (many were from my friends). As soon as payday rolled around I sat on my couch with my list of books to one click, and Loving Mr. Daniels was on the top of my list. I was determined to have this book. So, I bought it, and I couldn’t wait to start it. That day on my first break at work I started in on page 1 “Absorbed in a stream of murky thoughts…” ooo this sounds promising already. Fifteen minutes later I had devoured the prologue and most of chapter 1, and I was trying to keep myself from crying. Sigh. From that point on sitting at my desk and trying to focus on my work was impossible. I kept looking at my kindle and I could hear it calling to me. “Jessica…Jessica, you know you want to read me.” I fought the good fight, but lunch hit and I was out of my seat scurrying to the break room hoping to get 45 minutes alone. I wanted to be alone with these amazing characters and pages.The story of Ashlyn and Daniel was so fresh, which is exactly what I needed. Lately it seems like all the contemporary romance, new adult romance, and even the erotica books are all the same, and I was demanding something fresh. This was that story! Yes, it is a boy meets girl, woos her with Shakespeare inspired music, falls for her, and finds out she’s his student…WHAT?!?! Immediately, I thought of Pretty Little Liars, which I LOVE! Aria and Ezra’s story started like this…minus the Shakespeare band. This story has a twist to it, and I loved it. I loved that the author didn’t leave us hanging.The characters in this book were phenomenally written. I felt like I knew them. I felt like the loss of a sister and a dear friend was changing me the same way it did Ashlyn. I laughed with her, I cried with her, and I regained faith in mankind with her. I loved that she had that one person for her that completely changed her world. Loving Mr. Daniels turned her world on its axis and changed her views on everything she held true.”I was convinced that everyone in the world had a form of weirdness to them. And the cool thing, at least I hoped so, was the idea that there was someone out there just as quirky as you were. The idea of finding your other weirdo was so attractive to me.”Ashlyn and Daniel are written in such a way that you feel like they are two people cut from the same mold. Ashlyn is young and hurting, torn apart by the death of her twin sister. She’s trying to move on, but is suddenly ripped out of her world and forced to live with her absentee father and his new family. Daniel is an English teacher and he is reeling from the recent death of both of his parents. Neither one knows how to move on and move past it, but together they forge ahead in this strange new world.Hailey, Ryan, and Gabby are amazing supporting characters. Hailey and Ryan are brother and sister and they are the children of Ashlyn’s father’s new family. When they all first meet Ashlyn doesn’t like this dynamic duo. She doesn’t hate them but doesn’t really know what to think. As the book goes on there is a wonderful bond that forms between these three characters pulling them closer together, and has them sharing secrets with each other they never thought possible. Gabby is Ashlyn’s twin sister who loses her battle to leukemia at the opening of the book. She isn’t present in the physical sense, but she very much has a presence in this book. Each of the characters gets a chance to know Gabby in their own way.“You’re the reason people believe in tomorrow. You’re the voice that scares the shadows away. You’re the love that makes me breathe. So for the next few seconds, I’m going to be selfish. I’m going to say things that I don’t want you to listen to…Don’t go. Stay with me forever. Please, Ashlyn. Let me be your everything. Make me your golden. Don’t go.”If you’re a romance junkie like me, love Pretty Little Liars, or even a fan of P.S. I love you, than I implore you to go out and buy this book. If there is one book you read this summer, make it this one. Let yourself get swept up in this brilliantly beautiful love story. Spend time with these astoundingly well written characters and remember what first love feels like.I give this book not just 5 stars, but all of the stars in the sky. Brittainy Cherry deserves every one of them. It’s been a long time since a book has stayed with me the way this one has. Loving Mr. Daniels will be my absolute favorite book of 2014 and possibly ever, I guarantee it. I’ve got a book hangover that's going to take me months to recover from.

This Australian author uses Australian words and brand names which makes me so happy. It could have easily been called CORAL SEA AFFAIR (BEN HOOD THRILLER, BOOK 1)followed by BLACK MOUNTAIN AFFAIR(BEN HOOD THRILLER, BOOK 2), etc.

First I want to say I’m a big fan of shifter books. I saw this story different than some of the other readers. I spent many years in my life as a single mother and can honestly say I understand the concept of being strong, yet deep inside you never lose that need for the one you love. This is a fantasy and I think people tend sometimes to forget that. In the Lycan world the author created, as in most werewolf novels it’s impossible to fight the call of your soul mate. In all that time she never loved another man because she still loved her Alpha.Kaden, as with most Alphas is prideful and that hurt pride prevented him from confronting her. There are many truths that come out about the original incidents that explain some of his attitude, but I won’t give that away. I personally think they both screwed up, but they did a good job in the end of fixing things.The fact that Kaden came into the picture right as she’s considering dating another man is inconvenient. I didn't like the new boyfriend much so it was no real loss. Taylor was a jerk, but in the end the author allows him some redeeming qualities to make up for it. I liked the little bit of mystery thrown in to liven things up. I immediately picked up on the clues written by the author so the traitor wasn’t a surprise to me, but I still enjoyed the twist in the story-line.Other than the grammar/spelling errors the only complaint I have is in the time frame. While I do understand the concept of falling back into someone’s arms that you love or the whole pride thing I find it difficult to rationalize his behavior in the shifter world. It seems off to me for a wolf to allow his mate and his child, even when pride is involved to remain unprotected for 17 yrs. The natural need to protect that the author portrays should have reared its head much sooner. Even if he didn’t force her home, he would’ve at the very least found a way to take care of her behind the scenes.This is more a 3.5 stars, but I’m bumping it up to 4 because of the lack of half ratings available. An abundance of spelling/grammar errors always means a loss of 1 star in my ratings. I believe the story itself to be entertaining and great for a quiet afternoon. Overall I enjoyed this quick read and would not object to reading other books by this author.

I must be a glutton for punishment or something because I did NOT like this authors first book and chose to read another. It was marginally better than the first, but not by much. This is a novella, not a full length novel so it makes sense for it to be short and sweet. Honestly? It was not short enough... As with Crashing Into You, it was well written, but this one just did not make any sense. It kept flipping back and forth between Maddie and Colin's POV. All fine and dandy, but it would cover something that had happened a few times between the two before finally moving on. This made it a bit repetitive and drawn out.Maddie and Colin apparently love each other even though they have barely exchanged two words. It seemed like the attraction was all based on looks and not so much on personality. With it being a novella, we never really learn a whole lot about either character. I think you learn more about Colin and he did have a rough past so his actions are somewhat understandable. Their boss is a random character that is portrayed in two different ways so it's hard to really know what she is like.Overall this was very mediocre. It seems like it would be a hot little story, but it's really just back and forth with a small amount of spice at the very end. As much as I did not like it, it is better than the author's first novel. I'm pretty nice so I may or may not read more by this author-only time will tell!

The fourth book in the Reborn series or twelfth in The Calling series is an intriguing and mesmerizing read.Diana and Ryder face the most difficult choice of all, turn Diana or risk losing her and the baby, even if the wrath of the council means he will face death at the hand of their friend Michaela. An FBI agent, Michaela has long searched for the vampire that killed her mother, but since meeting FBI Director Jesus, she’s lost a bit of her edge imagining a life of happiness and passion.  Now the hunter has become the hunted and her new found friends and love r are risk and now Ryder and her both must make the difficult decision to break the rules for love.This steady to fast paced plot is full suspense, emotional angst, romance and action.  The author brings the world to life with vivid images and strong compelling characters that grab the reader’s attention and doesn’t let go. She also adds some extra spice with some unexpected twist. The author brings all the characters together in a way that highlights their differences and personalities and makes for a passionate story that captures the emotions as well as the imagination and makes it feel as if the reader is part of the story.The attraction between Michaela and Jesus radiates from the pages and the sex scenes sizzle with passion but the relationship has some bumps as Michaela tries to reconcile her professional life with her new found ability to care.  The reader can easily relate to all the characters and their situations which add depth to this riveting tale of vengeance, friendships and true love.The author has created a fantastic paranormal world that I fell in love with in the very first Calling book and has continued to the Reborn novels and this one has certainly lived up to expectations. I can’t wait for the next one and see where this new development takes the council.

Book 5Stranded with a Cajun Werewolf.Stormy Weather"a 5-in-1 anthology" - books 1-5 in the one place, at the one price!Plot:When a hurricane grounds his plane, Andre makes some life-changing decisions - to drive his old flame Juliette home, and then to keep her no matter what. But can they get past The Past, or will it continue to haunt their future?Comments:- Contemporary paranormal (werewolves) erotic romance.- 1735 kindle locations, 30,500 words. Finishes around location 1667.- m/f - not overly frequent but explicit, generous and loving.- Picks up a month after the house burnt in "Seduced by a Cajun Werewolf".- Reference to Andre's past relationship with Angelica. See Book 2 "Bitten in the Bayou" for some hot'n'heavy m/f/m lovin'.- Includes an excerpt fromSurprising Darcy.Opinion:Extremely relationship driven, we delve into the resurrection of a past relationship when all we have is Hot Sex to get us through the night. Andre and Juliette hurt each other through words and actions, and while we resolve why that happened pretty early on, we are left wondering when they're going to have The Conversation. But it's a good story. The paranormal is incidental - really only the fact they are long-lived comes into play. Shifting occurs but could work just as well if it was a Mafia Hit. But it's still an enjoyable addition to the series, a nice reconciliation for Andre, and sufficiently erotic to sit in the genre.3.5 stars rounded down. I'm getting frustrated at the lack of editing in these books. By the fourth book I'm expecting a tighter story and less obvious errors. Self-publishing may be difficult, but still...-CR-

reviewText: You can make an interesting drinking game out of this book though. Get yourself a full bottle of your favorite liquor and a shot glass. Every time the author makes a point of saying how she is not boasting about the money she makes, take a shot. Every time she makes a note of mentioning how much money she makes, take another shot. Every time she mentions the title of one of her own books, take a shot. By Chapter Two, you should probably put your Kindle down, as you will not know which Kindle is the one you are reading (hint: Try the one in the middle), and maybe call 911, just to be on the safe side.*This does make some good points and have some useful information for the neophyte author, it pretty much requires that you have already published more than one book, either with a vanity predator or some other place. It also places a high reliance on Amazon's KDP Select, the usefulness of which devolves with every algorithm change. This had the remotest chance of working back in the beginning of 2012, but is almost totally unfeasible right now.*Please note that this reviewer does not condone the actual playing of this drinking game, nor does he accept any legal liability for anyone stupid enough to try it.
summary: A book you can play "Hi Bob" while reading.

reviewText: A collection of simple-but-original recipes, Jason James offers a great variety of dishes for any palate. From a one-bag-snack to pepper and pasta dishes. It is noteworthy to mention that the recipes contained in this book are very different than the average. You will not find your typical family favorites mentioned yet again. Instead, James gives a twist to typical American cuisine and adds exotic ingredients that are sure to please just about any type of palate. For example, the lasagna recipe that most cookbooks contain is given a spicy twist by making it into a spinach, and black bean dish that can be enjoyed by low-carb dieters everywhere. Not to mention that the consistency of many of these dishes relates almost entirely to the original, making it a clever and delicious alternative to traditional cooking. I strongly recommend this book and hope that James continues to publish more alternative ways to use food to the best advantage. Support your local farmers' market and use the findings to try these original recipes. Everyone wins in the end!

The Blood Gate by David Ross Erickson was also another book which the author hadn't approached us for, but again the blurb and excerpt worked in its favor. The story begins by introducing several characters in a land which is similar to Egypt and is called Tygetia. The author begins the story by introducing us to the two main characters Xanthippus and Hurrus, who are the main focus of the story.Xanthippus is a warrior who travels to Tygetia with his blood brother Nydeon for a specific cause as some one is looking to hire them for a job of sorts. Hurrus is a prince of a far away land who is looking to return as a conquering victor. They however will have to contend with a lot more issues than they think are present. Also in the midst of things is the titular object which can grant mystical powers but also granting madness at the same time. There are many more characters and thus there is a lot more drama. The story is a myriad one wherein there are multiple plot threads and the author slowly introduces each and every one of them, slowly and surely building a tapestry for the reader to view. The story then spiral to its fantastic conclusion and has an epic ending of sorts.What I liked about the book was its understated epicness, whilst the characterization was a strong point. The main draw of the story is the plot twists, the author has thoroughly planned the story and made sure that the reader who closely follows it will be thoroughly rewarded. Another excellent point about the story is its standalone nature, nowadays with huge series with more than 5/6 books, its very heartening to see an author pitch out an epic story and then contain it within the confines of a single book. This move helps as nowadays a lot of readers are left waiting to read the next chapter/book in their favorite series and so a standalone book will definitely be appreciable.Lastly what is a focal drawback for the story is its tepid pace, through out the first half of the book, the pace of a story is a major deterrent. With the author structuring the story the way he has. I believe the narrative pace of the story was destabilized and that can cause certain readers to be disenfranchised with the story as the major plot points are being built up. However I would advise such readers to not lose their way and read through to thoroughly enjoy this book which reads partially like historical fiction. Recommended for readers who enjoy well developed stories with good characterization akin to stories by Kate Elliot and J.V. Jones.

Zoe Archer is officially one of my new favourite romance authors! I've read her Blades of the Rose Series and just finished her sci-fi romance Collision Course which follows Mara Skiren, Scavenger extraordinaire and Kell Frayne, 8th Wing Commander, as they battle the PRAXIS(Not unlike the Empire in Star Wars), smugglers, drone bots, plasma rays, Liden's Lash (a meteor belt that is on fire) and not to mention their feelings for each other.  Which by the way are hot, hot, hot!Mara is coerced into helping the 8th Wing and Kell is sent with her on  a rescue mission deep into territory that only smugglers and scum traverse. Which is why Mara's help is so crucial being a scavenger herself. Right off the bat the two protagonists lusty feelings are apparent and the sensuality builds with each page, despite the fact that they are on opposite sides of the fence.Good things about this book- Great characters, fantastic dialogue, very Star Wars feeling without going overboard and making me say, "Oh, that's just like Return of the Jedi", sex scenes were HOT but not overdone and the two characters didn't just jump into bed after meeting there was a lovely build up of tension and the ending was more than believable and, of course, as all romances go, very happy.Minor improvements- I personally would have loved to see some more build up before the first chapter. Meaning I would have liked some more insight into Mara's past as when you learn about it there is a desire to know just how she survived her last fifteen years coming from the beginnings she did.(Can't say more without putting in a spoiler alert) With Kell, it's easier to see how he became the man he is from the story of his past, but with Mara I think I could have used more background in order to really believe her history, but really, that's only a minor complaint.I very much enjoyed the book, it is the first Sci-fi romance and I was pleasantly surprised at the satisfaction the blend of the two genre's brought. Action, adventure, romance and moments of humour that made for a great read and one I would highly recommend.

reviewerName: MAD LOVE BOOK BLOG "MAD LOVE BOOK BLOG"
reviewText: This book has been one if the few that has kept me until the wee hours of the morning. Yes, i literally went to sleep at 5:30am and woke up at 7:30am to go to work.I got up in auto-pilot. After maneuvering a "Flash Gordon" stunt, in-and-out of the bathroom, and three shots of coffee later, i was out of the door to the ruthless world.While driving like a zombie high on codeine, (guess the shots did not kick in as fast as i supposed) i was still reeling on Mischa, Lauren, the whole story, my likes and dislikes.I will try to be brief, but in a nutshell i loved it. I liked the smooth transition. I like the chapters she used as mezzenines, between events. I liked the way the author developed the relationship between Mischa and Lauren; step by step, nothing hurried, taking the time to describe the scenes. The way Mischa conducted himself, with such class, careful and reserved despite his young age, due to his position and lifestyle. However at the same time giving himself time to get to know Lauren, as a pure gentleman.I liked Lauren's behavior and the way she took charge from time to time.The entanglement and the disentanglement of the plot. The anxiety and suspense.What i didnt like, honest to God, it needs editing...ASAP! I didnt like the cliffhanger, i am NOT a fan of them...and the fact that i have to wait until Speing 2014 to find out the conclusion.However, i have sent an email to the author asking her, if there was a chance the second book could have an early realease date?...and i dont consider myself as a stalker, but I really wanted to know? Anyways, the good author reply saying, NOT PROMISES! But it could happened. She made my day.I was going to give this book 4.5 stars, but decided to round it up to 5 stars.OMG! I was trying to be brief, but i just wrote a freaking newspaper...Oh Lord! I hate long reviews...including mine!!! Well, I guess, the three coffee shots finally kicked in; i still feel like a zombie, but now high on steroids!

For some silly reason I'd totally forgotten about this series - what was I thinking? Not thinking is more like it. You can probably read this as a standalone but I wouldn't recommend it because these are pretty much written as a serial. This one picks up immediately after leaving Erin and Blake declaring their love for each other in Beauty Touched the Beast (Beauty #1).In this novella, Blake gets a chance to come out of his self induced hibernation and go back into the public eye. He's been offered a position as an associate professor at the same college where graduate school student Erin is in her last semester. The conflict is small in scope but it's a big deal in light of the focus that Erin has put into her eduction;  it could significantly change not only her future career plans it can also put a dent in the burgeoning and fragile relationship with Blake.We get to peak a bit more I the minds of both and bedrooms (smexy times) of these characters and I liked what I read. Neither Erin nor Blake are unrealistic in their expectations of the other. Erin is emotionally very typical of her age group, not to say that she's immature and childish but she has a fair amount of angst about where she's from and how that compares to Blake's background. reviewText: Heroine:  Fiona Haines must travel to Scotland to warn her rogue brother, Jack, that he is being sought by the Prince Regent's men because it is believed he has bedded the prince's wife.  If they find him, they plan to hang him.  She has been away from Scotland for some years and isn't excited to return but loves her brother, so off she goes.  Once she arrives in Edinburgh, her elderly uncle insists that she seek out their clan's laird - Duncan Buchanan - who will be traveling to Fiona's destination during the Christmas holiday.Hero:  Laird Duncan Buchanan was formerly considered handsome, gifted in sport and had a reputation for hunting and bedding beautiful women.  Further, Duncan and Fiona have some history and Fiona isn't keen on asking Duncan nor his "people" for any favors.  Unbeknownst to Fiona, Duncan is no longer the rake she remembers due to a fire at his estate wherein one of his best friends was burned to death and Duncan himself sustained severe disfigurement and injuries.  He is now a recluse and although currently in Edinburgh, doesn't go out in society.Story:  Because Duncan can't refuse Fiona's uncle's request to provide her with transportation to Blackwood, where Jack has gone off hunting, he agrees to give her and her maid transportation.  He will travel along with most of his face covered up and Fiona will believe him to be a servant.  Of course, things immediately go awry - Fiona's maid runs away and Duncan's servant must try and find her - leaving Duncan and Fiona alone to try and get to Blackwood, Duncan's estate before they freeze and starve.  Still in the guise of a servant, Duncan is mostly silent and Fiona chatters a mile a minute and relates many stories of her life in London, once in awhile making sarcastic comments on Duncan Buchanan who insulted her years ago and was one of the major reasons she left and spent all those years in London.Fiona begins to have feelings for this tall, strong, Highlander even though she believes him to be a servant. Duncan, starved for the attention and affection of a woman, chastises himself for his past cruel and selfish behavior, especially when he realizes he has caused Fiona pain.  Although he doesn't remember his hurtful comments to Fiona, he has no doubt he is guilty because that sounds just like something he would have done during his former life.I was dialed in with this little novella and truly enjoyed the storyline.  It's nice to find a story where someone who was selfish and somewhat cruel thinking only of their own pleasures is given the opportunity to have a turnaround and becomes an individual who cares about others.  After all the revealing, there is some anger but of course, the H/h have their sweet HEA.
summary: Disfigured Hero... Feisty Heroine... Kept Me Dialed

Not only because she needs it to be a financial success but to also prove to her family that she can be a successful business woman. So, when Marina encounters the sexy real estate tycoon, Gage Emerson, at a local party, she isn't all to happy to meet him; especially, since Gage is determined to snatch up a piece of her family's real estate. Marina instantly has a strong distaste for Gage and tries to knock down his ego by throwing insults as him. Soon these two are having a battle of words while trying fighting the immense sexual attraction they feel for one another. Will this real estate tycoon obtain his coveted piece of property or is he in danger of losing his heart (and the million dollar bet with his best friends) to the beautiful bakery owner?"Is it just me you say idiotic, sexist disgusting things to, or do you talk this way to all the women you encounter?"Gage and Marina were a really fun couple to get to know. I loved seeing them evolve from being enemies to lovers. Aside from the steamy love scenes some of my favorite parts of TORN were when these two were hurling insult after insult at each other. In some ways, the way these two treated each other at the beginning reminded me of school kids. Even though they said some pretty hurtful things, deep down they really liked each other but were too scared to admit it. The heat in their war of words only helped spark the flame between these two and when they got together for some angry sex....whew they melted your face off!"Flaws and all, and despite that, the attraction is still there between us. Like a living, breathing thing."Murphy brings back characters we met in Crave and you see how much Archer is enjoying watching Gage fail at their ridiculous bet. I mean really, these guys should have known that as soon as they laid one million dollars on the table that, they would sooner rather than later meet the women that would change their thoughts on being single bachelors forever. If you are looking for a quick, fun, sexy, and passionate series with hot billionaires, then you definitely need to start reading Billionaire Bachelors Club. Monica Murphy makes seeing sexy, confident billionaires loosing a million dollar bet a lot of fun. TORN was a wonderful installment in this series and I am really looking forward to seeing the third man in this club, Matt, fall on his knees for his assistant with the googley eyes. Monica Murphy, please bring us Savor a little sooner!

I received a free copy of this book in exchange for my honest review.I'm going to start this review off by saying that I do believe in psychics, mediums, etc. I'm going to assume that you are at least open to the idea. Why else would you have gone so far as to read the reviews? I'm not going to swear that the author is the real deal; that's up to you to decide. But I believe you can appreciate this book even if you are a skeptic. It gives you a lot of food for thought about the afterlife, and as long as a book makes me think, I believe it's worthy of a read.Though I have an interest in the paranormal, I do not spend a great deal of time researching people and I had not heard of the author. In the case of most self-published authors, I don't feel that researching an author is all that necessary. But this genre is a bit different. The introduction tells you about her life, but a little bit of Googling will you give you some background on her before buying. She's led an extremely interesting life and, if you're concerned about the authenticity, I think you'll find enough to justify the purchase.One thing I do wish the author would do a little more of is explain the method of her channeling. I find mediums fascinating and am always wanting to hear more about the experience itself. She relates stories about her experience in the introduction, but I wouldn't mind hearing more about her experiences with these interviewees and what her approach was in terms of writing out and editing the text--for example, is the connection strong enough to get full sentences, or is it more of a puzzle?This book is a set of interviews with people who have passed on. The stories are told from their perspectives. Some editing is clear throughout, but in a published book that's to be expected. The voices vary as the people change, but a few times it feels a little overly polished. Even so, each interview in this book is unique. There are people of all ages and walks of life. And time periods. The mental state of them during their lives also varies. In just the first few you see a little boy with a heart problem, an elderly man who is the town go-to for anything broken, and a runaway who finds a loving family. You'll see what life was like for people in different places and historical periods. You'll also see how even people with very destructive personalities end up finding their own peace in the end.The only thing I wish there was more of in the interviews is clear biographical detail at the start of each. After you get into every interview, it becomes clear the gender, age, and rough time period for each interviewee. But I feel I would benefit from having that information before I dive in. On the other hand, each one felt like a mystery and there was something nice about unravelling the story as you go.Either way, the stories are fantastic and captivating. The narratives start in the middle of people's stories--getting right to the part of their lives that relates to their death and how their souls recovered from any pain they experienced while alive. Some spend a great deal of time on the living part of their existence while others focus more on the death and afterlife part. Each one focuses on the most relevant parts; those that could help the reader. And they end with advice from the afterlife. They try to reach the readers and encourage them to live in the moment and not be focused on death or those they've lost. There are several "please learn from my mistakes" stories. So even for the skeptic, there is a lot to be gained from reading these interviews.Because they have a colloquial feel, they move quickly and you feel like you're in a café just chatting with an old friend describing their last big trip. The information about the afterlife is very interesting. Like I said earlier, even if you are skeptical, it gives you something to think about. We're all curious (and anxious) about the afterlife, and any information or idea that we haven't already encountered is useful. There are things you hear about in these interviews that will make you think about what you believe. Not to say you should be constantly reevaluating your views. But if you are still reading this review, I suspect you are looking for information or ideas that you can find here. Because it's such great food for thought, I recommend this book.

Love is blind.In 906 A.D. Mercia, England was defending themselves against Viking attacks. At that time Ranulf was only sixteen and forced to fight in the King's army. Years later he returns, but with scars that he hides with a mask. Fearing he is too hideous for his old love Gisella, he lets her believe he is dead, but after hearing that she is being forced to marry, tries to intervene to make sure Gisella can find a proper spouse. However, sparks fly and in the end a mask is but a slip of cloth.This is such a sweet and heartwarming romance I didn't want it to end. The chemistry between Gisella and Ranulf was electric and I couldn't help but root for them. I also really liked the childhood love aspect. It gave their relationship a bit more depth and made their short courtship more realistic.Ranulf is such a sweet hero. For all his scars, he has a heart of gold. His love for Gisella ran deep and I admired his determination and willingness to do what he thought was right to help the one he loved.Gisella was a wonderful woman who I found to be the perfect match for Ranulf. It wasn't hard to see how he fell in love with her in the first place. She is intelligent, giving, and she loved Ranulf just as fiercely as he loved her. She was a fun character to get to know.I only wish their story was longer, but it was a sweet and heartwarming love story that I am sure to read again and again!Reviewed by Katie Codyfor TheRomanceReviews.com

Minna is a young woman with special talents. She's a wizard but her father, legendary dragon jockey Wynn Westerfield, has a problem with wizards since one ruined his last game, and his career. He won't have anything to do with wizards, and doesn't want to acknowledge Minna is one. Nor does he want her honing her talents.Unfortunately, the great wizard Thaddeus Bartholomew, whisks into town accompanied by his latest protégé, the handsome Evan Valentine. They desperately need Minna's help retrieving an enchanted knife. Before they can make any concrete plans--such as picking out an engagement ring--they must travel to an alternate universe and retrieve that knife, before the fabric of reality unravels.S.G. Rogers' Minna & the Valentine is a short, sweet fantasy romance, with just a hint of YA elements. Don't let the title fool you: this one isn't a holiday title, so it can be read any time. I can honestly say I think fans of fantasy, dragons, wizards and alternative worlds will find it delightful too.

reviewerName: David G "science fiction and fantasy  fanatic"
reviewText: Reminiscent of Thomas Deprimas Jennifer Carver series, Space Vikings series by Terry Mancour. the Frontiers Saga by Ryk Brown, empire series by Chris Nuttall, Slaver Wars by Raymond Weil.  Slightly better reads of this type are The Lost Fleet by Jack Campbell, The Serrano series by Elisabeth Moon, Longknife series by Mike Shepherd, Berserker series by Saberhagen.  David Weber and Steve White do this type of military fiction even better but I have read all their older published books and they are getting excessively greedy with their latest books. If you like this type of book try try their books In Death Ground, The Shiva Option, The Stars at War, Honor Harrington series, or Posleen War series by John Ringo, , Empire by Michael Hicks...  But this book is inexpensive and a fun mindless read. Not as good military space opera as some of those mentioned but still mindless romp through galactic battles at a very attractive pricing.  This military space battles is one of my favorite type of reads, so I did enjoy this book, particularly at the this reasonable price.I am going to give same review for entire series as the quality and pricing is consistent. These are not deep reads, nor the best military space books published. A single ship and her captain against all odds repeatedly saving their space fleet by simply fighting smarter/braver/good guys win.  Reminiscent of Star Trek,  What they are are an inexpensive good way to fill a day on the beach when you want to be entertained but not so engrossed you are unable to check out the bikini's (or speedo's depending on your preference) occasionally.

I received my copy from the publisher through Love Romances and More and rated it 3+ stars.Sex & Candy is the third book in the Arbor Heights series but the first title in this series for me. Having just checked the blurbs for the two previous titles, ‘Learning to live’ and ‘Learning to Breathe’ I think I can safely say this book can be read as a stand-alone title.Brad has had a crush on his best friend Geoff ever since they shared a kiss when Brad was 14. Having waited for Geoff to come to terms with his homosexuality for years, Brad is devastated when he receives an invitation to Geoff’s wedding. Determined to forget about his old friend, Brad finds himself at a private party at ‘Blue Dogs’; a party where men leave their inhibitions at the door and enjoy themselves and each other.Tristan has been throwing the Blue Dogs parties for years when he lays eyes on Brad. From the moment he sees the newcomer, Tristan knows he’s something special. One night of no strings sex leads to dates and deepening feelings. The path to love rarely runs smooth though and doesn’t for Brad and Tristan either. Geoff’s post-honeymoon regret is only one of the obstacles the two men will have to overcome.I’m not entirely sure what to say about this book. I liked the basic story-line and I liked the two main characters but there were quite a few things I was less than happy with.To summarize; there was too much happening in this story. In fact there was so much going on that not a single story threat felt sufficiently filled out. As it is we are reading about one character, Brad, getting over a crush he’s had for years, going to a sex party for the first time in his life where he meets and falls for the party’s organiser. Tristan has been organizing these M/M sex parties for years and feels real attraction to one of his guests for the first time when he meets Brad. If this book had only been about the developing relationship between those two men and how they deal with the disparity between their growing connection and the free-for-all atmosphere of the parties this book would probably have been perfect. However, that’s not all we’re dealing with. Thrown into the mix are Geoff’s denial of his feelings, his wedding and his subsequent turn-around; Geoff’s younger brother’s despair because he is also gay and Geoff’s homophobic parents throwing their youngest son out. And, to top it off, Brad and Tristan play cupid for two other side-characters.This was just too many story-lines for a novella this length. As a result everything felt rushed and unfinished. I liked Brad and Tristan but never really got to know them. A parent rejecting their own children because they’re gay is a something I’ll never get my head around and definitely something worth exploring in a story. The problem is that it wasn’t explored in this book; it was only mentioned but didn’t get resolved.My final quibble concerns the title. While there is plenty of very yummy ‘sex’ in this book, I’m not sure where the ‘candy’ comes into it.I can’t help feeling that this would have been a brilliant romance if only the author had been able to resist the temptation to throw everything bar the kitchen-sink into it. The writing was smooth, the dialogue well done and at times funny while the characters – what we saw of them – were interesting. This was a very pleasant read that left with a yearning for a lot more.

reviewerName: Joseph M Chiron "Author of Tagged The Apocalypse"
reviewText: Conrad Blake walks the reader through all of the necessary equipment. He covers hydration, layers, shelter, getting lost, how to get found..all of the essential tools and techniques necessary for survival in the wilderness. Any serious hiker knows that the difference between life and death in a tough situation is 1% luck and 99% preparation. Mental and physical preparation coupled with knowledge and use of the right equipment. I highly recommend this book to any beginning hiker. Happy hiking!

This book starts with general preparedness tips and advice, but progresses to specific advice concerning the contents of a Bug-Out-Bag. This is where the book comes into it's own as the author draws on his numerous years of backpacking and outdoor survival experience to offer practical advice that bucks the typical trend of overloading an emergency Bug-Out-Bag.The author constantly encourages the readers to evaluate the absolute necessity and usefulness of each piece of gear, while offering specific recommendations that will help the reader keep his or her pack weight down.The book also has some interesting stories that help to drive home the points about preparedness and survival.This book is well formatted for the kindle with a linked Table of Contents. Unfortunately, the "Go To..." menu doesn't take you directly to the TOC. It sets you on the copyright page where you have to flip forward several pages to the TOC. The book flows well and you should be able to consume all the content in a sitting or two, but I would have preferred a easy access to the TOC for later reference. I like how the author has lots of bolded and italicized headers to break up the book and make it easy to read and skim.If you enjoyed this book, I also recommendUltralight Survival: Make a Small and Light Bug Out Bag That Could Save Your Lifefor even more advice along these lines on creating the lightest and most efficient bug-out-bag possible.
summary: Practical Advice That Obviously Comes From Experience

In this future reality poverty is abundant and ordinary people struggle everyday to survive. Most items we take for granted are no longer available and there is a thriving black market that supplies even the most basic of necessities .Into this setting enters Max (a wolf shifter) whom has been voted in as governor of California and unknown to most also leads the shifter resistance . He has worked alongside Audrey in his congress office and has always denied his attraction for her. Audrey is desperate to embrace her shifter ancestry and unlock her inner wolf. Doing so however would mean leaving her job and the man who she craves.Max is no longer safe as a hidden faction is hell bent on destroying him. His life is on the line and Audrey is drawn more into his world then she ever expected and the consequences could be disastrous !I found this to be an enjoyable read and totally unlike any other shifter book I have read. Ms Gimpel set the scene really well as the possibility of our planet running out of resources is a real issue even today. This isn't an easy throwaway read as I feel the issues raised will resonate for many. Yes it's a paranormal romance but its much more than that. This is a book to awaken minds and the enticing characters are sure to delight.I would rate this a 5 as I found I didn't put it down until I had finished !

First off, when I bought this book it was for free. It sat in my Kindle for over a month before I finally started it. Before I was finished I was thinking to myself, this should not be given away for free. In spite of the editing issues, (which in the grand scheme of things really aren't as numerous or as bad as they could be, I've seen more egregious errors, trust me) there was some really good writing here. There were some very descriptive scenes, and some that were just very well worded. ("I hear my name whispered into the sunrise"? Can I steal that? No? OK.)What I did not like about the book: Even though I don't understand abuse and think abusive people should be pushed off a bridge, I understood the reasoning behind the father's abuse: he was a mean drunk. But there was never any reason given for why the brother was so angry and abusive. He was a complete and utter a**, I do know that. And a total wackadoo. I did not like the mother, because though she was accepting of her son Logan and generally sweet to everyone, being that completely oblivious to something under your own nose I simply can't fathom. Even if my kids don't tell me I know when something's going on with them. This mother is practically aiding and abetting. And I especially hated the fact that even if no one wanted to go to the police, they should have at least taken Logan to the hospital, even if they felt the need to lie about what was going on. What if he'd gotten an infection in that cut on his neck? What if his ankle had been broken towards the end?!? But I did have a bit of an issue with not going to the police, because what if Brian found Logan again? Abusers do that, you know. Also, it was never mentioned what these young men did for a living, so I was left wondering how someone at age 20 or 21 could afford a house on his own...What I did like: I loved Logan. I loved Felix. I loved their relationship. I love William! His hyperactivity was hilarious, but he was such a good friend. I even came to really like Jerry once he accepted what was going on. (Did anyone else feel like there could've been something between Jerry and William?) Anyway, now that I know this is a series, I'm looking forward to the rest.
summary: Well worth the time and the price

A Hunter's Blade is so packed full of excitement, paranormal elements, mystery and romance that any paranormal fan could appreciate using it as an escape from their everyday realities :)Brigit is a born werewolf that has been around for many years. She's one female to be admired; very strong, independent, beautiful and kind.  When humans start being found dead right after her turning during the full moon she's in a panic. She's not killed a human in a long time, yet has no recollection of some of the time she was in wolf form. She gets even more panicked when a hunter named Austin shows up in her place of business and starts asking questions. It's not only the questions that are bothering her, but the feelings his presence invokes within her.Austin is a fairly new vampire and also a hunter. As a human he worked with the FBI and was darn good at his job. Now as a vampire, there are different rules, different hours and different dietary requirements, but he still gets to help the way he's always loved. Currently on the hunt, he must investigate the murder of many humans. All clues are pointing in one direction, but he finds it very hard to believe, especially with the feelings he has whenever he's around her.Loved the characters and the fact that two sworn enemies come together in the very best of ways. One can never mess with the path fate has set and even trying to do so is just a waste of time and energy. I look forward to what Cera will bring us in the next of the series
