Bloodline is a very dark, different type of story. Luna Lanchester, the main character, knows she has demons in her and, at the beginning of the book, is wanting to find someone that can be a demon slayer for her. She had just moved to a new home with her mother after her parents' divorce. You're sort of given information that her father apparently abused her and she's mad at her mom because she just turned a blind eye to her daughter's tortuous life. She meets Sean, a handsome guy that she can see demons in as well. She's both drawn and repelled by him, and of course he's evil. There's also Dammon, her next door neighbor, but he's basically too good to be a demon slayer. Thirdly, there is her dark angel, Bane. He's been in her dreams forever and is the one she's completely in love with. Even though he tells her he is real, she doesn't believe it since he is just a dream.Things happen though and, even though she's warned to stay away from Sean who is a warlock and high priest to a coven of warlocks, she sees him again. She has no backbone when it comes to him, even after he kidnaps her, drugs her, sucks her blood etc. It's all very dark and Sean is nothing but a sadistic demon possessed man. He wants to just inflict pain and fear in Luna.It was around here that I just wanted to stop reading because it just kept getting worse (such as when Sean sees Luna and Dammon talking he commands her to stay away from him and if she doesn't he says he'll kill Dammon and then rape her in his blood.) I continued on, though, and after some events, Luna and her mom move to a new town and things definitely start to lighten up a bit and became more interesting. There's still demons - like Luna meeting Bane who can be just as dark as Sean. But he's in love with Luna, something that should never have happened since he's a son of Lucifer. She makes a couple new friends, Izzy and her brother Roman and she starts to find out more about who she really is and why the sons of Satan and the covens of witches are all interested in her - more specifically, her blood.The beginning of the book sort of dragged and, as I mentioned, was very dark. Once they moved to Sleepy Hallow the story definitely became more interesting and you finally start to learn things about Luna and the Lanchester line. Luna also becomes a more developed character and you can finally start understanding things about her and sympathizing with what turned her into the person she is. I feel like she would have been a more likable character for me if I had known the information at the beginning instead of so late in the book.Another thing with the book is it needs a really good edit. For instance, names would be misspelled (like Satan in one sentence and then Satin in the next) and just a lot of mixing up of homophones as well as some sentences that just made no sense. I try to overlook grammar issues, but there were just too many.Overall, if dark, sadistic demons, and the like are your sort of thing, I'm sure you'll enjoy the book.

The premise of this story is absolutely unique and intriguing; however, the execution leaves a lot to be desired.  Abby and Reginald (Rocky) were in love and engaged at the ages of 17 and 22 respectively.  Rocky was the heir to a Dukedom, Abby the third daughter of a Baron--in no way an eligible parti for a Duke.  Rocky is forced to break the engagement; a few years later he married a more "appropriate" woman.  In the meantime, Abby served as governess to her sister's daughter; she never married.  Thirty years later, immediately upon his wife's death, Rocky returns to reclaim Abby...the woman he has always loved and never forgotten.  For her part, when Rocky ended their engagement, Abby was a broken woman.  Even now, thirty years later, she still feels the pain of the loss as if it were just yesterday.  The story moved at a quick pace to it's conclusion, including HEA and epilogue (I love epilogues!)One issue I had with the story is, IMO, Abby took Rocky back way too quickly.  I mean the second time the two meet, she accepts a marriage proposal!  Furthermore, when Rocky first proposes they be together, Abby believes he is asking her to be his mistress, and she agrees!  I found it unacceptable that she would be willing to debase herself to that degree, especially considering Rocky was single and available to marry her.  In my mind, if he had had the nerve to ask her to be his mistress, she should have kicked him to the curb, not agree to the arrangement!  Personally, I would have liked it if Rocky had actually had to fight to get Abby back.  IMO, it was just way too easy for him.The main problem I had with the story; however, is the fact that I did not believe the entire premise of the story--that Rocky had been forced against his will to leave Abby.  And, since I had problems believing that, the entire story just seemed contrived.  We are told that at the time of their engagement, Rocky is 22, his father, the previous Duke, died when Rocky was 6 years of age.  It is Rocky's mother who threatened to disinherit him, should he fail to comply with her demand that he set aside the engagement.  First of all, as the eldest son (indeed the only son) as soon as Rocky's father died, he would have inherited the Dukedom, thus his mother would not have the power to disinherit him.  Furthermore, at the age of 22 Rocky is of legal age, so even IF his mother had been his legal guardian and had any authority over him, that would have ceased by this time (and more than likely a male would have been appointed as Rocky's guardian, not his mother.)  Then there is the fact that during that time period, a man could not break an engagement, (only a woman could) not without causing an enormous scandal and impugning his own honor...though I guess we could assume that in this instance, Abby was willing to release Rocky from the engagement, although that is not what we are told.Then there is the issue with the timeline.  When the engagement is broken off, Abby decides to go live with her sister and serve as governess to her niece.  Thirty years later, said niece is only twenty years old, when she could not have been any younger than 30, not if she was alive when Rocky and Abby broke up.  But, honestly, there are so many glaring mistakes in the book that the niece's mistaken age is just par for the course.  For example early in the story, we are told the niece's fiancé left when she was 16 and has been missing for four years (which is why I assumed she was twenty.)  Then later in the story, we are told the fiancé has been missing for 10 years, and then again, just a few lines down on the same page, we are told it's been 8 years!!!!!  How can there be so many blatant mistakes in one story?  Then there is also the minor issue of inaccurate forms of address (which typically is a pet peeve of mine, but in this instance got overshadowed by the more overt mistakes.)  As the daughter of a baron, Abby would be titled Honorable Miss, NOT Lady.  The same is true for her niece, who is also the daughter of a baron.Ms. Eaton has such a wonderful talent for storytelling, but fails to take the time to review her book for blatant mistakes, doesn't bother to make sure that the facts of her story coincides with its timeline, and neglects to research the time period in which she sets her story.  The end result is that the entire story comes across as though it has been carelessly thrown together, without much thought or consideration.  It wasn't until I finished this book, that I realized that I've read another book by this author..."The Winter Wish."  That was another lovely story that suffered from a deluge of historical inaccuracies.  If historical romances aren't really your thing, or if you don't care about historical inaccuracies in the books you read, then you may very well enjoy this story.  Based on the number of 4 and 5 star reviews, I see a  lot of people enjoyed it quite well.  If however, you are a historical romance purist, or if you're like me--I'm not a purist, but I do like the period in which the story is set to be as historically accurate as possible, although I am willing to allow the author some creative wiggle room--then avoid this book like the plague.  If Amazon allowed I would rate this book 2 1/2 stars.  BTW this is not a clean romance.  Happy reading!

reviewText: A beautiful love story set against the backdrop of a small town, Andy’s story will strike a familial cord with many. Piali Roy is a teacher at a residential school in Mussouri and one day she gets a phone call that brings her past before us. Sathya Nair wants to marry her at any cost and he is not about to listen to a ‘no’. Who is this Sathya? Why did she run away from him?Piali and Sathya meet at a teacher training program. She is one of the teachers while he is the Principal’s son. He is engaged to be married while she is wildly attracted to him. Piali tries to dismiss her love as infatuation but Sathya sets her aflame when he confesses to love her.She tries to stay away from him but Sathya pursues her persistently with a single-minded devotion. He breaks off his engagement and boldly declares his love for her to his parents. Piali’s father is livid.A rigid minded man who values his tradition and culture, he finds it difficult to accept the fact that his daughter would want to marry a non-bengali. Sathya’s parents are equally frustrated with him for breaking a good match and they view Piali as a home breaker. I liked the way Andy deals with a sensitive subject such as inter-caste love and marriage. Piali’s father’s character is very well developed in this book. Using him as a mouth-piece, Andy brings out the small-town mentality and general outlook of people. Will Piali and Sathya come together again? Do their parents overcome the barrier of caste and creed?  You will need to read this intriguing social romance to find out the answers.Fantastic language and prose. Andy’s style of writing is very lucid that sucks you into the story right from the first line.

A life changing and tragic thing happens to her that she just can't get over and for the last two years she's hidden herself away from everyone. She blames herself for what happened that valentines night. The guilt and heartache are hard for her to endear. This year is going to be different. No longer will Frey allow her to do this to herself. He's got to find a way to prove to Liese that she deserves to be happy and loved and he's the guy to do all that. He's know Liese practically all his life and he knows her better than anyone. He's loved her from afar all these years. He's been her best friend, her shoulder and now he wants her to know how strongly he feels and he's pulling out all the stops.I can't say enough about the swoon worthiness of Frey. He's the kind of guy you've wanted around you growing up. The friend, the trouble maker, the lover? Maybe, maybe not. Why don't you find out.  I'm glad I did.

reviewText: Get ready to fall in love! Ms. Williams characters will grip your heart and you'll find yourself wanting to do anything you can to help.David Langley is a minister who is especially drawn to orphaned children. He himself is an orphan, having lost his parents and a sister in a fire when he was 2 years old. David was left with horrible burns, now scars, from this fire. He hasn't let anyone see them because he's afraid of what people might say or think.Sadie Miller has just recently lost her father. Her mother died years before. After the death of her mother, she devoted her time to taking care of her father. Sadie didn't get out and didn't have friends over. Her "social" circle was home and church. It's pretty apparent that she has her eyes on Pastor Langley. She loves baking him cookies, pies, etc.I really enjoy Shawna's writing! She has the ability to take you right to the time periods, and the towns she writes about. Her characters are so real! I feel like I know them. Little Caleb is an orphan, with a physical disability, that was supposed to be adopted by a local family in Brady Hill. But shortly before he was due in town, the family changed their minds. The Sheldon's found out they were expecting their own baby and didn't feel they could take care of a little boy during Mrs. Sheldon's pregnancy. I just wanted to reach into the book and pull Caleb out and take him home!Sadie is asked if she can take care of Caleb until David can find a home for him. Of course she falls in love with little Caleb and wants him for her own. What will the orphanage have to say about a single lady taking charge of a child? Can Sadie and David overcome the barriers that keep them from opening up and loving?  I've given "Orphaned Hearts" 5 stars! It deserves every one of them!

Friendly Fire by Megan Hart* I received a copy of this book from NetGalley in exchange for an honest review*Friendly Fire is a story about forgiveness and love with lots of hot sex thrown into the mix.  Kendall's partner is killed in the line of duty and she blames herself.  She had issues with him but didn't want to see him dead.  She agrees to a weeklong "vacation" that is sanctioned by the bureau where she will undergo physical and psychological testing while trying to enjoy the beach.Zane is also an undercover agent and the one that shot Kendall's partner.  They were working a case and Zane tried to stop the slaughter but caught Kendall's partner with a stray bullet.  Zane now has to live with the fact that he shot & killed another agent, even though it was ruled an accident.  Will Kendall be able to forgive him, will he ever forgive himself?The air is sexually charged whenever Zane and Kendall get within 10 feet of each other.  Both find the other attractive and interesting but Kendall is angry with him and herself because of what happened with her partner.  Fate puts them in a cabin that shares a balcony and things definitely heat up.Kendall constantly had to prove herself to her partner at work that she was just as competent as any of the men.  She is used to being alone.  Her job doesn't allow for much time to date so she has become self sufficient, so to speak.  She doesn't realize how unfulfilled she is until Zane enters the picture.I like that she is a strong female lead but she still has a feminine, girly side.  We see that in her delight at simply putting on a dress and makeup instead of work clothes.  She is also comfortable enough with her sexuality to know what she wants and isn't afraid to go after it.  She is still cautious as her and Zane start the dance.I loved the scene where each was in their own bedrooms; it was very erotic to read.  The scene on the tour was also very hot.  There is good chemistry between the main characters so the story flows nicely.  I wish we had a little more time with this couple.  I would be interested to see if there is any truth to the concerns the doctor had.The scenery was beautiful, the characters were interesting and the story had plenty of steam, what's not to love?  Overall I enjoyed Friendly Fire and give it 4 Flaming Hearts.

reviewText: I have never read a book on the paleo diet and only picked this up to find out what it is.  If you haven't read "Fast Food Nation," then get this book to find out why you are unhealthy; if you have read it, get this book to find out how you can fix your health and help to prevent disease.  I have an auto-immune disease that I was able to cure myself by changing my lifestyle and what I eat.  At first I was very strict which led to the disease going into remission.  Although I didn't stay on my healthy eating plan 100%, I can confirm that spikes in the processed food that I ingest spikes my auto-immune disease.I wouldn't call this a "diet book;" it outlines why you are unhealthy and how to change that.  If you're tired of being tired, this well written book will give you plenty of reasons to change.  I like that it has a 7-day sample diet at the end of the book which would give you a way to test it to see if it's something you want to continue.  It makes sense and from my own past issues, I know it can work to prevent disease and reduce the effects of disease.
summary: Change your lifestyle; eliminate the disease!

Koboah was indeed a interesting read for me.  I am a African American  and I am very careful of my reads with any 'slaves' however, the book cover caught my attention and I thought I would see just  what "Dark Genesis" was about.This novel dealt with the story of Luna who was a beautiful slave with supernatural powers...having the gift of the second site, that had been through so much....taken from her mom, then be served up to two masters (Henry & John) then taken away by Avery (demon). Teaching her to read, riding  Julia (horse) and shoot a gun.  Oh my what a  story!....Avery left her with a gold chain, farmhouse and even ...Dembi......now  you will have to pick up this novel ..."Dark Genesis" and get all of this well written story.The characters were a real lively group ....Luna, Jupiter(Dembi), Father Geoffrey, Mama Akosua, Ebenezer, Mr. Walker, Matthew, Zila, and Avery, Lina... and a few others I have left out.  The author really knew how to keep the reader interested in the read because each chapter got even more engaging in its twist and many turns.After reading "Dark Genesis"  I thought it was a novel that I could recommend as a good read.

reviewText: Some decisions are easier to make than others. The trick is to figure out ahead of time exactly how far you’re willing to go to reach your goals.This was my first introduction to this author’s work and it has whet my appetite for more. Mr. Power did quite well at introducing this reader to his characters through a series of subtle hints about their personalities that are sprinkled throughout fast-paced plots.“The Loving Husband and the Faithful Wife” has a strong, intriguing premise, but I had trouble piecing together some of the clues the narrator provides about what is happening. A few of them seem to be mutually contradictory, and I would have preferred to see more time explaining how all of them fit together. I don’t know if the author intends to write a sequel to this tale, but I would be quite interested in reading one if it is ever published. There is still so much these characters haven’t revealed about themselves yet.It took a few paragraphs for me to adjust to the Cockney dialect and nearly-constant swearing in “The Debt,” but Del’s predicament snagged my attention right away. At times it was a little difficult to believe he had grown up in such a rough neighbourhood due to how he reacts to certain things that are common in that sort of environment. Having an explanation for how this occurred would have resulted in a higher rating for this book. The pacing is strong, though, and Del’s journey is so compelling that I didn’t want to stop reading.The Loving Husband and the Faithful Wife is a promising collection. I look forward to seeing what Mr. Power writes next, and I’d recommend these stories to anyone who is new to the mystery genre. Either tale is a good place to start.Originally posted at Long and Short Reviews

I tend to be a tough (some might say harsh) judge of the books I read. I look for 1) strong female heroines, 2) plot twists that keep me engaged, 3) coherent writing with appropriate editing, and 4) character development.  This book has everything I enjoy most about leisure reading. Melody was fun and courageous while Gavin was an honorable guy. They were stuck in a horrible situation and Gavin's caring nature shone through to support Melody and give her the ability to rise above the situation.  This plot could have been tragically written and made the readers hate both of the H & h, but here the writing was skillfully done and the readers end up cheering for Gavin and Melody.  There are the expected misunderstandings and hurt feelings that drive the plot forward after Melody returns to society following the death of her husband. These only serve to further develop nuances to both characters which ultimately draw the reader in.  I hate to add spoilers in my reviews so - I'm leaving a LOT of information out. Please give this one a shot!  Ms. McNare should be encouraged and supported in her writing. I am eagerly anticipating reading her books in the future!  Keep them coming!

I enjoyed this book because of my interest in Sam and Nick, as well as the secondary characters we learn more about throughout the series.  The main plot was a bit over the top for me.  What I enjoyed most were the subplots: Sam learning how to best interact with the detectives under her charge; Sam's relationship with her father over the cold case he'd asked her to leave alone; Nick and Sam dealing with infertility issues.I started shaking my head in the first chapter when Nick and Sam decide they need domestic assistance and turn to Shelby, Washington's preeminent wedding planner.  It is absolutely unbelievable that someone who has spent years creating a business involving the most elegant events in Washington would suddenly be interested in cooking, cleaning, buying groceries and running errands.  The fact that she is called their assistant instead of their housekeeper changes nothing.Ms. Force would have us believe that the reasons for Shelby's desire to change career paths is because she is sick of being around couples in love when she has no relationship of her own and that because she wants to have a baby.  The first reason doesn't wash because we all know there aren't two more crazy in love adults in D. C. than Nick and Sam.  Can you imagine being around all the PDA going on in that house?  Since the main reason Sam and Nick need Shelby is for childcare, does it make sense to hire someone without any experience in that field?  I understand the desire to keep Shelby in the series, but am not sure this was the best way to go.I agree with some reviewers who think Scotty is a little too perfect for a 12 year old boy.  Even Sam and Nick are allowed to have flaws.As for the 50 Shades influence, I could have lived without it.

reviewText: Up-and-coming advertising agent Stella Sinclair is determined to score the Toliver account, but to get it she's stuck in Montana for a weekend.  Stella doesn't know what she's going to do in the small town. What she does know is that she has to find a bathroom because there's no way she'll make it all the way back to her hotel.  When Stella stops at a local bar, she's saved from a fall by gorgeous cowboy JD Foster.  Instant attraction sparks between the pair, but what Stella doesn't know is that JD happens to be a member of the family whose business she's courting.  JD wants Stella, for the right reasons, so he doesn't tell her everything about himself.  After all, what's the harm in one little white lie?A Little White Lie is a sexy romance that'll capture you hook, line, and sinker.  Stella, a fish-out-of-water city girl in Montana, is smart, funny, and sweet, which makes her immensely likeable.  As for JD...get out a fan - Mackenzie McKade sure does know how to write some seriously hot cowboys.  I found JD every bit as irresistible as Stella did and together those two practically burned the pages of the book to ash.  A Little White Lie zips along at a rapid pace, but though it's a fast read, it's a thoroughly satisfying one.  I absolutely adored A Little White Lie and am thankful to Ms. McKade for penning yet another utterly delicious cowboy hero.ShaynaReviewed for Joyfully Reviewed

Unchain My Heart is the continuation of Ryder and Jade's love story and takes up where Two Worlds Colliding left off. "The Biker and The Princess."This time we also meet Harrison and Eva, Jade and Ryder's respective siblings and see how their relationship begins.As it is with all of Jani's books, I enjoy her writing style. It is a fast paced read, and there is always something happening to keep you interested in turning those pages and jam-packed full of emotion.Unchain My Heart is told via four different points of view- Ryder, Jade, Harrison and Eva. All these characters have very different personalities and have likeable or admirable traits.Ryder is showing less of his "bad ass biker" side, and we see more of a caring loving man that any woman deserves. He isn't developed too quickly in this direction and the shift feels realistic.Jade is still the feisty princess that we know and love, and all she wants is to be with Ryder and for her family to accept it.Then there is Harrison, Jade's brother and a police officer out for revenge. This character is hard to judge as he's clearly a broken and angry man, he doesn't come across as a very nice guy. I found him hard to like at first because he was quite hostile. However, I believe he has good intentions, and that makes him admirable.Finally, we meet Eva; Ryder's half sister. She comes across as a very smart, sophisticated woman and is very likeable from the word go. Eva is drawn to Harrison as he is to her, and the start of their relationship is anything but normal. Interesting nonetheless.This story contains violence, drama and very steamy sex scenes. All the elements a good biker book needs. The ending has been left open ready to carry over to the next installment in this series that may or may not appeal to you. I didn't feel shortchanged by this as I expected the opening to be left knowing that there are more books to follow.Love your biker boys then you need to read this.4 stars!*copy of book gifted to me by the author in return for an honest review*
summary: The Biker, The Princess & The Beast

reviewText: A great book to read, short but very sweet. Nice couple, good plot, good characters. Wish it was longer though.

Imagine that your best friend is getting married and she asked you, yes, YOU, to be the Maid of Honor!  How awesome would that be?!  Except there's one problem.....You.Are.A.Guy.This exactly how Kiss the Bride begins.  Herman Edward Heckley III (Heck) is now Maid/Man of Honor in his best friend Caroline Ann Oakenfield's (Caro) wedding.  She's marrying a man that Heck can't stand and her family isn't to fond of either.  Little does anyone know the reason Caro is marrying the "pencil-necked geek."  And Heck better figure it out before it's too late for everyone involved.Kiss the Bride is short novella that isn't lacking anything.  The characters are very likable.  It's easy to relate to them and it pulls from very realistic scenarios.  There are times when men and women just can't communicate anything properly.  Kind of like the tv show "Three's Company" ~ half of the show focused on misunderstandings between the 2 female and 1 male lead, and don't get me started on the landlords.As Caro's wedding day gets closer both Caro and Heck have some serious soul searching to do in order to get to their Happily Ever After.  What a wild ride it is, too.  Even as Heck begins to realize his feelings, he still proceeds with doing the Maid of Honor duties for Caro's wedding, while she is questioning herself at the same time.  The bachelorette party, complete with Officer Sexy, had me in stitches.This is a quick and easy read that is entertaining and has depth to the characters.  The secondary characters were written pretty well and certainly knew all along that Heck and Caro has feelings for each other.  Caro knew but Heck didn't provide any indications that he thought of her as anything other than a platonic friend.I enjoyed every bit of this novel and am glad that I had the privilege to read and review "Kiss the Bride" for Jody Wallace.ARC Review Copy Courtesy Of:  The publisher, Entangled: Ever After, via NetGalley, at no cost in exchange for an honest review.

I'm not that good of a cook. I definitely can't barbeque, but I was able to follow the recipes in this cookbook, which I appreciated because a lot of the time cookbooks assume a certain amount of knowledge that I don't have. The recipes were delicious as well, and I love steak, and my husband really loves steak so I was quite pleased with myself for being able to cook them.My personal favorite was the Garlic Butter Steak, but you should try them all!
summary: Easy to follow, delicious recipes for steak

reviewText: Bass player for white hot rock band Dazed, Reno Rocket is riding a career high though he's the first to admit his personal life is the complete opposite. In all truth the twenty one year old is controlled by an overbearing father who has gone so far as to handpick a girl for him to marry.Reno is ambivalent about his fiancée. Hell, he's never done more than kiss her goodnight after a date when he's back home. The only time his libido feels alive is when lead singer Tanner Star is rubbing against him on stage. It's a good thing he's playing his bass so that he can hide a massive erection. No question, Tanner can light him up and set Reno on fire.Finally making his own intentions known, Tanner introduces Reno to the world of BDSM and explains the balance of a Dom/sub lifestyle. Reno agrees to explore his sexuality with Tanner, but unfortunately their relationship is leaked to the public and everything implodes for the young sub. Reno's only safety net is Tanner. Hopefully he will be willing to catch Reno before he falls.Take Me, Break Me entertains with true erotic delight. The world of BDSM unfolds in great detail as Tanner leads Reno into sexually charged ecstasy. They are shadowed by a father's brutality and a mother's lies, both of which are quickly and tidily resolved. Watching their relationship's roller coaster drama is the key to enjoying Take Me, Break Me. And it's a hot, wild ride.This book was reviewed by Lisa for Joyfully Reviewed (JR), and was provided by the publisher/author at no cost to JR for the purpose of being reviewed.

Alive at 5 is the romance suspense debut from Linda Bond who was a television reporter and just so happens that’s what the heroine Samantha Steele is. No time is wasted in throwing you right in the middle of the action. How these two first meet was defiantly a new one. Zack Hunter is a police officer and has gone undercover to try and find out how his uncle died. It’s tied into a company that provides adventure vacations. Zack is currently on a skydiving excursion and when it comes time for him to land there is a woman directly in his way with no way to avoid her. Samantha Steele is their along with her camera man to film all the adventures her mentor will be doing with the adventure company. Problem is when its his turn to jump there is a problem on the way down and he dies before hitting the ground. It doesn’t take Samantha long to figure out that Zack isn’t there for just the thrill seeking, that he lost someone too on one of the trips. So these two forge a alliance to basically go undercover together to figure out who is murdering the clients of the adventure group.If you like your romantic suspense fast paced with plenty of action scenes this is defiantly one you wont want to miss.
I did not care for this story. Did not make any sense to me. Going into a sleep to play a game. Way out of the there.

Man, this book really over delivers. It contains a ton of recipes.You just look in the refrigerator and there is good chance you can make a healthy & tasty juicing recipe from it. I tasted some of them and really they taste good!

This is a short story that has a lot of content and romance to keep in interesting.The story has small town girl Michelle Kolson, who always dreamed of living in the city.  Her father is the only one supportive of her new adventure.  Her mother and former boyfriend not so much.  She recently started working for LightWave Tech for the call center.  She doesn't know anyone in Chicago, and has not met everyone in the company.Noah Frellish a hot, computer geek.  He loves coding in his spare time and biking.  His circle of friends are mainly the people from the Help Desk and engineers in the company.  He is a billionaire and the CEO of LightWave.  His company went public recently.  He hasn't met any woman recently that likes him for who he truly is.  The women just pretty much go after him because of his billionaire status.I love Michelle and Noah's first meeting. She happens to have issues with the printer in her work area and Noah happens to be there.  He did not dress like a CEO: wore T-shirt with a term a techie would understand and a baseball cap.  He assists her with resolving what the issue with her printer was. They get to know a bit about one another that evening.  Only thing is, Noah introduces himself to Michelle as Sark, the nickname his friends call him.  Michelle has no clue he is the CEO of LightWave.  She thinks he is one of the help desk technicians.I enjoyed seeing the romance building up between the two.  At first, it was like they were feebly trying not to go on their feelings for one another since they work for the same company. That did not last very long since it was evident they were so attracted to one another.  Sark did make an attempt to let Michelle know who is really is, but she really did not understand his handwritten letter.This is the first time I have read a story of Lynne Silver.  I enjoyed how it was put together and the buildup of the entire story.  It's one of those sweet romance short stories that is worth reading.  You have to love those smart guys.  Of course it's a bonus if they're hot!  Good job Lynne!

AfterMoving On With Brock: A Passionate Second Chance Romance, I figured I needed another second chance kind of story. I've read Norah Wilson a number of times and she has never disappointed as a romance writer, and of course I thoroughly enjoyed this second book in her series. Protecting Paige is the story of a single mom and a broken cop--both very endearing in the way they uphold their responsibilities in everything that they do. Paige, although the lesser gender, is a force that threw Tom in a loop. She just couldn't be stopped when her mother instinct gets triggered, especially when she knew she's doing the right thing. So not even Tom's grumpiness was able to waylay her in trying to care for him without making it look like she's pitying him. Not that it's her mother's instinct that's the only thing triggered when she looks at Tom and see how manly he is. Tom, on the other hand, may resent accepting anyone's help particularly when he suspects he is being pitied, but the call of duty could not be denied when his cop sense smelled that Paige and her headstrong son is in danger and needed protection. So honorable and romantic that he tried every possible means, eventhough he's not a cop anymore and he's injured, to protect them. It's really delicious chemistry that Ms. Wilson has cooked for her characters. I loved how the story has heart, and how easy it is, a relief even, to relate to Paige and Tommy's characters because of background info written about them. Not to mention to care for other characters like Dillon, then bring in the injured dog that managed to not feel like a timely trigger to get them all together. Nice writing the dog-handler relationship, too. It made the whole story more solid. This is one of the best books of Norah Wilson that I've read, and I'm updating my list of her other titles, too!
summary: Compelling characters, smack on chemistry, well-written story.

reviewText: This is a different sort of story, a platoon of Army Rangers seconded to a UN peace-keeping force, trying to get out of strife-torn Africa and encountering an alien intelligence? Yet the plot doesn't bog down in absurdities, and remains more or less plausible and imaginative all the way through.About halfway though this one I bought two other of Mr. Cawdron's books.Well done!

The story begins with Pete and Daisy traveling to Vegas. They want to make money and live their dream of Daisy opening a nail salon and Pete a car garage.  They meet Aiden who basically owns Vegas and likes Daisy on sight. He offers the couple a million dollars for one day/night with Daisy. Daisy and Pete are from small town in Kentucky but Daisy has always had big dreams and wants the finer things in life. Pete, on the other hand, is okay with living in a small town and living a normal life. However, he will do anything to make Daisy happy for fear of losing her.There are a few reasons why I can't give this more than 3 stars.1) Daisy is selfish. She doesn't know her own mind and I wonder if she loves Pete or the idea of her and Pete. Pete in my opinion really loved Daisy but in his own way he was dense and fully consider who she was and what she wanted in life.2) Daisy basically having sex with Pete then having sex with Aiden two days later. I honestly didn't even need to read about her and Pete having sex in such detail and so many times. I guess it worked for the plot but I just hate things like that.3) Aiden made both Pete and Daisy an offer. I just don't think Daisy could have been that stupid to think they would just hang out for a day, especially when she felt an instant attraction to Aiden. Aiden, was the one I liked the most, he was the most honest of three.  I don't think Pete or Daisy was honest with themselves much less each other.I would have liked if things took place over the course of a week or two. I think it would have made the story better.Either way, It was a good read and I enjoyed it enough to want to read the second book.
This book was excellent from start to finish. It wasn't too dramatic. I love to read books that make you feel as though you were there. Awesome job. Please continue to produce.
There is a powerful message in this small book.  Recommended  to anyone caring to increase the power of their brain.
summary: How can you challenge your mind's power?

reviewText: Sacrifice is, at its heart, a coming of age tale, filled with laughs, tears and plenty of creepy and frightening moments. I thoroughly enjoyed this one. Left me a little sad to be honest, but it was real to life. Lots of scares and great characters in this one. Deals with teens in the 1980's and the present as they return to their small Long Island town to deal with issues (including a wicked ghost) from their past. FEAR the Woodsman!!!! Highly Recommended!!!!
summary: A Filled-with Horrors Coming of Age Tale

reviewText: A short, fun, sweet Christmas story about second chances at love. A fun way to relax and enjoy a few quiet moments during the holiday season.

This book was amazing!!  In book #1 Blue Love I wanted to smack Lucas for what he had done to Tessa.  I kept thinking Tessa walk away you deserve better. Don't be his friend! But, we all know girls always want that one who screws up.  Wasn't sure where New Love was going to take me.  I was unprepared for the emotional roller coaster that I went on.  I cried so hard and then turned around and felt so happy. You want to hate Lucas for all his screw ups but in turn he is so sweet and truly loves Tessa.  I kept hoping for everything to work for them but alas Lucas does it again.  MJ Fields has written another cliffhanger and I can't wait to read the next book.  She is truly an awesome writer and her books are so worth reading. I recommend this series to anyone who likes a good love story that is not always easy.

I found this story to be very thought provoking. I would say don't go into this story just expecting another zombie tale running a basic formula. There was a deeper look at how cold and distant the post apocalyptic world could be. A wonderful look of what hell just might be like for the damned and cowards, guilty of various crimes. The soul must die a thousand deaths. How long does one have to journey before retribution is awarded. I definitely think this is a story worth checking out if you're interested in following a different path and view on a zombie tale. An exploration of a broken mind and the broken souls that make up the cold foul world they now live in. I highly recommend reading this. Must read.

Our Review, by LITERAL ADDICTION's Vivacious Valkyrie - Marta:*Copy gifted in exchange for an honest reviewI first discovered this authors work when I read Never Again last year and was immensely surprised by how much emotion Ms Paolo generated in me. This book returns to characters previously discovered but switches the story to Josh who had been a supporting character. In this book we learn how he's coping after suffering through a heinous event that has left him traumatised and needing support.Josh met Kat two years ago but failed to convince her just how much she really meant to him. Now he's facing the aftermath of the terrible events that took place at his college, a massacre that left his friends dead and him wounded. Josh is understandably traumatised by it but is struggling with his physical recovery but when he meets the woman who is assigned to help him it's Kat the only girl that he's ever loved!This is a story that will resonate with many readers and although it's a romance aimed at young adults will appeal to those of all ages. Josh is a young man who is facing the very real prospect of never realising his dreams of being a baseball star but he is written as a guy full of humour and I thought the author captured a young mans viewpoint beautifully .I had genuine laugh out loud moments as he's so entertaining and I just wanted him to have his happy ending and get the girl!Kat is the heroine of this book and she's a young woman who sacrifices much to do what she feels is the right thing and I liked her so much. She's had to be strong and unbeknownst to Josh has suffered truly harrowing events in her life. Unfortunately her problems may not be over and she will need all her strength to face what's coming. She is quite hard on a Josh at times but he needs that as he needs for those around him to make him see that he's still normal in spite of his recent injury. As for his injury there's a moment in this story when I am unashamed to admit I had tears in my eyes as Josh recounts what happened .I would imagine most readers who pick this up will be expecting a second chance romance and yes it is that but so much more besides. It's an emotional story that's very well written about believable characters. I started reading this and admit I kept going as I just had to finish it. This story and indeed this series is most definitely recommended

Lindsay Wade is a shy, boring, and uptight receptionist. She's won an office raffle and reluctantly accepts the prize - one ticket to the celebrity magician Angelito Tarrago's new magic show. She's quickly seduced by the handsome magician and is pulled into a world of a secret society of those who possess real magic. She is eventually told that she is a female magi, and the subject of an ancient and scary prophecy. She's quickly torn between trusting her new lover Angelito or the mysterious rebel Demitri. Will Lindsay fulfill the prophecy and will she find love with one of these powerful men?I almost stopped reading this several times, but I hate not finishing books, even if I'm not enjoying it. Conceptually, this is interesting. The magic and the secret society is a great premise. The problem is that rather than examine and truly illuminate the world created, the book is mostly just one giant orgy after another. I didn't feel like I really understood the powers that were had by different people, Lindsay in particular. I didn't feel like I was given enough to truly grasp what the society did besides have sex. Lindsay is kept very much in the dark, and what she is told is only the same stuff repeated.It was also kind of surprising to see Lindsay be so shy in the beginning to become a total nympho who was willing to have sex with pretty much anything and anyone she came in contact with (how romantic!). This, to me, was not an erotic "romance," but rather straight erotica. While the sex scenes are not bad, they actually became annoying. I got tired of seeing every single character we met get it on. I wanted Lindsay to have a ROMANCE and stop masturbating for a minute.I would not recommend this for someone looking for an erotic romance (like I was), which is what the book is advertised to be. I was really annoyed by this, and I'm glad I got it free.
Thank you for the delightful book on cleaning the quick way! I shall be working on every member of my family getting to understand the shortcuts that can save us all such valuable time.

3.5 StarsBe sure to read The Do Over before you read It's Not Over.  Even though it can be read as a stand alone, you will have a better understanding of the characters if you read The Do Over and are introduced to them first.  In all honesty, after being introduced to Rick in The Do Over, I wasn't too excited about reading his story.  He kind of seemed like a jerk to me and I really didn't like him.  But in this book, he did redeem himself.  He showed that he finally knew what he wanted and did what it took to get it.  I enjoyed the story between Maddy and Rick, but there did seem to be a lot of back and forth that almost seemed TOO much.  A little of the "I like you but I don't like you", "I want you but you're not good for me" back and forth usually makes a book interesting for me because I like for the characters to fight for their love and to really show that they want it, but this book kind of took it to the extreme.  Overall, it was a good story and I loved that Maddy didn't put up with any of Rick's s***.  I thoroughly enjoyed the last bit of the book more than the beginning and I look forward to more from these characters.~Lauren~
summary: I thoroughly enjoyed the last bit of the book more than the beginning and I look forward to more from these characters.

reviewText: An amazing reading experience in unexpected places and towns. The characters were very entertaining and exciting to read about. A must read for those who enjoy historical romance kindle books.

This is another case that makes me wish I gave half stars. This book was more than a three, but not quite a four, for me. It was a sweet and sometimes sexy romance between two characters who have known each other most of their lives and have always been ultra-competitve.Ellie returns home to her small-town to run the family's funeral home after her dad is diagnosed with Alzheimer's. Her former crush, the guy who crushed her and beat her as valedictorian, is back from the Marines and running his family's funeral home as well. They're competitors again after all this time. He wants to buy her out, but she's not giving in. They forge a friendship and grow close again. They can't deny their attraction to each other and come to an agreement to enjoy each other physically, with no strings or expectations, but inevitably, feelings get involved and things become complicated.I really enjoyed both of these characters – as well as the supporting cast of B.B., Ashley and the others. Ellie and Finn had a ton of chemistry and you could cut the sexual tension with a knife. There are a couple steamy scenes in this book, too. It's a great romance and has a good focus on family – as imperfect as it can be at times. There were a couple scenes that made me more than a little emotional, but the book ended on a note that left me smiling.I received a copy of this book from the publisher in exchange for an honest review.
summary: In Review: Her Summer with the Marine (The Donovan Brothers #1) by Susan Meier

reviewText: This is the perfect diet. It is not difficult and it is easy to follow. The restriction are limited and the guidelines are easy. If you are looking for a simple way to lose weight just buy this book and follow the paleo diet.

reviewText: Very weird... but enjoyable to read.  Would not like to read an other of the same, but liked it.If I am enjoying thrillers a lot, I found that lately, they became a little too "out of space"!The story are not believable and that is the problem,

Elise survived the AllFather, but now her life on Earth is coming calling on her. Except she's not so sure that's what she wants anymore. Merrick has always been a loner being a hybrid no many want to be around him as it and he life certainly doesn't have the space or desire for a bride, not that there's a woman who would want someone like him anyways. But the two of them find peace in each other, until they realize it's because of an ill formed bond.Now they must set off to find a cure before the bond kills them. If the journey doesn't kill them first they might find happiness in the end, if they can open up to each other.Elise has her share of emotional scars, she keeps them locked up in "the vault" in her head, she goes through life, but never really lives it. Merrick has scars on the inside too, but he has even more on the outside. He's a big scary looking guy, but he's really a sweet caring man who would do anything for those he's closest to, he knows keeping the pain in isn't good and does his best to help Elise even when he doesn't know exactly what to do.Their story has allot of pain, but it shows that even those with a screwed up past can find their happiness as long as their willing to try.We see more of the new threat and what it is he wants and how he came to be.
summary: not that there's a woman who would want someone like him anyways

reviewText: Is there anybody in this world who doesn't want to have better sex??  Well, if those people do exist and you are one of them - then this book most definitely isn't for you.  As for people who want to create a steamier love life, boost an already steamy love life to a new level, have an exciting new journey, learn more about their partner or simply want to have some exciting new adventures - then this book is most definitely for you.  Many sexual topics are delved into - such as foreplay and orgasm control and many ideas are played forward into our minds.I don't think that Stephen Williams is trying to reinvent the wheel here and I do feel, as with many of his books, that he could go into a bit more detail and elaboration in each section and give the book a bit more `meat'.  However, I do appreciate how he challenges people to take new views and perspectives and recreate the every day into something special and new.  I also like that he emphasizes communication.  While we are becoming a more sexually aware and sexually open nation, I find that people are still quite shy to discuss their sexual wants and needs and this can often cause major intimacy issues that simply aren't necessary.I think the enduring message of this book and similar-themed books by Williams, is that as long as we are alive, we will always be learning new ways to do everything.  I think for something as pleasurable as sex, there will definitely be extra effort put into finding new ways to reach different heights of sensual bliss and I imagine that there will never cease to be a shortage of ideas.  Thank you for sharing your imagination with us Stephen Williams!
summary: Soaring to new levels of sensuality

Malorie Blackman has shown that she knows one of the deeper aspects of the Seventh Doctor. His character had a clown like personality on the outside, but on the inside he had a sadness, a seriousness, and a loving nature that proved for the rest of the years that Doctor Who has lasted and the rest of the years it will last that the Doctor has a heart (or two). reviewText: If you are a fan of Lora Leigh's Breed Series or Laurann Dohner's New Species series concepts, you should like this one.  Evil corporation using DNA manipulation to create a supersoldier with animalistic powers.Minus the random spelling errors or editing mishap - it was a good story. I would have liked more detail and for a few more things to be explained better.  For example - what determines what makes a Vestal?  how can a human tell?I have read all 3 and my feelings about the series have remained the same.  I like it, will keep reading them - just want more details.

I'm trying not to give five-star reviews any more. Those should be life-changing. But J. F. Smith's "Falling off the face of the earth" is a wonderful book, don't get me wrong.  It is full of people who you grow to care about; it is full of ideas that make you think; it is a love story that involves a community, not just two people.James Montgomery has returned to his small-town Georgia roots to recover.  His glittering career in NYC has crashed and burned, and he has suffered a hideous personal loss. No wonder he seeks solace in the red Georgia clay.As James begins to settle into what he sees as a temporary recovery period in his career, he begins to re-learn all of the unhappy truths that made his adolescence in Lawter, Georgia so painful. He begins to look more closely at the people he knew and the place he fled, and gradually comes to understand that there's more to small-town life than he might have supposed.  Don't get me wrong--there's plenty of pain still, but pain is part of life no matter where you live. This book is all about being gay in America--but not ONLY about being gay.Kevin, Roddy, Bea, Lindsey, Jerry, Carrie-Ann, Cory, Jesus, Stefanie, Ian--these are the characters you'll meet, and whose humanity and flawed goodness will touch you, even as they begin to shape James's world and thaw the frozen emotions in his heart.  While unusually long, this book didn't feel long to me; and if the editing isn't as sleek as I might like it, it never interfered with my appreciation of the solid core that makes this book an enormously satisfying read.
summary: Sometimes your dreams end up in your own back yard...

reviewText: What started off as a fairly decent story, quickly dived into "OMG, WTF?!!" At first the characters were pleasant enough, intelligent and intriguing... that is, until they started sharing scenes together. I'm almost positive their IQ's dropped to a collective 10. The smexy times were so comical, I was just completely O_O. I swear the sex scenes in this book put cliched porno's to shame.I mean absolutely no offense to the author, but it was as if it were written by an adolescent boy. I thought I was reading something out of American Pie! By far the most un-sexy erotica/romance novel I have ever come across. That said, this will make an awesome gag gift for a friends birthday coming up! I can't recommend this book unless you're in the mood for a good laugh. Although for me, the novelty wore off at 47% and I just DNF it. But I will remember it for a very long time to come...

L.W. Wilson's little book, "How to Overcome Depression Fast," is a fast read, and yet it covers all the basics in a well organized fashion, clearly describing the different levels of depression, from mild to severe, and discussing commonly used traditional methods of treatment. While the author advises us to seek a professional diagnosis, first, he then goes on to give details of alternative and natural treatments that we can pursue ourselves, in lieu of, or in addition to traditional treatment, all of which are extremely good advice, logical, clear and attainable. As one who has bouts of mild depression, from time to time, it is good to know what I can do to get back in control and to be reminded of how best to avoid future depression. Also, it is good to know the symptoms of severe depression, so as to know when to seek outside help.Regardless, of the title "Fast," the author points out that we should not expect immediate results. Recovery and healing take time.
summary: Good Advice to Keep in Mind

reviewText: Excellent ending. I very much enjoyed this book and the series as a whole. I would recommend it to anyone for a good read.

Only a few chapters in. I hadn't come to a point where I couldn't read any further but I could tell based on what I'd read so far I was going to have to take notes in order to provide an honest review. I wanted to provide constructive criticism.Star rating subject to change as I read further… (have finished the book and I'll leave it at 2 stars but it's more like 1 1/2 stars)So far I've noticed exact phrases repeated more than once within a few paragraphs of each other which can be annoying. This gives the impression of beating a dead horse. You're trying to convey something to the reader so you feel if you repeat it enough we'll get it. It's not necessary. When I come across this it makes me think the author doesn't think I'm very intelligent, or that I have a short attention span (which I do usually but I think I can manage to retain information from one paragraph to the next).Wrong words used, poor spelling and bad grammar (I know I'm not one to talk about grammar) so far and I'm only a few chapters in.A couple of example of wrong words"I must of looked…" should be "I must have looked…""The idea was to appealing…" should be "The idea was too appealing…"Okay so have read a little bit further and I REALLY recommend this book be edited.All that considered I like the plot so far but I'm not far enough along to comment fully on it. Twice the word 'since' was used when sense was the intended word."…she got caught me looking at me." is a perfect example of an awkward sentence which just happens to be one of many.Having finished the book I can say that serious editing is required but beyond that the story is cute. Cute is really all I can say because I didn't develop any attachments to characters. I wasn't emotionally invested in the story. It evoked nothing in me really and for the most part I was distracted by the incredibly poor editing.
summary: Story was not enough to save it

This review is based on an ARC provided by the author in an exchange for an honest review.There is the seed of something very original and quite intriguing at the heart of T.S. Alan's The Romero Strain. Wrapped in what looks like a very run-of-the-mill zombie apocalyptic thriller is the concept that what caused the dead to rise might affect certain people in a very different way - something that the protagonist of the Romero Strain learns first-hand.It's a pity then that I had such trouble relating to him.I'm not sure if Alan was trying to make his main character edgy, or just different to the usual hero that populates this type of read. Well, he certainly succeeded, but not in a way that endeared J.D. Nichols to me. At the beginning of the novel, J.D is taking his dog for a walk when the zombies begin running amok. Within 30 pages, he has managed to act entitled, stuck up, sexist, and creepy - all while putting down barely a handful of zombies. This made for a tricky read, as the entire novel is told from his first-person perspective. He does seem less off-putting by the end of the novel, but not before becoming uber-creepy (view spoiler).Troublesome main character aside, Alan does create some better minor characters for J.D. to riff off, though his habit of quoting movies with another survivor stopped being quaint by the end of Part One.The other main issue I had with The Romero Strain typifies that found in first-time novels: namely, the pacing was wildly inconsistent. After a frenetic beginning, Alan slows things to a crawl, detailing buildings and structures that no-one other than a native New Yorker could possibly care about. Things then meander through the middle part of the novel, before building nicely toward the end, only for the action to completely stop when J.D. has one of his many selfish moments and decides to go visit his old neighbourhood - dragging the reader for a stroll down a memory lane that had zero impact on the overall plot.The ending would seem to leave things wide open enough for a sequel, and despite the above issues, I suspect many will be interested to see where Alan intends on taking his characters. Hopefully, he'll dedicate more of that sequel's run time to fleshing out the idea of what else other than zombies people are becoming in his version of the apocalypse.I rated this 2 stars elsewhere, but with Amazon's recommended rating system suggesting 2 stars = "I don't like this", this is actually a 2.5 to 3 star read for me.

That Which is Human is more than just a great Sci-Fi book, it's a great book full stop!Although this story is set in the future and in outer space, it is not the main focus of the book. The reader could just as easily believe that the events are taking place on board an aircraft carrier serving in the Gulf today. The gritty and realistic terminology used by the author helps to pull the reader into the day to day life on Mac's ship. The battles and the communications during these scenes are particularly good. The reader has an almost voyeuristic view of the battles as they unfold. This type of detailed writing brings to mind the footage from Desert Storm. I could picture every maneuver, as if I were watching the grainy footage from the battle front itself. It is this realism that makes this tale such an enjoyable and exciting read. However, this book has far more to say about how a man deals with sacrifice, loss, duty and addiction than it does about blowing up aliens. I am sure there are many men, and women serving today, who struggle with the same issues as Mac.Bruce Davis has won himself a new fan with this book. If you're a Sci-Fi fan, or not, you need to read, That Which is Human.

I'm afraid I'm going to have to take this author off my automatic buy list. It's almost as if another, newer writer has taken over the pen name and the quality is just not there.There were so many things that didn't make sense that I found myself constantly being thrown out of the story.For example, we're told that when Rayne was 5 years old there had been a letter from the wife of the High Ruler of Katzmann. But in the first book of the series we're told that she was killed 30 years before the series was started. Ok, so Rayne should be at least 35 years old when the story starts, right? But he's referred to as an adolescent during the first real chapter -- so what's up with the timeline?Then we find Rayne (supposedly a bruter and confined to his family estate) going to a clinic run by Saris (from the second book of the series) so what, are they on Katzmann or Elquone? And what's Saris doing running a clinic on Elquone? Does that mean this story is set before the second book - but no, we find out it's after the third so what's Saris doing on Elquone?Suddenly it seems like Elquone and Katzmann are next door to each other - but that's completely inconsistent with the first and second books. And suddenly it's ok to sign a contract with a bruter - but that's also inconsistent... you get the picture.Then, Hassan couldn't be more of an ass to Rayne outside the bedroom - I mean that I got whiplash from the changes in his behavior.There are so many non-sequiturs in this book:o The pridehome is supposedly way out in the mddle of the desert, but Rayne can ride across a road and reach another pride within an hour... and there are roads in the sand? since when?o Bogden and his new bruter mate live in the same house as Hassan and Rayne, but somehow no one takes responsibility (financial or otherwise) for the household except Rayne. Where the heck do Anjali and his brother go during the day? Why aren't they also responsible for the pridehome?o There's a real attempt to make this a Bedouin type civilization, but the neighboring Shaikh is named Angus McGuffery -- I kid you not! And Rayne's name is Rayne McCarthy. So the scots settled both worlds? Really?Essentially, this book seems like a rush to capitalize on the quite interesting and successful Katzmann series -- unfortunately the author seems to have 'phoned it in.'After the equally unsatisfying Lady Blue Crew series, I'm no longer going to automatically buy this author's works -- I'd rather have fewer books from her than this mechanical and poorly constructed flotsam.

The word loss diet is the book I needed.  I am a writer, but I am not a great editor of my own work.  I have always found it hard to know exactly what to cut from my writing and what to leave.  I found that after I read through the Word-Loss Diet, it made a difference in how I look at my own writing.This is a short book, so Rayne Hall showed me how to do it best. By having a short book, I was able to "take away" some of the great ideas.  This is not meant for a beginner writer, because had I not been writing for a while, I wouldn't be able to understand some of the concepts.  Because I have been writing and reading for a while, this gave me a lot of points on which to build and improve my writing. They have many other books written about the writing craft, but this one I was able to put to use with my editing.I recommend this for writers who have written a few drafts, but are not getting to where they want to go.  This is straightforward and clear to me, and for that, Hall has done a good job.  I only wish it was bit longer.

Oh joy.I don't think this is supposed to be teen fiction, but it sure reads as if a teen wrote it.

reviewText: Bound By Her Ring by Nicole Flockton is my kind of book!Jasmine is recovering from amnesia when she's confronted by Luciano who claims to be her husband.  She doesn't remember Luciano but has memories of a "Lukas".  Jasmine feels like she's being slowly woken from her internal nightmares when she's with Lukas.  Memories start returning and nothing makes sense; she feels longing for Lukas but has a complete mind blank as to how and why.  Her memory is patchy but small things trigger recollections. Each flashback not only fanned the flames but keep the questions coming, some of which Lukas refuses to answer.  Jasmine is determined to find out her history and is frustrated when Lukas or her father won't assist in recovering her memories.Lukas is driven by revenge and deep hurt when he reappears in Jasmines life.  H blackmails Jasmine to accompany him on a business trip.  He wants to lash out at the world for past hurts which are fed to the reader drop by glorious drop but his overall qualities shine thru.  Things don't go to plan when Lukas quickly realises he physically feels the same way about Jasmine as he did prior to her accident which in turn makes him question how he feels inside.  The new Jasmine is an enigma to Lukas; things just don't add up.  After spending time together it's hard for Lukas  to remember his desire for revenge.  He clearly loves Jasmine and knows he's in trouble when reaches the conclusion he wants to protect Jasmine and not let her find out her past actions.I adored Bound By Her Ring because I love second chance stories.  I enjoyed the passionate and emotional ride I was taken on with Lukas and Jasmine.  Their love for each other shone thru.  The memory sequences are first-class. As each piece of the puzzle clicked into place I could understand Lukas's feelings and my heart just dropped when Jasmine recovered her full memory.  I want to start over and read the book again... not later, now!I impatiently wait for Nicole Flockton's 3rd book!

In a review of a companion story, I've described some of the main similarities between the Belgian detective Hercule Poirot and the French detective (and perhaps inspiration for the Poirot character) Jules Poiret. In this short story Poiret and his friend Harry Haven are faced with the unexpected murder of a personal friend and former love interest of Poiret's. This adds a more human emotional dimension to the character that is not very evident in the other two stories (available on Amazon) and is mostly lacking in Agatha Christie's stories too. It accounts for the additional star that I have given this story. Poiret's unusual emotional upset and the fact that few of the suspects seemed to have actually liked the victim probably explains why at the end he seems to take some delight in showing up the various failings and shortcomings of several of these suspects before proclaiming the innocence of most of them in the murder and fastening the guilt on the actual perpetrator.
summary: Very like Hercule Poirot but in this story at least a little more human

Looking for a sweet, romantic tale of soulmates bound through time with a love strong enough that after 100 years, one soul is still waiting for the return of his true love? Joseph still waits patiently for his Margaret to return to him someday. His ghost walks through time unseen and unheard because of a vow he made to his wife, who died in childbirth.In modern times, Maggie has had a gut-wrenching, emotionally debilitating marriage and divorce from a narcissistic man who saw her as unappealing, overweight and embarrassing to be around. Her ego is crushed and she needs a break, a short sight-seeing trip to an old mining town in Arizona. On a tour through an abandoned mine, she sees and talks to a man who no one else can see or hear. He claims she is his wife, Margaret, reincarnated and returned to him. Is she losing her mind or is she having flashbacks to a previous life with this kind and gorgeous man? How can a living being love a ghost? How can they be together?Yesterday’s Kiss by Carly Fall is pure romantic perfection with its gentle pace, emotional tension and a heart-melting ghost who is everything his Margaret/Maggie needs and dreams of in a man. Both characters have felt the pain of loss, but Joseph has the advantage of time eternal and his love and his memories. Maggie has been through the emotional wringer and finding Joseph still doesn’t always feel real, even though she is “seeing” things that she knows really happened. Her reactions were very realistic! Ms. Falls has created a beautiful tribute to true love that is meant to be. The world she has created almost fades to the background as my focus was on the interaction of Joseph and Maggie, their words, their shared life, even a trip to the home they once lived in. If you’re looking for a sigh-worthy romance that will glide through your heart and imagination, I recommend you read Yesterday’s Kiss and leave reality behind for a short while.I received a review copy from the author in exchange for my honest review.

reviewText: Rules of Survival is the story of Mikayla (aka, Kayla), on the run for the past year for the murder of her mother, that she didn't commit. Bounty hunters, some of which have been after her and her mom all her life, are after her now. When Kayla is cornered by Patrick and Shaun, two of the hunters, while trying to figure out how to clear her name, the game of survival just kicked into overdrive. Honestly, I have mixed feelings about this one. There were parts I really liked, parts that were exciting, parts that were mysterious, parts that were predictable, and parts that just didn't work for me. Here's a bit of what I liked and didn't like:What I Liked:• I would place this between Mature Young Adult and New Adult. I liked that this is a gentler transition between the genres. Kayla is 18 and Shaun is 20-something. But it's from Kayla's POV and reads as an 18-year-old. While there is sexuality, it is not the heavily-ladled borderline erotica many "new adult" books are putting out there.• The main characters had sympathetic pasts that had a decent complexity. I enjoyed getting to know them. Kayla is a tough girl, a survivor, who has lived a very unique life, and she never quits. I liked her, even though she was easily distracted by a cute boy. And Shaun's backstory, especially the bits with Patrick, was both heart-breaking and sweet. Once you get past the superficial, Shaun is very endearing.• There was a certain complexity that Accardo created that made the story interesting and not run-of-the-mill. There's mystery and suspense, trying to puzzle missing pieces together, trying to read through lies, deceptions, and misconceptions. While some of it was predictable, it was still interesting and thoughtful.• Though the mistakes here were big and far-reaching, it does showcase that even parents make mistakes, and how a child might cope with those mistakes, forgive, trust, and unconditionally love.• I liked the ending and the story itself felt complete. Not everything was all rainbows and flowers in the end, but what started as a very difficult reality for Kayla, ended with peace and hope, and I liked that.Not so much:• The first chapter sets the precedence for the tone of the book that didn't sit great with me, and affected the rest of the read. Kayla doesn't run away. Kayla kept trying to read the letter instead of stuffing it in her pocket for later when she was out of mortal danger. Kayla's eying Shaun like she's never seen a cute boy before. Kayla says there's no alternative exit when there's suddenly an exit. No one seems to have any weapons or protection. Of course, if she had the letter there would have been no story, but I was still bothered by the girl's poor choices. It set a precedence for future blunders.• Insta-whatever it was. I don't mind insta-attraction or even insta-love in general. I remember the first time I met my husband fondly. But for me the "insta" between Kayla and Shaun just didn't work for me considering the delicate situation they were in to begin with. In the first few chapters, reading about all the flirty looks and lusting and being so easily distracted just felt far-fetched and forced. They were in a life-threatening situation minutes into meeting each other. There should be no googly eyes! Their growing feelings felt more realistic, but the beginning kinda ruined the spark for me.• A couple predictable parts I figured out and was just waiting for Kayla to catch up. And there were a few things that were just off or plot holes, which I won't spoil. The book was still enjoyable, but these left it a little less satisfying.Overall, this standalone was a quick, enjoyable read for me, but nothing to jump up and down about. I love Accardo's Denazen series, and her writing here was still really good, I just didn't like it as much. But I am still a fan of Accardo and will continue to read her books. But don't let me discourage you. If you are looking for a suspenseful read, a bit of a whodunit with a sweet romance, and some action-filled moments, then Rules of Survival may just be for you.

Okay, I loved this novella. It is short but I don’t think the length is an issue. It’s perfect for the story.Todd is a guy in his early twenties that awakens inside a box. His sister, Kayla was kidnapped a few years ago and Todd fears the same has happened to him. His parents are rich but will they pay? Todd doesn’t think he was the favorite child like Kayla was.Matt Shaw did something quite unique with his storytelling. I’m quite used to seeing him use flashbacks in his novels but in Buried, the flashbacks are in the form of hallucinations. The air in the box is running out. Is Todd seeing his life flash before his eyes? Todd will think about an event in the past but at the same time, feel enclosed and hard to breathe. He envisions his family eating at the dinner table with him still being in the box. Todd thinks his sister, Kayla has the answers. She was kidnapped before. How did she survive? As he creates her as a character in his head, she helps him in trying to remember how he got into the box. Characters appear and disappear as he tries to put the pieces together.One would think this story would have such a simple plot: A man buried alive. It, however, is not the case. There are many twists and turns. By the end of the story, you’ll have all the answers but they are not at all what you may have expected in the beginning.It should be noted that this story also appears in Matt Shaw’s collection, “Tastes of Horror.” You can’t go wrong with either.
summary: Hidden treasure buried in Matt Shaw's collection

Books/novellas should be read in order:Book 1: BegBook 2: TeaseBook 3: SubmitBook 3.5: Jessica & SharonBook 4: ControlBook 5: BurnBook 5.5: RachelBook 6: ResistBook 7: SingIn Beg, book 1 waitress and aspiring singer Monica Faulkner meets hotelier Jonathan Drazen while accidently spilling a tray of drinks on him.  He fires her, but not before giving her a contact for another waitress job. Whereas Jonathan is open for no-strings-attached sex, Monica is looking to focus on her career.  So Jonathan turns to seduction...Tease, book 2 is the continuation of Jonathan and Monica's story.  They have hooked up for some off-the-charts sex and have come to an agreement that since neither is "available" they will just enjoy each other sexually whenever....Jonathan has however taken charge of Monica's orgasms and is playing her like a violin. Jonathan is set on keeping things very casual.  He admits to being in love with his ex-wife and Monica is dealing with her fears of their relationship taking over her life and pushing her singing career to the side. Outside of those, your body is my playground."Part 2 ends abruptly, but no worries just jump right over to part 3, Submit for the continuation of their story.  Spellbinding storytelling!  Compelling characters!  Scorching sex scenes!  I don't want it to end!"Our connection didn't have the bandwidth to sustain the pain buried far enough in our past to cause the grind of our present. His past belonged to her, even though she'd cut the line, taking it with her, tugging at him, leaving no one else for him to give it to."***Hero rating: 5+ starsHeroine rating: 5+ starsSex scenes rating: 5+ starsSex scenes frequency: 5 starsStoryline concept rating: 5+ starsStorytelling skills rating: 5+ starsStory ending rating: N/ABook editing rating (5 = no edits spotted): 5 stars************************************************Overall rating: 5 starsWould I recommend this series: Yes.Would I re-read this series: Yes.Would I read future books by this author: Yes.A gifted copy was provided by author/publisher for an honest review.

reviewText: Another great transition from one book to another for Terah Edun! Ciardis Weathervane had so much happen to her in Sworn to Transfer from betrayal to blossoming love that the third book had to jump right back into the action but also provide some sort of way to get Ciardis back into the action with all the characters that I loved from the first two books since she was so removed from them. Having her be in a coma solved a lot of that! Being a fantasy book has it's advantageous ;)Ciardis is thrown into wars and conflicts that seem so far over her head, until she shows you what kind of character she really is and that she has a back bone. I loved that we connected with her long lost family and that gave a sort of contrast to her life, from the beginning of the series where she is strong because of being alone and having to survive to the present were she not only is she falling in love but learning to have a family member to love. She maintained her innocent nature but also is turning into quite the young woman and I am happy to watch this progress unfold.The story is thickening nicely as well. There is so much going on in this world that it seems difficult that we are going to wrap so many story lines up, but I am very interested to see where we are going. As we got to know more about the conflicts within the kingdom, I thought this installment did a very good job of maintaining a clear picture about what these conflicts are and where they are as well. That can be difficult in a high fantasy novel, and can sometimes get muddled with so much information. Not so in Sworn to Conflict and I thought it paced itself nicely. Ciardis Weathervane is the kind of heroine that I can picture myself following into the biggest, scariest battle to end to the world.....and that might be where we are headed here!
