I've read a few expat biographies before, I have friends and relatives who have made the move to foreign climes but I can honestly say I have never read any of this type of book as good as this one before. I had seen this in the amazon recommendations and read a few reviews-some readers mentioned about there being a lot of errors in this book-well I wouldn't agree. Yes there are a few, eg. two missing commas in the acknowledgement page, but hey, the book is so good it really doesn't matter, it more than makes up for it. This isn't your average story of a family deciding to swop their normal lives for a place in the sun and having loads of money to get their luxury home; Jill's plans all turn sour when her husband is found to be having an affair with an ex-neighbour in England and he never makes the move to Italy, leaving Jill and her three children alone with no job. Jill is an amazing woman and she makes a go of things, a real strong character, she can turn her hand to anything. I really admire her, it's amazing to think what she has achieved and she is just about my age and from the town where I live. I would have liked some photos in the book but there is a link to her website and an excellent collection of photo albums on there. The pictures don't take ages to load and they are separated into albums relevant to each chapter. It's nice to see a Huddersfield Town shirt in one of them! There are so many adventures and problems which happen and it's amazing how Jill keeps her 'chin up' throughout each episode, always ending with a jokey punch line. Her ex-husband is mentioned quite a few times but she just tells it like it is, doesn't bad-mouth him and doesn't name him, very dignified about it all. I like the diary format, the book does have structure (one reviewer said it didn't) it is very well presented. Being a musician, I like how Jill often mentions exactly what track she was listening to on the radio or CD at the time as it helps conjure up the atmosphere, a nice touch. Great descriptive writing about the foods-so good you can almost taste them! Jill also includes recipes in the book which also really add to it. I could go on ages about the excellence of this book. Jill is just one year younger than me and yet she's dealt with so much. A memoir with balls! (Hope I can say that in a review!) Some of this reads like a novel, yet this really happened to Jill. I feel she would be successful writing a novel and I also hope she writes a sequel to A Single Parent Abroad-I've read somewhere that she is so I do hope this comes to fruition.
summary: What a woman!  What a book!

reviewText: The love story between Jaleesa and Niko was awesome.  The author describe there first meeting in such a way that a person could visualize it.  Even though the story was very descriptive, it was not drawn out.Each had there own problem to deal with but they did not let outside forces interfere with there relationship.Also interwoven into this story is a little mystery and attempted murder.I have read other books by this author.  This one did not disappoint.  Cannot wait for her next story to come out.

Back in 1979 young Perry Griffin was an only child. His father was gone and it was just his mother and himself; and The Man. From a young age, Perry had been unable to say his own name, running the two words together to form Per-grin, which eventually became Peregrine – forever more that was his name, with the only people calling him Perry being his teachers.On the day his mother tried to kill him, his life changed forever – badly wounded he escaped from her, running through the woods until he could go no further. But the vision he saw when he regained consciousness was...it had to be a dream, or most definitely a nightmare. For in front of him was his dead father, and all around him, watching cautiously, suspiciously, were other dead people – the thickness of the air was frightening. And young Peregrine discovered he had a new purpose in life…Book #4 in the Timmy Quinn series is a short story, a quick easy read and gives a little background on the ending of book #3, and I guess the lead-up to the final in the series, Nemesis, which is on my wish list to read soon. I have very much enjoyed this series, which I surprised myself about at the start, as I have always had an aversion to horror. So there you go! A series to recommend.

This book was tolerable enough to tempt me to read it. Nothing in this book, to me, was believable. A fairy tale, maybe, more like a dream...  I wouldn't discourage you from reading the book. I can say I have read much better...

This was a wonderfully written, masterfully told story about a boy, a grifter, who doesn't want to run a grift anymore after losing his father during a con. The young man makes a new life, in a strange and wonderful place. But the man is scared and seems ready to rabbit at any moment. Will he run or will love keep him happily ever after?
summary: Beautiful story by the Queen of Angst

reviewerName: So many books, so little time
reviewText: The final book in the series.After Carrie sneaks into Howard's office and finds the information she needs, she accepts an invitation to meet Howard for a “job interview”.  She purposely gets there early to do some more snooping.  What she gets is drugged and kidnapped.She wakes up tied to a bed and naked.  She knows she’s in the Club Prive’ members room and knows the voice of the person who has her.  She can’t scream or move.  She’s fighting the impulse to vomit because her assailant is cutting her clothes off with a knife and telling her all the depraved things he is going to do to her.  Telling her how he’s going to make her succumb to the things he trains the other girls to take.  The ones he sells to the highest bidder and all the activities they do with their pets.There are too many spoilers for me to go any further but here’s my advice.  Get these books, all of them.  Follow the plots and enjoy the hot sex.I loved this book the best.  Not because it was the end but because the whole trip was worth it.  All of the books were good.  This one brought them home.If you like hot, steamy sex, a plot that will keep you guessing and on the edge of your seat, you need to read this series. I never saw the ending coming.I gave this book 5 stars.
summary: I hated to see this end!!!

reviewText: This is a quick, fun read about life in the Yukon.  The main characters are a woman owner of a dance hall and a male member of the Northwest Mounted Police.  The dance hall owner's father was killed in an avalanche and the Mountie is hunting for clues in the death of his sister.  This historical romance all comes together in the solving of the mysteries.  I would suggest that anyone who enjoys a mystery or historical romance, or both should spend the time to read this story.

Andrew has done it again! I always know I'm going to get the best book there is to get when Andrew releases a new one. I absolutely love this one. I just wanted to hold Cody and never let him go! Thank you Andrew!

I enjoyed reading this book very much! It is a granddaughter's true story of her grandfather's land and how the very first T-Rex in the United States was discovered there!  Set in Montanta, the author does an excellent job explaining the entire process from how it was discovered to how the bones were moved and assembled at the museum.  I would highly recommend this book to history buffs and especially those with an interest in dinos!  Well done! Thanks for sharing this part of your family history and also how the first T-Rex was discovered!

Masked Encounters is an exciting and sexy short story by Felicia Tatum! She had impressed me before with her first book, The White Aura and now with her newest offering; I couldn't help but agree with the other readers/reviewers. This novella is intriguing, captivating and really intimate. I can't wait to read the next book in the series!Korah's character is as mysterious as Dane's. In this book, we get to meet Korah who had built an entire wall around herself because she got hurt from a previous relationship. Despite this wall, her best-friend Leela still set her up with blind dates, which turned disastrous in the end. And one night, during a masked Halloween party, Korah let out her inhibitions, wore a sexy angelic dress and captured the eye of Dane. Unbeknownst to her, Dane had seen her before and had unnerved him with her uneasiness and aloofness to the guys. And when the barefoot Korah was tended by a gorgeous masked man, she retaliated and ended up doing the unthinkable. Whatever it was, I'm not telling...This book is really engaging. No boring scenes, no dull dialogues, just pure blissful reading! Thanks so much, Felicia for trusting me with your book. Gonna read the next one now!
summary: a barefoot angel kissed a masked stranger.. what happens next?

reviewText: A well written romance.  A few twists and turn to make it interesting.it keeps you glued with the suspense.  I enjoyed it very much.

First off I'll say that Ms. Geary gave me a free copy of this "novel nibble" after I reviewed Matchmakers 2.0. I'll try to be as objective as possible, but wanted to be upfront about that.Like Matchmakers, this is a fun, short read that is great for airplane rides, waiting in line, or just an afternoon of light reading. The story is fast-paced and interesting. I don't normally read paranormal fiction, but the witches are fun and interesting, and the author's inclusion of a group of people looking out for the social welfare of teen witches was amusing and clever. The characters were decent, considering the length of the story, although I thought Romy was a little trite as a character. She came off a bit like a stereotyped "tough girl" to me.There were no formatting errors or kindle problems that I noticed. Definitely enjoyed the story, and will read more of this author's work when I'm looking for light fiction!

This was a nice, quick read. There was a lot of action, some steamy seduction and lots of sparks between the main characters, Riley and Jenna. They meet because of an investigation of Riley's. One thing leads to another and they are spending time together and feelings things that neither of them think they should. Riley's investigation leads him down a path that he had hoped he would and wouldn't have to travel, especially since he can't get Jenna out of his head. However, the same goes for Jenna, she can't stop thinking about Riley and wondering when she'll see him again. Things definitely heat up between Riley and Jenna, and then everything seems to happen at once. Now the question is will Riley and Jenna make it past what was between the sheets? Or is it all too late? Genie did a great job with this, I didn't put it down once I started. Loved Riley and Jenna together, they were passionate and sweet, good for each other I think.I received a copy of this book in return for an honest review.
summary: Between the Sheets has it all - action, romance and sizzling chemistry.

reviewText: Just wow! I don't even know where to begin! Convicted was probably my fav book from the consequences series, so when this novella turned into a full length novel from several males POV's I couldn't have been more thrilled! Yes it was hard to relive some moments as it has been in all the companion novellas. But I do love getting inside Tonys head and this book dove so deep and seeing the whole breakdown, jail, fire...etc in such detail was amazing! This book was the absolute perfect ending to the the series and the epilogue was beyond amazing! I'm going to miss Tony and Claire!!!! Well done, Aleatha! You truly are a mastermind!

Hot, cowboy and firefighter what more could you ask for! The sub story line brings little to the actual main plot but does bring to a conclusion a small subplot through all of the bad in boots stories. Great read.

I fell in love with L. Chapman's writing in 'Trust' book 1 of the Believe Series, and I have to say that this follow up blew me away.You think you know how this story is going to play out but as you read it, L. Chapman slaps you in the face and says 'think again sweetheart'.Never did I expect Jenny's story to unravel the way it did.Of course, we met Jenny in book 1 and I liked her character than, but when we get to see some much more of her in Veiled, I now realise I love her to bits. With her wedding day only a month away, we experience so many things with Jenny and of course her best friend Megan. Her hen's night which was excellent, the distance Rich is creating between them and his reason and resulting consequences for the distance, the meeting of a new delicious man and unexpected surprises as well.The friendship between Jenny and Megan is one that I think a lot of woman would envy, they are each others constant and they support each other no matter what. Megan's boyfriend Mark also appears in the storyagain and every reason I fell for him in book 1 is still apparent in this book.The twist for Rich was something I was completely shocked with and his actions towards Jenny broke my heart, I don't think I have ever read a character that changes so completely.But enter Warren James in all his beautiful glory and Jenny's story gets VERY interesting. He handles everything thrown at him with such understanding and support for Jenny that you can help but swoon and wish he was yours.I will openly admit that at the end of the book I contacted L. Chapman because I thought my kindle was playing up and I didn't get all of the story....There is no way the story could possibly end like that....When she got back to me it took everything in me not to throw myself on the floor kicking and screaming 'Noooooooooooo'. You are killing me L. Chapman by leaving it like that and making me wait for more :)Seriously though, L. Chapman truly made this story hard to put down and it ended wayyyyy to quickly from my liking. I love these characters and I will wait VERY IMPATIENTLY for book 3 to be released,because I HAVE to see where their lives are heading and find out all the unanswered questions this book left in it's wake.Veiled has cemented the fact that I will without a doubt read absolutely anything that this author writes. It was a brilliant, exciting, surprising and an all round wonderful read.I absolutely recommend that you read The Believe Series by L. Chapman, you wont be disappointed :)

Tiffany is a smart women at a point in her life for a change. she is king to be a P. I. with the help of some new friends. I really enjoyed this and looking forward to the next installment of Tiffany Black in Vegas.
summary: Cute mystery set in Vegas. What more would you want.

reviewText: I was immediately drawn to Rick and Maddy's story in Do Over and was very excited to continue it in It's Not Over.  Not going to lie - was not on Team Rick, but was so happy to see how Maddy infiltrated herself into his psychie.  Now, Ms. Maddy has a suitcase full of issues of her own, but in that aspect, I think she and Rick are perfect for each other.  I will be anxiously waiting to see how Maddy's little bomb is going to play out in the next book.
Quick fun easy read....waiting for a couple more from thus series. I enjoy the characters,  i read about a book a day an need more material, o keep them coming

(Spoiler Alert)Mona Risk writes a very moving story in Christmas Wedding Muddle.  While our heroine, Julia, deals with a cheating fiance' dashing her "perfect" happily ever after, she actually discovers Tony, who turns out to be her friend, confidante, and finally true love when she invites him to take the cruise with her that was booked for her honeymoon.I was so caught up in the story that I read it in one night; it seemed so real with great highlights of Spain, Rome, etc.  I'm now an avid fan of Mona and hope she keeps writing more beautiful stories like this one. Kudos to you Mona for my wonderful experience of a cruise I was never on, but certainly wish I was.
Buckle in and forget about putting any one of the books in this series down.  Just hunker down and read!

Earphones need to be comfortable for me.  The comfort is secondary to the sound.  I plug these into the Kindle Fire.  And my preference is not for the movies, but for the music that is downloaded to the Fire.  The earbuds are not exactly a tight fit, but at least they don't hurt.  You need to learn how to fit them in the ear, and how to keep them in place at all times.  This set comes with three sets of ear tips.  Plus, a neat feature is the clip!!  I tend to plug in the Ipods and walk outside, and chores around the house.  It is critical that the cord remain out of harm's way.I have several earphones, over the ears, and these are handy.  At nighttime, I prefer these over the other kind, as I generally have wires, earphones,  portable DVD players, Kindles, Ipods, and whatever at the bed stand.  So, the tiny earbuds are just perfect to keep in place with all the gadgets.I have used these with the Ipods also, and I love the sound.  Even though the design is with a flat wire, I don't quite notice the importance or difference.  But I assume the idea was to have less tangling.The small case is not efficient for me.  I would rather just wrap the cord around the Ipod, or the Kindle Fire.  It is not important to keep them in a case.Again... my preference for the buds is to listen to music....and these sound great!ONE NOTE:  DO NOT GIVE THESE A WASHING MACHINE WASH!  Rizzo
I just wanted to acknowledge a good book and had to have at least 20 words!!  I will definitely be looking for more from this author.  Funny!  Funny!  Funny!

I received a complimentary copy of this book for review purposes.Better Left Buried is a well written, engaging story with well developed characters.  When I read the synopsis, I thought I was getting a paranormal story.  Although there are paranormal overtones, the story itself is more about friendship, loss and, well...life.  For those who cannot deal with stories about abuse, you may want to avoid this one.I liked this book and found myself looking for moments when I could sneak in a little reading.  This is my first experience with this author and I am most assuredly going to be seeking out more of her books.  Happy reading!

Although this hot little story definitely fits it's title, it still was enjoyable for a day when I really needed something to get me through a rough morning.A sexy tale about 2 high school seniors who cut class to go off and have a "quickie", what it lacked in length, it fully compensated for in content.Pick it up while it's free, there's nothing to lose, and only pleasure to be gained.After all, most times, it's not the size, but the content that really matters. ;-)

I have read very little about slavery.  This book was very enlightening to me.  One thing I read about was the children of slaves being sold to other owners was a shock.  That never occured to me. I guess I assumed they all stayed together as a family.  I have little doubt that most of what she writes about did actually happen.  I do think there may be a bit of embellishment to the story.  Regardless, if even three quarters of what she wrote about is true it is a travesty that people were treated so badly.  No one in this day and age could comprehend what it must have been like to live that way. I enjoyed the book but at the same time my heart went out to all the people she mentioned as being held and abused.

Cleo's job was to protect the man in the seat in front of him.  Simple enough.  All he had to do was foil the attempt of the CIA to blow up the plane.  Which turns out to be anything but simple.  Aliens, CIA cleaners and assassins, and one of the most famous actresses in the nation seem to be conspiring to make his covert operation as complicated as possible.Government conspiracy at its best, Joe Crubaugh creates an all too possible world in Terminal Departure.  A world where some of the most powerful governments on the planet are controlled by a secret international association made up of the world's elite.  On top of that, alien watchers really do abduct people and the deaths of a couple of hundred innocent people are justified by the need to control the populace.  With keep you on the edge of your seat action, this book will have even the most unbelieving readers turning the pages to see what happens next.Written with the spirit of Christopher Buckley over his shoulder, Joe Crubaugh knows how to spin a tale of political satire.  The main characters are quirky but entertaining.  The secondary characters are sometimes frightening but definitely interesting.  All in all, this was a great read.  I thank the author for providing me with a review copy and I give the book five stars.

Cue Me In was a quick, fun read. Fae and her sister Izzy, along with Rod and Flash, make great characters in the story. With the backdrop of a ghost, a castle,a huge dog and a mysterious howling wolf it's an easy story to love. But the best part is how two of the characters fit into an ancient ghost story. This is my first book by this author, but it won't be my last.
I have several of Leslie Langtry's books and this was another great read.  I got the book quickly so I had it for my enjoyment during a boring winter.  I've recommended this series to several people.

I love this cover for the Kindle Fire. I like the fact you can zip it shut. It also is padded to help protect the Kindle. You can also bend the cover back and there is a pouch where you put your hand to hold the Kindle. I recommend this to anyone that is looking for good protection for your Fire.
summary: Great cover for the Kindle Fire

reviewText: We start this book straight from where the last left off.... and Hindley can tend to let Rory get away with things a bit easily. I would let him stew a bit more, sexy good looking or not...he needs to crawl!!Omg Kay Manis! The secret trip for Rory after the massive fight! ? Holy sh%t...... That was quite the show! But Rory what a c&ck;! Men and their freaking double standards.......At least Rory put him in his place....but I wouldn't have let him know.. Not let him off that easily! No freaking sirreeeeeee!But wait.....that wasn't the secret......oh...the doo doo is going to hit the fan...Kay...you tease me!!The twists and backstory certainly come out in this one.....and both have some seriously tough pasts! Seriously and just when you think you know it all Bam! you get book slapped again...Hindley's work life is not going smoothly, everyone seems to be in on the fact that she and Rory are an item and are using it to their advantage.....Twists and turns at every page, I did miss Dana in this book, she wasn't around as much and although she did come into it towards the end, I would have loved her witty advice when Rory was being a Boy Naughty!!I love Kay's writing, it flows, it doesn't stick on parts and dwell....i had a few tears threaten towards the last quarter as the final bit of drama was unleashed. This book was gifted to me from the author and I am very pleased. There are six short stories in this book and each one deals with the world ending in a different way and how it effects people. It is a very good book and very easy to get into as each story is only a few pages long. Perfect for that read on lunch or before bed unless you're like me and have to read it from front to back, the stories are that good , well worth the $2.99

I am not a big romance reader, I usually find the language clunky and the plot secondary to the sexy stuff. However, this book breaks that convention. The female lead is not your typical head in the sky type, she has an important job that leaves her in unpredictable circumstances. The love scenes are done well, not too heavy handed, but still steamy enough. The book is also rather suspenseful, so it ends up being a story with all the right elements.

This book is great! I didn't know too much about Ketogenic diets when I first read this book and it has helped to give me a good understanding of what this diet is about! It has all the information needed to go on this type of diet and I was surprised at the many health benefits this diet presents. My partner is borderline diabetic and I think this book will be great for him to get himself back on track!
Loved it!  Finally we hear his side if the story and his struggles for Lacey. I hope there's more in the kin series

The Hot Ice series is blazing! I love Lily Harlem's characters and world building. Her heroes in this series are all tasty alphas without being alphaholes. Their jobs are part of who they are, not just the fantasy of a sports player. I really like that. The author is either a fan or really sank her teeth into the research, or both. Her heroines are smart, strong modern women I'd choose to be friends with. I hope to see a lot more from Ms. Harlem.

This is the second part of Mid Life Love, where we see Jonathan and Claire preparing for their wedding. There are some flash backs for both Jonathan and Claire that provide us with some insights about each of them by looking at some of the things Jonathan went thru as a child and some of Claire's experiences after her first husband betrayed her. Her ex husband comes back on the scene, his wife Amanda, Claire's former best friend who he had an affair with while married to Claire is very sick and wants Claire's forgiveness. I think this book was entertaining but I still wasn't a big Claire fan at the end of it. To me, Claire's extreme rage over her husband's infidelity 6 years later was puzzling since she was now supposedly head over heels in love with J, as I said in my review of the 1st book, she needed to be in therapy to help her move on. Her daughters came across as spoiled brats, not sure why either J or C tolerated their self centered, ungrateful behavior. J's possessiveness of C was sometimes a little scary as well. I found myself skipping ahead because I just wanted to see what kind of wedding they would have, and the extravagance of the wedding and the difficulty C had about making up her mind about what she wanted for the 'perfect' wedding seemed out of character for a woman who in the 1st book didn't want J to think she was after him for his money and who wanted to sign a pre-nip in book 2. So, again the book was entertaining, had  a great premise but didn't quite live up to its potential.
summary: Didn't Quite Live Up to Its Potential

reviewText: I like this author's novels, because they're short and to the point. Also they're easier/quicker to read versus other "seasoned" authors. What I loved about this book is that it featured some characters from "always and forever" and it had an actual ending without needing a sequel.
This was perfect reading for a long night at work. I love the side stories she writes to go along with Outlander.

He finds that living at home in the end always is the best.  His desire for a wife falls through.  The ending is not what you expected.

I wasn't sure what to expect from this book. The blurb had me interested but I was still a bit uncertain. There were slow spots in the book but it was still very well written and as such I can only give it 4 stars, I would give it more if it didn't have the slow spots. Once you pass the slow spots and get into the nitty gritty of the book, it becomes a great contemporary romance story.Grayson and Mia are both 'broken' and seeking to find their way in their new relationship when tragedy strikes just as things are already rocky, however out of the bad comes the good and they save things between themselves. While it's not a picture perfect relationship, it does mirror in some aspects what happens to all of us with our ups and downs.In the end though, I did like this book, and I'm glad I received a copy for an honest review.

Cassianna Baxter steps into The Lewiston Academy For Girls for the first time in twelve years.  This time, instead of walking the halls as a student, she is now the Deputy Head Mistress at the academy.  As she looks out at the stables, a place that she has spent countless hours, memories flood her thoughts.  The memories aren't only of her days riding, but of Lawrence Taylor ... her riding coach, first love and the man who broke her heart.  Those days were well in the past though.  Cassianna hasn't seen Lawrence since she fled the academy and was positive that he had left the school years ago.  To her surprise, she bumps into him while giving a tour of the school.  He not only still works at the academy, he is the Chairman of the Board of Trustees there.  Seeing Lawrence again brings back all of the memories they shared.  Memories of their passion and her strong attraction to him.  But Cassianna is hesitant to walk down that road again with him.  He walked away from her before without even an explanation.  Her fear was that he would do it again.  But her feelings and the strong sexual attraction that they share is too much for Cassianna to deny.  Reluctantly, she decides to go with her heart.  She just hopes that he doesn't break it again.I really enjoyed reading Academy of Love.  The chemistry that the characters had was undeniable, their passion was hot and the scenes were steamy.  I thought that the story was well written and couldn't wait to find out what was going to happen next.  If you're looking for a hot story with even hotter characters, then this book is for you.  I would definitely recommend this book to others and look forward to seeing what the author has in store for us next.
All I can say is yum! Its a great hot steamy book! I couldn't put it down. This is a must read!

This book takes place in the near-future. The government has been seized by the Unionists, any propaganda that the US is still a free country has long since passed, and the hunt is on for any insurgent who committed a perceived crime against the homeland. Warren Linder, a former CIA agent now working with the newly formed DSS, hunts these exiles, whether they are in the US or abroad.A mission goes wrong in Beirut, and Linder is falsely accused of collaborating with the enemy. Arrested, interrogated and tortured, he is finally sent to a Corrective Labor Camp in the Yukon’s far north. Fighting for survival and searching for meaning and redemption, Linder takes the reader on a wild ride that ranges from Beirut to the Yukon to Utah and beyond. Readers who enjoy the works of Al Franken and Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn will love this intelligent book. The plausible plot, realistic dialogue and unrelenting pace make this novel hard to put down and will leave you wanting more.To be honest, I'm not sure why Preston Fleming’s books haven't yet made it onto the NY Times Bestseller List – this is an author to watch! I am happy to recommend this book with a full five-star rating.
summary: Well Written, Great Plot, Engaging Characters - Read This One!

Little does she know that those secrets could cost her life if she doesn't uncover them in time.Victoria must learn to embrace that she is a witch and develop her powers before the ghouls club can sacrifice her during the Blue Moon Ball, an event that only occurs once every 60 years.

(not upstairs)" ...and the setting sun that hovered low in the distance found its way over the highest row of seats in the grand stand, ..." reviewText: This is not the first time I’ve read something by this awesome lady and I certainly wasn’t disappointed with Logan and Claire’s sweet story of a second chance romance. Once engaged, it’s been two years since they last saw each other when a winter storm intervenes. After cancelled flights, they run into each other in the crowded airport and Logan offers up his place to stay and wait out the storm…for four days. Sounds like plenty of time for these two to kiss and make up, right? And boy do they! I loved Logan. He was swoony. He was masculine. He was sweet. He was the sexiest dad I’ve read in a while. All in all, a 10 in my book. I thought Brighton handled their tense reunion and gradual fall back into comfort and then into love with a very genuine and natural hand. Logan’s daughter, Sophie, was completely adorable and the moments between the two were enough to make my ovaries explode. The author mentioned in her acknowledgments that there is nothing more sexy than a good dad. This story definitely made me a believer.Four stars. While the love story and everything about their time in isolation had me rolling in feels and swoons, I had a few issues with the ending. I think that due to the shorter format, I didn’t get enough backstory on the problems that led to the end of their engagement and were the main conflict of the story. Without that, I ended up feeling frustrated with Claire for acting selfish and immature instead of frustrated with Logan, as the story intends. I still loved the story but the ending made me like Claire a little less than I did at the onset.

Disclaimer: I know the author, but I am not receiving anything in exchange for this honest reviewThis novel made me wish I could live in Toronto, dance, produce music, play guitar and bake mouth-watering pastries in under an hour while surrounded by the coolest multi-ethnic cast I have ever read about. In other words, Lucia Mpobo-Riddell is my newest hero.When we meet Lucia- Luce/Lucita/Lulu- she's just embarked on what's going to be a stormy relationship with London-based producer Marcus Grant. Taken together, they're an interesting study in human potential: Lucia lost both of her parents when she was very young, but she's taken her grief and channeled it into all of her creative outlets. Marcus, born with an equal amount of talent but blessed with loving parents, has achieved respect in his chosen profession but is still thisclose to being great. The reader quickly understands that it's Marcus who can't get out of his own way, but like Lucia- and his family and friends- we're rooting for him to do the right thing.Like Lucia's sisters, I alternated between wanting to punch Marcus, wanting him to make Lucia happy, and wanting him to walk away because he just wasn't good enough and he'd had his chance. Just when those feelings peaked, in walked the equally compelling (and more accomplished) Greg McMullen. He's "all that", and he treats Lucia like gold. But even though I'm squarely on Team Greg, I can understand why Lucia still isn't entirely done with Marcus. (But here's hoping she comes to her senses in the sequel!)As much as I enjoyed Lucia, Marcus and Greg, I also appreciated the large supporting cast, particularly the close knit family members that are like best friends and the best friends who are so close that they're like family. But not everyone is milk and honey: the sins of Lucia's mother and grandmother loom large over the lives of their family members, and it's heartbreaking how much Lucia and especially her sister Noor still pine for their parents' love. While the tone of the novel is mostly adventurous and fun, these reminders ground the piece.Plenty of humor here, but the funniest line is "I'm taller, my eyes are green and I too speak fluent Korean." So take that!Highly recommended.

Reading the little of him we did in the first two books in the series (Claimed (Brides of the Kindred)andHunted (Brides of the Kindred)), who really knew where his character could have gone. But we saw the progression of him and his character inSought (The Brides of the Kindred), which was a necessary parlay into this book. I will say that Xarin never really gave himself enough credit, for even though he was raised by his father, he was still half of his mother. Even though he wasn't around, I guess it would have been nice if someone brought that up.*SPOILER* It was also interesting to see a virgin be a male for a change. But of course Xarin ends up knowing what to do, lol. *END SPOILER*Overall I really liked this book. I liked how the two protagonists were both minorities (Xarin being Scrouge, though having grey skin, and Lauren being biracial -- African American and White), though it wasn't a big deal. I love when that happens in books! Especially since I sometimes forget that these books take place in the future, let's hope that race isn't an issue -- that would be fabolous! But I appreciated reading something other than the standard fair skin, blue eyes etc, and Evangeline Anderson was able to include that I genuinely appreciate that, for not many authors choose to be diverse with their characters especially when they are writing a series, and it can get old.One of my favorite books in the entire series. My Take:The book opens introducing Thom and Dru in a cute scene about muffin making. You are quickly introduced to Thom's insecurities regarding the age difference between him and Dru. You are also quickly introduced to Kara, their neighbor and good friend.Skye is introduced by page six, and is debuted by page eighteen, so all the characters are ready to come out and play rather quickly. I do enjoy that. However, the reason Skye is coming to join this happy couple is not happy at all. He and Dru had been best friends (and Dru had a secret crush on him) when they were younger. That all changed when Skye's parents died when he was 17 and he was forced to live with a relative who held him captive and did awful things to him.To Dru, it was like his best friend abandoned him. To Skye, he was living a nightmare. When he escaped, he was sent to a home to deal with his issues (and he has a lot). Skye has no other family, and when he's set to be released, the only person he has to call is Dru.And therein lays the problem. Dru and Thom are committed to each other and then Skye, Dru's past crush, joins the party with a slew of emotional issues.The idea for this story is BRILLIANT! Brilliant, I say. There were a lot of curves and twists the author could have taken and played with. There were a lot of different ways she could have taken us from beginning to end. Lots of different layers to play with. I was excited to read it.But that's where my excitement ends.Instead of this story being character driven, it's plot driven, which in turn, makes a lot of the characters actions/emotions/etc seemed forced and faked. This is sad because this plot has the means to make a MEAN character driven story.Telling. Telling. Telling. This author told us everything instead of showing us. I mean everything. Since there is so much telling going on, the story is wordy. Unnecessarily so. This book could be tightened up substantially. I found myself skipping large sections so I didn't have to read about the play-by-play of dinner cooking.  And at the same time you are missing the opportunity to give the reader a true glimpse of the characters and their surroundings.And this author did something I have never seen done before. She actually referred to the characters as "the blond one", "the man", "the woman" "the younger man", "the dark brown haired one". It was off putting. Why not just say the character's name? I realize that sometimes it's difficult to deal with a lot of people in one scene, but really? Those things are so generic. The generic descriptions continue throughout the rest of the story, with the author describing the the home as nothing more than a "large, modern house".The characters themselves are also very bland and two dimensional. The only exception is Skye, who you get to "see" a little more of because of his emotional problems. But not NEAR enough. Dru is an emotional crybaby (which I was not expecting) and Thom sounds like a forty year old man most of the time taking care of his young children. Kara, while funny, it obviously just a character thrown in the mix in order to shake up the relationship aspect of the story. Skye was really the only one I cared about and even then, I didn't get enough of what I needed from him. Character development was not near what it could have been for a story of this length and depth.And on a final note, these are the most smiling characters I have ever seen. I swear, one of them is smiling ever other sentence.  And most of the book is not very smiley worthy. Note to the author: get a thesaurus and learn how to convey that your character is smiling with different words ... or by SHOWING us they are happy about something. No more telling!I was just expecting a great deal more from this plot and I was disappointed all the way around.My Rating:* * Two Mews~LD(as a reviewer, I was given a copy of this book free of charge)

He is very specific which I appreciate because I don't really like reading books that stray too far from the point giving you a hard time to follow the content.Grant has a 'let me put it to you straight' approach which a lot of women who need his advise will benefit a great deal from. He's practical, no pie in the sky suggestions that only look good on paper. Its good that the advise given is coming from a male perspective so you know that this is exactly what men want. Clearly you can see from the direction the book takes that men are not nearly as complex as women. There aren't too many spider webs that could snag you along the way.I used to think that I had all the answers when it came to my husband. But the truth is, I didn't and sadly I had to wait until now to realize how wrong I was. I kept thinking that my humor was enough to keep him coming back for more. Then I started making more and more of an effort to step into his shoes and figure out what really got him peaked.The importance of your attitude is emphasized and there is a lot of focus on "being happy.". We tend to forget how to be happy at times, forgetting that happiness is a state of mind. This is a very short but enlightening book.

This "mystery" was a treatise on feminism, even distinguishing between plain feminism and Marxist feminism. The indentation of the "textbook" quotes made the novel seem terribly, terribly long. I frankly didn't mind the refresher course, but I did mind the long, tortuous path to the solution of who was killing the "swans." Everybody became a suspect, including the woman with whom Inspector David McClennan was falling in love. Back and forth, back and forth the investigative team would go, and meanwhile we would see the several students asking themselves questions about one another. There was suspense as the bodies piled up and fears became monumental. The author employed rumor, secret-sharing,and lack of communication as plot-twisting tools. Ms Greaves is a very clever writer, and a clear writer. She also was careful to describe the layout of the campus, the location of rooms, the use of doors, but she doesn't provide much in the way of English atmosphere; to the contrary,the ordinariness of the town was almost depressing. Too depressing to go on for 36 chapters. John Waddington-Feather, for example, also writing about the North and about contemporary problems, stops to smell the roses.The Graveyard Mystery (Blake Hartley Detective Novels)
Like the final book in this series. Author closed with leaving the reader wanting to know how the future will be for Esposito family

I am ashamed to say this is one of the few books I couldn't seem to get engross into the story, and it's usually not that hard within the first chapter. I actually quit within the first 20 pages, I find something lacking in the writing or there wasn't that "OMG  MUST CONTINUE" drive within the story.
I really liked the trilogy, but the end left me wanting somewhat.  I guess that was the point so you'll read the next series!

I don't care who you are, if you are in a relationship there will be issues and especially conflicts. There is no way around this. So the only solution is to be better prepared to deal with them if you want to have a happy and healthy relationship. So this is what made me give this book a try and what probably isn't mentioned in the initial book post is that you don't need to be married for this book to save your relationship, because I am not in a marriage but in a LTR and the tips work great for me. The book covers all the bases in terms of conflict resolution from the causes, to the approaches to resolve them so both sides are happy and how to prevent them in the first place. If you want a happy Relationship/Marriage this is a mandatory buy.

I have loved every moment of this series and this was such a great way to end it! I love this group of characters so much and it is sad to see it end, but man, what a way to go out! Logan and Triss just keep getting stronger. And the ending, oh my goodness YES! Perfect.

I have had a Rebel XT (Canon) in my closet for the last 3 years and with summer coming really have wanted to start using it again. The hard part with using it though is i can read as much as i want on the internet but when i am out actually wanting to take a shot i don't have a manual with me to help me along.I take my kindle with me everywhere now and having this book with me as im out and about has been great. Although i am still an absolute novice i was able to work my way around the camera (after a few reads) fairly stress free.I would recommend this book to any beginner - its easy to follow and definitely made me more confident
summary: Got me using my Rebel XT again!

reviewText: The author is Philip van Wulven, not Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, although he uses the same style as Doyle. Dr. Watson is again the story teller and recalls the events of the mystery just as in the original works. Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson are invited by the mayor of the city, Mayor Pink (hense the name in the title), to stay after a formal royal event to help him in a personal matter. It turns out that the Mayor has had a very valuable jem stolen and needs Holmes to find it before an upcoming event the next week. Holmes sifts through the facts and discovers things are not what they seem to be when first presented. If you are interested in a short mystery story, this is entertaining but not particularly complex. If however, you are expecting something of the magnitude of quality of the original doyle mystery classics, you will be somewhat disappointed. It is a good mystery, not a GREAT one.
summary: Sherlock Holmes Investigates: The Pink Jewel Conundrum

reviewText: This amazing story continued where Fierce and Fury left off. Delving deeper into the lives of Hunter and Autumn (Leafy).It was a hot, sexy, emotional read. I laughed and cried, while reading Flame.I had goosebumps through most of the book, I'm so glad I got to be part of this wonderful journey.** I received a copy of this book in exchange for an honest review **All thoughts and opinions expressed are solely mine, and mine alone.If you haven't read Clarissa Wild's writing before, (why not?!) I suggest starting with Fierce or Fight.I highly recommend Flame, and I so enjoyed getting to know Ms. Wild's fabulous characters.I look forward to more from this exceptional author!
I actually really enjoyed this book, I enjoyed the characters...I don't know why but I think Silas is my favorite. Good job!

3.5 stars actually. Unfortunately, if you're not from New England I'm afraid some of the location details will be a little confusing because the story relied heavily on the Berkshires and then Boston. This is a political story revolving around Peter & Madeline who are not only political opponents in the governor's race but former lovers. What was never quite explained is why they broke up 6 years ago.
It starts off good and gets better..It's witty, funny, and I read it in one sitting. It goes pretty fast but I'm sure you'll like it because at one point in marriage, everyone has felt this way.

I enjoyed the story. Just hate soon as you get to learn the storyline- has to stop at the good part I am just not a fan of short reads. This book would of passed me by if it was not for my book club. I will read Part 2 this book kept me turning pages.

I think what grabbed me most about this story was just the pure human aspect to it, that maybe on some level we can all relate to. Ms. Wynne has created a living, breathing character in Henry. He's shy, a bit of a loner, and we get get this glimpse of a man, who, like so many of us, is just going through the motions in life. Henry works as a security guard at a museum when the painting first arrives. In it, is a woman who captures his imagination. As Henry grows more obsessed with the woman in the painting, it is both sad and beautiful at the same time. The magic that comes next is unexpected, but it is what makes this story truly special...and I won't spoil it ;) I know it's technically a holiday story, but If you're looking for a quick read--ANY time of year, I would definitely recommend this!
summary: A Story to Warm your Heart During the Coldest of Months

reviewText: This book was a very good read about a boy whom is in jail for a crime that he did not commit and makes a friend through the pin pal program who helps him through his journey.

I suspect the author to be an executive at the NRA because of the way the right to have a gun was advertised in this book. But the context could explain it so I give him the benefice of doubt.What was a second book! I have been checking the Kindle Store for its release every week since I read the first book. And I could hardly stop reading it over the last few days.The story covers space battles, social dynamics, genetics, inter races psychology, century long unfolding story.What a pity that the third book is only planned for the end of 2013!
Nia Forrester has done it again. This is the third book with these characters and it was a great read.
I would recommend it.  I liked the characters and how their story developed.  It was an enjoyable read.  I would recommend to my friends.

I enjoyed this book!  Anne is such a strong woman who is struggling financially.  She has overcome so much from her childhood and life just keeps throwing her curveballs.  Mal is probably the biggest curveball she will ever get but she finds that she doesn't mind.  Mal is funny and cute but he is also hiding something.  Anne and Mal are a fun couple to read and I found myself unwilling to put the book down.  Their relationship was like a rollercoaster ride that is very well written and sweet.  Kylie Scott is a fantastic storyteller and I highly recommend this book!  I do think you will get more enjoyment if you start with the first story in the series, Lick, though this could be read without reading it.
Is very well written and a different twist.  A good read if you like horses and paranormal romances.  Not bad at all.

Have you ever read a book that at the end you turned the paged and read and thought NO! and then you get to the cover and thought- that's the end? well yup. That's what happened. I thought the ending was just awful. Only the fact that the author wrote the book well earned it two stars and not one. I mean- really- UGH. I am so happy I did not pay for the book. I say that because, I don't understand how this book ended up in the 'romance' category.Pros to the book- The author does a good job describing the kidnapper/ scene. That he looked nervous. Also, when the 'physical line' first gets crossed- I thought that was written well.

I have just finished this book, it took me six days to read it, only because work got in the way! If I had had a full weekend, I don't think I would have put it down before the last page. It really is that entertaining!I have chosen to give this book 4 stars, only because they don't allow you to choose four and a half. The only reason I didn't give it five stars, is the occasional departure from reality. The fact that the heroin was drained of what seems like copious amounts of blood and then jumps up to start a fight was one such departure, other times there are just too many 'easy' in's for the protagonists to accomplish their tasks, though we all want things to go smoothy for them to defeat their enemies, life is not like that. The story occurs in our physical world, albeit a kind of post-apocalyptic world, therefore in my opinion, should follow the physical rules of our world, the Nephilim equipment not-withstanding, as to our physical capabilities.Otherwise it is an engaging, rich novel with likeable characters that are well thought out and interesting for the most part; Stu and Bern could use some further fleshing out, but are sufficient enough for the read.Looking forward to book 2!

From the beginning Columbia was destined to do something big other than help out the tree huggers.  Dimi seemed to be a little too into himself and revenge, but when these two accidentally collide WATCH OUT!  The sexual chemistry is amazing and you can't help but wanting to submit to Dimi yourself.  I was glad to see when things turned out well for both parties.  GREAT STORY!
Awesome I love these books the farther I get the more conclusions I can makeI totally love it oh by the way Ian sounds so so hot

I received this book in exchange for an honest review from the author through the Goodreads' group "Lovers of Paranormal". The Marked Ones drags you into the depth of the world of mermaids-their customs, their desires, their lifestyles, and more. The heroine, Ivyanne, is torn between two lives and more men that she can keep track of. Trying to find solis from the decision of choosing between three suitors in line to be king, mermaid Princess Ivyanne, travels to the place that gave her her fondest memories, unknowingly putting herself in the path of her childhood love. Now she has decisions to make and buried feelings to overcome.Holy cow! That's all that comes to mind. This is such a great and unpredictable story. I laughed at parts, cursed at others.  I actually felt my heart hurting, right along with the heroine's. The author does a wonderful job of pulling the reader in and keeping them there to the very end. I found it funny how I didn't want it to end, but at the same time, I couldn't wait for the end to find out what was going to happen. Because of the holidays, I had to put the book down more than I liked, but it was never far from my mind, wondering what was going to happen. The best part... What actually happened, wasn't anything I had thought up.The beginning was a little confusing when trying to explain the mermaid extended family, but became more clear later on. There also were some grammatical errors with the author leaving out small words here and there. It was more prevalent in the first have and I actually went back and forth between a 4 and 5 star review because of it. In the end, I thought the story was too good to get anything less than a 5. Great job! Keep them coming, because I will definitely be reading them. Thank you.
summary: Wow! Completely unexpected, and a book that needs to be read.

reviewText: I like this book on how to build a house and esure it that it goes smoothy and all the phases is success. It is really great to discover how to successfully navigating planning, design and contruction process that all descision will be in your hand. Its nice to have a new home on what you want to have and accomplish your dream by your own design procces and programming phase to define your ultimate objectives. The author does excellent job to discussed all we need to know especially for the permitting process works and important considrations in signing a cotract with a contruction. This book is very helpful and useful. Great Job!

I received an Advanced Reader Copy of this book from the author in return for an honest review.I am fascinated by Egyptian gods and the history of Egypt in general, so when I was given the opportunity to read a fictionalised story containing Isis, Osiris and Set, I jumped at it!Isis is a very fascinating character. She is a goddess and an immortal. She has been kept as a prisoner by her brother-in-law, Set. She is understandably bitter and angry, and is out for revenge. She and the other gods also drink blood for extra strength; this seems to be where the myths and legends pertaining to vampires comes from.I thoroughly enjoyed this book. It is a very original story that should have a lot more recognition. However, I did have a slightly negative reaction to it. Revenge may be best served cold, but I'm not an advocate of revenge. I believe an eye for an eye can be more damaging than turning the other cheek. However, it is more easier said than done. I'm not saying that Isis shouldn't feel what she feels, but acting on it is another matter. The flow of the story was excellent, and the tale was interesting enough for me to want to continue reading the series.It is near the end of the book that things get even more intriguing! I have read an anthology, Morbid Seraphic, with S.K. Whiteside's short story Fallen in it. There is a sneak peek of Fallen at the end of Vexed, which introduces Malachi. He's a fabulous character, who seems to have lost his way. I'm now looking forward to reading the next installment of this series!S.K. Whiteside has written a fantastic story that is well written and unique. I love her style of writing, which is fast paced and descriptive. I recommend this book if you love YA, Paranormal Romance, Egyptology fiction, Vampires, Goddesses and other mythical supernatural beings. - Lynn Worton
summary: A Promising Start to a Series

reviewText: This book is written well and the story line is very realistic - I found myself wondering what steps I would take to survive

This is very short story but it a fun story.  If you have read the Riyria series then this short story is a nice little vignette of the early days of Royce and Hadrian's partnership.  If you have not read the series then it great way to introduce yourself to the story.  I loved the books and really like the characters. I think the plot is engaging, exciting and the characters are very interesting.  The contrast between Royce and Handrian makes their partnership interesting and often funny.  The dialog is good and I think Sullivan is an excellent writer.  This short story made me smile and laugh.  It was also very interesting to see how they came to know the Viscount.  Lastly, I enjoyed finding out a little bit about the author.

Cristin Harber hits it out of the park again!  I loved Brock and this novella so much.  I loved how Ms. Harber took Brock, who could have been portrayed as the villain in this situation, and gets the reader to empathize with him.  To see him as a man in an unthinkable situation who made mistakes all in the name of keeping his family safe.  As the reader, I found myself rooting for him to get his family, his friends and his job back.  Kudos to Ms. Harber for making me fall for a man whom I probably should have hated.And did I mention how hot Brock is?  That scene in the back of the truck with Sarah?  Wow!  I needed a cold drink after reading that scene!I loved how the men sorted their s*** out.  Jared’s means of revenge on Brock was priceless.I loved everything about this novella and desperately want Brock back on Team Titan!  This is a must read for fans of the Titan Series and romantic suspense.

This book has some good ideas in identifying and reducing stress, rather than just managing it.  The concept makes a lit of sense as stopping a problem at its source is far mire effective than after it is out of control.  The backgammon analogy was more drawn out the what was needed, but the premise is solid and the concept easy to understand and intuitive.  I liked the book and have already recommended it as stress reduction and looking at the root cause of stress to stop it as soon as it starts are good ideas that are explained well.

Way too short a story but one that keeps you wanting more.  I was rooting for Gabe for good reason.  And you will too.  Sometimes your Prince Charming is literally staring at you, if you let yourself believe.  Definitely Kathleen Lee knows how to keep her readers enthralled.

Women Serial Killers of the Nineteenth Century was an interesting read. The short but complete stories about the different killers were extremely well researched and summarized. (I can't imagine all that information about each one would still be around but the historical references and images help to support the vignettes.) This is one of a series of such books including women serial killers from the 17th Century, 18th Century and the 20th Century.
summary: Women Serial Killers - Well Researched and Interesting

reviewText: If you read my review of A Kiss By Design you know that I was NOT a fan of Zach. Being able to read his side of the story was very helpful in changing my opinion. He isn't really a bad guy but I still think that when it came to his relationship with Emily he was very selfish and pretty naive. While I don't condone cheating I had a hard time with how Zach made Emily and Dylan out to be the bad guys in the whole. My biggest irriation stems from the fact that he thought that he was SO fantastic and wonderful that, even though he knew Dylan was in love with Emily since way back in high school and was always there to comfort her, Emily would just always be there for him to support him and his football career no matter what.I get it, that was sort of the point, that he and Emily had a relationship based on all the wrong things. I also know that he realized this but he still continuously seemed to put all of the blame off on Emily and Dylan. Then Jenna started to do the same thing. P.S. You guys kissed while he was still dating Emily but I guess that doesn't count against you? That was my least favorite part of their story. I think I still just have a lot of love for Emily and Dylan. Haha.I did love that Jenna gave Zach a hard time and that she didn't treat him like he was some sort of god. I LOVE that she never went out of her way to dress up and "make herself pretty" just to tutor him. She was exactly what Zach needed without either of them knowing at the time. It was good to see another side of Zach in this book. He tends to come across as a cocky, selfish jock but in reality he is so much more than that. He doesn't like to party and he cares about getting good grades, he hopes for a future in football but is realistic that it might not be in the stars for him so he isn't banking on that alone. I think it showed a great maturity for him to put the responsibility of deciding the outcome of their relationship on Jenna. He didn't want her coming to him because she felt sorry for him or obligated but because she wanted to be with him. It was important that their relationship was decided based on their feelings without outside interference.It was great to see Zach and Jenna get their HEA. I'm just hoping we get to see little brother Nick grow out of his pervert stage and into his own relationship in the next book, if there is one? A reconciliation between Dylan and Zach would be a welcome surprise in a 3rd book as well. :)*I received a complimentary copy from Net Galley in exchange for an honest review
summary: Great to hear Zach side of the story

reviewText: I love this book! The author does a superb job of bringing a small Southern town to life with very funny secondary characters such as Miss Beulah and Essie Mae, the town's gossips. The baseball and fried chicken scenes had me laughing out loud. And the poignant resolution had me crying. This book is great romantic comedy, but it also explores deep conflicts as Reverend Paul Donovan is torn between his own needs and those of his congregation. Don't miss this lovely, lovey book, the first in the Donovan series!

First reviewed at RedHotBooks.comThis is the third book in Crane’s romantic suspense series, The Associates.  Although each can be read as a stand alone, there is an over reaching arc that threads through the books; some readers might find themselves a bit lost with missing information.Thorne McKelvey has been working his way up the notorious Hangman game for years.  No one knows that he’s really a plant for Dax, the head of the super-secret spy ring, The Associates.  Many years ago, Dax noticed Thorne’s skills and made a deal with him.  Dax would give him the new identity of the man who murdered his sister in return for working for him.  Since then, Thorne’s focus has been to getting to the top of the gang food chain to take out his sister’s murderer and give Dax the names for of the crooked politicians, judges and cops aiding them.  Unfortunately, he fell for the wrong woman in the process.In the past two years, Nadia Volkov’s life has changed drastically from being the pampered mob princess she was raised as.  The man she fell in love with (and knocked her up) left her high and dry. Shortly thereafter, her father was gunned down.  Nadia has had only her sister and her former bodyguard, Richard, to help her raise her son, Benny.  While going through the family house, she discovers a treasure trove of information about her father’s business in human trafficking and a picture that leads her to believe that her mother might be alive.  Nadia manages to convince Richard into helping her raid the workhouses to find her mother.  It’s these very raids that bring Thorne back to her doorstep.Thorne is being fingered as the rat and he desperately has to find the CD that he knows is hidden in his former boss’s house.  He’s shocked to find not only Nadia still living at the house, but a young child too.  After Nadia gave birth to Benny, she was relieved that Thorne ditched her before she was able to tell him she was pregnant. She doesn’t want Benny to have the criminal life she grew up in. Thorne’s reemergence in her life is putting everything she’s worked for the last two years into jeopardy.  Time is running out for both of them as they frantically try to complete their missions and come to some stalemate.Let’s just say that Thorne is one HOT mess of a man.  His parents were deadbeats who sold their kids off. He blames himself for his sister’s death even though it wasn’t his fault.  Thorne survived being tortured by scorpions and escaping by breaking his own hand.  ROUGH, right?  Then the Party Princess comes along and they play some dirty kinky games. Thorne has never had anyone care about him in his entire life, so why would he believe that Nadia would?Nadia felt like Thorne is the only person who ever saw past the superficial exterior.  She was devastated when he dropped her without a second look.  The second go-around for the couple has both of them dancing warily around each other while Thorne lights fires with some dirty talking.  The sexual tension is incredible and the payoff sweet.  I could’ve done with a little more of their backstory, but that’s minor.If you enjoy suspense, the action is pretty much nonstop.  Though the main mystery wasn’t that hard to figure out, puzzling out where the author will be taking these characters still has my brain spinning.  The ending was a bit predictable but that didn’t negate any of the enjoyment of the story.  Crane has, once again, written intelligent unusual (did I mention Thorne is a Bruce Lee devotee?) characters with a fast paced story full of high suspense and sexual tension.Rating: B+*ARC courtesy of  CrushStar Multimedia
summary: Crane has, once again, written intelligent unusual characters with a fast paced story full of high suspense and sexual tension.

reviewText: If you're looking for a sexy read with a well-written power struggle, Cristal Blue might be the story for you.Ayers sets up the character Cristal Blue as the dominant in all her sexual encounters, but things don't go as planned this particular night, Valentine's Day. The guy she brings home with her affects her in ways that challenge her normal role in the bedroom. While there's a power struggle between who's dominant during the encounter, there's also the struggle between what Cristal normally wants and what her body is allowing to take place. That made the story that much more enjoyable for me.There's not much more to say about this because it's short and I'd be spoiling the rest for you, but it's made me check out more of Ayers works, and I'm currently reading (and enjoying) her follow-up to Cristal Blue, Sweet Treats.
summary: Review: Cristal Blue, by Suzy Ayers

reviewText: Ok for a quick read, but only the main people stood out, so why add other characters? Oh well it was ok but still rushed in my opinion.not quite sure what went wrong.but I'm sure something did.

You know, I could so see this turned into a tv series if there wasn't already one similar. 9 episodes in and I'm still thoroughly engrossed in it. There is always suspense with a smattering of snarky humor and love. I don't know how many episodes we are going to get, but I'm doing them all!

You're going to want to quit this book early, either after the girls get drunk or after the long bartender/redhead scene, and that's the shame of it because this book has a lot going on and the stories are pretty well executed.  I found the intersecting lives interesting and the doubts believable, even if the fiction is often vivid.  The other unfortunate fact is that a lot of work went into this book, but not quite enough, as there are many, too many, errors.  As changes were made, sentence structure suffered so there are extra/missing/incorrect words, that kind of thing.  This author thanks her publisher and beta readers profusely but this book needs and deserves a dedicated PROOFREADER.
The female character talked strong, but didn't act strong. There was something strange about the progression of her character. Could have been better.

This novella was a great fast read, with characters I wanted to get to know better. I totally loved the angle the author took, and I like that the characters were able to talk to each other and solve problems instead of the long-drawn out issues you see in some romances. I'm not one who goes for the angsty-hero and too-stupid-to-live heroine who just won't listen and keeps misunderstanding his behavior and the love is twisted and badly communicated...ugh. This was straightforward and packed a lot into a short framework. The characters actually communicated--YEA! There was a crazy plot twist and it was kind of crazy that the old girlfriend was willing to go to those lengths... but, I went with it because I liked the story. And yea, Mason was a nice guy so I see how Priscilla was able to take advantage of him! He wasn't an alpha dick like in so many books--he was a normal, nice guy--and that's what the heroine needed. :)Thanks for a great read, Hayden!
Another brief, yet direct piece by Truant. I like this one almost as much as his "the Universe..." one. If you're confused about what direction to go in life, this little book is for you.

Christian (The Beck Brothers, #4)by Andria Large4.5 starsChristian Beck has a loving family and wonderful friends but he is keeping a secret from them. He feels that if he reveals that he is a gay man that they will not see him in the same loving, accepting way he has become accustomed to. Christian has always hid his sexual orientation from his family. To make matters even worse he is in love with his best friend Shay, who is a heterosexual man.Shay is a beautiful caring man that has had his share of heartbreak, tragedy and secrets. His parents and sister were killed which leaves him with no real family and he recently found out that his best friend is gay and has been hiding it from him. Christian finally decides that upon telling Shay that he is gay he can no longer continue the relationship with him. The feelings he has for him are to overwhelming to continue a non romantic relationship. Shay takes the news as a shock but does something that Christian does not see coming. He agrees to a trial relationship with Christian. Shay tells him that he loves him and his family more than anything and he doesn't want to loose him and will do whatever it takes to keep them together. If they need to become lovers than that is what they will have to do. Will they be able to develop a romantic relationship after all these years of being friends, how will their family take the news. Could this be the beginning of something beautiful or will it all come crashing down around them.This was a wonderful end to the series and the epilogue gave you closure on each book. I truly feel in love with these men and their family.~~Michele~~
summary: I am so very disappointed that this series has come to an end!  I loved getting to know these beautiful men!

reviewText: I loved this story when it was first released years ago and was disappointed to hear it would be a stand alone. I was so excited to find out Flynn Eire was re releasing this book and continuing the series. The story line is original and Stryker and Rafe are made for each other. I can't wait to find out what Flynn has in store for the next book.

*sigh*What can I say? I loved it. Then again it shouldn't have come as a surprise, at least for me.Shiloh is eighteen and having a difficult time dealing with the way his life is going. Being bullied at school and still in the closet to his family, he believes that everything would be better for every one if he just went away. Until at the last moment, he has a revelation that would forever change his outlook in life and love.A story of fate, faith in the unknown and letting go of demons past, In Another Life is everything I have come to expect from a Cardeno C story. The characters were adorable, interesting and relatable. The emotions each one portrayed jumped off the page to impart the most impact in the reader and the chemistry was sizzling hot.I enjoyed each interaction, each funny moment and all of the emotional ones. The yearning, the trust and the love that the story invoked in me were the sentiments that make this such a heart-warming and touching holiday read for me. But most of all, what made this story so perfect, was the sense of rightness that the story drew from me.Another winner for Cardeno C and a fabulous holiday read to curl up to this Holiday season (well, anytime really!).
summary: Another winner for Cardeno C and a fabulous holiday read to curl up to.

reviewText: Yes, there really were Brave Japanese, but I never saw them....I was in Germany and never heard of them during WWII. It is only now that their stories come out. Good book.
When I started reading the series I couldn't put it down. Now I am hooked can't wait for the next book. Loved it.

I can't decide between 3 1/2 stars or 4 so I'm ging with four.We met Jack and Payton in book one Wilde Ride and I was anticipating this book once I finished book one but I have to say it wasn't all I was hoping for. Jack was an undercover cop and Payton and Jack met while he was undercover, once Payton found out that Jack had lied to her she cut him out of her life. Payton was never the type to fall for a guy or want more than just one night but with Jack she did. Now one year later Payton has moved to the town she met Jack and she soon runs into Jack. *Review first published on Goodreads*I have a feeling KA was watching GoT and was so obsessed with the Daenerys Targaryen-Khal Drogo pairing that she decided to write a fantasy about them. Perhaps it's because I kept seeing Dany and Drogo being cast as Circe and Lahn in reviews, that I couldn't help picturing them in my mind when I read GD. And I'm not gonna lie, they were indeed the perfect 'casts'.Circe Quinn woke up from her sleep into a living nightmare. One moment she was sleeping at home, and the next moment she was huddled up against strange looking women in a pen. She has no clue where she was, no clue how she got there, no inkling of what lies ahead. The next thing she knew, she was on the ground, claimed by a savage beast who is King and who eventually becomes her husband. For the next three days and three nights, her body was violated, and her soul broken.Realising that this is her new reality, she gradually opened up her heart, accepting her new role as Queen. With the help of Diandra, she learns their language and grew accustomed to their primitive ways. And slowly, she grew to become the beloved and revered Queen of the Korwahk Horde, as she courageously faced challenge after challenge.With each day, she grew to accept her responsibilities as Queen, friend, wife, and lover; falling in love with the primitive land, her people, and especially her Dax Lahn.Romance > FantasyUnlike Wildest Dreams, GD emphasised more on the romance. With Wildest Dreams, we had witches, elves, magical trees and relics, dragons, and all this you know right from the beginning. GD on the other hand spent the first 70% of the book building the premises of a primitive nomadic tribe, and building the love story between Circe and Lahn, and her people. And the culture, though strange, were not fantastical. You could imagine it happening back in the early days, or happening still in existing tribes.Now, I'm not one to shy away from a fantastic romance like this =D There were a lot more lovin' in GD which I thought was necessary for Circe and Lahn. That's because they could barely understand each other, and the only way to communicate their desire, and eventually love, is through deeper, more intimate physical relationship that replaces words.The Golden Dynasty > Wildest DreamsYou would have gathered that I preferred GD over WD. But it's not just the rocking lovin', the crude jokes, and the witty dialogues. I felt that the plot for GD is more complete. I did mention in my review of WD that the backstory about the captured Queen, and also about Sjofn were lacking. Perhaps fans of KA had gave her similar feedback because GD ended impeccably. We learned that Circe the Enchantress had decided to move to a different state, and the book ended with Harold Quinn listening to a 'message' from Circe with an old witch as her mouthpiece, and with the knowledge that even if he had lost his baby, at least he knew that he lost her to the greatest love.Conclusion: Kay anhay tee...chah! <3*For better review experience with gifs and the works, do proceed to Goodreads!*
