It probably seemed like just another year to Fodor, but looking back, 1936 seems like an especially interesting year to travel in Europe. Or risky, depending on your point of view. The Spanish Civil War was starting, the Nazi Party was rising in Germany, Mussolini was making changes in Italy (tourists were already noticing that the notoriously unreliable trains in Italy had suddenly become quite punctual).Despite the political tensions, there were many attractions for the tourist. In Paris, Josephine Baker was at the height of her popularity and Picasso was in his prime. Britain was preparing for a coronation and Berlin was gearing up for the Summer Olympics.It was the Great Depression. Unemployment was high all over Europe and America and it wouldn't be until the 1950s that middle-class Americans considered travel abroad as a possibility. It would be later than that for middle-class Britons. So the book is aimed at the Bertie Wooster set, upper-class people of wealth. There are occasional tips for people hoping to economize in their travels, but they are no doubt intended for the gap-year youth of means who hesitates to wire Papa for cash so soon after the last request.Still, it's surprising to find that much of the advice from 1936 applies today. In Italy, "do not attempt to discuss birth control." And leave your firearm at home, since in Italy, "foreign permits to possess firearms are invalid ... if you refuse to part with your revolver during your stay in Italy you may be exposing yourself to a great deal of unpleasantness." For travelers to London, "The ageless significance of Westminster Abbey will be thrown into relief ... when, [this spring] the ancient and gorgeous ceremony ... takes place at the church." No, not a royal wedding, but the coronation of  King George VI. The ceremony had originally been scheduled for Edward VIII, who abdicated the December before.On the other hand, some travel advice is peculiar to the times -- in Germany, it is suggested that you refrain from discussing politics, and as a foreigner you will be forgiven for failing to return a Heil Hitler salute. And some information is just peculiar, such as this - "Do not be surprised if you see well-dressed men made up just as heavily as the women. Such men are not necessarily perverts, for it is a recognised custom in Roumania for men to make up."There are ample suggestions for cabarets and clubs for men to attend with or without their wives where they can enjoy the spectacle of "lightly-clad" women singing, dancing, waiting tables, etc. For women, there is advice on day spas and shopping.This is a great book for browsing, and massive at 1,200 pages. It's inspiring in a way -- people didn't let Nazis and revolutions stop them from traveling.Also recommended --The American 1930s: A Literary History
summary: Great Year for Travel (Aside From That Civil War and Those Nazis)

reviewText: I grabbed this book, along with a dozen others, due to it's price tag of 'free' this morning. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much. I had already discarded half of the freebies due to horrible grammar errors and a dull story on the very first page.Sector C was different. I've spent most of the day reading it. I was hooked on the very beginning. The description of the hunt was very vivid, and it came as a shock when it was revealed that it was a setup. And then that the animals were genetically modified/cloned - another interesting twist. It's one of those rare books that I find I just can't put down - and if I do, my mind won't leave the story.The characters are very well written. I love the tiny details - the veterinarian rubbing the cow's forehead as she put it down, the interaction with the ranchers as they witnessed the death of their herds and their livelihoods. These are characters that the author has made very realistic, very three dimensional. I've found myself caring about the characters (and disliking others), and everything that they do seems well researched and very plausible.I am overall extremely impressed with this author and want to look for what else she (he?) has written. I'm assuming that this is a self-published novel, which makes it all the more surprising a find.
summary: Very Interesting and Very Well Written

Shay Mahone has 100% focus on her goal of owning a yoga studio with her best friend; he’s the yogi, she’s the business mind.  To attain her objective, she’s willing to do whatever it takes including work three jobs.  With a huge loan to repay for the restoration of their studio, she’s a bookkeeper, cater waitress, and nude model for art school.  On the emotional front she happens to despise people of wealth and entitlement, which mainly goes back to abandonment by her mother for a rich stepfather.  She also allows this and a failed college relationship to taint her view on men entirely.As a famous drummer, Brodie Davidson can’t be less of what Shay loathes.  He’s affluent and cocky celebrity with woman falling all over him.  At a closer look, he is all of those things but also just wants to return home to Charleston because he does not always enjoy the limelight.  He hasn’t had a true relationship in forever because he realizes women only want him for his fame and money.  He has a softer side which becomes apparent throughout.Initially Shay comes across as an indisputable self-reliant person who lets know one break through her exterior or come between her and her goals.  She’s quite spunky and feisty, having no trouble telling people her thoughts.  It’s this behavior coupled with instant physical magnetism that causes Brodie to approach her at a charity function where she’s working.  I was a little vexed by how contradictory she was towards him from the get go.  I suppose it’s part of the allure of their enchantment with one another but in some ways took away from the projected angst.  The relationship moved very quickly from its inception but that still made sense given the characters’ backstories.  I found it interesting how Brodie demanded her to open up while he still kept parts of his past hidden, fortunately he did finally give her every part of him.  I truly love the secondary characters, her best friend and her grandma.  They are quirky, dynamic, and add to the Shay’s growth.  Overall, this is a fun and entertaining which allows us to see their entire journey.Rating:  3.5 Stars~Complimentary copy received in exchange for honest review.~

First off, why doesn't this get a full five stars?  Passive verbs.  So much use of the word 'was' bring the action to a crawl.  It's more compelling to read "He was kissing her" or "He kissed her" in a romance scene.  I wondered if the author used so much passive voice intentionally when writing from Candy's point of view, but it ran throughout Black's POV as well.  Ms. Dark's writing will be a lot more stronger with a reexamination of passive versus active voice.This is good writing.  The author has a great way of telling a suspenseful story.  Even if we know what's going to happen, we still care about the characters and not everyone can do that.  The love scenes popped with excitement, the story's ending, while a cliffhanger, also satisfied.I very much want to see more work from this author.  This is every bit as good, if not better, than anything I've read from H. M. Ward.  Also, fans of Twilight, Fifty Shades of Grey, and a host of other sexy billionaire stories will eat this up with a spoon.

reviewText: This is a cute little romp most suitable to a younger person's taste. It is nicely written with a good flow to the narrative . The characters are fairly conventional with not much depth but I don't think this book was written as the great American Novel. This is more of a book designed to inform the public of what is happening in the world of pets in America. It explains how animals can be caught and sold as strays for nefarious purposes . There are numerous groups that are trying desperately to get all animal testing closed down and for good reason. It is not really needed in today's age of useful science especially having to do with cosmetics . Then you get into the fur trade and happily, "Dognappers" does not go there.  yet. As the story winds down or maybe I should say up;, as it gets much more exiting toward the end, we find the outcome fairly predictable  and all the ends nicely tied up. It is useful in making people see what can and often is going on  surrounding the business of caring for the family pet here in the USA.
summary: What Can Happen to Your Pet.

Liam, Julia’s boyfriend (now ex) was a jacka**. After he pulled a particularly d**k move and broke up with her in front of their – on the night she planned a surprise party for him – she decides to get even. With the help of friends Giff and Ava, she plots to make Liam jealous, win him back and break his heart. Additionally, a school project leads her to create a blog where girls can tell their equally hideous boy betrayal stories. Her plan for revenge moves along beautifully until Jesse comes along and makes her question why she’s even bothering.I liked Julia. She wasn’t a doormat. She was a strong and determined girl, someone I would be friends with in real life. Ava and Giff were both interesting characters, but I wish we had learned more about them. Jesse, on the other hand, I adored. I couldn’t get enough of him. He was a perfectly sweet and sexy love interest for Julia. A much better fit than Liam.In this short and sweet book, Julia eventually comes to realize revenge isn’t always the answer. She learns a lot about life, love and friendships in her journey. I enjoyed every minute of it. What wasn’t to like? This book gave me a strong heroine, a seriously swoony love interest, little angst and an interesting, if a bit predictable, storyline. I can’t ask for much more than that. And after that epilogue, I can’t wait to get my hands on Just Desserts.I received a copy of this book from the author in exchange for an honest review.

reviewText: The stories in this book are decent, but the lack of proper grammar, punctuation, and word usage really ruins it for me. In one of the stories, it appears that the author decided to change the character's name from Leigh to Scarlett, but didn't replace all the occurrences of "Leigh" with "Scarlett." There are also several other occurrences in that story where she calls the main character by her friend's name, making some of the lines confusing. Luckily, that's the only one that has this problem. In all the stories she uses the possessive "submissive's" instead of the correct plural form "submissives." There are several occurrences of misplaced or incorrect punctuation, honestly more than I can count. There are also a few (very few, maybe two or three) instances where the author uses the incorrect word. The correct word is similar, but has a completely different meaning. If not for the complete lack of proper editing, I'd probably give it a 4-star review. I would venture to say that a good 80+% of the pages have some sort of error. I realize the book was extremely cheap and that's why I'm not contacting Amazon and demanding my money back. That isn't, however, an excuse for the author to give less than her best to her readers. I read the excerpt from her new book. It seems like it might be good, but I'm leery about purchasing it because of this book. Also, the book refers to the main male character as a succubus, however that is the name for a female demon/creature. A male is called an incubus. Just throwing that in there.

Every book I read and love resonates with me. As I'm sure it does for others who enjoy a good book. This one, as I read it, made me think of my relationship with my husband and the power of a transcendent love.Summary: The sight of the red door saves Colin Baxter in his dream, but very quickly a man appears and the dream becomes a thing of raw sexual need with a person Colin can't identify. He just knows the man needs him, and Colin aches to find and heal his lover...even if the man doesn't really exist.Marek Donovan just wants to be left alone to lick his wounds and recover from a terrible loss. The rundown house in Fiji suits his minimal needs just fine. He doesn't want to face the world again, and on a small, secluded island figures he's safe from everyone and everything. Particularly guilt from his past.Dreams of this nameless man and his house plague Colin for two years, but he's come to care about his phantom lover so deeply he doesn't want them to end. Then Colin visits Fiji and comes face-to-face with the house from his visions, prompting him to believe these dreams just might be his destiny.Colin knocks on the door, determined to find answers.What I liked about this book: This is one of the Cameron Dane books that is not just smoking hot but grips your heart, clenches it in a tight fist and doesn't let go from start to finish! I have to admit that I had a harder time reading this one than the other books because it deals with such a huge loss and the pain that guilt from losing someone you love because of your own pride causes and I was not prepared emotionally to delve into that quagmire.But Marek and Colin kept drawing me to their story and with every step into their budding and troubled relationship, I fell deeper into the hope of their "happily ever after". Cameron Dane has that wonderful ability to not just make the characters come to life, but their raw emotions slam into you with such fierceness, you find yourself gasping and verbally outing yourself while reading her books in public.

I thoroughly enjoyed the roller coaster ride of emotions Rivers served up with this first helping of the Burnside family. Once I got into the story I genuinely connected with the characters. By the end I was laughing, choking back tears, and wishing I could talk some sense into the two, as well as Destiny's three siblings. While Destiny's unemployment/underemployment situation strongly resonated with me, making her more accessible than most of the love interests I've read about recently, I do think Rivers adeptly wove together a very emotionally driven romance with Live. There are somewhat graphic love scenes, but the emotions at play really made them sweet and not feel excessive or superfluous.While we are not far into 2014 yet, I suspect this will sit at the top of my best romantic reads of 2014 for some time. I've not read any other books by Mary Ann Rivers before, but after reading this one and her short bio at the end I'll definitely be seeking out some of her other titles as well as keeping an eye out for the rest of the Burnside siblings stories.It took me much longer to read this title than most lately and that typically means it did not resonate with me well. I will agree that it took a fair bit for me to get hooked, but I'm going to blame the slowness of reading this book on work/life and binge watching an old TV series with my DH that just showed up streaming. Once I pulled together some measurable bits of time to really sink my teeth into the story I got hooked. reviewText: The recipes in this book are easy to make. But they certainly aren't balanced recipes (therefore, you could cause your pet problems if you only fed one of them exclusively). In some places the recipes are unclear. They call for things like "1/2 cup vegetables." While most vegetables are fine for dogs, some (like onions) are not. Also one just calls for leftover meat (hopefully that meat isn't full of pepper, garlic, or onions, because those can make your dog feel sick).Nowhere does the book suggest which vegetables would be appropriate. If you fed meals from this maybe a few times a week, you would be OK. But I would try for a more comprehensive and better researched book if you want to feed exclusively homemade to your pet. Rick Woodford has a book that I would recommend someone who is going that route consider.
summary: Some fun recipes, but be cautious

This is the first in a new series by the talented Ms Mayburn and features her trademark heat and storytelling but this time the author enters the world of Motorcycle Clubs. It's not the usual tattooed bad boys though as this book primarily centres on the two leading characters and the journey they are both about to take. This book is just the beginning of what looks set to be a truly wild ride!Smoke is many things, a biker, an ex soldier, a security expert and a man obsessed by the strangely innocent young woman Swan. Swan just happens to be the twin sister of Smokes club presidents lady and as such it's been his job to watch over her. Swan has no idea that the gorgeous man who keeps showing up is about to change her life  but when she is mistakenly kidnapped instead of her twin sister Sarah it's Smoke who rescues her and he's not about to let her go!Swan has had a difficult childhood and her dysfunctional family are so not what most consider normal. Swan has severe trust issues and yet there's something about Smoke that just screams safety. Swan may not have wanted to be dragged into her families problems but when her mother chose to steal from dangerous men it put Swan firmly in the firing line. Swan may have tried living a normal life but the madness her mother has released is coming Swans way. Can she really trust Smoke or is he just using her? He seems determined to drive her crazy but it's a madness that's heating up her blood and Smoke truly sets her on fire!Oo what an opener! Smoke is such an enigma in so many ways. He is a hard man and will do whatever it takes to protect  his own and yet with Swan he is the most patient that I think I've ever seen in a sexy book. He is constantly showing the heroine that he wants her and yet determined to show her nothing but pleasure as she learns to trust him.Swan is an odd mixture of sensuality and innocence and when nervous just let's her mouth run away with her and because of this can be quite amusing to read about. She is not the usual kick ass or whiney heroine but an intruiging mix of the two and her way of communicating with her father is truly mind blowing! With Swan I think we can always expect the unexpected!So another biker book but it's not at all like any other that I have read. Scary guys yes and the odd sweet butt but this book has so much more to offer. It's a hot read and Smoke really knows how to satisfy his lady ! My only complaint is the somewhat abrupt ending but just like others I will be eagerly anticipating the next book. Not exactly a cliffhanger as such but there's a lot more to come and it's going to be fabulous !A gifted copy was supplied by the publisher for an honest review

reviewText: *Mild Spoilers*Even though I knew going into this one that I wasn't going to be gaga over these 3 and their situation, I did expect the "Love Triangle" to be a little more intense & developed, considering all the events that happened in previous books concerning Hawk, Dorothy, & Jase that led us to their book.I appreciated the little snippets of how things got rolling in the first place concerning their past, but it still just lacked something. It wasn't raw or really all that deep or emotional for majority of the book. Even the flashbacks lacked depth. They didn't tell/show me WHY Dorothy remained with Jase in spite of everything, all those years. They didn't show me why she ultimately turned to Hawk all those years ago & couldn't just walk away from him either. Why she felt torn between these 2 men in the first place and why she ultimately couldn't choose between them. NONE of this was given within their story.And I still for the life of me can't understand why these two men were so crazy in love & sprung on a woman like Dorothy to begin with. The woman had no education at all. She didn't even have a GED. No ambition or drive for life outside of wanting someone to love her in all her "bland personality glory". She had no back bone to speak of. No fire within her or pride for herself. So.... I just don't get this all consuming love & lust Jase & Hawk had for her, then or now.The story, all of it, just read as very impersonal and boring to me. Like we only received the headlines & not the true meat of the story. It just wasn't all that interesting for me.I felt that the book had good pacing & other things going on early on, mainly concerning just Hawk and his past. These things were a bit intriguing to me. But once I hit the 48% mark of this book, the story, pacing, everything began to drag and become quite lackluster. Honestly, this one didn't really start to become somewhat interesting or touching, til about the last 15% of the novel. Almost like Ms. Sheehan finally got her groove with the story & characters. But by then it was way too late. And the strength we are "Told" Dorothy finally embraces just was not convincing. At. All.But like I said before, I really expected this type of journey/outcome with these characters anyway. So I'm not really all that disappointed cos I was right, just wish there was something else to kind of grab onto or truly appreciate about the novel. Well, I can count on 3 fingers, instances that were truly funny to me. So I guess that's something.Jase- is a freakin cry baby. I didn't really care for his redemption/sobriety plot, until the tail end of the book. But I also never cared for Jase anyway. I did like Hawk, and honestly he's the reason why I read the book.But I have to be honest here, this was the most tame & unsexy novel in this series. WHERE WAS THE HOTNESS?! There was none. And I am NOT exaggerating here. Considering the standard already placed here for this series, this book most certainly missed the mark. It didn't even get close to the mark. If you weren't getting a fade to black scene, you got a HIGHLY glossed over one. So not only was there not a real story here, there wasn't anything to somewhat appease me for so many things that this one was lacking. *shrugs*So I understand why many readers were not happy with this book. It really should have been released as a Novella or better yet, as Ms Carrie pointed out, just a side story in Dirty & Ellie's book. (Which we are never getting) or you know what? This story shouldn't have been released at all, IMO.The Epilogue I don't get the "ick factor" or uncertainty that many claim they feel concerning this. Maybe cos it didn't bother me in book 1 either. But I gotta say ZZ definitely has me curious to find out. Honestly, I was hoping for his book in place of this one. I've wanted ZZ's story for awhile now.So.. No. I wouldn't recommend this read. If you want to know what the end result is leading into the next book? Borrow it and only read the last 20% and you will be good. Trust me, anything before that 20%, you're not missing out on much.

When I began reading Laced In Malice I could not have predicted where author Riley Gray was going to take me. In fact, I'm not sure where I ended up. I love that she had this suspense aspect to the story that my mind was doing somersaults trying to find which way was up cuz it just got completely handled. When I got done with the final words, I sat there thinking 1--WTF just happened? and 2--WTF just happened? I was convinced I was Team Oliver, yet then again I'm not so sure. No, I must be Team Oliver right?Riley Gray did a fabulous job of hooking you into the story from the get go. She didn't let up either. I kept turning the pages trying to figure out what was going to happen next. I like to think of myself as a great problem solver. Well Riley Gray shook that confidence out of me and stomped on it. Right when I thought I had it all figured out, Ms. Gray decided to switch it up and go left. She had great character development where you really thought you knew the characters but she made them so multi faceted that I honestly don't think that she wanted you to be able to figure everything out. And there lies the beauty and brilliance of Laced In Malice. I think that you can take the story and run with it. You can decide what the sequence of events means in the end. You can decide the true intentions of individual characters.Amongst all this brain labor, Riley Gray distracts you with gorgeous book boys who steal your heart. Oliver is a delicious a**hat who you want to slap yet let him have your way with you. I teetered on a fine line with him but I think in the end, he came out on top and he is so on my book boyfriend list.The female characters of Laced In Malice make me want to spit evil words and slash every designer top in their closet. Definite mean girls--that have their own chapter on how to be one. Lizzie was the ultimate bitch. She was the ideal antagonist and the character that draws you in with her callous and devious ways.Zara I don't even think knows what hit her. She doesn't know whether to run, to hide or to put it all out there. The Nixon twins (Oliver and Lizzie) are sending out signals like a graceful and unassuming jelly fish that has the sting of death.This is an absolutely fun and Machiavellian read. It definitely has the movie vibe of Mean Girls and Cruel Intentions, which makes it a great summer read with all the right elements--cunning, devious, gorgeous, delicious, evil, sexy, and sinful!I am absolutely looking forward to book two Laced In Deceit of this wicked tale.

In Hiding Away,  we are given a peek into Cal and Jane's relationship (since it was discussed very little in 'Letting Go').  We are also given information about Jane's background, that isn't as pretty as we may have thought.  She decides to leave her abusive boyfriend and move back home to sort her life out.  She isn't looking for love, but it finds her when she meets Cal.I absolutely loved this book!  The best things happen to you when you aren't expecting or looking for them... which is exactly what happens with Jane and Cal.  Once Cal sets his sights on Jane, there's no holding back.  Neither one was looking for a serious relationship, but once fate steps in, there's no stopping it.  Their attraction is immediate, as if their souls were made for each other.  They are that couple that you could picture being together forever and make you believe in soul mates.  Cal is the guy you want piecing together your broken heart, if you ever find yourself in that situation.This book is a novella that ends in a cliffhanger.  Don't let that stop you from picking it up.  There is so much emotion packed into this book, that you'll forget it's a short read (until you get to the last page and wish there was more).  This book is written so beautifully that you can feel the love between Cal & Jane.  She had me right from the Prologue.  I do need to add that the last line in the book.... if you were to google 'the right way to do a cliffhanger in a book', THAT line should be there.  Holy Cow!!!  Go big or go home! And JM Witt went big with that ending!This was, without a doubt, a 5 star read!  Cannot wait for the next book!  (JM Witt, that means no facebook... we need that next book, pronto!).
summary: You find what you're looking for when you least expect it....

At 18 Siobhan meets the handsome Blake and for a few glorious weeks she falls in love with him only to be sent away and not see him again until she is ten years older. Trudy Tucker is a 27 year old Oklahoma girl who has finally come to terms with her psychic abilities.  She sold her share of her grandfather's pawn shops to her brother and sister, bought an rv and set out with her trusty sidekick Mouse to make a living helping to solve crimes by using her ability to see through the criminals eyes.Levi Wolfe is a famous and extremely sexy psychic you uses his popularity to help him build his name in relation to his ability to solve crimes.  Not only is he a well known psychic, but he is also a very wealthy business man in the construction business.Trudy and Levi meet through Quintara and her round table discussions and workshops for new psychics trying to finesse their abilities and gain a better understanding of what they are capable of.  Quintara uses her relationship with Trudy to help Levi convince her that she should come to Florida to help solve the murders of several women in Key West.I have not read many crime stories in awhile.  To have the chance to read not only a crime novel, but a romance and crime novel in one was fantastic.  I was not let down in the least.  Deborah Camp writes a wonderful store that keeps you not only extremely turned on by the heated encounters between Trudy and Levi, but she throws in the suspense of the continuing crimes that are being committed.  The way that she lays out the story is perfection at its finest.  I absolutely loved how she used both Trudy and Levi's psychic abilities to help solve the murders.  I also want to give her kuddos on how she sets us up for the next story in the series without leaving us hanging on a cliff.  I must say thank you for that because I hate nothing more than to be all into a book and it just abruptly end.  If you are looking for a book that will turn you on and make you want to find out what happens next then this is a good book for you.  Look out James Patterson and J.D. Robb this one could give you some competition.
summary: Great story that will keep you hot and bothered and wondering what will happen next with the murders

Have you ever moved into a house where other families have lived.  All spruced up, painted, your own furniture in place - ever lie down in you bed and wonder . . . what secrets this house holds?I am not really into Horror stories.  I had read Stephen King's "Pet Symetary" and Dean Koontz's "Odd Hours" several years ago and decided my preference was "reality" Police procedural and Detective novels.Then, becoming a member of SHAMELESS SELF-PROMOTION for Authors here on Amazon, I found ALISON BUCK, the extraordinarily talented Author of "ABIDING EVIL" and "DEVOTED SISTERS", exceptional HORROR novels.  My taste in this genre heightened.  I then met in this forum Author STUART LAND.  I bought, read and thoroughly enjoyed his novel ORIGINAL BLOOD.  When he released his newest novel, SHADOW HOUSE, I was already hooked.SHADOW HOUSE is AWESOME!  It will keep you turning the page (or clicking Kindle) and you will not stop!!!Aaron Molina can best be described as a stereotypical American guy.  He has a beautiful wife, Clarire; a daughter Laurie (aged 12), a son Biran (8) and Laurie's German Shepherd "Brad".  They live in a middle-class suburb and have a normal, every-day American lifestyle.  Aaron is a Web Site Designer and Claire is a Real Estate Broker.  Aaron has fleeting thoughts of dissatisfaction with how his life has turned out. On an outting to a flea market with his sister, Rebecca (whom he is not overly fond of) and her third husband, Fred, Claire and his kids, Claire suggests he "find a hobby".  At the flea market he buys a small estate of tools and hand-carved furniture and children's toys.  The reader is then taken on a hair raising journey into a dead man's life . . . a man who refuses to stay dead.  A hint of Aaron's greed and flashbacks into PJ McAvoy's violent life are so well crafted, you feel as though you are hiding behind every corner, watching as PJ takes over Aaron's life and you are caught up in fear as you turn the page . . . scared of what will happen next.  The twists and turns take you into a mind-boggling state, and you will never guess how the Molina family's horror will end.SHADOW HOUSE should be on The New York Times Best Seller List!!!  It deserves to be out there, available to the mass market.  This is absolutely a FIVE STAR BOOK.Michael Phelps

reviewText: Holy Cannoli!!! What a finale or should I say beginning? I have been patiently waiting for the last installment of the Broken Angel Series by L.G. Castillo. I don't read paranormal romance very often, but when I do I turn to my co-blogger Ria for recommendations. She was the one that introduced me to this PHENOMENAL series! I love angels!!!!!! L.G. Castillo's amazing talent has made me love them even more! This story was beautifully written and it captivated me from beginning to end.It's very hard to review this book without giving anything away. When I finished reading After the Fall (Broken Angel, #2) I wanted answers. This is the book where all of our questions get answered. I think that out of all the series this is the book that was most emotional to me. To see how Lash and Naomi's love started was just breathtaking. When they shared that first kiss ... Oh, my God!!!! I got shivers!!! This is where their journey started and what an emotional journey it has been! Eternal love, it's a beautiful thing! <3What I really love about L.G. Castillo's writing style is that the connection she makes us feel with the characters is OUT OF THIS WORLD! I felt a connection to every single character in this series. Even Lucifer! I loved seeing all my favorite characters again : Lash, Naomi, Jeremy, Rebecca, Raphael, Uri, Rachel, Michael, Gabrielle, Chuy, Lalo and let's not forget my favorite one ... Welita!!!!!! I love her to pieces!!! Even if she was not very present in this book my heart burst with happiness when I read the scenes where she was mentioned.  What was amazing about Before the Fall, is that we get to see how the main couples found love and what they had to go through to find their HEA. It was emotional, intense and powerful!I am so sad that this series is complete. I wish I could read about these characters FOREVER! I am still crossing my fingers that a certain sexy angel is going to get his own book. He totally deserves a HEA <3I give, Before the Fall, by L.G. Castillo 5 beautiful, emotional, mesmerizing, eternal, powerful, irresistible stars! I want more!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Pretty please?!?!?!?! reviewText: I miss Zach and Beth and wanted more of them, and was so glad to immediately be taken in by Noah and Leia's stories.  They have that instant connection that Zach and Beth had, but they have issues that pale in comparison to Zach's!  Dual POV and sexy times aboard the IL plane!  I didn't see the cliffhanger coming.  Can't wait for the next book this fall!!!

Ready for a nice, light, contemporary romance? This is certainly to be the book for you! It is written in a very easy-to-read style, and the characters--especially Leslee. The story has some great points of humor, and there is really nothing tragic that happens to anyone in the book.I found Leslee's "dates" in the book quite humorous. When it comes to men, she indeed had bad luck. I think many women can relate to that. Although the dates are outlandish, they are certainly within the realm of reason in light of today's dating scene. It was nice to see her discover her true calling, and when she did, her luck seemed to change as well.I was glad that in spite of the zaniness in the book, the author used Leslee's situation to point out a great message that all single people should hear. Leslee spends her time looking for love, and she works very hard at it. She is counseled to stop looking for love and let it find her. I certainly appreciate this point of view, and it is indeed something that has proven true for many over the year.I must admit that I got tired of the profanity in the book, but at least we did not have to witness bedroom scenes. I would have preferred the characters being a little less promiscuous, but I know that my views of sex are different than the majority of people's today.If you are looking for a fun, romantic read for the summer, this just could be the book for you!I was sent a copy of this book in exchange for my honest review. I was not financially compensated, and all opinions are 100 percent mine.
This one was not at all what I expected. I was expecting something dark and serious but I would actually consider this more of a romantic comedy.

4.5 Stars!Desperate Match is the fifth installment in the Coded for Love series.  Even though this novel is part of a series, you can still read this as a standalone.  Each book focuses on a different soldier and his match, but the characters that were the focus in the other novels are still part of the story.  In this novel, we meet another hot soldier named Rowan.  Rowan decides that he wants to be matched to someone.  The soldiers in this series are genetically enhanced.  They are tall and strong which makes them very useful going against the enemy.  The soldiers are DNA matched to a partner.  Down the road, they give birth to future genetically enhanced soldiers.A lot of the genetically enhanced soldiers already have someone and Rowan feels alone.  Rowan decides to sign up to get matched.  Jill hears about the Program through the media and decides to sign up to be matched to a soldier.  Rowan and Jill end up getting matched.  There was a little bit of awkwardness when they first meet.  Jill did admit to Rowan that his missing arm bothered her.  At first it ticked off Rowan, as this has been a sensitive subject for him for his whole life.  Then he learned that Jill was running away from her abusive husband.  When her husband learns where she went, he still made things difficult for her by telling the media she was brainwashed by The Program.Even though at the beginning Rowan wasn't sure what was in store for the future between him and Jill, he stood by her.  Rowan is so good to Jill and he knew he had to protect her.  Knowing Jill was still very fragile, he was very patient with her.  He didn't rush her or force her into anything.  He allowed her to set the pace with things between them.  This tough soldier was very gentle with her. Even though Jill has been through a lot physically and emotionally, she's very smart.  She went for the first opportunity that was out there to start over.  She had the advantage of being protected on base and by the soldiers.What I like is that this group is like a really close knit family and help one another out.  Since Jill's family wasn't close by, they became her second family.  Rowan and a couple of the soldiers went to serve the divorce papers to Jill's husband, which did not go well.  This made her husband aware of what he is going to be dealing with if he comes near her.  When Jill decided to go to the media to let them know the truth about herself and The Program, one of the soldier's significant other worked with Jill in preparing for what to expect.I enjoyed reading this installment and encourage you to not only read this one, check out the other ones as well!  I look forward to reading the sixth novel, hopefully there will be one!

I just love a happy ending and even rock stars deserve them. I like the way Jess shows us the insecure man behind the World's Most Beautiful Man who doesn't want Sophie to be 'Just another groupie'. The idea of having a dream lover is brilliant, wish we all could meet the man of our dreams. I like the way this book and book 2 mesh but stand on their own. I like overlapping characters, you don't have to say goodbye to them when the book ends.

I love being a parent. I love my family. I love my children... and I know I need to be reminded of all the things I love about parenting and all the things that are important in our family--because at times, the world gets busy, the kids behaviour seems unruly and I can lose sight of the true nature of these angels--and this book is a great reminder of the truth: they are angels. They need out love and time and attention.I enjoyed this book immensely and was (again) inspired to be the best father I can be.
summary: We All Need Reminding Of These Truths

reviewText: That Which Destroys Me, WOW! I definite must read and I'm rating this book 5 stars.  I will be the first to admit, we all as readers have our own genre of books we love and ones we tend to stay away from. As an avid reader and blogger, ones I personally tend to stay away from is dark erotica. Not saying they can't be well written, but it's not necessarily my cup of tea. So after going back and forth about reading this book, I decided to go for it....there was something about this book that peaked my curiosity (the teasers and book trailer helps too).This book has three points of view: Stella, Wesley, & the mysterious "monster".  I personally love the inner dialogue between Stella & Wesley.  They both come from different upbringings, both severely damaged in different ways, it's amazing they made out the other end alive at all.  The both live day by day in passing, if it's even living. They work, sleep, one has nightmares and the other goes through women to get by.They both cross paths by Stella becoming an intern for Wesley, the familiarity is there, but they are both attracted to one another. Wesley has the need to dominate, Stella becomes a student in submission not knowing she's naturally submissive after a lifetime of unfathomable abuse. No one in their world will ever understand these two but each other, the only ones that can make their world tilt at the right angle.The "monster" comes into play, it's disturbing the thoughts that go on in this person's brain but you see how becomes this monster, and it's unfortunate.  This monster sneaks his way into lives that disrupts the world that has already been damaged in both Stella & Wesley's eyes. Who the monster? It's a mystery at first and when you find out, it's shocking and some what upsetting. Which makes is what makes this person the every definition of a monster.That Which Destroys Me is only I'm thrilled I didn't pass up, if I had to choose a book that was classified as dark erotica, I'm glad this book was it.  This book made me laugh, fall in love with the characters by being able to emotionally connect with them, sympathize, and cry. Definitely not one to pass up by anyone. ~Reviewed by Shannon (Book was gifted in exchange for honest review)
summary: Completely Immersed, A must read for every romance reader

reviewText: Well, I'm 30, but I'm not single, and yet - I WANNA GET MY ASS TO THE GATHERING! *winks* Celia Kyle writes snarky, sassy heroines that make me laugh out loud. The Wickham Sisters in her Alpha Marked series are completely nutty and I love them. The only thing better than the sisters? Their men. And those lucky bitches get not one, but TWO hot guys in each book. <- That's the reason I want to get my ass to the gathering! Can you blame me?Scarlet, Gabriella and Whitney all have their own hang ups. Scarlet's is that she resents being summoned to The Gathering where she'll have to sit through the werewolf version of speed dating and then be mated off to an Alpha Pair of wolves. Lack of free will can piss anyone off, so I don't blame her. Gabriella's problem is that she's had a line of jerky ex-boyfriends who have told her she's frigid. Now she worries no one will truly want her. Whitney's problem is that she shouldn't have been summoned to the Gathering at all! Her sisters carry the "Mark" that identify them as a future mate for an Alpha Pair, but she doesn't. Each book is a quick, delightful read with super smexy scenes (so you probably shouldn't read them at work). Whitney's book was my favorite story line wise, but my favorite men came out of Scarlet's book. And good news for you all - Whitney released today! So if you like your men alpha and sexy, your women quick witted and cute, and your stories to leave a smile on your face - then this series is for you. ;D
summary: I wanna get my ass to the Gathering now too!

Book -  Calculated (Book 1, Discovered series)Author - R.S. NovelleStar rating - ★★★☆☆Would I read it again - Probably not.Plot - okay, bit predictableCharacters - okay, a little regularMovie Potential - ★★★★☆ (probably better on screen)Ease of reading - easy.**I WAS GIVEN THIS BOOK, BY THE AUTHOR, IN RETURN FOR AN HONEST REVIEW**So this was a confusing read for me. I was a little surprised and confused by the first chapter, because it wasn't at all what I expected, then the character I was just getting used to was murdered. So bye bye, interesting character.To start off my review, let me say that there was a little too much description in this story for me. It wasn't just throughout the story, there was far too much description put in one bit after another. There was so much description in one paragraph that I was getting a little cross-eyed trying to force my imagination of this character to change to conform to the author's description of her. It ruined the flow of the story for me, to continually adapt my imagination to the writer's decisions. The descriptions were so focused and so intricate that there was really no way of allowing your imagination to run free.I have to say that I wasn't really that interested in the main character Ana. She seemed a little self-centered and career driven (not necessarily a bad thing) and lacking a conscience. She did things that drove the story forward, sure, but a lot of her reactions were odd and uncalled for, or really nave. I couldn't root for her at all.I'm not sure if it's because I just came from reading a fast paced, lovable main character driven story with limited detail, but Calculated seems slow and overly detailed to the point that it detracts from the story. The author has said and done all the right things in all the right placed, adding intrigue, curiosity, mystery etc and the chapters are short enough for a quick pick up every now and then, making it a quicker read, but it just didn't draw me in.As for the story, we're never told what Ana's big 'secret past' is and I'm really not sure that Book 2 will give me those answers either. I may not be interested, but it is a bit of a plot gap. In my opinion, the entire case is left unsolved, as well, with key persons left free to walk the world and never face the consequences of their actions. No-one is held responsible and not one of the bad guys, even the little ones, are caught.Apart from innocent men getting murdered (for a pretty elaborate reason, in an elaborate way, with a pretty strange background) we're really given no reason to care about the story. We don't get to know any of the victims, not enough to care that they're being slaughtered needlessly. We don't get to really know anything about Ana that makes her relatable or likable, so when she's in danger, I didn't really care what the outcome was.

I never thought writing a review for a book that I adore and love could be so difficult. But I have to admit, I have had a lot of problems coming up with what I want to talk about first when it comes to Used and I have to be careful so as not to spoil this book for anyone reading the review. Out of all of the books I have read, this one just stands apart. Yes, there is a hot guy or several and yes there is drama. Denver has more drama in her life than I care to imagine and in those regards it is like several books I have read. But the story sets Used apart from the others. It can turn a city girl into a cowgirl with the turn of the page and make every cowboy you see turn into a Greer or Ransom in the blink of an eye. You suddenly will start seeing big black trucks and wondering who is behind the wheel and some of you will even have to Google what an eight track tape is...which of course will completely break my heart and point out once again how old I am... but if the track fits the scene, you gotta turn it up and ride with it!So did all of that happen for me? Well, yes and no. I am a small town mountain girl so horses and cows really were nothing new to me; I've got several pairs of cowboy boots and hats to match. I think if I dig into storage, I could probably produce an eight track tape, but finding that black truck with the stereo to play it on may be a bit more difficult. I didn't have to look up pole bending and I tend to think of myself as a small town girl trapped in the big city and cowboy butts do indeed drive me nuts. What Used did for me was something different, it took something I dearly love and turned it into an amazing ride.Denver and Greer have grown up together. They know everything there is to know about each other. They are best friends and best friends with benefits. But Denver knows that she can never be what Greer deserves. She can't do a relationship. But that's the thing; Greer is so in love with Denver that it doesn't seem feasible to him to not win over her heart. That's why Denver has chosen to go to a different college than Greer. She wants him to be able to find what she can never be. But Greer is not giving up that easily. That's why he follows her to school but she doesn't know it until she is there and getting ready for her fresh start. A new beginning to become the person she wants to be without the reputation she has always held following her.So one of the first people she meets when she gets to college is this amazing bull rider by the name of Ransom... The attraction is there between the two of them, but he is a man-whore. But really is Denver any better being a slut? There lies the problem... Ransom doesn't want any part of a woman like her... but that attraction is there and no matter how much he wants to be away from it, it isn't going anywhere.So wait... so Greer is in love with Denver who is attracted to Ransom... oh my...This book is a page turner and so hard to put down and yes, as I told the author, I had to put it down because of prior commitments and that crazy thing called a day job and I hated every moment of it. I wanted to consume this book and devour each and every word in it.The thing about it is that you don't have to like cowboys or the rodeo to appreciate this book. The characters will make you fall in and out and back in of love with each one of them. I loved each of the characters for very different reasons. I loved that Greer was so in love with Denver that he would do anything for her. I loved that Ransom wanted to protect her. I loved that Denver was a sassy girl who didn't take crap from anyone.I have so much love for this story and I am so very excited that there is more of it to come. For those of you worried now that I have added that last sentence, there is no cliff hanger at the end of the book, but there is definitely more of the story waiting to be told and I cannot wait to get my hands on it. I am already getting ready to read this one again, it is THAT GOOD! No, it's better.Lynetta Halat has such a great writing style and it just captures me. I don't want to put the books down and this one seriously drove me over the edge to actually do it... I was dying! I even had this great little set up at my desk so people couldn't see me sneaking in chapters at work... Yes, that good.I just completely adore Lynetta Halat and she amazes me more and more each time she writes a book. Her books are beautifully written and so full of love and character and completely balanced out with angst and heartache. But Used definitely sold me on a new standard of greatness. I am so in love with this book that five stars will never do it justice. This book deserves all 10 stars that I am going to give it. It exceeded all of my expectations in a good book and has set such a high standard for which all books must follow.Whether it's the eight seconds on the back of a bull or the time to beat in tie-down roping or digging in with your heals and making every turn count... this book had every aspect of a great read all between the covers. When you read Used, hold on to your hat and get ready for a great ride! It is a ten out of five star read and I CANNOT WAIT for more!*I received a complimentary copy of Used in exchange for an honest review... and I honestly loved every moment of it!
summary: Denver, Ransom, Greer... GAH! This book deserves 10 stars!

reviewText: Remember the Moon is the perfect combination of nearly every emotion - sadness, happiness, humor, frustration, love. It is just as uplifting as it is heartbreaking. Abigail Carter has crafted an imaginative story that is beautifully and poignantly written. What a triumph! I can't wait to read many more books from her in the future.

This was an absolutely darling short story!  When Mavis wins a real live leprechaun in a raffle, little does she know that her life is about to change.  Greenberry Muldoon, aka Berry, is not just any leprechaun, he's loaded with gold, and a talent for housekeeping, decorating and fashion.  His goal is to stay with Mavis until there is nothing left for him to do, and he transforms her life, in a good way.  Then it's time for him to go, and Mavis auctions him on Ebay.  Before he leaves he give Mavis a kiss on the forehead, a real sign of luck for her.Truly a delightful tale.  Nancy Smith Gibson has created a whimsical character in Berry.  The story is clever and fun.  A great read that is well worth the time.
summary: Whimsical tale that's sure to delight!

reviewText: I absolutely loved this book!  I loved all of the twists and turns. I liked reading all of the different POVs although sometimes it wasn't clear exactly who's point of view I was reading. I don't want to spoil anything, but I wonder if her parents ever told her the truth? Still loved it and was so glad there was an epilogue. I wonder if any of the fighters will get their own stories?

This dystopian fantasy is a riveting and intriguing future of humans and vampires that keeps readers on the edge of their seats.  Vampires have become slaves to humans and fight in the arena as gladiators and Mira is undefeated, uncompromising and seemingly unbreakable. Lucian is Regent of the arena finds Mira intriguing and becomes her patron and his life has become expendable and they are both on the run.This fast paced and smooth flowing plot keeps the reader on their toes with action, suspense and drama. The author brings this futuristic world to life with great details and descriptions that provide vivid images that captures the imagination.  The fight scenes are well orchestrated and believable and with each scene the reader gets drawn more into the story.  The strong compelling characters are easily related to and keep the reader’s attention from beginning to end.There is no time to get bored with the non-stop action that takes place throughout the story with fights, escape attempts, snarky and humorous attitudes and intriguing twists that the reader doesn’t see coming.  There’s also no time for romance, though there is some hint of a romance blossoming between Mira and Lucian, of course they have to stay alive for that to happen. The series is obviously going to continue with Mira and Lucian’s uprising and it ended on a spectacular scene, and though it does end with a cliff hanger, the author chose a good spot.The author has created a fascinating and thrilling futuristic world that has lots of future entertainment potential and possibilities and readers can’t help but get caught up in the captivating characters and their story.  I was totally engrossed in the story from beginning and the concept and characters inspire lots of curiosity and I can’t wait to read the next book, although I feel I must warn you that the story is very violent and bloody as while the author does inspire vivid images, she is not overly graphic.

Left heartbroken at the altar, Ashley moves on with her life. Five years later, Jake comes back to town and wants her back. Can she forgive and forget or will she do everything in her will power to push him away, especially when those baby blues eyes ignites familiar emotions she tried so hard to forget?This was a great read, one that I could not put down. You could feel how much Ashley still cared for Jake. It had all the elements in a romance story that I love…humor…heart aches…and off course sparks that flew off the pages. Thank goodness there is book 2. If you like heartwarming stories, this is for you.

reviewText: I fell in love with Xander in the first book in the series. Now that may sound strange but I just thought there was more to him than what he was letting on. I was right he could be a softy when he wanted to be but yet he was still badass if you ask me. Hope was strong in her own way but she was a little nerve racking to at times. It made her character good because you didn't know if she was going to be strong and kickass or if she was going to just be weak and give up. There were parts that were really bad and had me cringing and asking why am I reading this? Of course if you read Madeleine Abducted or Joseph Fallen then you know that M.S. Willis has a way of sucking you in and not letting go. Same thing with this one. I can't wait for the next book to see what happens next at The Estate.

The author has a rather disconcerting habit of including the lead character's "thoughts" in quotation marks as though they were said aloud - particularly annoying amidst a "real" conversation - maybe they would have been better in italics as it could be less confusing?There is also a predilection to place "closing" quotation marks at the end of a paragraph while the "thought" or "conversation" is progressing - should be no marks at the end of the paragraph, opening quotation marks at the beginning of the next paragraph, and closing quotation marks at the end.The idiosyncratic thoughts, interesting aside comments, ancillary explanations and quirky expressions of the lead character are clever and amusing to keep you entertained and chuckling amid the drama.

First off, you cannot miss out the title. The title alone is interesting enough for you to take a peek into what the book is really about. It's title is Paleo Diet -- How to eat and exercise like a caveman -- is exactly what it sounds like. The whole book is about the diet adopted thousands of years ago by our ancestors.The book emphasizes that this type of diet is better, helping you to lose weight and helping your body to be revitalized to a healthier state. It does show you a lot of pros but it will also give you the opportunity to decide for yourself when it mentions the cons of the diet. Plus, you get Paleo recipes at the end part -- which is a good bonus.Overall, the book is worth reading. The content is informative. As for the diet part, well, it's up to you to decide.

This is part of an ongoing space opera series.For me, it has just the right combination of humour (yes, I prefer the British spelling :), action and a decent story line, along with a good selection of characters, good and evil.

Roberta Pearce' A Bird Without Wing starts with a common, cute situation: a mousey girl secretly head over heels for her boss, Luscious--erm, Lucius. Soon enough, though, we discover that things are not quite what they seem: there are many layers to Callie's personality, and her family and upbringing played no small part in shaping who she is when the story begins. I won't spoil it for you, but she's definitively not your average 'employee in love with the rich guy'.Lucius himself makes for an interesting hero as well, likeable, but a just a bit arrogant at time and with issues of his own, namely his family, which is the very definition of degenerating old money. Unfocused, cut from reality, and hoping that some mysterious family treasure will solve all their problems if they can put their hands on it.Brought together by a common friend and colleague, Callie and Luscious (yeah, I'm gonna keep call him that) work on a 'secret' assignment he came up with to finally set his family straight: Callie must demonstrate with absolute certainty that the Ransome's family legendary treasure doesn't exist.Again, I won't spoil, but overall, this makes for a fun, different read. At times deeply intimate and emotional, at times a bit hot, and that manages to explore very convincingly the dynamics of a budding relationship (Something that, oddly enough, 90% of all romance books fail to accomplish, choosing to go for the easy way, which is not the case, here).The book is also served by an excellent, consistent writing, that was really the cherry on top of the cake for me! :)
summary: A breath of fresh air in the market!

reviewText: I read this book thinking that I knew what was going on. I didn't I don't know what in the world is going on. This book is just enough to get you hooked and then it's over. Now I will have to get the next one because I have to get to the mystery.The author did a great job of getting me hooked and the characters are very mysterious.

I was given an ARC of Darker Days in exchange for my honest review.  This was my first Jus Accardo novel, but I "knew" her from #yalitchat and was really excited to dive in.  The synopsis sounded awesome!  And I wasn't disappointed.  From line 1, I knew I was going to like Accardo's writing style.Jessie (awesome name, btw!) Darker takes teen snark to a whole new level.  This girl has a quip for everything and can't manage to keep her mouth shut unless a witch is forcing her to.  But it wasn't annoying at all.  Jessie just had that kick butt personality and when you're a teen, sometimes your only (or best) weapons are words.  Not that Jessie has a shortage of weapons, because when it comes to "monster mashing" (her term), she and her mom are on top of their game.  They take down zombies, possessed dogs, and any sort of Otherworlder that comes their way.The book sort of reminded me of a teen version of Kim Harrison's The Hallow Series (starting with Dead Witch Walking).  Jessie is tough at nails even if not completely competent.  She's got a bit of a hidden power -- she's not a witch but her abilities are arguably cooler.  And there are a collection of cool paranormal creatures in the mix.Perhaps the best paranormal creature is Lukas.  Sweet, yummy Lukas.  Lukas is full of Sin himself (at least it's not Lust), but he does a really good job of keeping his inner evil at bay (I can't tell you more than that without spoiling things). But the best part about Lukas is how at peace he is with his fate because just a small amount of time with Jessie has given him peace. Who doesn't want someone to love them like that?  Jessie and Lukas felt so star-crossed, it made me root for them even harder.The plot was relatively complex, meaning I didn't guess precisely how the ending was going to come down.  That's a good thing!  And it certainly kept me flipping the pages.  It's action-packed and I never once felt bored or wanting the pace to move along more quickly.  But then again, with 7 deadly sins rampaging your town, there's never going to be a dull moment.In short, if you like snappy dialog and a fast-moving plot with paranormal hotties and baddies, you won't want to miss Darker Days.  I'll be very interested to see where the next book in the series goes.

The world has experienced natural disasters that have changed the face of the planet and there is also a man made disaster thanks to a terrorist group that have been nicknamed DOG's.  Then you throw in some gods that have decided they do not want humanity to end and here we go!I am very glad I started this series at the beginning and I am very excited to begin the second book in this series.  I can only imagine what I will think when I actually start the third book that started this whole fun adventure for me!

reviewText: Maryann is fast becoming a favorite author of mine!! This is the second book in this series and it's a wonderful heartfelt love story! get wrapped up and fall in love!

I loved this book. Granted I like zombie tales only if they have a viable plot and with the zombie and dead craze saturating not only the realm of books but television and cinema as well, we're on overload! So when I got the chance to find and read this little gem in the rough I could not put it down! READ IT!It starts off simple enough and from the beginning we get an idea this may be about an old lady that might have been driven insane because of the zombie epidemic and all the horrors she faced. And while some of this is true, the woman is hardly insane, a crazy or even the anti social she is made out to be. May is a true survivor of the darkest period in her life and humanity. She is credited for truly bringing the world and human race back from the brink of extinction.This small lone and lonely woman surviving the hordes of dead yet able to stay a step ahead because of hard learned lessons is the beginning of a great adventure. One can only imagine what she is going through as she carries the fight against thousands in a very intelligent and methodical way. Her journey is one that will get you thinking and wonder if maybe you would have the courage or even the will to continue to survive in a world gone mad. Yet survive she does. And while the first half of the book is about her and how she has managed to survive the second half does not disappoint as other survivors chance upon her. It is the lessons she imparts upon them that sparks the beginning of hope and the initial rise of humanity against the dead. To say this book was a pleasure to read is not giving it enough credit.May is a wonderful character and the author weaves a sad and lonely tale around this woman who survives at any cost. He also tells a tale of courage, perseverance and survival although I think he should have developed the secondary characters a bit more. It still works. I don't care for trilogies too much because I feel it is just a way to continue to sell books when many an author has nothing more to say and try to weave too many characters and plots that should end with the first book. In this case, I was sincerely sorry this book did not have a second and even third installment. May is the kind of character you would love to follow as she travels the country in her lonely and very effective war against the dead.Maybe the author will one day see fit to give us more tales of May and her trials and tribulations against a world that has lost all hope..until May arrives.

First let me say that it was a good story. My main issue was that I didn't have a good grasp of what the characters looked like. I didn't even realize they were black until I was well into the book. This the fourth book I have read by this author is a masterpiece of LIFE, relationships broken, hatred stored time lost and then restoration of family relationships. As usual throughout her stories she always brings God in to our everyday lives in a powerful way. Great work Melody Carlson
This story was really good except for having way too many typos in it.  I read for the immediate pleasure.

"A 13th Tail" by Daniel Kelley is interesting because it is so different from pretty much any other book I've read. Up front the author admits he has a phobia about the number 13. Consequently he faces his phobia head on by inserting 13 "things" 13 times into this book. He throws out a challenge to the reader to identify as many of those "13's" as possible. I only found 3 of them.First, let me say it is not easy locating the 13's, because they are very well hidden within the text. Second, even if they were easy to find, the storyline captures your attention so you just aren't paying attention to finding the 13's. (That's my story, and I'm sticking to it!)Having gotten that taken care of, I can move on and tell you this was really a nice little fairy tale story about a young horse on a global trek to find the "greener pastures" he's always heard the older horses talking about. He has found many places he thought were greener pastures, but come autumn they always turned brown, so he would move on until he found another green pasture.When he gets to the greener pastures in this story, everything is just so perfect he is convinced he has finally found it. Imagine his amazement, when he awoke one fall morning to realize the grass was turning brown! He was very sad; he didn't want to leave this place, because he really had enjoyed himself here. The other animals were all very friendly, the humans were kind and took good care of him, and he was positive the grass really was the greener pastures he sought.While he is looking downtrodden and discouraged, an older horse asks him what was wrong. When the older horse heard his tale, he started laughing! He told the younger horse that "greener pastures" is just an expression, and is something that is inside you, not something you will find externally.This story holds a very good lesson for young and old alike. Many, many adults continue to leave their jobs, their marriages, their families, their homes, always looking for greener pastures. Younger people as well hear the clarion call of greener pastures and move on in search of something they will only find if they look inside themselves. This is really quite an excellent story, and would be a great and thoughtful gift for any child on your gift-giving list. With any luck, their parents may read it, too.
summary: Fine, Fun, Fantasy for the Whole Family

reviewText: Michael Collins writes well, very well. This is a fast-paced story that is told well. The plot is believable and the characters life-like. I thoroughly enjoyed the book and felt I wanted more when I reached the end. Great stuff.

Ah, Shane, my favorite sociopath and assassin. I don't know what it is about him that appeals to me, well other than he has a wickedly dry, sarcastic sense of humor. No matter how many times I hear everyone in the coalition talk about how psycho leopards are and they're only good for killing, I can't help but feel that maybe growing up with Owen and Andrew affected Shane enough that he can have more than the lonely existence everyone seems to have slated him for. 'An Assassin's Touch' is book nine in the 'Lost Shifters' series and I would recommend reading these in order as there is too much backstory for them to be stand alones, in my opinion.Shane has been after a cobra shifter for several months now, and he's getting pretty angry that he keeps failing in his attempts. It doesn't help that the other snake shifter breeds are helping and they continue to attack Shane in his quest. No, the only thing that matters to Shane is that he keeps failing. His foster father taught him early on that leopards do not form attachments to others, they are incapable of love, and are only good for killing. He trained Shane to be the best killer he could be and when he failed in a task there were severe punishments. The problem is that Shane does feel emotions. When feline shifters turn away from him as if he's the bogeyman it hurts his feelings. He has nightmares every night where he hears the screams of the dying. None of this makes any difference though, because Shane knows all leopards are crazy, so he must be too. If only he could get the one encounter he shared with Trevor out of his mind.Trevor is a panther shifter and he's been very happy just playing around; he never sleeps with the same guy twice. So why can't he get Shane and their one encounter out of his mind? Even worse, he's very much afraid that if he succumbs, he'll lose his heart and since leopards don't form attachments, Trevor will be left with a broken heart. Doesn't keep him from wanting Shane, and when Shane stakes a claim, it's all Trevor can do not to jump him. But when another panther warns Trevor away from Shane, stating he doesn't want Trevor and his slutty behavior to mess with the rehabilitation they did on Shane, Trevor is shoved right back down to feeling like a worthless piece of crap. None of that matters though when Shane declares Trevor, "mine", in front of the coalition.Oh how I loved this book. Shane and Trevor are my favorites and, I'm sorry Andrew, you've been replaced in my affections. In fact, Shane and Trevor are being added to my list of favorite couples. And, in the spirit of the author, I am going to jump immediately into the next book and write my review. It's the only time in this series that the author wrote back-to-back books because she loved the characters so much, so I will follow that tradition.

Pushing Limits shines right off the pages. The plot edgily explores sexual preference, pushes boundaries, and equals in both angst and fun. It's well written with smart dialogue. The characters of Pushing Limits help the book thrive. Amber journeys through a new normal after she's cast aside by a politically driven, loveless mother. She's suffered a tragic loss involving her first love who is a woman. This was my first bisexual female lead and I enjoyed it. She's rebuilding herself, discovering her passions and living. Her character is formidable against change. I liked her sass, her edge, her expressiveness. She's forging a path for herself, doing her own thing; she's real. Her honesty is her most attractive attribute. Lightning strikes hot when Amber meets Tommy Bolt. Tommy is a strong character, an alluring hero. He's charming, sexually demanding, and funny. There's a charged passion in every scene with Tommy. The characters have interesting back stories and the pace at which they're developed makes for an easy read. The secondary characters make the book better as well. Sally is Amber's gay roommate; they're often engaged in flirty, fun, banter. Sally owns who she is completely and it's refreshingly honest. I liked where the author took us, I liked the conflict, and I adored the characters. I did not, at all, enjoy the way this book ended. Being part of a series, there is always the chance of a cliffhanger but this wasn't exactly a cliffhanger the book just abruptly ended; literally just in the middle of scene, done. That's my biggest issue. I'm excited for the second book to see where this author takes all of these characters. Pushing Limits is a recommended read that will leave you entertained.

I loved this story up until the end. I love Patrick and Emma together. I love that they got to have it all...almost. But I felt sad when I finished the book, and not just because it was the end of the series - which makes me sad, too. It almost felt like a death in the family even when there wasn't one. I read to escape reality and life. I can take a sad ending when there is one more book in the series to pick me up. I know from reading the comments that I am in the minority here, though, so don't let my comment keep you from reading the book. It was well written and a great book, just not the ending I personally wanted.

A Cat Called Cupid had me laughing out loud so often that I just couldn't help but love it. It's told in a cat's point of view which made me wonder if I really wanted to read it but I am sure glad I did.This is about a cat named Cupid who decides his Lady Ann needs to dump her boyfriend and get a new one.  Since he believes she has terrible taste in men, he arranges these events. Her current boyfriend, Jimmy who Cupid calls The Cat Hater is gotten rid of after Cupid puts his plan for this in motion.  Then he arranges for his Lady Ann to meet Craig who lives down the hall with his Siamese called Bella. Craig soon becomes Ann's new boyfriend.The author did a good job of writing this story from a cat's point of view.  We got to read what the cat would do in the situation, being a cat, and what the human should do in the cat's opinion. OK, so there were a couple of things the cat did that just could not have happened but, hey, this is fiction so I thought it was funny and liked it.

Book exchanged for an honest review:Professor Adewole, a Jerian who specializes in ancient languages, hopes to ease his heartache from his sister's passing. Being in Eisenstadt is a trying experience for Professor Adewole where he comes from there are no talking birds at all. Professor Adewole closest friend is Professor Karl Deviatka of the engineering department at The University of Eisenstadt. When Hilegard Goldstien lands her autogyro on the legendary isle Inselmond causes an unexpected uproar. Professors Adewole and Deviatka are selected to be apart of the diplomatic mission. Upon reaching Inselmond, the diplomatic party is in for a state of shock. Inselmond is known as Risenton by all appearances is primitive culture with a common phrase~Metal and Magic No More. Professor Adewole is stunned to learn that nobody can read or write any more. He's given access to the only library in Risenton and makes shocking discovery. Can the residents of Risenton survive? What is Professor Adewole's discovery? What does metal and magic mean? Your answers await you in The Machine God.Unique perspective for this series so far. I particularly enjoyed the whole Metal and Magic No More phrase because it should just how vastly different the two cultures were. I thought that Professor Adewole was very much like the bumbling professor from the movie Flubber just not so absentminded. There just seems to be so many stories that can be created in this series. I will definitely look forward to the next installment in The Drifting Isle Chronicles.

I always find it difficult when I don't like a book that everyone else loves,  but this didn't work for me.  It starts at the end - we know that Mattie and Simon have been apart for 3 years and then go to the beginning.  I think I would have enjoyed the book more without trying to see what is going to go wrong or create the separation, but that wasn't my main problem with the book.Spoilers aheadI just thought Simon was awful to poor Mattie. Mattie was so vulnerable and he could see that Simon had difficulties too,  but Simon could only see his own issues and couldn't see Mattie's needs or vulnerabilities at all. After a while I got so cross with Simon,  I thought Mattie could do better!  I know Simon was an unexpected single dad,  but he was in a much better space than Mattie and only afraid of emotional risk.  Mattie was fully prepared to emotionally risk everything for Simon, including his dreams of a future in New York,  but his poverty was putting him at real risk,  and he couldn't bring any of that to the relationship.  The scene at the birthday party was just too awful,  it was a deal breaker for me.  I couldn't forgive someone who had done that to me either...I read it to the end,  so that's an automatic 3 stars,  but I was really disappointed with one of the main characters,  so really it's a 2 stars rounded up.
summary: wanted to like it more,  spoilers ahead

reviewText: I read "She Belongs To Me" and found it to be quite a good mystery/thriller without the overt physical descriptions that overflow from other Romance novels I've ventured into. The Romance is more of a caring, loving sort."Split Decisions" is different. Not that the romance changes, but the story is stunningly better - and that is saying a lot. It opens with Jaynee sliding uncomfortably toward her 40th. Then the suspense and tension take off and keep rising."She Belongs To Me" dips a toe (the little one) into the paranormal. "Split Decisions" thrusts in a full foot. It surprised and delighted me, and it kept me avidly reading. DeSousa managed a twist I'd never encountered before and made it believable and suspenseful.You don't have to read "She Belongs" to read "Split Decisions" it is a complete story in itself, but I do recommend both books.
summary: A Romance Novel for People Who Don't Like Romance Novels
